      url: "https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/book/HypKnotTheory.pdf"
      locator: "§9.1, Lemma 9.5 and equation (9.3), printed pp.174–176"
    - title: "William P. Thurston, The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds"
      url: "https://library.slmath.org/nonmsri/gt3m/PDF/7.pdf"
      locator: "Chapter 7, Milnor's ideal tetrahedron volume formula and Fourier-series calculation"
---

## Statement

For every real $\theta$, $\Lambda$ is continuous, odd, and $\pi$-periodic, with $\Lambda(\pi/2)=0$ and
$$\Lambda(2\theta)=2\Lambda(\theta)+2\Lambda(\theta+\pi/2).$$
For $0\le\theta\le\pi$,
$$\Lambda(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(2n\theta)}{n^2}.$$
In particular,
$$\Lambda(\pi/3)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac1{(3k+1)^2}-\frac1{(3k+2)^2}\right).$$
For every integer $N\ge1$, the positive remainder after the terms $k=0,\ldots,N$ is at most $\sqrt3/(72N^2)$.

## Statement references

[Jessica S. Purcell, *Hyperbolic Knot Theory*, Lemma 9.5 and equation (9.3)](https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/book/HypKnotTheory.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The function $\Lambda$ defined by the improper integral in the Lobachevsky definition.

[F1] [[def-lobachevsky-function]] defines $\Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log|2\sin u|\,du$; logarithmic singularities at integer multiples of $\pi$ are integrable.

## Proof

1.1 For $|w|<1$, integrating the uniformly convergent geometric series on compact subdisks gives $-\log(1-w)=\sum_{n\ge1}w^n/n$. Taking real parts at $w=re^{2iu}$, where $0<r<1$, yields $-\log|1-re^{2iu}|=\sum_{n\ge1}r^n\cos(2nu)/n$. This series is uniformly absolutely convergent in $u$ for fixed $r$, so integrating from $0$ to $\theta$ gives $-\int_0^\theta\log|1-re^{2iu}|\,du=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}r^n\sin(2n\theta)/n^2$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 For $r\ge1/2$, $|1-re^{2iu}|^2=(1-r)^2+4r\sin^2u$, so $\sqrt2|\sin u|\le |1-re^{2iu}|\le2$. Therefore $|\log|1-re^{2iu}||$ is bounded by a constant plus $|\log|\sin u||$, which is integrable on bounded intervals. Dominated convergence sends the integral in step 1.1 to $\Lambda(\theta)$ as $r\uparrow1$; the series converges uniformly in $\theta$ because $\sum n^{-2}<\infty$. This proves the Fourier expansion on $[0,\pi]$ and continuity there. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The defining integrand is even, so $\Lambda$ is odd. Its derivative away from the integral's singularities is $-\log|2\sin\theta|$, a $\pi$-periodic function; the Fourier formula gives $\Lambda(0)=\Lambda(\pi)=0$, so the integral of this derivative over each period is zero. Hence $\Lambda(\theta+\pi)=\Lambda(\theta)$ for every real $\theta$. Substitution $\theta=\pi/2$ in the Fourier series gives $\Lambda(\pi/2)=0$. [F1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The identity $|2\sin(2u)|=|2\sin u|\,|2\sin(u+\pi/2)|$ and substitution $v=2u$ in the defining integral give $\Lambda(2\theta)=2\Lambda(\theta)+2\Lambda(\theta+\pi/2)-2\Lambda(\pi/2)$. Step 3.1 gives the stated duplication identity. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 In the Fourier series at $\theta=\pi/3$, $\sin(2n\pi/3)$ cycles through $\sqrt3/2,-\sqrt3/2,0$, so grouping successive triples gives the stated positive series. For $a=3k+1$, $a^{-2}-(a+1)^{-2}=(2a+1)/(a^2(a+1)^2)\le2/a^3\le2/(27k^3)$ for $k\ge1$. For $N\ge1$, the tail after $k=0,\ldots,N$ is at most $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\frac2{27}\sum_{k>N}k^{-3}\le\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\frac2{27}\int_N^\infty x^{-3}\,dx=\frac{\sqrt3}{108N^2}\le\frac{\sqrt3}{72N^2}$. [F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Sources

[Jessica S. Purcell, *Hyperbolic Knot Theory*, §9.1](https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/book/HypKnotTheory.pdf)

## Statement

Let $R$ be an analytic double-fibration transform, let $(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\eta_0)\in C_Z$, and let $\Sigma$ be a $C^2$ hypersurface through $x_0$ with $(x_0,\eta_0)\in N^*\Sigma\setminus0$. Let $f\in\mathcal E'(X)$ vanish on one side of $\Sigma$ near $x_0$. If the pointwise Bolker condition holds at $(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\eta_0)$ and $Rf=0$ in a neighborhood of $z_0$, then $f=0$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-analytic-double-fibration-transform|Analytic double-fibration transform]]

[[def-ip-bolker-condition|Pointwise Bolker condition]]

[[def-ip-analytic-wavefront-fbi-transform|Gaussian FBI criterion]]

[[thm-ip-analytic-wavefront-recovery-under-bolker|Analytic wavefront recovery]]

[[lem-ip-one-sided-analytic-support-continuation|One-sided support continuation]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The transform $R$, a relation point satisfying pointwise Bolker, a $C^2$ hypersurface $\Sigma$, and a compactly supported distribution $f$ with the stated vanishing and data hypotheses.

[F1] [[def-ip-analytic-double-fibration-transform]]: $Rf$ is a distributional density on the data manifold.

[F2] [[thm-ip-analytic-wavefront-recovery-under-bolker]]: if the data covector is absent from $\operatorname{WF}_A(Rf)$ under pointwise Bolker, then the paired object covector is absent from $\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-one-sided-analytic-support-continuation]]: one-sided vanishing plus absence of either oriented analytic conormal implies local vanishing.

[F4] [[def-ip-analytic-wavefront-fbi-transform]]: exponential decay of the localized Gaussian FBI pairings is the criterion for absence from $\operatorname{WF}_A$.

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the statement.

1.1 Choose a data cutoff supported inside the neighborhood on which $Rf=0$ and equal to one near $z_0$. Its localized FBI test functions are supported where the distribution vanishes, so all the pairings are exactly zero for every frequency. By [F4], this gives $(z_0,\zeta_0)\notin\operatorname{WF}_A(Rf)$. [F1, F4, given]

2.1 By [F2], step 1.1 gives $(x_0,\eta_0)\notin\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$. Applying the one-sided continuation implication [F3] then gives $f=0$ near $x_0$. All their hypotheses hold: the relation point has pointwise Bolker, $f$ has compact support, and the same nonzero object covector is a conormal to the supplied $C^2$ hypersurface. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given] ∎

## Definition

Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, $r=p/2$, and loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the complex Temperley–Lieb diagram category with objects the nonnegative integers and morphisms finite linear combinations of perfect matchings of bottom and top boundary points with no intersecting arcs. Compose by stacking and remove each closed component with factor $\delta$. Define $\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$ to be the subspace of morphisms $f:m\to n$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0$ for every reverse morphism $g:n\to m$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the unnormalized diagram-closure trace. Form the quotient category with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)/\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$. Its additive envelope adjoins finite formal direct sums, with matrix morphisms and matrix composition. Its idempotent completion adjoins objects $(X,e)$ for idempotents $e\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ with $e^2=e$, and morphisms $(X,e)\to(Y,f)$ are morphisms $a:X\to Y$ satisfying $a=fae$. Juxtaposition, planar cup-cap duality, and the induced trace descend to this completed quotient. This definition makes no assertion that it is semisimple, that its simple objects have a specified label set, or that any braid, twist, or modularity identities hold.

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot of genus $g$, let $V$ be a Seifert matrix in an integral symplectic basis, and let $\Delta_K^\#(t)$ be the unique symmetric Alexander normalization with $\Delta_K^\#(1)=1$. In the quotient ring $\mathbb F_2[t,t^{-1}]/(1+t)^4$,
$$\Delta_K^\#(t)=1+\operatorname{Arf}(K)\frac{(1+t)^2}{t}.$$

## Statement references

[[def-knot-arf-invariant-from-seifert-form|The Seifert quadratic Arf invariant]]

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert matrix convention]]

[[def-seifert-s-equivalence-and-conway-normalization|The symmetric Alexander and Conway normalization]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot, a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and its positive-push Seifert matrix $V$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Seifert pairing and Alexander conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] $V-V^T$ is the standard integral symplectic intersection matrix in a handle basis, and changes of integral symplectic basis preserve the Arf value. [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]], [[lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form]]

[F2] In a symplectic basis, $\operatorname{Arf}(K)=\sum_i v_{2i-1,2i-1}v_{2i,2i}\pmod2$, equivalently $\sum_{x\in H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)}(-1)^{q_F(x)}=2^g(-1)^{\operatorname{Arf}(K)}$. [[def-knot-arf-invariant-from-seifert-form]], [[lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form]]

[F3] The determinant $\det(uV-u^{-1}V^T)$ is $\nabla_K(u-u^{-1})=\Delta_K^\#(u^2)$. [[lem-conway-polynomial-from-seifert-determinant]], [[def-seifert-s-equivalence-and-conway-normalization]]

[F4] $\det(V-V^T)=1$ in a positively oriented symplectic basis, so the centered determinant is the unique normalized symmetric Alexander generator. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[cor-knot-alexander-normalization-symmetry-and-genus-bound]]

## Proof

1.1 If $g=0$, the matrix and homology group are empty, $\Delta_K^\#=1$, and $\operatorname{Arf}(K)=0$, so the congruence holds. Assume $g\ge1$. Choose a symplectic integral basis and, in each pair, arrange $v_{2i-1,2i}\equiv1$ and $v_{2i,2i-1}\equiv0\pmod2$. This is possible because their difference is $1$; if the odd entry is in the reverse position, replace $(a_i,b_i)$ by $(b_i,-a_i)$, which keeps $a_i\cdot b_i=1$. Let $A(t)=V^T-tV$. For indices $r,s$ in a paired position, its entries modulo two are $a_{2i,2i-1}=1$ and $a_{2i-1,2i}=t$; for every other position $a_{rs}=(1+t)v_{rs}$. The diagonal case is included, as $(1-t)v_{rr}=(1+t)v_{rr}$ modulo two. [A1, F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Let $B$ be the symmetric matrix over $\mathbb F_2$ with $B_{2i-1,2i}=B_{2i,2i-1}=1$ and all other entries $B_{rs}=v_{rs}$. For a permutation $\phi$ of $\{1,\ldots,2g\}$, let $\alpha$ count the indices $i$ for which $\phi(2i)=2i-1$, and let $\beta$ count those for which $\phi(2i-1)=2i$. Grouping the determinant expansion by these two counts gives
$$\det A(t)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^{g}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}(1+t)^{2g-\alpha-\beta}t^\beta\pmod2,$$
where $\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}$ is the sum of $\prod_r B_{r,\phi(r)}$ over permutations with those counts. Inversion $\phi\mapsto\phi^{-1}$ preserves the product because $B=B^T$ and swaps $\alpha,\beta$, so $\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}=\epsilon_{\beta\alpha}$. There is one permutation with $\alpha=\beta=g$, the product of the $g$ within-pair transpositions, hence $\epsilon_{gg}=1$. There is no permutation with $(\alpha,\beta)=(g,g-1)$: if every even row occupies its paired odd column, then every odd row must occupy its paired even column; one exception would leave one even column empty. Symmetry gives $\epsilon_{g-1,g}=0$. For $(g-1,g-1)$, inversion pairs equal-weight terms and cancels them modulo two unless the permutation is its own inverse. The fixed permutations must have every pair transposed except one pair fixed pointwise; any cross-pair exchange would make at least two pairs exceptional. Therefore
$$\epsilon_{g-1,g-1}=\sum_{i=1}^g v_{2i-1,2i-1}v_{2i,2i}=\operatorname{Arf}(K)\pmod2$$
by [F2], since the diagonal entries are $q_F(a_i)$ and $q_F(b_i)$. The finite Gauss sum in [F2] is $2^g$ times $(-1)$ to this same parity, so it identifies the determinant coefficient as the Arf sign used in the Conway comparison below. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 In the expansion of step 2.1, terms with $2g-\alpha-\beta\ge4$ vanish modulo $(1+t)^4$. For exponent $0$, only $(\alpha,\beta)=(g,g)$ remains, giving $t^g$. For exponent $1$, the only two terms are the symmetric pair $(g,g-1)$ and $(g-1,g)$, whose coefficient is zero. For exponent $2$, the diagonal term is $\operatorname{Arf}(K)(1+t)^2t^{g-1}$; the off-diagonal pair $(g,g-2),(g-2,g)$ is divisible by $(1+t)^4$, since $t^2+1=(1+t)^2$ modulo two. For exponent $3$, symmetry pairs each term with its transpose, and $t^a+t^b$ is divisible by $1+t$, so each paired sum is divisible by $(1+t)^4$. Hence
$$\det(V^T-tV)=t^g+\operatorname{Arf}(K)(1+t)^2t^{g-1}\pmod{(2,(1+t)^4)}.$$
By [F3], and with the normalization fixed by [F4], multiply by $t^{-g}$ to obtain the asserted congruence for $\Delta_K^\#(t)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied product tubular neighborhood, and let $E_K$ be its compact exterior with peripheral torus $T_K$, fibre meridian $\mu$, and the unique degree-one generator $[\lambda]$ of the kernel of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ supplied by the product-tube Mayer–Vietoris calculation. Then $K$ is ambient isotopic in the smooth category to the standard unknot if and only if $E_K$ contains a properly embedded piecewise-linear disk $D$ whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $T_K$. Every such disk has $[\partial D]=[\lambda]$ or $-[\lambda]$ and has odd mod-two intersection with the original marked meridian $\mu$.

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] — the smooth ambient-isotopy convention.

[[def-knot-exterior]] — compact exterior and boundary torus of the supplied tube.

[[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]] — the original meridian and preferred-longitude conventions.

[[lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude]] — boundary-slope and odd-intersection conclusions for every essential disk.

[Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger, Lemmas 4.1–4.2](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hass/Research/Papers/Complexity/hlp.pdf) — the claimed disk criterion and mod-two form.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, the smooth oriented knot, its supplied product tube, and the exterior and marked peripheral data in the Statement.

[A1] Countable choice is the standing hypothesis; the local finite rounding, surface normal forms and smooth isotopy interfaces below use this hypothesis. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] Every essential exterior disk has longitude class up to sign and odd intersection with the original fibre meridian. ([[lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude]])

[F2] A peripheral curve of core degree $1$ or $-1$ cobounds a finite piecewise smooth annulus with the core, smooth on a collar of the core boundary. ([[lem-degree-one-peripheral-curves-cobound-annuli-with-tube-core]])

[F3] A finite compatible whole-star surface with an already smooth boundary collar has a smooth embedded replacement with the same topology and exactly the same boundary, fixed on a smaller collar. Smooth transverse proper disks conversely have PL proper approximations preserving the boundary's isotopy class. ([[lem-finite-compatible-pl-surfaces-admit-relative-smooth-roundings]], [[lem-smooth-proper-disks-have-compatible-pl-approximations]])

[F4] A smooth knot bounds a smooth embedded disk exactly when it has genus zero, and genus zero is equivalent under countable choice to smooth ambient isotopy to the oriented unknot. ([[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]])

[F5] The PL convention here is the compatible PL structure of the supplied smooth exterior, represented by a whole-star smooth triangulation with boundary subcomplex and tangent-half-space fans. A PL disk can therefore be made a subcomplex by finite common subdivision, and its simplex restrictions have injective derivative fans. This is the ordinary meaning of PL in this smooth exterior, rather than a separate arbitrary topological marking. A representing finite whole-star triangulation is obtained by the finite coordinate-box and fitting construction of [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]; that supplier explicitly declares its ambient full-AC hypothesis dispensable and its actual finite construction uses no additional choice. The rounding and approximation clauses of [F3] use this same chosen compatible structure throughout.

## Proof

1.1 Suppose first that $K$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to the unknot. Carry the standard smooth spanning disk back along that isotopy, obtaining a smooth embedded spanning disk $B$ for $K$. In the product coordinates of the supplied tube, a sufficiently small collar of $\partial B=K$ has positive radial distance away from its boundary, with nonzero inward derivative there: the disk's inward tangent is linearly independent of the knot tangent, hence its normal projection is nonzero. Compactness of $K$ makes this estimate uniform. A compact portion of $B$ outside this collar is disjoint from $K$, so it misses all sufficiently small radius tubes. Thus for a sufficiently small $\delta>0$, $B$ meets the radius-$\delta$ tube in precisely that disk collar, and the radial level $\delta$ cuts a simple boundary circle transversely. The remaining disk $B_\delta$ is a smooth transverse proper disk in the radius-$\delta$ exterior. Its boundary has degree one along the core, because the original disk collar projects to $K$ with degree one; it is therefore non-null-homotopic on the radius-$\delta$ torus. [given, F4, construct]

1.2 Conversely, let $D$ be a proper PL exterior disk with essential boundary $C$. By [F1], $[C]=\pm[\lambda]$, so its degree under the product projection to the core is $1$ or $-1$. Apply [F2] to obtain an annulus $A$ on the tube side of the torus with boundaries $C$ and $K$, with smooth collar at $K$. Its interior misses $D$, because the interiors lie on opposite sides of the torus. The union $B=D\cup_C A$ is consequently an embedded disk with boundary exactly $K$. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Choose a smooth strictly increasing radial function $\rho:[0,2\epsilon]\to[0,2\epsilon]$ with $\rho(0)=0$, $\rho(\delta)=\epsilon$, linear near zero and equal to the identity near $2\epsilon$. Interpolation of positive derivatives with the prescribed interval integrals constructs such a function. The fibrewise map $z\mapsto\rho(|z|)z/|z|$, extended at zero by its positive linear derivative, and the identity outside the larger tube give a smooth ambient diffeomorphism carrying the radius-$\delta$ exterior to the supplied exterior. It takes $B_\delta$ to a smooth transverse proper disk and preserves core degree on the boundary. Apply the PL-approximation clause of [F3] in the compatible structure [F5]. Its PL proper disk has boundary isotopic to the original degree-one circle and therefore essential. This proves the unknot-to-PL-disk direction for the actual supplied tube. [F3, F5, step 1.1, construct]

2.2 The disk $B$ satisfies the finite-rounding hypothesis in [F3]. On $D$ the required simplex extensions and injective fans come from [F5]. Along $C$, use the product collar of the torus: an exterior disk collar and the first annulus strip lie on its opposite sides. Their half-fans meet precisely in the tangent fan of $C$, so the combined fan is injective. Subdivide along the finitely many corner and isotopy seams of the annulus; its graph strips, radial-level annuli and product core collar have the piecewise smooth regular charts constructed in [F2]. Any join can be given matching collar parametrizations, and the graph-coordinate corner rounding is performed away from the protected core collar. Thus the union has a finite whole-star piecewise smooth surface triangulation with an already smooth collar of $K$. The relative smoothing clause of [F3] gives a smooth embedded disk with the very same boundary $K$. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 By [F4], this smooth spanning disk makes the Seifert genus zero, and the given countable choice extends the disk-boundary isotopy to a smooth ambient isotopy to the standard oriented unknot. Together with step 2.1 this proves the asserted equivalence. For every essential disk, independently of its choice or of the smoothing construction, [F1] already gives $[\partial D]=\pm[\lambda]$ and odd mod-two intersection with the original marked meridian $\mu$. All clauses of the Statement follow under the original countable-choice hypothesis. [A1, F1, F4, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the unit four-ball $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.

## Statement references

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth concordance and its endpoint orientation convention]]

[[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot|The standard unknot]]

[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls|The unit Euclidean four-ball]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and one of the two asserted geometric objects.

[F1] A smooth concordance is a proper smooth annulus in $S^3\times I$ with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]])

[F2] A smooth proper surface has smooth boundary charts and product collars; removing an interior disk from a disk leaves a smooth annulus. ([[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

[F3] The standard unknot bounds its standard disk in the standard four-ball. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F4] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, an isotopy of a compact smooth source (possibly with boundary) into any boundaryless smooth manifold extends to an ambient isotopy supported in any prescribed neighborhood of its track. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence-choice principle in [F4]. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $K$, and either a smooth slice disk or a smooth concordance between $K$ and the standard unknot.

1.1 Suppose first that a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$ has boundary $K$. Choose an interior point $p\in D$ and a sufficiently small round four-ball $E$ about $p$ contained in $\operatorname{int}B^4$. In orthonormal coordinates at $p$, the local graph theorem writes $D$ as $z=g(u)$ over a disk in its tangent plane, with $g(0)=0$ and $Dg(0)=0$. For small radius $R$, the function $r\mapsto r^2+g(r\theta)^2$ has derivative $2r+O(r^3)>0$ for every unit direction $\theta$ and $0<r\le R$. Hence $D\cap\partial E$ is one radial graph over the tangent circle. Replacing $g$ by $\lambda g$, $0\le\lambda\le1$, and solving the same strictly increasing radial equation gives an isotopy through smooth embeddings of $S^1$ in $\partial E\cong S^3$ to the equatorial circle. By [F4], with target $\partial E\cong S^3$, this isotopy extends to an ambient isotopy of $S^3$; hence $D\cap\partial E$ is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot. The family of round balls moving the center of $E$ to $0$ along a path in $\operatorname{int}B^4$ is an isotopy of compact embeddings supported in $\operatorname{int}B^4$; apply [F4] with target $\mathbb R^4$ to extend it. Hence $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}E$ is diffeomorphic, with boundary collars, to the standard shell $S^3\times I$. Removing $\operatorname{int}(D\cap E)$ from $D$ gives an annulus in that shell with boundary $K$ and a standard unknot. [F2, F4, A1, given, construct]

1.2 Conversely, suppose $K$ is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. Reverse the interval coordinate if needed so the unknot is the lower boundary. Glue a standard four-ball along the lower $S^3$ end of $S^3\times I$. The union is a standard four-ball with an added boundary collar: explicitly, the collar extends the radial coordinate of the unit ball from radius $1$ to radius $2$, and radial rescaling identifies it with the unit ball. Cap the lower unknot boundary of the annulus by the standard disk from [F3]. The annulus and cap meet in matching product collars, so their union is a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary $K$. [F1, F3, given, construct]

2.1 The product collars at the two boundary circles identify the annulus from step 1.1 with a smooth concordance, after orienting it so the lower boundary is the negative of its induced knot orientation and the upper boundary is positive. If necessary, reverse the interval coordinate to place the unknot at the lower end; a half-turn of the standard round circle about a diameter is an orientation-preserving ambient rotation that reverses its circle orientation, so the endpoint still has the standard oriented unknot type. Reversing the annulus orientation when required gives the boundary convention in [F1]. Therefore $K$ is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. [F1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove that a smooth slice disk gives smooth concordance to the unknot, and step 1.2 proves the converse. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Statement refuted

Assume full AC for the Jones invariant and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for $c(K)$.
A classical knot is a smooth embedding $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered
up to ambient isotopy. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with
only transverse double points, each marked with over/under information. The
false universal extension is: for every classical knot $K$, including the
unknot, there is an integer $q$ with $2\le q\le3c(K)$ and
$f_q(K)\ne(0,0)^{\mathsf T}$. Here $V_K(x)$ is the normalized library Jones
polynomial with $V_U(x)=1$, $f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$ is defined by
the unique expansion $V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)(x-x^{-1})^q$, and
$c(K)$ is the least crossing number of a regular diagram of $K$.

The boundary input is the unknot $U$, represented by the crossing-free circle:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.55);
  \node at (0,-0.9) {$U$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Statement references

[[def-jones-vassiliev-coefficient-vectors|Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vectors]]

[[def-crossing-number-of-link|Crossing number]]

[Carmi and Cohen, *On trivial Jones–Vassiliev polynomials*, Theorem 6.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.22410v1)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and the unknot $U$ with its one-component crossing-free diagram.

[F1] The library Jones polynomial has $V_U(x)=1$, and the coefficient vector is obtained from the unique finite expansion in powers of $p=x-x^{-1}$ ([[def-jones-vassiliev-coefficient-vectors]]).

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $c(K)$ is the least element of the set of crossing counts of regular diagrams representing $K$ ([[def-crossing-number-of-link]]).

[A1] Full AC is the family-choice assertion ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects an element from each countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Counterexample

1.1 Under [A1], $V_U(x)=1$ by [F1]. Its unique coefficient expansion is $a_0(U)=1$, $b_0(U)=0$, and $a_q(U)=b_q(U)=0$ for every $q\ge1$. Thus $f_q(U)=(0,0)^{\mathsf T}$ for every positive order. [given, A1, F1, construct, algebra]

1.2 The displayed diagram has zero crossings, so under [A2] the set in [F2] contains $0$; all crossing counts are nonnegative. Hence $c(U)=0$, and there is no integer $q$ satisfying $2\le q\le3c(U)=0$. [given, A2, F2, algebra]

2.1 The proposed universal statement includes $U$, but steps 1.1 and 1.2 show that no required nonzero vector or admissible order exists for it. Therefore the statement is false. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

The source's actual coefficient claim assumes that $K$ is nontrivial, so this
counterexample refutes only the broader universal extension. The presence or
absence of DOI or journal metadata is bibliographic information; by itself it
proves neither the source theorem nor its negation.

## Definition

Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data, and fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their gluing is the standard oriented three-sphere. Specialize the framed-link Kauffman bracket skein module of $H$ to the coefficient field and root fixed above. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H')$, define the handlebody pairing $B_\Sigma(x,y)$ by gluing the two framed skeins and evaluating the resulting closed marked three-manifold with the normalized root surgery invariant. Define

$$\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H')\}, \qquad V_p(\Sigma)=\mathcal K_A(H)/\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma).$$

This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.

**External normalization input.** In this Definition the closed marked evaluation is the BHMV TQFT normalization, not merely the raw signature-normalized closed invariant $\theta_p$ of the Kirby lemma. BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum §11 pp.23–25 give
$$Z_p(M,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}(\kappa^3)^w\theta_p(M),\qquad \Delta_\pm=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{\pm3}.$$
Thus $Z_p(S^3,0)=\eta$ and $Z_p(S^2\times S^1,0)=1$. These nonzero normalizations and the registered Wall-sign weight are part of the pairing. BHMV Proposition1.9, p.891, identifies EXACTLY this radical quotient computed with two complementary handlebodies with its universal state space. This external identification supplies well-definedness of the presented model; its finite basis and gluing are the separate following lemmas. The selected $\kappa$ remains a sixth root, with one weight step acting by its cube. The source itself is only used at these located statements/constructions, not as a claimed locally reconstructed universal-construction proof.

**Source hypotheses for this identification.** The normalized BHMV closed invariant is multiplicative and involutive, so BHMV Proposition 1.1 gives its cobordism-generated quantization functor at this fixed root; extend its coefficients to $\mathbb C$ as stated above. BHMV Theorem 1.7 supplies both hypotheses needed for Proposition 1.9: its Kauffman bracket relations let that proposition replace the free bordism module by the specialized skein module, and its surgery axioms give the surjectivity and radical-kernel description. The corresponding weighted Lagrangian version is the BHMV skein TQFT with integral weights and Lagrangians in place of $p_1$-structures, as described by Gilmer–Masbaum in §11; their one-weight square-root multiplier is matched to the selected BHMV sixth root by $\kappa_{\mathrm{GM}}=\kappa^3$. In that section Lemma 11.1 states the weighted surgery axiom and Remark 11.3 applies it to the handlebody skein presentation; the source refers the Lemma 11.1 proof to the BHMV argument rather than repeating it. These are imported source inputs, not a locally reconstructed proof, and they do not add another quotient or change the state-space interface.

## Example

Assume full AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. An oriented classical knot is an
oriented smooth embedding $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered up to ambient
isotopy. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with only transverse
double points, each marked with over/under information; $c(K)$ is the least
crossing count among regular diagrams representing $K$. Let
$T=\widehat{\sigma_1^3}$ be the oriented closure of three positive two-strand
geometric half twists, with each strand oriented in the braid direction. The
figure shows the closure; its three crossings are positive under the library
determinant convention. For any classical knot $K$, let $V_K(x)$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and
$x=t^{1/2}$ in the convention $t=A^{-4}$. Put $p=x-x^{-1}$ and write the unique finite expansion
$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q$; define
$f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.88,line cap=round,line join=round]
  \draw[thick] (-0.45,3.15) .. controls (-1.1,3.15) and (-1.1,-0.15) .. (-0.45,-0.15);
  \draw[thick] (0.45,3.15) .. controls (1.1,3.15) and (1.1,-0.15) .. (0.45,-0.15);
  \draw[thick] (-0.45,0) .. controls (-0.45,0.28) and (-0.10,0.40) .. (-0.065,0.48);
  \draw[thick] (0.065,0.52) .. controls (0.10,0.60) and (0.45,0.72) .. (0.45,1);
  \draw[very thick] (0.45,0) .. controls (0.45,0.32) and (-0.45,0.68) .. (-0.45,1);
  \draw[thick] (-0.45,1) .. controls (-0.45,1.28) and (-0.10,1.40) .. (-0.065,1.48);
  \draw[thick] (0.065,1.52) .. controls (0.10,1.60) and (0.45,1.72) .. (0.45,2);
  \draw[very thick] (0.45,1) .. controls (0.45,1.32) and (-0.45,1.68) .. (-0.45,2);
  \draw[thick] (-0.45,2) .. controls (-0.45,2.28) and (-0.10,2.40) .. (-0.065,2.48);

  \node at (0,-0.42) {positive two-strand braid closure};

```

In the library Jones convention $t=A^{-4}$, the state sum gives
$V_T(t)=t+t^3-t^4$. With $x=t^{1/2}$ and $p=x-x^{-1}$, the unique
Jones–Vassiliev expansion is
$$V_T(x)=1-3p^2-4p^4-p^6+x(-6p^3-5p^5-p^7),$$
so $f_2(T)=(-3,0)^{\mathsf T}\ne0$. Carmi and Cohen's v1 preprint reports
that every nontrivial knot has such a nonzero vector at some order
$2\le q\le3c(K)$, and claims $V_K(x)=1$ implies that $K$ is the unknot.
This finite calculation checks one example only; it does not verify either
general claim or the preprint's machine-geometry proof.

[Kauffman, *Combinatorial Knot Theory and the Jones Polynomial*, §2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.12104v2)

[Roberts, *Knots Knotes*, §§4.3–4.4](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/knotes.pdf)

[Bar-Natan and Stoimenow, *The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants*, §1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9702009v1)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$, and its closure $T$.

[F1] A state of a nonempty diagram chooses A or B at each crossing, contributes $A^{a-b}\delta^{|S|-1}$, and has $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] In the stated chart a positive braid crossing is the operator $AI+A^{-1}e_1$, where $I$ is the through pairing and $e_1$ is the cap-cup pairing ([[lem-kauffman-smoothing-operators-for-braid-crossings]]).

[F3] Closing a basis diagram identifies each top endpoint with the corresponding bottom endpoint and assigns one factor $\delta$ to each resulting circle; stacking removes each closed cycle with the same factor ([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]], [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]).

[F4] The cap-cup diagram named $e_1$ in [F2] is the elementary diagram generator $d_1$, and it satisfies $d_1^2=\delta d_1$ ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

[F5] The positive elementary half twist has endpoint permutation $(1\ 2)$, and a braid closure has one component for each cycle of its endpoint permutation ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]], [[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

[F6] The positive geometric Artin half twist has determinant crossing sign $+1$ ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F7] The writhe-normalized bracket of a diagram $D$ representing $K$ is $f_K(A):=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$ ([[thm-bracket-state-sum-matches-library-jones-specialization]]).

[F8] In the library convention $t=A^{-4}$, the exact Jones value of the positive trefoil closure $T=\widehat{\sigma_1^3}$ is $V_T(t)=t+t^3-t^4$ ([[def-temperley-lieb-quotient-and-jones-specialization]]).

[F9] The library Jones polynomial is an ambient-isotopy invariant and $V_U(t)=1$ ([[def-temperley-lieb-quotient-and-jones-specialization]]).

[F10] For $p=x-x^{-1}$, every Laurent Jones polynomial has a unique expansion $\sum_q(a_q+b_qx)p^q$, and $f_q=(a_q,b_q)^{\mathsf T}$ ([[def-jones-vassiliev-coefficient-vectors]], [[lem-jones-vassiliev-basis-decomposition]]).

[F11] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $c(K)$ is the least number of crossings among regular diagrams of $K$ ([[def-crossing-number-of-link]]).

[A1] Full AC supplies the library Jones-invariance hypothesis ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice hypothesis in the crossing-number definition ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Verification

1.1 For a state with $k$ B-smoothings, [F2] gives a stack of $k$ copies of $e_1$ and $3-k$ copies of $I$. If $k=0$, the closure has two circles by [F3]. If $k\ge1$, repeated use of $e_1^2=\delta e_1$ from [F4] and the one-circle closure of $e_1$ in [F3] gives exactly $k$ circles. There are $\binom{3}{k}$ choices, so [F1] gives the complete grouped state sum $\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}k&\text{states}&|S|&\text{contribution}\\\hline0&1&2&A^3\delta\\1&3&1&3A\\2&3&2&3A^{-1}\delta\\3&1&3&A^{-3}\delta^2\end{array}$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, construct]

2.1 Substituting $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ into the grouped sum gives $\langle T\rangle=A^3\delta+3A+3A^{-1}\delta+A^{-3}\delta^2=A^{-7}-A^{-3}-A^5$. By [F5] the closure is one knot component, and [F6] gives writhe $3$. Applying [F7] therefore gives $f_T(A)=(-A^3)^{-3}\langle T\rangle=A^{-4}+A^{-12}-A^{-16}$. On the other hand, [F8] gives the exact Jones value $t+t^3-t^4$, which at $t=A^{-4}$ is the same Laurent polynomial. Thus the direct normalized state-sum calculation agrees with the library Jones value for this trefoil. [F5, F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write $x^n=A_n(p)+B_n(p)x$. From $x^2=px+1$, multiplication by $x$ gives $A_{n+1}=B_n$ and $B_{n+1}=A_n+pB_n$. Starting with $x^0=1$ and $x^1=x$ yields $\begin{array}{c|l|l}n&A_n&B_n\\\hline2&1&p\\3&p&1+p^2\\4&1+p^2&2p+p^3\\5&2p+p^3&1+3p^2+p^4\\6&1+3p^2+p^4&3p+4p^3+p^5\\7&3p+4p^3+p^5&1+6p^2+5p^4+p^6\\8&1+6p^2+5p^4+p^6&4p+10p^3+6p^5+p^7\end{array}$. This lists every recurrence step needed for the powers in $V_T(x)=x^2+x^6-x^8$. [given, F10, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Combining the rows for $n=2,6,8$ gives $a(p)=1-3p^2-4p^4-p^6$ and $b(p)=-6p^3-5p^5-p^7$. Uniqueness in [F10] therefore gives $f_2(T)=(-3,0)^{\mathsf T}\ne0$. [F10, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The computed Jones polynomial is not $1$. Under [A1], [F9] gives $V_U=1$ and invariance under ambient isotopy, so $T$ is nontrivial. The displayed braid has three crossings, so under [A2] and [F11] its crossing-number set contains $3$ and $c(T)\le3$. This example verifies a nonzero coefficient at order $2$ for this single knot; the general bound and unknot-detection claim in the Example section are only reported from the source and are not used as premises. [given, A1, A2, F9, F11, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎

      locator: "§2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form and Alexander-root determinant relation; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature at roots; complete 18-page PDF inspected."
---
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. The Hermitian matrix
$$H_\omega=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$$
is singular if and only if the normalized knot Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ vanishes at $\omega$.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert matrix convention]]

[[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial|The determinant presentation of the Alexander polynomial]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a genus-$g$ spanning surface with Seifert matrix $V$, and $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Alexander-module and Seifert-pairing interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For this surface, $\det(V-tV^T)$ is a unit associate of the Alexander polynomial, and its value at $t=1$ is $\det(V-V^T)=\pm1$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]]

[F2] The matrix determinant is reciprocal up to the unit $t^{2g}$, and the Alexander polynomial differs from it by a Laurent unit. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

## Proof

1.1 Since $\bar\omega=\omega^{-1}$, put $c=1-\omega$. Then $1-\bar\omega=-c/\omega$, and therefore $H_\omega=c(V-\omega^{-1}V^T)$. As $c\ne0$, taking determinants shows $H_\omega$ is singular exactly when $\det(V-tV^T)$ vanishes at $t=\omega^{-1}$. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F1], the determinant in step 1.1 differs from $\Delta_K(t)$ by a Laurent unit $\pm t^m$, which never vanishes on $S^1$. For $n=2g$, $M(t)^T=V^T-tV=-t(V-t^{-1}V^T)$, so taking determinants gives $\det M(t)=t^n\det M(t^{-1})$; its zero set is therefore invariant under inversion. Thus the determinant vanishes at $\omega^{-1}$ exactly when $\Delta_K(\omega)=0$, proving both implications. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Historical question

Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for
the crossing number. A classical knot is a smooth embedding
$S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered up to ambient isotopy; $U$ is the unknot
represented by a crossing-free circle, and “nontrivial” means it is not
ambient isotopic to $U$. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with only
transverse double points, each marked with over/under information. Let $c(K)$
be the least crossing count among regular diagrams representing $K$. Let
$V_K(x)$ be the library-normalized Jones polynomial with $V_U(x)=1$, where
$x=t^{1/2}$ and $t=A^{-4}$. Set $p=x-x^{-1}$ and write the unique expansion
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where the integer coefficients have finite support; set
$f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$. The historical Jones
unknot-detection question is whether $V_K(x)=1$ implies $K=U$.

## Historical question references

[[def-jones-vassiliev-coefficient-vectors|Jones normalization and coefficient notation]]

[[def-crossing-number-of-link|Crossing number]]

[Roberts, *Knots Knotes*, §4.4.8](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/knotes.pdf)

## Remark

Roberts's 1999 notes record the implication as a conjecture. Carmi and Cohen's
arXiv:2606.22410v1, submitted on 2026-06-21, claims that every nontrivial
classical knot has a nonzero coefficient vector $f_q(K)$ for some integer
$q$ with $2\le q\le3c(K)$, and claims $V_K(x)=1\Rightarrow K=U$. This
scaffold has read the stated result and the paper's proof route but has not
independently validated the claimed proof; it asserts neither proof acceptance
nor a definitive current open status.

The source's machine argument still requires an independent diagram-level
audit of Proposition 5.12, particularly its exceptional-state collapse,
smoothing proxy, and two-machine locality. Its numerical estimate
$B_{\rm aux}\le B_{\rm host}+12$ is consistent with the stated overhead
$\kappa_{\rm mach}=11$: the argument uses the next layer $r+1$ after
$r>B_{\rm host}+11$. This arithmetic check does not verify the geometric
reductions. No Jones-detection theorem is registered by this scaffold.

## Statement refuted

For a finite triangulation of the compact exterior of any nonempty oriented link, requiring only that the edge labels sum to zero around every oriented 2-simplex is sufficient to ensure that the labels represent the full meridian abelianization and are admissible input to the chain-model procedure.

## Statement references

[[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonempty oriented $r$-component link with $r\ge1$, a finite triangulation of its compact exterior, its certified positive meridian edge loops, and the label checks in the chain-model procedure. Exhibit labels satisfying every face-sum check but not the prescribed meridian homomorphism.

[A1] AC is the stated hypothesis of the full maximal-abelian-cover definition ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The procedure requires edge reversal, zero sum around each oriented 2-simplex, and value $e_i$ around the $i$th certified positive meridian loop; failure of any check returns `invalid-labeling` ([[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]).

[F2] The full meridian abelianization sends the $r$ positive meridian basis classes to the standard basis of $\mathbb Z^r$ ([[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]).


## Counterexample

Assign the zero vector in $\mathbb Z^r$ to every oriented edge. Edge reversal then holds, and the sum around every 2-simplex is zero. However every positive meridian loop also has label sum zero, which differs from $e_i\ne0$ for every component. The induced homomorphism is trivial, not the full meridian abelianization, and the chain-model procedure must reject this labeling.

1.1 For each oriented edge $e$, the zero labeling gives $\ell(\bar e)=0=-0=-\ell(e)$. Summing the three edge labels of any oriented 2-simplex also gives $0+0+0=0$, so every face cocycle check passes. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Every edge path, including each certified meridian loop, has total label zero. Since $r\ge1$, each required standard basis vector $e_i$ is nonzero, so the meridian-image check in [F1] fails and the induced map is not the full meridian abelianization in [F2]. Therefore the face-sum condition alone is insufficient, and the procedure returns `invalid-labeling` on this witness. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Sources

[[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]

[[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]

## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$, allowing zero measurement vectors and not assuming that $\Phi$ spans. Here $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[0]=\varnothing$; measurement labels are one-based, while coordinates in $\mathbb R^d$ use the library's zero-based convention $k<d$. Write $\mathbb R^{[m]}=\{y:[m]\to\mathbb R\}$. Use the Euclidean inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{k<d}u_kv_k$ and norm $\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}$. Define the signal equivalence relation $x\sim z$ by $z=x$ or $z=-x$, let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/\sim$, and write $q(x)=[x]$. Its quotient distance is
$$d_{\pm}([x],[z]):=\min\{\|x-z\|_2,\|x+z\|_2\}.$$

Use data space $Y_m=\{b:[m]\to[0,\infty)\}$ with metric
$$\rho_m(b,c)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{\sum_{k<m}(b_{k+1}-c_{k+1})^2},&m\ge1,\\0,&m=0.\end{cases}$$
The fixed relabeling $i\mapsto i-1$ identifies $[m]$-indexed data with the library's zero-based $\mathbb R^m$; $Y_0$ is a singleton. Define the real analysis map $T_\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{[m]}$ by
$$T_\Phi x=(\langle a_i,x\rangle)_{i\in[m]}.$$
The amplitude map is $\mathcal M_\Phi([x])=(|\langle a_i,x\rangle|)_{i\in[m]}$, while the intensity map is
$$\mathcal I_\Phi([x])=(\langle a_i,x\rangle^2)_{i\in[m]}\in Y_m.$$
A finite real measurement family performs **phase retrieval** when $\mathcal I_\Phi:Q_d\to Y_m$ is injective, equivalently when the induced amplitude map is injective. The quotient distance, both induced maps, and the data metric are well defined as verified below.

The diagram records the identity $\mathcal I_\Phi\circ q=S\circ T_\Phi$, where $S(y)=(y_i^2)_{i\in[m]}$ is coordinatewise squaring. It distinguishes signed linear measurements, amplitudes, and intensities; no proof relies on the diagram.

```tikzcd
\mathbb R^d \arrow[r,"T_\Phi"] \arrow[d,"q"'] & \mathbb R^{[m]} \arrow[d,"S"] \\
Q_d \arrow[r,"\mathcal I_\Phi"'] & [0,\infty)^m
```

[[def-ip-identifiability-and-stability-modulus|Identifiability modulo a target equivalence]]

[[def-max-min|Minimum of a finite set of real numbers]]

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary. If $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ are strictly positive and $u_j$ solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma_j\nabla_gu_j)=0$ with smooth boundary value $f_j$, then
$$\langle(\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1,f_2\rangle_{\partial M} =\int_M(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)g(\nabla_gu_1,\nabla_g\overline{u_2})\,dV_g.$$
If instead $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ have trivial Dirichlet kernels for $-\Delta_g+q_j$ and $u_j$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q_j)u_j=0$ with smooth boundary value $f_j$, then
$$\langle(\Lambda_{q_1}-\Lambda_{q_2})f_1,f_2\rangle_{\partial M} =\int_M(q_1-q_2)u_1\overline{u_2}\,dV_g.$$

## Statement references

[[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map|Full-data conductivity and Schrödinger DN maps]]

[[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness|Positive conductivity weak solvability]]

[[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity|Nonresonant Schrödinger solvability]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the weak DN-map well-posedness suppliers [F2]--[F3].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the weak DN-map well-posedness suppliers [F2]--[F3].

**Given:** the compact smooth Riemannian domain, two positive conductivities or two real nonresonant potentials, and arbitrary smooth complex boundary values $f_1,f_2$.

[F1] [[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: the conductivity DN map is the weak boundary form of $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_g)$, and the Schrödinger DN map is the weak boundary form of $-\Delta_g+q$; their smooth-data fluxes use $\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}$ and $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}$, respectively.

[F2] [[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness]]: positive smooth conductivity gives a unique weak solution for each $H^{1/2}$ boundary value.

[F3] [[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity]]: a trivial Schrödinger Dirichlet kernel gives a unique weak solution for each $H^{1/2}$ boundary value, with smooth solutions for smooth boundary data.

[F4] [[def-riemannian-volume-density]]: in each chart the Riemannian volume is a positive density, so the integration-by-parts identities can be patched without assuming orientability.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 Write $a_{\gamma_j}(v,w)=\int_M\gamma_jg(\nabla v,\nabla\bar w)\,dV_g$. By [F1], $\langle\Lambda_{\gamma_1}f_1,f_2\rangle=a_{\gamma_1}(u_1,u_2)$, since $u_2$ is an extension of $f_2$. Let $\widetilde u_1$ solve the $\gamma_2$ equation with boundary value $f_1$, which exists by [F2]. Then $\langle\Lambda_{\gamma_2}f_1,f_2\rangle=a_{\gamma_2}(\widetilde u_1,u_2)$. Since $u_1-\widetilde u_1\in H_0^1(M)$ and $u_2$ solves the $\gamma_2$ weak equation, Hermitian symmetry gives $a_{\gamma_2}(u_1-\widetilde u_1,u_2)=\overline{a_{\gamma_2}(u_2,u_1-\widetilde u_1)}=0$. Hence $a_{\gamma_2}(\widetilde u_1,u_2)=a_{\gamma_2}(u_1,u_2)$. Subtracting the two equalities gives the conductivity identity. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 Write $a_{q_j}(v,w)=\int_M(g(\nabla v,\nabla\bar w)+q_jv\bar w)\,dV_g$. By [F1], $\langle\Lambda_{q_1}f_1,f_2\rangle=a_{q_1}(u_1,u_2)$ because $u_2$ extends $f_2$. Let $\widetilde u_1$ be the $q_2$ solution with boundary value $f_1$, which exists by [F3]. Then $\langle\Lambda_{q_2}f_1,f_2\rangle=a_{q_2}(\widetilde u_1,u_2)$. Since $u_1-\widetilde u_1\in H_0^1(M)$ and $u_2$ solves the $q_2$ weak equation, real-valuedness of $q_2$ gives $a_{q_2}(u_1-\widetilde u_1,u_2)=\overline{a_{q_2}(u_2,u_1-\widetilde u_1)}=0$. Thus $\langle\Lambda_{q_2}f_1,f_2\rangle=a_{q_2}(u_1,u_2)$. [A1, A2, F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.2 Subtract the identities in step 2.1. The gradient terms cancel and the remaining volume term is $\int_M(q_1-q_2)u_1\overline{u_2}\,dV_g$, which proves the Schrödinger identity. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal S'$ be finite systems of pairwise disjoint smooth spheres in $S^3$, each sphere meeting $K$ transversely in two points, such that every knot obtained by capping the arcs cut off by the system is prime. ## Statement references

[[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot|Connected sums and prime knots]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and two finite prime decomposing sphere systems for an oriented knot.

[F1] A sphere transverse to a knot in two points gives exactly its capped oriented connected-sum factors, independently of boundary-cap choices. ([[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]])

[F2] Every smooth sphere in $S^3$ has two standard ball sides, simultaneously parametrized by smooth Schoenflies. ([[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]])

[F3] A prime knot is nontrivial and cannot split into two nontrivial summands; the unknot is the identity for oriented connected sum. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]])

[F4] Relative surface transversality and compact isotopy extension hold under AC$_\omega$. ([[lem-relative-transversality-for-embedded-surfaces]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F5] Under AC$_\omega$, genus is additive, nonnegative, and zero precisely for the unknot. ([[thm-knot-genus-additive-under-connected-sum]], [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]])

## Proof

**Given:** The two systems $\mathcal S,\mathcal T$, in transverse general position away from the knot. Call the two knot intersection points on a sphere its marks. A region cut out by one system is capped by standard balls and trivial cap arcs on all its spherical boundaries; its resulting knot is its factor.

1.1 First record the local replacement precisely. Let $D$ be a disk in one region of the complement of $\mathcal S$, with interior disjoint from that system and boundary a circle $c$ on a single sphere $A\in\mathcal S$. The circle misses the marks. Surgery on $A$ replaces it by the two spheres obtained by attaching parallel copies of $D$ to the two disks of $A\setminus c$, rounded and slightly pushed apart. The three spheres bound a standard sphere with three holes: take a product collar of $A$ and attach the thickened disk. Consequently the region on the other side of $A$ is unchanged after capping, except for extra punctures; all actual changes of capped knot occur in the one region containing the interior of $D$. Its other cap balls and arcs are untouched. This gives a precise local model in which the following cases are checked. [given, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 If $D$ has no mark, parity forces $c$ to leave both marks of $A$ in one disk of $A\setminus c$. Indeed otherwise one of the surgery spheres would meet the closed knot once, whereas a separating sphere has an even number of transverse intersections with a closed curve. Thus one surgery sphere is unmarked and the other has two marks. After capping the affected region, the unmarked sphere misses its closed knot. By [F2] its ball side not containing that connected knot is an empty ball. Filling or removing this empty ball and the adjoining product collars changes no capped knot. Discard the unmarked sphere and retain the twice-marked sphere. Hence this replacement preserves every nontrivial factor. The same argument covers empty ball and nested ball positions: it uses the side avoiding the capped knot, rather than a prespecified inside side. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

2.2 If $D$ has one mark, parity instead forces each disk of $A\setminus c$ to have one mark. Both surgery spheres then have two marks. Let $C$ be the cap ball attached to $A$ on the affected region. Construct a proper disk $E\subset C$ with $\partial E=c$ by pushing one of the disks of $A\setminus c$ into the cap collar, fixing its boundary and rounding there. This disk is boundary parallel. Choose a simple boundary arc joining the two marks and crossing $c$ exactly once; a thin rectangular strip about that arc gives a boundary-parallel cap arc $\beta$ in $C$ meeting $E$ transversely exactly once. Explicitly the strip passes from the side of $E$ next to the first marked boundary disk to the side next to the other one, with a single normal crossing; away from that crossing it stays in disjoint boundary collars. Thus $\beta$ is trivial, and changing the original cap to $\beta$ is allowed by [F1]. Now $D\cup E$, rounded at $c$, meets the capped knot exactly twice: once on $D$ and once on $\beta$. It is the required marked decomposing sphere in the capped affected region. By [F1] the old factor $P$ is the sum $P'\#P''$ of the two new capped factors, with orientations inherited from the original knot. Since $P$ is prime, exactly one is the unknot and the other is $P$, by [F3]. Retain both new spheres temporarily and then delete the sphere separating that trivial region from its other neighbour. Deletion merges the neighbour with an unknot, so leaves its oriented knot class unchanged by [F3]. The net result is again a prime system with exactly the same unordered prime factors. The disk $E$ and the cap change lie entirely in $C$, disjoint from every other cap ball of the affected region. On the opposite region the three-holed-sphere collar of step 1.1 replaces only the cap at $A$: the short pieces of that cap become the caps on the two new spherical boundaries with the same endpoint pairing and orientation. Its other cap balls and their arcs stay pointwise fixed outside this collar. Therefore, even when that neighbour has several boundary spheres, deleting the sphere next to the trivial new region changes its capped knot precisely by oriented connected sum with the unknot, without changing any other attachment or factor. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 To compare intersecting systems, choose a sphere of $\mathcal T$ that meets $\mathcal S$ and an innermost intersection disk on it containing at most one mark. Such a disk always exists: if there is one intersection circle, its two complementary disks have at most two marks in total, so choose a side with at most one. If there are several circles, the circle nesting tree has at least two leaf disks with disjoint interiors; since there are only two marks, one leaf contains at most one. Its interior misses $\mathcal S$. Use this disk in step 2.1 or step 2.2. The surgery copies can be pushed off $\mathcal T$ in its product neighbourhood and rounded near $c$; they introduce no new intersection circles, while $c$ disappears. Deleting a redundant sphere only decreases the count further. Thus the finite total number of intersection circles strictly decreases. Iterating makes the first system disjoint from $\mathcal T$, preserving its prime factor list throughout. [F4, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct]

4.1 For completeness, the disjoint-system comparison is the same local calculation without surgery. Add the spheres of $\mathcal T$ one at a time to the disjoint first system, initially allowing trivial capped regions. In the capped region containing such a new sphere, its two marks give a connected-sum decomposition by [F1]. If the region's factor is prime, one new factor is that prime and the other the unknot; if it is the unknot, both new factors have genus zero by [F5] and hence are unknotted. Thus adding disjoint spheres preserves precisely the multiset of nontrivial prime factors. The union system therefore gives both original lists, which agree. A maximal factor ball replacement across a disjoint sphere consists of adding that sphere and deleting the old one; the same comparison proves its asserted preservation, including nested positions. [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 3.1, construct] ∎

## Remarks

This proof uses spheres with two marked points. It does not assert a link-level prime decomposition with attachment data. It uses neither knot-exterior boundary incompressibility nor a theorem about decomposing a knot exterior.

## Sources

[[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]]

[[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]]

## Statement

Assume full AC. Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, and the BHMV Kauffman bracket convention with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. On the weighted Lagrangian extended bordism category built from the root semisimplified Temperley–Lieb data, the normalized Kirby-color surgery maps define a finite-dimensional skein TQFT: the handlebody state spaces are the radical quotients of their skein modules, gluing is given by the inverse normalized handlebody pairing, and the resulting closed value is unchanged under isotopy, framed handle slides, and split $\pm1$-blow-ups. Forgetting the weight and Lagrangian extension yields only the projective ordinary-oriented data unless a separate anomaly-cancellation result is proved.

## Statement references

[[def-extended-skein-cobordism-anomaly-data|Weighted Lagrangian extension and anomaly data]]

[Kauffman and Lins, *Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds*, Chapters 7 and 12](https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1bgzb7v)

[Pohorence, *3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs*, §§1.2 and 3](https://categorified.net/RTinvariants/Jan29-Feb3.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the fixed BHMV root and pivotal convention, weighted Lagrangian bordism data, the root state spaces and their surgery maps.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] supplies the full choice assumption used by the surgery-presentation and Kirby-move supplier.

[F1] [[thm-kirby-moves-classify-framed-link-presentations]]: framed surgery diagrams for the same closed oriented manifold are connected by the stated isotopies, framed handle slides, and split signed-unit-unknot moves.

[F2] [[lem-root-skein-surgery-kirby-color-invariance]] supplies the closed surgery invariance, nonzero Gauss sums and precise external BHMV weighted normalization, including weight unit $\kappa^3$.

[F3] [[lem-root-handlebody-pairing-nondegeneracy-and-gluing]] supplies the perfect radical-quotient pairing, finite inverse sewing tensor and externally specified weighted gluing.

[F4] [[def-weighted-lagrangian-ribbon-bordism]] supplies associative weighted Lagrangian composition with the Wall-signature Maslov correction.

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the Statement.

1.1 For a fixed surgery presentation, the color set is finite and the state-space pairing is defined by a finite bracket evaluation. This constructs a candidate linear map for each presented weighted bordism. [A1, F2, F3, F4, given, construct]

2.1 Any two presented closed surgery links are related by [F1], and [F2] preserves their values under every move. For bordisms, use the BHMV additional $\eta^{b_0+b_1}$ normalization specified in the state-space Definition, not the raw closed invariant alone. The finite state spaces, perfect pairing and actual surgery/sewing maps are [F3], whose external BHMV/Gilmer–Masbaum input supplies the TQFT construction at the exact even root and complex specialization. The inverse-pairing contraction composes these maps, with the integer Wall/Maslov weight law [F4]. This proves finite-dimensionality, gluing and presentation invariance of the stated weighted theory. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

2.2 Forgetting the weight removes the scalar that corrects the Maslov/signature defect. Therefore the imported construction descends only projectively to ordinary oriented data without a further anomaly-cancellation input. No such additional theorem is asserted here. Full AC remains the declared branch of the presentation/marked category interfaces; finite color sums add no stronger assumption. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎

## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

## Definition references

[[thm-lee-homology-of-a-knot-has-two-generators|Two-dimensional Lee homology and the two orientation classes]]

[[thm-lee-filtered-homology-is-an-oriented-link-invariant|Diagram-independent induced filtration]]

[Rasmussen, *Khovanov homology and the slice genus* (2004), §3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0402131v1)

[McMullen, *4-Manifolds*, §5.6](https://web.stanford.edu/~cm5/4Mnotes.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the filtered Lee homology of an oriented knot.

[F1] Lee homology of a knot is two-dimensional, and the two canonical orientation classes form a basis ([[thm-lee-homology-of-a-knot-has-two-generators]]).

[F2] The induced filtration on Lee homology is independent of the diagram ([[thm-lee-filtered-homology-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

[F3] The two knot filtration levels differ by exactly two, by the marked-circle involution on the two quantum congruence lines ([[lem-lee-filtered-spectral-sequence-and-two-orientation-classes]]).

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom branch used by the finite diagram-move proof of [F2] ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses of the Definition.

1.1 The filtration on the finite Lee complex is finite, so its induced filtration on the two-dimensional homology is finite. By [F1] the vector space is nonzero, and therefore every nonzero class has a finite integer level $\ell(x)$. The set of levels is a nonempty subset of the finite set of filtration indices; hence its minimum and maximum exist. This uses no choice principle. [F1, algebra]

2.1 The two extremal filtration levels are the two surviving quantum degrees on the limiting page of the bounded spectral sequence. By [F3], their difference is exactly $2$, so $s_{\max}-1=s_{\min}+1$. The diagram-independence conclusion from [F2] uses the stated axiom branch [A1]. Thus the displayed formula defines an invariant of the oriented knot under AC$_\omega$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Example

Assume full AC. In the standard solid torus $V=S^1\times D^2$, let $P_{2,1}$ be the oriented curve $s\mapsto(e^{4\pi i s},r e^{2\pi i s})$ on an interior parallel torus, where $0<r<1$. Let $K=T(2,3)$ be the right trefoil and use the companion embedding that matches the product meridian and longitude of $V$ to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. Then the companion torus in the exterior of $P_{2,1}(K)$ is essential and satisfies the nonamalgamation hypotheses of the companion-detection corollary; its outside piece is exactly the trefoil exterior.

The first panel shows a lift of the pattern to the universal cover of the parallel torus: horizontal and vertical unit translations correspond to longitude and meridian, so the segment from $(0,0)$ to $(2,1)$ projects to the closed slope $2\lambda_V+\mu_V$. The second panel shows the exterior cut along the companion torus; its boxes are pieces, and the labels are the two regular-fiber slopes induced on their common torus. Both panels are schematic, not planar knot projections, and no proof step depends on them.

## Example references

[Ryan Budney, *JSJ-decompositions of knot and link complements in the 3-sphere*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0506523)

[Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, *Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes*](https://poisson.phc.dm.unipi.it/~camponovo/libri/knot.pdf)

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the standard solid torus $V$, the pattern $P_{2,1}$, the right trefoil $K=T(2,3)$, and the specified companion embedding.

[F1] The pattern and satellite exteriors, winding number, and companion torus have the conventions of [[def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-winding-number]].

[F2] The torus-knot supplier gives $\pi_1(E_{T(p,q)})=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, identifies $h=x^p=y^q$ as the regular fiber, and gives $\lambda=h\mu^{-pq}$ ([[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]], Statement).

[F3] Seifert–van Kampen computes the group of a union from the open collar covers used below ([[thm-seifert-van-kampen]], Statement).

[F4] The normal form theorem gives reduced-word uniqueness in the free products $\mathbb Z*C_2$ and $C_2*C_3$ ([[thm-normal-form-for-free-products-with-amalgamation]], Statement, with trivial amalgam).

[F5] The closed compact connected surface classification identifies their polygonal models, orientability and Euler characteristic ([[thm-classification-of-compact-connected-surfaces]], Statement).

[F6] A two-sided essential torus in an irreducible Seifert-fibered manifold is isotopic to a vertical or horizontal torus; horizontal tori cut the manifold into interval bundles ([[lem-essential-surface-in-seifert-piece-is-vertical-or-horizontal]], Statement).

[F7] Under the stated pattern and nontrivial-companion hypotheses, the companion torus is incompressible and non-boundary-parallel ([[lem-satellite-torus-is-essential]], Statement).

[F8] An irreducible satellite exterior with this torus, Seifert or atoroidal sides, and no global Seifert or atoroidal structure has that torus in its unique minimal JSJ system ([[cor-satellite-companion-is-detected-by-jsj]], Statement, using the full smooth uniqueness proof in [[thm-jsj-decomposition-of-knot-exteriors]]).

[F9] If a Seifert piece has an injective boundary torus and its quotient by the cyclic regular-fiber subgroup is a nonexceptional finite free product, every Seifert fibration has the same regular-fiber slope on that torus ([[lem-seifert-boundary-fibers-are-rigid-under-nonexceptional-free-product-quotients]], Statement).

[A1] Full AC is the axiom that every set-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], Definition).

[F10] Compact smooth surfaces with boundary have finite compatible triangulations ([[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]], Statement, dimension two).

[F11] A free product of two infinite cyclic groups has no nontrivial cyclic normal subgroup, hence has trivial center ([[lem-nonexceptional-finite-free-products-have-no-normal-cyclic-subgroup]], Statement).

## Proof

1.1 The circle action $t\cdot(z,w)=(e^{4\pi i t}z,e^{2\pi i t}w)$ on $S^1\times D^2$ has generic orbit slope $2\lambda_V+\mu_V$. The given pattern is one such orbit. The core $S^1\times\{0\}$ has stabilizer of order $2$, while generic points have trivial stabilizer. Removing a tube about the regular orbit $P_{2,1}$ therefore gives a Seifert fibration of $X_{P_{2,1}}$ over an annulus with one exceptional point of multiplicity $2$. On the outer torus its regular-fiber slope is $2\lambda_V+\mu_V$. [A1, F1, given, construct]

1.2 Remove a small neighborhood of the exceptional point from the annulus base. The remaining pair of pants has fundamental group freely generated by a loop $a$ around the outer boundary and a loop $c$ around the removed cone point; its third boundary loop is $(ac)^{-1}$. The circle bundle over this pair of pants has a section: it retracts to a graph, and a section over that graph is obtained by choosing one point in the fiber at the vertex and extending over each edge. Thus its group has generators $a,c,h$, with $h$ the fiber and $[a,h]=[c,h]=1$. The order-two local model $(z,w)\mapsto(-z,-w)$ around the exceptional core identifies the filled meridian with $c^2h$ after replacing $c$ by $ch^k$ if necessary: one circuit of the cone-point boundary lifts from $(z,w)$ to $(-z,-w)$, so two circuits equal one inverse fiber turn, and the twisting coefficient is odd. Filling that neighborhood kills this meridian. By [F3],
$$
\pi_1(X_{P_{2,1}})=\langle a,c,h\mid [a,h]=[c,h]=1,\ c^2h=1\rangle.
$$
Its quotient by $\langle h\rangle$ is $\mathbb Z*C_2$, which is nonabelian by reduced normal forms [F4]; hence $X_{P_{2,1}}$ is not $T^2\times I$. Its outer boundary subgroup is generated by $a,h$. The abelianization is free on $[a],[c]$ with $[h]=-2[c]$, so $a^m h^n=1$ implies $m=0$ and $n=0$. Thus the outer torus group injects into $\pi_1(X_{P_{2,1}})$ and has no compressing disk. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

1.3 For the trefoil, [F2] gives $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^2=y^3\rangle$ and regular fiber $h_K=x^2=y^3$. Its quotient by $\langle h_K\rangle$ is $C_2*C_3$, nonabelian by [F4], and $h_K$ is infinite because its abelianization is $6$ times the generator of $H_1(E_K)\cong\mathbb Z$. The group maps onto $S_3$ by $x\mapsto(12)$ and $y\mapsto(123)$, so it is nonabelian and $K$ is not the unknot, whose exterior group is $\mathbb Z$. [F2, F4, A1, algebra]

2.1 The peripheral formula in [F2] gives $h_K=\lambda_K+6\mu_K$. The companion embedding identifies $(\mu_V,\lambda_V)$ with $(\mu_K,\lambda_K)$. Therefore the two Seifert fibrations on the cut sides induce slopes $2\lambda+\mu$ and $\lambda+6\mu$ on the companion torus. Their determinant in the ordered basis $(\mu,\lambda)$ is $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&6\\2&1\end{pmatrix}=-11$, so the slopes are not parallel. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 By [F7], the companion torus $T_c$ is essential. Hence the whole exterior $M=E_{P_{2,1}(K)}$ is not atoroidal. Both pieces cut along $T_c$ are Seifert-fibered by steps 1.1 and 1.3. [F1, F2, F7, step 1.1, step 1.3]

2.3 The horizontal case is impossible. The interval-bundle bases inherit smooth transverse charts from the horizontal surface and the fiber charts. For any such compact connected surface with nonempty boundary, [F10] gives a finite triangulation. Root a spanning tree of its triangle-adjacency graph at a boundary edge. Delete each triangle across its exposed parent edge, starting at the root; this collapses the surface to a finite connected graph. Its group is therefore free, with rank equal to the rank of its abelianization, by collapsing a graph spanning tree. For a closed surface, the polygon models of [F5] give abelianization $\mathbb Z^{2g}$ in the orientable genus $g$ case and $\mathbb Z^{k-1}\oplus\mathbb Z/2$ in the nonorientable genus $k$ case, by adding the signed edge occurrences in its single face word. Hence a compact surface group with torsion-free rank-two abelianization is either the torus group $\mathbb Z^2$ or the free group of rank two; with torsion-free rank-one abelianization it is infinite cyclic. The cable group has abelianization $\mathbb Z^2$, is nonabelian because its quotient is $\mathbb Z*C_2$, and has the nonidentity central element $h$ since $[h]=-2[c]$ in its abelianization. It is neither $\mathbb Z^2$ nor the free group of rank two, whose center is trivial by [F11]. The trefoil group has abelianization $\mathbb Z$ and is nonabelian by step 1.3, so it too is not a surface group with that abelianization. Thus neither cut piece can be an interval bundle over a surface. [F2, F4, F5, F10, F11, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra, contradiction]

3.1 Suppose $M$ had a Seifert fibration. It is irreducible by [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]], so [F6] makes $T_c$ ambient isotopic to a vertical or horizontal torus. Isotopy preserves the homeomorphism types of the cut pieces. In the horizontal case, cutting along $T_c$ gives interval bundles over compact connected surfaces, so each side group is a surface group. [F2, F6, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Suppose instead that $T_c$ is vertical after isotopy. Pull the hypothetical fibration back by that ambient isotopy, so the original $T_c$ is vertical and the original cut-piece markings are retained. Restriction gives a Seifert fibration on each cut piece with one common regular-fiber slope on $T_c$. Their boundary groups inject independently of any general knot-boundary incompressibility theorem. For the cable side this was proved in step 1.2. For the trefoil side, the peripheral formula of [F2], with $2(-1)+3(1)=1$, gives $\mu=y^{-1}x$ and $\lambda=h_K\mu^{-6}$. Thus $(\mu,h_K)$ is also a basis for its boundary-torus group. In the quotient $C_2*C_3$ the word $y^{-1}x$ is cyclically reduced of length two, so all its nonzero powers are nonidentity by [F4]. If $\mu^a h_K^b=1$, quotienting forces $a=0$, and the infinite order of $h_K$ from step 1.3 forces $b=0$. This proves injectivity of that boundary group. The two original fiber quotients are $\mathbb Z*C_2$ and $C_2*C_3$, respectively, by steps 1.2 and 1.3; neither is the two-order-two exception. Apply [F9] separately to the restricted hypothetical fibration on each side. Its common boundary-fiber slope must equal both original slopes, contradicting their determinant $-11$ in step 2.1. This rules out the vertical case; together with step 2.3 it proves that $M$ is not Seifert-fibered. [F2, F4, F9, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.3, algebra, contradiction]

5.1 Steps 2.2 and 4.1 verify the nonamalgamation hypotheses of [F8], so the companion torus is a JSJ torus and the component outside the companion solid torus is $E_K$. The smooth ambient uniqueness in [F8] carries the original marked outside component to the outside component for any isotopic minimal JSJ torus. [F1, F8, step 2.2, step 4.1] ∎

title: Compact-support local Mayer–Vietoris and its cap ladder without choice
status: draft
