## Statement

Fix a finite regular diagram $D$ of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, choose a basepoint $p\in D$ away from the crossings, and choose an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to the branched-cover surgeries, with the compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles of the link-surgery construction. Identify each first-page vertex group with the reduced state space of the corresponding crossingless resolution, based at the circle containing $p$. For every cube edge, the induced first differential is the mod-two map assigned by the saddle: multiplication when two resolution circles merge and comultiplication when one resolution circle splits, with the marked-circle quotient at $p$. Under these identifications the direct sum of edge maps is the reduced Khovanov differential of the mirror diagram $\overline D$, based at the corresponding point, in the Ozsváth–Szabó smoothing convention.

## Statement references

[[lem-os-link-surgery-filtered-complex-and-triangle|Surgery cube and first differential]]

[[lem-os-unlink-resolution-covers-and-floer-tqft|Unlink Floer groups and saddle maps]]

[[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-based-link-over-f2|Based reduced Khovanov cube]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, §6, Propositions 6.1–6.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0309170v1)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §5.3](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed finite regular diagram of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, a basepoint on the diagram away from the crossings, its surgery cube, and the mod-two Heegaard Floer groups and edge maps for every crossingless resolution.

[F1] The surgery complex has the vertex groups and edge filtration described in [[lem-os-link-surgery-filtered-complex-and-triangle]].

[F2] The unlink vertex groups and all marked/unmarked saddle maps are identified, in simultaneous state bases, as the reduced Frobenius TQFT ([[lem-os-unlink-resolution-covers-and-floer-tqft]]).

[F3] The reduced Khovanov complex uses precisely the marked-circle quotient and merge/split maps in [[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-based-link-over-f2]].

[F4] **External input — local surgery/mirror smoothing identification.** Ozsváth–Szabó, arXiv:math/0309170v1, Section2 Proposition2.1 and following paragraph, pp.6–7, together with Figure1 p.2 and Theorem6.3 pp.34–35, identifies the three branched fillings with crossing/0/1 resolutions and the immediate surgery edge with the saddle. In its displayed chart the over-strand is northwest–southeast, the 0-resolution joins the left pair and the right pair, and the 1-resolution joins the top pair and bottom pair. After switching over/under to form the mirror, this is exactly A then B in the library source chart. Thus the surgery bits agree with the mirror Khovanov 0/1 bits. Only the fixed-diagram mod-two assertion is imported.

## Proof

1.1 On the associated graded cube the diagonal differential is the ordinary vertex differential. Therefore its homology is the direct sum of the resolution Floer groups. The next differential is induced by the components changing one coordinate: higher polygon components lower the increasing filtration by at least two and cannot contribute to this first differential. Each surviving component is the actual surgery triangle map of that edge. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Use the SAME vertex state identification simultaneously for all incident edges. By the exact Floer supplier [F2], an unmarked merge has table $1\otimes1\mapsto1$, $1\otimes X,X\otimes1\mapsto X$, $X\otimes X\mapsto0$; an unmarked split has $1\mapsto1\otimes X+X\otimes1$ and $X\mapsto X\otimes X$. Marked merge kills the input with the other circle labelled $X$ and sends its $1$ input to $1_{\rm marked}$. Marked split sends $1_{\rm marked}$ to $1_{\rm marked}\otimes X_{\rm new}$, with the tensor order determined by which child contains the point. These last two formulas are obtained by quotienting the marked factor, not by keeping an extra unreduced factor. Tensor the identity on every untouched circle. These are exactly the reduced Frobenius saddle maps of [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 For an explicit grading binding, let $n_+(D),n_-(D)$ be the signed crossing counts. By [F4] the surgery bit vector $I$ is the $0/1$ vector of $\overline D$, so the normalized cochain degrees are
$$i=|I|-n_+(D),\qquad \widetilde j=\sum_{c\ne p}\deg_q(a_c)+|I|+n_-(D)-2n_+(D),$$
where $a_c\in\{1,X\}$, with degrees $1,-1$, and the marked surviving label has reduced degree zero. Every saddle table in step 1.2 lowers the sum of label degrees by one, including marked merge and split. Increasing $|I|$ by one therefore raises $i$ by one and preserves $\widetilde j$. The spectral-sequence filtration index $p=n-|I|$ satisfies $i=n_-(D)-p$; it is not an independent Floer cochain grading. [F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 The finite direct sum of the simultaneously compatible vertex identifications in [F2] is consequently an isomorphism with the normalized reduced Khovanov cube of the mirror. The actual surgery-to-mirror chart correspondence is [F4]; the grading shifts follow independently from the library cochain definition in step1.3, rather than from an unconverted homological index in the source. No arbitrary separate edgewise changes of basis are used. This proves the direct-sum first-differential assertion for the fixed diagram, without a diagram-independence claim. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact connected smooth oriented $4$-manifold with rational homology of a point and connected boundary $Y$. Then $Y$ is a rational homology sphere, and $P=\ker(H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W;\mathbb Z))$ is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form $\lambda_Y$.

## Statement references

[[def-finite-linking-form-and-metabolizer|Finite linking forms and metabolizers]]

[[def-bounding-chain-torsion-linking-pairing|The signed bounding-chain formula]]

[[lem-linking-pairing-on-rational-homology-sphere-is-nonsingular|Nonsingularity of the rational-sphere linking form]]

[[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]]

[[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a compact connected oriented rational homology $4$-ball $W$, and its connected boundary $Y$.

[A1] Full AC is assumed wherever the cover and orientation conventions use the choice axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies $H_i(W,Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $H^{4-i}(W;\mathbb Z)$ and carries the relative fundamental class to the boundary fundamental class. [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]

[F2] The integral homology-pair sequence is exact. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]]

[F3] The cohomology universal coefficient sequence over $\mathbb Z$ is $0\to\operatorname{Ext}(H_{j-1}(W),\mathbb Z)\to H^j(W;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_j(W),\mathbb Z)\to0$. [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]

[F4] The finite-CW supplier assumes countable choice as defined by [def-countable-choice]; under [A1], full AC implies it by applying the choice function to the indexed family. [[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]] [[def-countable-choice]] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]


[F5] The linking form on a closed oriented rational homology sphere is perfect and its bounding-chain expression is the Bockstein–duality evaluation. [[lem-linking-pairing-on-rational-homology-sphere-is-nonsingular]] [[def-bounding-chain-torsion-linking-pairing]]

[F6] In a finite nonsingular linking form, a subgroup $P$ is a metabolizer when $P=P^\perp$. [[def-finite-linking-form-and-metabolizer]]

[F7] Poincaré duality on $Y$ identifies $H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $H^1(Y;\mathbb Z)$; Poincaré–Lefschetz duality and the cap-product boundary identity identify the homology boundary map $H_2(W,Y)\to H_1(Y)$ with cohomology restriction $H^2(W)\to H^2(Y)$ under these dualities. [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]] [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]] [[thm-cap-product-boundary-identity]]

[F8] The coefficient sequence $0\to\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\to0$ gives the natural long exact cohomology sequence and its Bockstein map. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-in-cohomology]]

## Proof

1.1 The rational homology-pair sequence and [F1], with $H_i(W;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $i>0$, give $H_1(Y;\mathbb Q)=H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$; connectedness gives $H_0(Y;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, and orientation gives $H_3(Y;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$. Thus $Y$ is a rational homology sphere. By [F4] and [A1], both $W$ and its smooth boundary $Y$ have finite CW type, so their integral homology groups are finitely generated. The groups $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, $H_1(W;\mathbb Z)$ and $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ have vanishing rationalizations and are therefore finite. [F1, F4, given, construct, A1]

2.1 Put $A=H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, $B=H_1(W;\mathbb Z)$, and $C=H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Since $A$ is finite by step 1.1, the universal coefficient sequence [F3] gives $H^1(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$; [F7] then gives $H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$. Also $H_3(W;\mathbb Z)=0$: [F1] identifies $H_4(W,Y)$ with $H^0(W)=\mathbb Z$, and its fundamental-class boundary maps to the generator of $H_3(Y)=\mathbb Z$; since $H_3(W,Y)\cong H^1(W)=0$, exactness forces $H_3(W)=0$. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F3], $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Ext}(B,\mathbb Z)$ and $H^3(W;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Ext}(C,\mathbb Z)$, because $B,C$ are finite and $H_3(W)=0$. Their orders are $|B|$ and $|C|$. Under [F1], these are the orders of $H_2(W,Y)$ and $H_1(W,Y)$, respectively. The pair sequence [F2] shows that $P=\ker(A\to B)$ is the cokernel of the injective map $H_2(W)\to H_2(W,Y)$, while $B\to H_1(W,Y)$ is onto because the next map $H_0(Y)\to H_0(W)$ is an isomorphism. Hence $|P|=|B|/|C|$ and $|A/P|=|B|/|C|$, so $|A|=|P|^2$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra, A1]

3.2 To prove isotropy, [F2] and the naturality in [F7] identify $P$ under Poincaré duality with the image of $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. For $x,y\in P$, choose lifts $\widetilde x,\widetilde y\in H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Since $W$ is a rational homology ball, the coefficient Bockstein $H^1(W;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$ is onto by [F8]: the adjacent groups $H^1(W;\mathbb Q)$ and $H^2(W;\mathbb Q)$ vanish. Choose $\gamma\in H^1(W;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ with Bockstein $\widetilde y$. By [F5], $\lambda_Y(x,y)$ is the evaluation on $[Y]$ of the restriction of $\gamma\smile\widetilde x$. This class extends over $W$, and the inclusion sends $[Y]$ to zero in $H_3(W)$ because $Y=\partial W$. Thus $\lambda_Y(x,y)=0$. [F1, F2, F5, F7, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra, A1]

4.1 The isotropy from step 3.2 gives $P\subseteq P^\perp$. Nonsingularity [F5] implies $|P^\perp|=|A|/|P|=|P|$ by step 3.1. Therefore $P=P^\perp$, so $P$ is a metabolizer by [F6]. [F5, F6, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra] ∎

## Unresolved proof obligations

The finite-CW step is supplied by [F4], and the boundary naturality and Bockstein steps are supplied by [F7] and [F8].

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary $K$. Let $W_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$. Then $W_D$ is a rational homology four-ball and its oriented boundary is the double branched cover $\Sigma_2(K)$ formed using the positive-meridian convention. This assertion concerns smooth disks only and makes no claim for locally flat topological disks.

## Statement references

[[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot|The positive-meridian convention for the cyclic branched cover]]

[[lem-double-cover-branched-over-a-slice-disk-is-a-rational-homology-ball|The smooth slice-disk cover homology result]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$ with $\partial D=K$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the published smooth-disk cover theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The cyclic branched cover uses the homomorphism sending a positive meridian to the generator of $\mathbb Z/2$; its boundary is the branched cover of the boundary knot with the induced orientation ([[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]).

[F2] The connected double cover of $B^4$ branched over a smooth properly embedded disk is a rational homology ball under AC ([[lem-double-cover-branched-over-a-slice-disk-is-a-rational-homology-ball]]).

## Proof
**Proof technique:** apply the smooth-disk cover result and identify the boundary cover.

**Given:** The data above.

1.1 By [F2], the connected branched double cover $W_D$ has the rational homology of a point; smoothness and properness of the disk are exactly the hypotheses of that supplier. [A1, F2, given]

2.1 The restriction of the covering map to $\partial B^4=S^3$ is the connected double cover branched along $\partial D=K$. Its monodromy sends a positive meridian of $K$ to the nontrivial element of $\mathbb Z/2$, because a meridian disk normal to $D$ has local branched model $z\mapsto z^2$. Therefore its oriented boundary is precisely $\Sigma_2(K)$ under [F1]. The supplier was used only for smooth disks, so no topological-disk conclusion follows. [F1, given, construct] ∎

## Statement

Let $C$ and $D$ be finite integer-filtered chain complexes over $\mathbb F_2$, each with total homology isomorphic to $\mathbb F_2$. A filtered chain homotopy equivalence consists of filtration-preserving chain maps $f:C\to D$ and $g:D\to C$ such that $gf$ and $fg$ are chain homotopic to the respective identity maps by homotopies that preserve every filtration level. Then $\tau(C)=\tau(D)$.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The first filtration level whose inclusion has nonzero image in total homology]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Knot Floer homology and the four-ball genus*, §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0301149v4)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $C,D$ and filtered chain maps $f,g$ satisfying the filtered chain homotopy equivalence hypotheses in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]]: for a finite filtered complex with one-dimensional total homology, $\tau(C)$ is the least integer $s$ for which $H(F_sC)\to H(C)$ has nonzero image.

## Proof

1.1 Put $t=\tau(C)$. By [F1], some class in $H(F_tC)$ maps to a nonzero class in $H(C)$. Since $f$ preserves filtration, its restriction sends $F_tC$ to $F_tD$. The square formed by these restricted maps and the inclusions into total complexes commutes, so the induced map sends that class to its image under $f_*$. The map $f_*$ is an isomorphism because $g_*$ is its homotopy inverse; hence the resulting class in $H(D)$ is nonzero. Therefore $H(F_tD)\to H(D)$ has nonzero image and $\tau(D)\le t$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 The same argument using the filtration-preserving map $g$ gives $\tau(C)\le\tau(D)$. Together with step 1.1 this yields $\tau(C)=\tau(D)$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let G be a countable discrete amenable group. For every right CG-module M and every integer q>0, the N G-von Neumann dimension of Tor_q^{CG}(M,N G) is zero. This dimension-flatness statement does not say that the Tor module itself is zero.

## Statement references

[Cha–Orr, Theorem 6.6 and proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.3700)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a countable discrete amenable group $G$, a right $\mathbb CG$-module $M$, and $q>0$.

[F1] The group von Neumann algebra, its canonical trace and the extended projective-submodule dimension have the stated meanings. The defining page fixes full AC as its foundational convention. [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

[F2] In a finite von Neumann projection module, Hilbert-dense submodules have dimension-zero quotient; zero-dimensional modules are closed under submodules, quotients, extensions and filtered colimits. [[lem-finite-von-neumann-module-dimension-and-dense-quotients]]

[F3] For a finite matrix over $\mathbb CG$, its algebraic kernel is Hilbert-dense in its full Hilbert kernel, and the quotient of its $\mathcal N G$-kernel by the right $\mathcal N G$-span of that algebraic kernel has dimension zero. [[lem-amenable-folner-kernel-approximation]]

[F4] Tensor products consist of finite sums of elementary tensors and preserve cokernels over arbitrary rings. Apply the stated left-module version to the opposite ring and flip elementary tensors to obtain the right-module version used here. [[lem-tensoring-with-a-right-module-is-additive-right-exact-and-preserves-direct-sums]]

[F5] Tor is homology after tensoring a projective resolution of the right module. Canonical free covers iterated on kernels give a free resolution; apply the left-module construction to the opposite ring for right modules. Under the standing AC convention it is projective. Any two projective resolutions are homotopy equivalent over the resolved module, under DC, which follows from this standing AC convention. [[def-tor-by-resolving-the-right-module]], [[prop-the-iterated-free-module-resolution-is-canonical-in-zf]], [[thm-projective-resolutions-of-the-same-object-are-homotopy-equivalent-over-that-object]]

[A1] Full AC supplies the projective-resolution comparison in [F5] and the Hilbert-space and von Neumann dimension arguments in [F1]–[F3]. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data and standing foundational convention above. Put $R=\mathbb CG$ and $A=\mathcal N G$.

1.1 First let $K\subseteq R^n$ be generated by finitely many columns, and let $B:R^s\to R^n$ be the corresponding matrix map onto $K$. Right exactness of tensor products identifies $K\otimes_R A$ with $A^s/\operatorname{im}((\ker_R B)\otimes_R A)$. The kernel of its natural map to $A^n$ is therefore $\ker_A B/\operatorname{im}((\ker_R B)\otimes_R A)$. This quotient has dimension zero by [F3]. The tensor-product identifications follow directly from the presentation $\ker_R B\to R^s\to K\to0$: relations among the chosen generators are exactly the elements of $\ker_R B$. [F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 For an arbitrary submodule $K\subseteq R^n$, take its directed union of finitely generated submodules $K_j$. A tensor is a finite sum, so every element of $K\otimes_R A$ comes from some $K_j\otimes_R A$. If its image in $A^n$ is zero, its representative already lies in the kernel of the natural map $K_j\otimes_R A\to A^n$. Thus the kernel for $K$ is the directed union of images of the zero-dimensional kernels from step 1.1; it has dimension zero by [F2]. This also proves the assertion if relations identify different representatives, since images are quotients of those kernels. [F2, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Let $F=\bigoplus_{i\in I}R$ be any free module and $K\subseteq F$. Every finite tensor in $K\otimes_R A$ involves finitely many vectors of $K$, each of finite coordinate support in $F$. Their supports lie in one finite free summand $R^n\subseteq F$. A kernel element is therefore the image of a kernel for a submodule of that finite free summand, handled by step 2.1. Taking the directed union over those submodules and finite supports, and applying [F2], proves that $\ker(K\otimes_R A\to F\otimes_R A)$ has dimension zero for every free $F$. [F2, F4, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Choose a free presentation $0\to K\to F\to M\to0$. In the resolution-dependent definition of Tor, first use a free resolution beginning with this presentation. For any other chosen projective resolution, [F5] gives chain maps inverse up to chain homotopy; this use of projective-resolution comparison relies on [A1]. Additive tensoring preserves the homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$, since tensoring respects sums and composition. Thus the tensor complexes are homotopy equivalent and their homology modules are isomorphic; the calculation below therefore applies to every retained resolution datum. A free resolution beginning with this presentation computes $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)$ as $\ker(K\otimes_R A\to F\otimes_R A)$: resolving $K$ and splicing onto $F\to M$ gives this equality by right exactness at the last differential. Thus step 3.1 proves the assertion for degree one. For $q>1$, successively apply the same construction to the kernels in a free resolution of $M$; the positive-degree homology after splicing shifts by one, giving $\operatorname{Tor}_q^R(M,A)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(K_{q-1},A)$ for the appropriate syzygy $K_{q-1}$. The degree-one argument applies to every such module, so every asserted higher Tor group has dimension zero. No claim that these algebraic quotient modules are zero is used or obtained. [A1, F1, F2, F4, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let P⊂S¹×D² be a winding-zero pattern. Assume the axis has nonzero classical Blanchfield self-pairing in the Alexander module of P(U), with the convention that the axis defines the class paired with itself. For either the locally flat topological concordance group C_top or the smooth concordance group C_sm, let Pⁿ be the n-fold composition of the induced satellite set map, with P⁰ the identity. For every n≥0, the quotient ⟨Pⁿ(C)⟩/⟨Pⁿ⁺¹(C)⟩ has infinite rank, where ⟨S⟩ denotes the subgroup generated by S and rank means dim_Q(A⊗_Z Q) for an abelian group A. For n≥1, Pⁿ is not a group homomorphism under the same hypotheses. No pairwise-coprime Alexander-polynomial assumption is part of these Theorems A and B.

## Statement references

[[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories|Smooth and topological concordance conventions]]

[[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator|Satellite operator iterates]]

[[def-blanchfield-pairing-and-higher-order-rho-invariant|Classical Blanchfield self-pairing convention]]

[Cha–Kim, Theorems A and B and complete proofs](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04629v2)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the winding-zero pattern and its nonzero classical axis self-value, the smooth and locally flat concordance conventions, and $n\ge0$.

[A1] Full AC is the chosen integral half-solution and analytic convention; it implies the countable-choice hypotheses of the smooth concordance constructions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

[F1] The actual exterior-to-zero-surgery comparison preserves the integral classical Alexander module and its Blanchfield self-values. [[thm-zero-surgery-identifies-exterior-classical-alexander-and-blanchfield-data]]

[F2] In the smooth category, actual integral solution sets are nested subgroups, satellite maps preserve concordance, and every next-iterate image lies in the corresponding integral filtration subgroup plus the cyclic class of the iterate of the unknot. The full proof supplies integral0-solutions, an actual annulus tube with zero boundary framings, homology cobordisms and deep-axis infection solutions. [[thm-smooth-integral-filtration-is-compatible-with-deep-axis-infection]]

[F3] The full finite-prime smooth obstruction theorem excludes every nonzero signed sum of each chosen finite family of $P^n$ iterates from integral $(n+1/2)$-solvability for $n\ge1$, and supplies a separate actual smooth nonslice nonhomomorphism witness. The finite-cyclic half-solution theorem supplies the actual $n=0$ obstruction. [[thm-finite-prime-smooth-infection-obstructions-use-actual-coefficients]], [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]]

[F4] The complete smooth all-iterate theorem assembles [F2]–[F3], including finite-cyclic connected-sum additivity, the $n=0$ case, rational independence modulo integral filtrations, the at-most-one cyclic rank loss and the separate nonhomomorphism conclusion. [[thm-smooth-winding-zero-iterates-have-infinite-rank-in-every-quotient]]

[F5] For supplied initial TOP integral-pair data and the actual finite standard pieces, the Blanchfield-bordism and full-forest meridian calculations hold. Actual finite-projective TOP duality/gluing and the lifted-half-pair vanishing theorem also hold, without smoothing that initial manifold. [[lem-cha-kim-integral-solvability-and-blanchfield-bordism]], [[thm-topological-finite-projective-l2-duality-and-boundary-gluing]], [[thm-topological-lifted-half-pairs-force-amenable-signature-defect-zero]]

[F8] **External TOP geometric input under CLAUDE.md §12:** locally flat concordance classes form the oriented connected-sum group; a locally flat slice disk has a collared normal product whose exterior is an integral homology circle, with prescribed meridian and zero-longitude surgery boundary. The TOP integral solution sets $\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{top}}$, defined by the same finite lifted intersection-pair conditions but allowing collared TOP four-manifolds, are nested subgroups. For winding zero,
$$\langle P^k(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle\subset\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P^k(U)\rangle\quad(k\ge1).$$
These geometric TOP assertions are imported from [Cha–Kim, §1 topological convention, §3 following Theorem3.1 and Lemma3.2, Lemma4.3, and §5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04629v2). They are not presented as locally reconstructed normal-tube or integral-filtration constructions. Full AC is retained.

[F6] The finite-stage selection and signed domination argument applies to supplied TOP initial bounds: its actual coefficient maps are supplied by [F5], and its boundary defects agree with the independent smooth invariants by the explicit external closed TOP equality in the rho-independence lemma. [[lem-cha-kim-higher-order-rho-bound-and-coprime-separation]], [[lem-l2-rho-invariant-bordism-independence]], [[thm-cheeger-gromov-uniform-rho-bound]]

[F7] An actual TOP integral half-solution with its canonical meridian map to $C_p$ has zero finite-cyclic bounding defect. The exterior/surgery comparison and canonical finite-cyclic signature means use the admitted finite prime signature families. TOP-versus-smooth boundary comparison is supplied by [F6], not assumed in the finite-cyclic theorem. [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]], [[lem-finite-prime-families-have-explicit-separating-knot-signature-bumps]], [[thm-canonical-finite-cyclic-knot-defects-equal-seifert-signature-averages]]

## Proof

**Given:** The complete rich Statement, with full AC as above.

1.1 In the smooth category [F1] identifies the stipulated nonzero classical axis self-value with exactly the integral surgery self-value used in [F4]. The winding and orientation conventions are the same, and AC verifies its actual geometric and analytic hypotheses. Apply [F4] to obtain infinite rational rank of $\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle/\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle$ for every $n\ge0$, including its separate finite-cyclic proof at $n=0$. Its finite families are chosen for each desired rank bound, so no assertion of a single explicit infinite independent sequence is needed. This establishes the entire smooth rank branch of the original Statement. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 For $n\ge1$, [F4] also gives a knot $J$ for which $P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#(-P^n(J\#J))$ is not smoothly slice. A homomorphism on smooth concordance would make this class zero, contradicting the actual witness. Thus the entire smooth nonhomomorphism branch follows as well. Neither [F4]'s rank proof nor this witness uses a pairwise-coprime Alexander-polynomial condition, so the original A/B scope is retained. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Work in the TOP group of [F8]. Fix $n\ge1$ and any desired finite rank $m$. Choose the finite family in [F6] for size $m+1$. If a nonzero signed sum of its $P^n$ iterates belonged to $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$, its defining TOP solution would have exactly the integral height-$n$ pairs and isotropic height-$(n+1)$ lifts needed by [F5]. The finite forest quotient maps in [F5] have amenable target in the specified $D(k)$ class, with top meridian of infinite order. The accepted TOP half-pair theorem gives zero defect of that actual solution; the smooth standard joining/infection pieces have zero defect as well. Whole-component additivity makes the actual boundary defect sum zero. But [F6] evaluates its bottom terms by canonical cyclic numbers and gives strict signed domination over all pattern terms. This is a contradiction. Thus these $m+1$ classes are rationally independent modulo $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$: a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation. [A1, F1, F5, F6, F8, given, construct, algebra]

3.2 By [F8], $\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$ lies in $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P^{n+1}(U)\rangle$. Quotienting a rational vector space by the span of one element loses at most one dimension. Step3.1 therefore gives rank at least $m$ for the image of $\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$ modulo that larger subgroup, hence also for its quotient by $\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$. Since $m$ was arbitrary, the rank is infinite. This uses finite families of each requested size, not an unproved explicit infinite sequence. [F8, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 At $n=0$, take any finite family of the signature bumps in [F7], with distinct selected primes. For a nonzero signed sum choose an index with nonzero coefficient and evaluate the canonical cyclic defect at that prime. All cross-prime terms vanish, so the value is the selected nonzero integer coefficient times its positive normalized mean. It cannot vanish. A TOP integral1-solution would give an integral half-solution at height0 and force the same defect to vanish by [F7] and [F6]. These classes are therefore independent modulo $\mathcal F_1^{\mathrm{top}}$. Since $\langle P(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle\subset\mathcal F_1^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P(U)\rangle$, the same at-most-one rank loss proves infinite rank of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}/\langle P(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$. [F8, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

3.4 For $n\ge1$, choose the three-branch companion in [F6] with normalized positive cyclic defect exceeding $3nL$. If $P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#(-P^n(J\#J))$ were TOP slice, [F8] would give an actual collared TOP homology-circle disk exterior. This is the zero-pair case of [F5], and its three-branch quotient kills the distinguished negative bottom restriction while at least one positive bottom restriction has the required cyclic order. The actual half-pair zero defect and piecewise gluing force total defect zero, while [F6] gives a strictly positive bottom sum exceeding all $3n$ pattern terms. This contradiction proves the TOP nonhomomorphism witness. Steps1.1–2.1 already supplied the smooth conclusions. No coprime Alexander hypothesis was used. The full original Statement follows, with precisely the TOP geometric foundations and closed TOP equality declared external. [F8, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. For every group extension
$$1\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1,$$
the maps induced by inclusion, quotient, and transgression form an exact sequence
$$H_2(G;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_2(Q;\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow N/[G,N]\longrightarrow H_1(G;\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow H_1(Q;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow 0.$$
Here $[G,N]$ is the normal subgroup generated by the commutators
$gng^{-1}n^{-1}$ with $g\in G$ and $n\in N$.

## Statement references

[McCleary, Theorem 8bis.14](https://pages.vassar.edu/mccleary/files/2011/04/MC08bis.fin_.pdf)

[Stees, Chapter 2.5](https://scholarworks.iu.edu/iuswrrest/api/core/bitstreams/54c7d68f-d982-4e1f-9550-e54140ada5ea/content)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC and the group extension.

[A1] Full AC, written AC, is [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[L1] AC implies DC by choosing one successor at each stage of a serial relation. [[def-dependent-choice]]

[F1] The extension has a strongly convergent homological spectral sequence with $E^2_{p,q}=H_p(Q;H_q(N;\mathbb Z))$ and abutment $H_{p+q}(G;\mathbb Z)$. [[thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-for-group-extensions]]

[F2] Every first-quadrant homological spectral sequence with finite abutment filtration has the exact five-term sequence $H_2\to E^2_{2,0}\to E^2_{0,1}\to H_1\to E^2_{1,0}\to0$. [[thm-five-term-exact-sequence-of-a-first-quadrant-homological-spectral-sequence]]

[F3] The bar model computes group homology; in degree one, $H_1(N;\mathbb Z)$ is generated by symbols $[n]$ with relations $[n_1n_2]=[n_1]+[n_2]$. [[lem-diagonal-bar-coinvariants-compute-group-homology]]

## Proof

**Given:** The extension and [A1].

1.1 By [A1] and [L1], the DC condition of [F3] holds. Apply [F2] to the spectral sequence in [F1]. Since $H_0(N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ with trivial $Q$-action, its terms identify as $E^2_{2,0}=H_2(Q;\mathbb Z)$, $E^2_{0,1}=H_0(Q;H_1(N;\mathbb Z))$, $H_1=H_1(G;\mathbb Z)$, and $E^2_{1,0}=H_1(Q;\mathbb Z)$. This gives an exact sequence with $H_0(Q;H_1(N;\mathbb Z))$ in the middle. [A1, L1, F1, F2, F3]

1.2 By [F3], $H_1(N;\mathbb Z)=N/[N,N]$ under the map sending $n$ to its class. The $Q$-coinvariants impose the relations $[gng^{-1}]=[n]$ for every lift $g\in G$ and $n\in N$. Their subgroup in $N/[N,N]$ is exactly $[G,N]/[N,N]$, because $[N,N]\subseteq[G,N]$. Therefore $H_0(Q;H_1(N;\mathbb Z))\cong N/[G,N]$. [A1, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Substituting this natural identification in the exact sequence from step 1.1 gives the displayed five-term sequence. The identification commutes with the map induced by any homomorphism of group extensions, since it is defined by the meridian-class map $n\mapsto[n]$ and the conjugation action. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot cobordism in $S^3\times[0,1]$, the ordinary even integral Khovanov assignment has source and target the bigraded groups $Kh^{i,j}$ and is defined up to an overall sign; after quotienting morphisms by sign, it is invariant under ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary and respects composition. If the surface is equipped with a dividing set and one $w$- and one $z$-basepoint on each boundary knot, the decorated knot Floer assignment has source and target the filtered complexes $CFL^-_{UV}(S^3,K)$ over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$, and is invariant up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. For a general gluing of decorated four-dimensional cobordisms, the link Floer composition law sums over Spin-c structures on the composite that restrict to the chosen structures on the pieces; for the product $S^3\times[0,1]$ this sum has one term. The two assignments therefore have separately specified targets, coefficient rings, decorations, and equivalence relations.

## Statement references

[[thm-barnatan-khovanov-cobordism-functoriality-up-to-sign|Even integral Khovanov cobordism functoriality]]

[[def-decorated-link-cobordism-and-floer-target|The decorated Floer target and dividing-set data]]

[[def-knot-floer-cobordism-map|The Spin-c-indexed decorated Floer map]]

[[lem-knot-floer-cobordism-naturality-and-movie-invariance|Floer naturality and composition law]]

[Bar-Natan, *Khovanov's homology for tangles and cobordisms*, Theorems 4–5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0410495v2)

[Zemke, *Link cobordisms and functoriality in link Floer homology*, Theorems A and B](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3)

[Jacobsson, *An invariant of link cobordisms from Khovanov homology*, §4.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0206303)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The retained even integral Khovanov functor gives the indicated bigraded groups and cobordism maps up to one overall sign, with boundary-fixed isotopy invariance and composition after quotienting by sign. This locally resolved result is reused unchanged. ([[thm-barnatan-khovanov-cobordism-functoriality-up-to-sign]])

[F2] The decorated Floer map construction and naturality lemma give the two-color filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariant maps, with one Spin-c label and the extension-sum composition law. Their explicitly external inputs are Zemke's Theorems A and B, arXiv:1610.05207v3, pp.3 and 85–98, at the full divided-surface, parametrized-boundary and colored-chain-complex scope; their explicit finite/countable-choice specialization is retained, and no full-Choice theorem is silently substituted for the stated hypothesis. Neither the hat-only Juhasz construction nor the graph reduction is being asserted to construct this two-variable functor. ([[def-knot-floer-cobordism-map]], [[lem-knot-floer-cobordism-naturality-and-movie-invariance]], [source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

## Proof

1.1 Apply [F1] to the smooth oriented surface. Its target is ordinary even integral $Kh^{i,j}$, and identifying a map with its negative removes exactly the one sign ambiguity. Its isotopy and composition conclusions are the first assertion of the Statement. [F1, given]

1.2 For the separately decorated surface apply [F2], coloring all w-regions by $U$ and z-regions by $V$. The intermediate multiply based link modules and their endpoint naturality identifications are part of that construction. Zero curvature makes the endpoint objects the specified complexes, and external Theorem A gives filtered equivariant chain-homotopy invariance. This assertion has coefficient field $\mathbb F_2$ and its own decoration and Spin-c data; no integral Khovanov sign ambiguity or comparison between the two theories is transferred to it. [F2, given]

1.3 The general composition law is the extension sum in [F2]. On $S^3\times[0,1]$ the Spin-c set has one element, so composition has one term. Combining the two independently established assignments proves the entire Statement with its distinct targets, coefficients and equivalence relations. It asserts neither equality of the functors nor a canonical chain-level top generator, and requires no new local reconstruction of the imported Cerf checks. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC and the ACω Heegaard Floer analytic package. Let $D$ be any finite regular diagram of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, with a marked point away from crossings. There is a spectral sequence over $\mathbb F_2$ associated to the link-surgery filtered complex for this fixed diagram whose $E_2$ page is isomorphic, with the normalized grading shifts of the chosen smoothing convention, to $\widetilde{Kh}(\overline L,p;\mathbb F_2)$ computed from the mirror diagram, and whose abutment is $\widehat{HF}(\Sigma(L);\mathbb F_2)$ with its image filtration. This is a fixed-diagram construction; it does not assert a diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism type.

## Statement references

[[def-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link|Branched cover convention]]

[[def-link-surgery-filtered-complex-for-double-branched-cover|Filtered link-surgery module]]

[[lem-link-surgery-e-one-differential-is-reduced-khovanov|E1 differential identification]]

[[lem-os-filtered-convergence-and-invariance-scope|Finite filtration convergence]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, Theorem 6.3 and proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0309170v1)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §5.3](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a nonempty oriented link diagram $D$ with a basepoint, and the stated ACω Floer disk and polygon theory.

[F1] The diagram determines the surgery cube of branched covers and its filtration ([[def-link-surgery-filtered-complex-for-double-branched-cover]]).

[F2] The surgery cube is a filtered chain complex with total homology identified with the hat Floer homology of the branched cover ([[lem-os-link-surgery-filtered-complex-and-triangle]], [[thm-hat-heegaard-floer-is-a-closed-three-manifold-invariant]]).

[F3] The first page and its differential identify with the reduced Khovanov cube of the mirror diagram ([[lem-link-surgery-e-one-differential-is-reduced-khovanov]]).

[F4] A finite filtration yields a convergent spectral sequence to the associated graded of the filtered homology ([[lem-os-filtered-convergence-and-invariance-scope]]).

## Proof

1.1 The crossing resolutions of $D$ give the vertices of the cube, and the surgery maps give the differential components. By [F2] these components square to zero and preserve the increasing cube filtration, so the associated spectral sequence is defined. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 The filtration has only the $n+1$ levels $0,\ldots,n$, where $n$ is the number of crossings. By [F4] the spectral sequence stabilizes and abuts to the image filtration on the total homology, which [F2] identifies with $\widehat{HF}(\Sigma(L);\mathbb F_2)$. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

2.1 The associated graded vertex groups form the $E_1$ page, and their first differential is the sum of the single-crossing edge maps. By [F3], this complex is isomorphic to the reduced Khovanov complex of the mirror diagram; taking its cohomology gives the stated $E_2$ page. [F3, step 1.1]

2.2 The proof used one fixed $D$ and the finite filtration only. It supplies no filtered map between the constructions for two diagrams, so it establishes the stated fixed-diagram spectral sequence but no diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism. Here [F2] uses the explicitly external OS surgery construction and filling comparison, and [F3] uses its actual compatible unlink maps with the proved finite reduced-algebra binding. Those imports retain their stated scope; no missing geometric map is inferred from finite convergence. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$. The normal framing along $K$ given by the inward unit conormal to $K$ in $F$ has self-linking number zero. Here self-linking is the linking number of $K$ with a sufficiently small disjoint push-off along that framing. In the framing-class parameterization by relative winding from the surface framing, this class has integer zero.

## Statement references

[[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing|Framings, self-linking by a small push-off, and the Seifert framing]]

[[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor|Framing classes parameterized by relative winding]]

[[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection|Linking number as signed intersection with a spanning surface under the Axiom of Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice implies the Axiom of Countable Choice through dependent choice. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

[F1] A Seifert surface is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is the specified knot; its genus formula assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]])

[F2] For a knot with a supplied oriented spanning surface, the inward unit surface conormal is a reference normal framing, and relative winding identifies its framing class with zero. ([[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the inward unit conormal defines the Seifert framing; its self-linking is the linking number with a sufficiently small push-off along that section. ([[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]])

[F4] For any normalized tubular-neighbourhood chart and sufficiently small radius, the push-off is embedded and its linking number is independent of the radius, the representative nowhere-zero normal section, and the normalized chart; hence it depends only on the framing class. ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]])

[F5] For disjoint oriented circles $J,K$ and an oriented spanning surface $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma=K$, if $J$ is transverse to $\Sigma$ and $D$ is a regular oriented diagram of $J\cup K$, the diagram linking number equals the signed intersection number $J\cdot\Sigma$. The theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice. ([[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]])

[F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every oriented link in $\mathbb R^3$ has a dense set of directions giving a regular diagram with finitely many crossings. ([[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]])

[F7] A regular oriented diagram is a projection with only finitely many transverse double points and no triple points. ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]])

[F8] A smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; a collar is a smooth embedding of the boundary times a half-interval, equal to the boundary inclusion at zero and onto an open boundary neighbourhood. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]) ([[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]])

[F9] A tubular chart exists under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. It may be normalized as in [F4]: its vertical derivative induces a smooth fibrewise isomorphism $B$ to the normal quotient, and precomposing the chart by $B^{-1}$ makes that identification the identity. A smooth isotopy of a compact boundaryless embedded source, stationary near its parameter endpoints, extends to an ambient isotopy; linking number is unchanged under ambient isotopy of oriented two-component links. ([[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]]) ([[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy]]) ([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]])

[F10] The standard smooth step function $\sigma$ is smooth, is zero for arguments at most zero, and is one for arguments at least one. ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]])

## Proof

1.1 By [A1], the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses in [F1], [F3], and [F6] hold. The given $F$ is a Seifert surface by [F1]. Use its inward unit conormal as the reference normal field. By [F2], this Seifert framing has relative winding integer zero. [given, A1, F1, F2]

1.2 Let $s$ be the inward unit conormal, viewed in the round-metric normal bundle. By [F8], choose a smooth collar $c:K\times[0,\varepsilon_0)\to F$ and orient its levels by the original $K$. For sufficiently small $\delta>0$, set $J_0=c(K,\delta)$. It is embedded, lies in $\operatorname{int}F$, and is disjoint from $K$. No prescribed collar velocity is assumed: since $c$ is an embedding onto a boundary neighbourhood, $\partial_t c(p,0)$ is inward transverse to $K$ in $F$. Its normal quotient is therefore $a(p)s(p)$ for a smooth function $a(p)>0$; a tangential component is allowed. [given, F8, construct]

1.3 Use a normalized tubular chart $\Phi$ of $K$ as in [F4] and [F9], and write $\Phi^{-1}(c(p,t))=(b_t(p),v_t(p))$, with $v_t(p)$ in the normal fibre over $b_t(p)$. Compactness permits one small interval of $t$ on which these expressions are defined for every $p$. At $t=0$ they are $(p,0)$, and normalization identifies the vertical derivative with $a(p)s(p)$. The maps $b_t$ are $C^1$-close to the identity. In a smooth oriented circle coordinate their lifts have the form $u+r_t(u)$ with $r_t$ periodic and $\|r_t'\|_\infty<1/2$ for small $t$; thus the lifts are increasing degree-one diffeomorphisms. Hence each $b_t$ is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Reparametrize the level over $x=b_t(p)$, obtaining a smooth normal section $w_t(x)=v_t(b_t^{-1}(x))$. Taylor expansion in finitely many bundle charts gives, uniformly on $K$, $w_t(x)=t a(x)s(x)+O(t^2)$. Because $a$ has positive minimum and $s$ is unit, after decreasing $\delta$ this implies $\langle w_\delta(x),s(x)\rangle>0$ for every $x$. [given, F4, F9, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

1.4 For $0\le u\le1$, interpolate in each normal fibre by $z_u(x)=(1-\chi(u))w_\delta(x)+\chi(u)\delta s(x)$, where $\chi(u)=\sigma(3u-1)$ is the plateau from [F10]. Every $z_u$ has positive pairing with $s$, so it never meets the zero section. Uniformly these vectors have norm $O(\delta)$; a common disk bundle about the compact zero section lies in the tubular domain, so all interpolating graphs lie in that domain when $\delta$ is small. Each graph projects identically to $K$, hence is an embedded circle, and $\Phi$ carries it to an embedded circle disjoint from $K$. With $K$ as the fixed first component this is a smooth two-component link isotopy, stationary near its parameter endpoints, from $K\cup J_0$ to $K\cup\Phi(\delta s)$. The orientation on $J_0$ agrees with the graph orientation because $b_\delta$ preserves orientation. By [F9] the family extends to an ambient isotopy and its linking number is unchanged. The endpoint $\Phi(\delta s)$ is exactly a sufficiently small normalized-chart push-off in [F3]–[F4]. Consequently the self-linking in the statement equals $\operatorname{lk}(K,J_0)$, without identifying the collar level literally with a chart graph of $\delta s$. [A1, F3, F4, F9, F10, step 1.2, step 1.3, construct]

2.1 Since $F$ is a compact embedded surface, it is closed and has empty interior in $S^3$; hence its complement contains a point $q$. Choose an orientation-preserving stereographic chart from $q$. It places $K\cup J_0$ and $F$ in $\mathbb R^3$. Let $F_0$ be the closure in $F$ of the complement of the open boundary collar $c(K\times[0,\delta))$. Then $F_0$ is compact, is disjoint from $K$, and has boundary set $J_0$. Give $F_0$ its orientation inherited from $F$; at its new boundary the outward collar-normal points back toward $K$, so the induced boundary orientation is the transported orientation of $J_0$, parallel to $K$. Apply [F6] and [F7] to choose a regular oriented diagram $D$ of $K\cup J_0$, with the projection-plane orientation induced from $S^3$. [given, F6, F7, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Apply [F5] with its first component $J$ equal to the original knot $K$, its second (boundary) component equal to $J_0$, and the oriented spanning surface $\Sigma=F_0$. The curve $K$ is disjoint from $F_0$, so it is transverse to $F_0$ with empty intersection and has signed intersection number zero. Thus [F5] gives $\operatorname{lk}_D(K,J_0)=\operatorname{lk}(K,J_0)=0$. This computes the linking number in the same order as the self-linking convention.       url: "https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03115v1"

## Definition

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

    - title: Jae Choon Cha and Kent E. Orr, “L²-signatures, homology localization, and
        amenable groups”
      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.3700

---

## Definition

Assume full AC, matching the chosen finite twisted-chain and maximal-abelian-cover conventions. Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). Put π^(0)=π and π^(j+1)=[π^(j),π^(j)]. A right Zπ-chain complex with coefficients in a left Z[π/π^(j)]-module is formed by tensoring over Zπ with that module.

For n≥0, W is an integral n-solution for K when H₁(M(K);Z)→H₁(W;Z) is an isomorphism, H₂(W;Z) is free of rank 2r for some finite r, and there are classes x₁,…,x_r,y₁,…,y_r in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n)]) whose equivariant intersection pairings satisfy λ_n(x_i,x_j)=0 and λ_n(x_i,y_j)=δ_ij. It is an integral (n+1/2)-solution when, in addition, each x_i is the image of a class x̃_i in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n+1)]) and λ_{n+1}(x̃_i,x̃_j)=0 for all i,j. Here λ_j is the equivariant intersection pairing induced by the orientation of W.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The von Neumann dimension of a finitely generated projective N G-module represented by a projection E is τ_G(E); for an arbitrary module it is the supremum of the dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules.

For a compact oriented 4-manifold W with boundary, sign(W) is the inertia difference of the symmetric intersection form on H₂(W;R) modulo its radical (the subspace pairing to zero with every class), equivalently on the image of H₂(W;R)→H₂(W,∂W;R). Given a closed oriented 3-manifold M, a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G, a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G of φ, the L²-signature sign_G^(2)(W,ψ) is the von Neumann signature of the nonsingular part of the N G-coefficient intersection form. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

## Example

In the implemented first-Born optical-scattering benchmark, the unknown is a real $128\times128$ array $z$ of cellwise permittivity contrasts, each equal to the object's permittivity minus the background permittivity. For each transmitter $j\in\{1,\dots,20\}$, $u_{\rm in}^{(j)}$ is its fixed incident illumination field, and $H_{m,r}$ is the fixed Green response from cell $r$ to receiver $m$. The released forward implementation reports measurements

$$y_{j,m}=\Delta x\Delta y\sum_r z_r\,\overline{u_{\rm in}^{(j)}(r)}\,H_{m,r}+e_{j,m},$$

where $m$ indexes receivers, $r$ indexes grid cells, $\Delta x=\Delta y=18\,\mathrm{cm}/128$ are the grid spacings, and $e$ is additive Gaussian measurement noise with reported level $\sigma_y=10^{-4}$. Thus the implemented map is real-linear in $z$. The reported physical field is $18\,\mathrm{cm}\times18\,\mathrm{cm}$, the wavelength is $0.84\,\mathrm{cm}$, the background permittivity is $1$, and the receiver count is $360$, $180$, or $60$. The paper reports $10{,}000$ training images of HL60-cell permittivity, $10$ validation images, and $100$ test images; it curates the test samples so their cosine similarities to training images are below $0.6$, where cosine similarity of nonzero image arrays $a,b$ is $\langle a,b\rangle/(\|a\|_2\|b\|_2)$. The paper's Appendix B.1 also prints a contrast-dependent total-field formula; this example follows the fixed-incident-field implementation and does not infer linearity from that printed formula.

kind: lemma

      url: "https://www.ime.usp.br/~glaucio/mat6704/textos/GMTLecureNotes.pdf"

## Statement

If an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is covered by a countable family of open sets $(V_\ell)_{\ell\in I}$, then there is a countable locally finite family of nonnegative functions $(\eta_j)\subset C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ summing to one, with each $\operatorname{supp}\eta_j$ contained in one member $V_\ell$ of the cover. Locally finite means that each point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many supports.

## Statement references

[[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls|A smooth bump can equal one on a smaller concentric ball and vanish outside a larger ball.]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and a countable open cover of $\Omega$.

[F1] Closed bounded subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ are compact. ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]])

[F2] Rational vectors are dense in $\mathbb R^n$, and $\mathbb Q^n$ is countable. ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]], [[thm-rationals-countable]], [[thm-product-of-countable]])

[F3] A smooth cutoff exists between any two concentric balls whose closures are nested. ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]])

## Proof

**Given:** The open set $\Omega$ and its countable open cover.

1.1 If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the empty family proves the claim. Otherwise, for $m\ge1$ set $K_m=\{x:|x|\le m,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega^c)\ge1/m\}$ when $\Omega\ne\mathbb R^n$, and set $K_m=\overline B(0,m)$ when $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$; put $K_m=\varnothing$ for $m\le0$. Each $K_m$ is compact by [F1], the sets are nested, $K_m\subset\operatorname{int}K_{m+1}$, and their interiors cover $\Omega$. The compact shells $S_m:=K_m\setminus\operatorname{int}K_{m-1}$ cover $\Omega$ and lie in the open sets $U_m:=\operatorname{int}K_{m+1}\setminus K_{m-2}$. The family $(U_m)$ is locally finite: any compact subset of $\Omega$ lies in some $\operatorname{int}K_N$ and hence in $K_{m-2}$ for all sufficiently large $m$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Fix once a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\theta$ equal to one on $\overline B(0,1)$ and supported in $B(0,2)$, whose existence is [F3]. In each $U_m$, consider the rational inner balls $B(q,r)$ for which $\overline B(q,2r)\subset U_m\cap V_\ell$ for some cover index $\ell$. Indexed by $(\ell,q,r)$, these balls form a countable cover of $S_m$: for each point choose a cover member containing it, then density [F2] gives a rational center and radius with the required doubled closure. Compactness of $S_m$ gives a finite subcover. Order all finite lists of eligible indexed balls by natural-number codes and take the first list covering $S_m$; thus no choice principle is needed. For each selected ball use the fixed rescaled cutoff $\psi_{m,j}(x):=\theta((x-q)/r)$. The family is locally finite because each shell contributes finitely many cutoffs supported in $U_m$, and each support also lies in its assigned cover member. Its sum $s:=\sum_{m,j}\psi_{m,j}$ is smooth and positive on $\Omega$ because the shells cover $\Omega$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, choose, construct]

3.1 Define $\eta_{m,j}:=\psi_{m,j}/s$. Then each function is smooth, nonnegative and compactly supported in $\Omega$, the family is locally finite, and $\sum_{m,j}\eta_{m,j}=1$. Each support remains in its assigned cover member, and enumeration gives the required countable family. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎

    - title: Jeff Erickson, Normal Surfaces and Knots, Computational Topology lecture
        notes (2009)
      url: https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/teaching/comptop/2009/notes/normal-surfaces.pdf

        surfaces and knots.

## Statement

Let $T$ be a good triangulation of a knot exterior with $t$ tetrahedra and a marked meridian path in its triangulated boundary torus. A certificate consists of a nonnegative integer vector $v$ with $7t$ binary-encoded coordinates, a set of active matching and zero-coordinate constraints, a nonzero $(7t-1)$-minor witnessing their rank, and the marked boundary data. A deterministic verifier can check the certificate in time polynomial in the certificate bit length. Acceptance verifies that $v$ is a primitive admissible extreme-ray vector of the Haken cone and that its associated normal surface is a properly embedded disk with non-null-homotopic boundary. The verifier uses arithmetic on the compressed coordinates and does not expand the normal surface into its potentially exponentially many normal disks.

## Statement references

[[def-normal-surface-coordinate-box]] — admissible vectors, primitive vertex vectors and normal surfaces.

[[lem-normal-coordinate-matching-equations-and-finite-bounds]] — coordinate bounds and matching equations.

[[lem-fundamental-normal-surfaces-are-connected]] — connectedness from fundamentalness.

[[lem-normal-disk-candidate-check-characterization]] — finite disk and essential-boundary tests.

[Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger, §8](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hass/Research/Papers/Complexity/hlp.pdf) — the active-constraint certificate and polynomial-bit verification strategy.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite triangulation $T$, its integer matching matrix, a marked meridian path of finite length in the boundary triangulation, and the binary certificate described in the statement.

[F1] [[def-normal-surface-coordinate-box]]: the Haken cone is the nonnegative solution set of the matching equations; admissibility adds the quadrilateral condition.

[F2] [[lem-normal-coordinate-matching-equations-and-finite-bounds]]: matching rows have four coefficients $\pm1$, and primitive extreme-ray coordinates have $O(t)$ bits.

[F3] [[lem-fundamental-normal-surfaces-are-connected]]: every nonempty fundamental normal surface is connected.

[F4] [[lem-normal-disk-candidate-check-characterization]]: connectedness, nonempty boundary, Euler characteristic $1$, and odd meridian intersection characterize a connected essential disk.

[F5] [[lem-small-integer-matrix-linear-algebra-in-quadratic-logarithmic-space]]: specified minors of small-entry integer matrices have deterministic polynomial-bit-time exact determinants via streamed prime-field elimination and bounded Chinese remaindering.

## Proof

1.1 The verifier first checks the vector length, nonnegativity, matching equations, and the at-most-one-quadrilateral condition by scanning $7t$ coordinates and the finite face-matching rows. It computes the gcd of the coordinates by Euclid's algorithm and checks that it is $1$. These operations use polynomially many integer operations on integers whose bit lengths are bounded by the certificate length. [given, F1, F2, construct]

1.2 For Euler characteristic, let $F(v)=\sum_i v_i$ count normal disks and let $A(v)=\sum_i q_i v_i$ count their normal-arc sides, where $q_i$ is $3$ for a triangle type and $4$ for a quadrilateral type. Let $B(v)$ count arcs on boundary faces; this is a fixed linear form in the coordinates. The number of surface edges is $(A(v)+B(v))/2$, since each interior-face arc side is paired and each boundary arc is unpaired. For each edge $e$ of the triangulation, choose one incident tetrahedron and let $N_e(v)$ be its local linear count of normal disk intersections with $e$; matching makes this count independent of the incident tetrahedron. Then $V(v)=\sum_e N_e(v)$ counts surface vertices and $\chi(v)=V(v)-(A(v)+B(v))/2+F(v)$. The boundary is nonempty exactly when $B(v)>0$. Put the marked meridian in transverse position to the finite list of boundary arc types; each type has a fixed intersection count, so parity of total intersections is another linear form modulo $2$. These local coefficients are computed once from constant-size face and tetrahedron templates; arithmetic on their compressed coordinate sums is polynomial in $t$ and the certificate bit length. [given, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The certificate lists active zero-coordinate rows and matching rows. The verifier checks every listed zero coordinate is actually zero, chooses the stated $(7t-1)$ square minor, and computes its determinant by the explicit prime-field/CRT algorithm [F5]. The minor has dimension $7t-1$ and entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, so that algorithm takes polynomial time in $t$, hence in the certificate length. Its determinant is reconstructed as an integer, not accepted from a claimed numerical value in the witness. A nonzero determinant certifies that the listed rows have rank at least $7t-1$; because the nonzero vector $v$ lies in their common kernel, the rank is at most $7t-1$, hence exactly that value. The face of the nonnegative matching cone containing $v$ therefore has dimension one, so $v$ lies on an extreme ray. The gcd check makes it the primitive integer generator of that ray. [given, F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 A primitive integer vector on an extreme ray is fundamental among admissible integer vectors. If $v=x+y$ with nonzero admissible integer vectors, then $x,y$ lie in the cone and their sum lies on an extreme ray. By extremality each summand lies on that same ray; since $v$ is the primitive integer generator, each nonzero integral summand is a positive integer multiple of $v$, which cannot sum to $v$. Thus $v$ is fundamental and [F3] makes its normal surface connected without expanding it. [F1, F3, step 2.1, contradiction]

4.1 If the boundary is nonempty, the Euler characteristic is $1$, and the meridian intersection is odd, [F4] identifies the surface as a properly embedded disk with non-null-homotopic boundary. Conversely, acceptance has checked admissibility, a primitive extreme ray, connectedness from step 3.1, and these three disk tests, so it certifies exactly such a disk. [F4, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra]

5.1 The certificate has $7t$ coordinates with their binary expansions, at most $O(t)$ constraint indices, and one determinant minor of dimension $7t-1$. Determinants have the polynomial bit-time implementation [F5]. Ordinary binary gcd descent has at most a constant times the input bit length many divisions (two remainder steps at least halve the positive remainder); each division is polynomial in the input bit length. Thus determinant and gcd computations, coordinate checks, and local linear-form evaluations all take polynomial time in the total encoded length. At no point is a disk copy expanded; arithmetic acts directly on its coordinate multiplicity. [given, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $K\subset S^3$ be an oriented knot, let $E_K$ be its compact exterior, let $X$ be a finite based deficiency-one two-dimensional spine with one vertex, $n\ge2$ oriented $1$-cells and $n-1$ oriented $2$-cells, certified by a based cellular simple-homotopy equivalence with $E_K$, and let $\psi:\pi_1(E_K)\twoheadrightarrow H\cong\mathbb Z^m$ have $m\ge1$. Let $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation over a field, and assume the degree-one twisted homology over $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$ is a torsion module. For any admissible generator column of the Fox block matrix of the certified spine, its deleted-minor Wada quotient represents the based twisted Reidemeister torsion of $E_K$ in $Q^\times/\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}$, where $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}=\{\pm\det(\rho(g))\psi(g)^d:g\in\pi_1(E_K)\}$. All admissible columns give the same class. If two such deficiency-one spines are related by a supplied finite based simple cellular equivalence carrying the same representation and deck map, their Wada quotient classes also agree. A group-presentation isomorphism alone is not such an equivalence.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-wada-quotient-for-deficiency-one-presentation|Admissible deleted-column quotient]]

[[lem-twisted-fox-jacobian-is-cellular-boundary|Fox matrix as cellular boundary]]

[[lem-knot-twisted-exterior-acyclicity-from-torsion-module|Exterior-spine acyclicity]]

[[thm-wada-deleted-minor-equals-twisted-reidemeister-torsion|Deleted-minor torsion identity]]

[[lem-twisted-torsion-cell-basis-change-ambiguity|Simple-spine unit ambiguity]]

[Kirk and Livingston, §§3–4](https://chuck-livingston.github.io/math/Livingston_papers/1999_Twisted%20Alexander%20invariants%2C%20Reidemeister%20torsion%2C%20and%20Casson-Gordon%20invariants.pdf)

[Conway, §§2.3–2.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.06678)

[Ranicki, basis changes and Theorem 15](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/torsion.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; the finite based knot-exterior spine certificate; a positive-rank free-abelian deck epimorphism; a field-valued representation; degree-one Laurent-ring homology torsion; and an admissible deleted column.

[A1] AC is inherited from the maximal-abelian-cover convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F1] The evaluated Fox block matrix of a based presentation complex is the cellular boundary matrix of its twisted chain complex, with the stated row-coefficient convention. [[lem-twisted-fox-jacobian-is-cellular-boundary]]

[F2] Torsion degree-one homology, positive-rank deck map, and the stated deficiency-one cell counts imply acyclicity over the fraction field. [[lem-knot-twisted-exterior-acyclicity-from-torsion-module]]

[F3] For an admissible deleted column of a certified deficiency-one spine, the Fox minor divided by its boundary determinant is the based twisted torsion class, and all admissible columns agree. [[thm-wada-deleted-minor-equals-twisted-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F4] Changing lifts, orientations or the certified simple cellular model changes torsion only by an element of the determinant and deck-unit subgroup. [[lem-twisted-torsion-cell-basis-change-ambiguity]]

[F5] The twisted-chain definition gives the based fraction-field torsion and its exact unit quotient. [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

## Proof



1.1 The supplied simple-spine certificate identifies the cellular presentation complex with the selected knot exterior model and transports the based cells, representation, and deck map. Therefore [F1] identifies the evaluated Fox matrix with the actual twisted cellular boundary matrix of this model; no conclusion here follows merely from an isomorphism of presented groups. [given, F1]

1.2 The spine has one $0$-cell, $n$ $1$-cells and $n-1$ $2$-cells, and the deck map has positive rank. The given torsion hypothesis is exactly the degree-one module hypothesis in [F2]. Hence its fraction-field complex is acyclic, so the torsion class in [F5] is defined and nonzero. [A1, F2, F5, given]

2.1 The chosen column is admissible by hypothesis. Apply [F3] to the based spine and the acyclic complex from step 1.2. It states that the deleted Fox minor divided by the selected $d_1$ block determinant represents the torsion class in $Q^\times/\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}$, and it proves the same conclusion for every other admissible column. [F1, F3, step 1.2]

3.1 If a second certified deficiency-one spine is related to the first by the stated finite based simple cellular equivalence, [F4] makes its based torsion class equal in the same quotient; the representation and deck map are transported by that equivalence, so the subgroup $\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}$ is unchanged. Applying step 2.1 to the second spine shows its admissible Wada quotient has that same class. This proves the permitted presentation-change assertion without promoting a group isomorphism to a spine equivalence. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Example

On the unit ball $\Omega=B(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$, define
$$\psi(x)= \begin{cases} \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{1}{1-4|x|^2}\right),&|x|<1/2,\\ 0,&|x|\geq1/2. \end{cases}$$
For any $\epsilon\ne0$ with $|\epsilon|\|\psi\|_\infty<1$, the positive conductivities $\gamma_1\equiv1$ and $\gamma_2=1+\epsilon\psi$ agree with all orders of derivatives at $\partial\Omega$ but are unequal in the interior. This example shows that equality of all boundary conductivity jets alone does not imply interior equality; it makes no assertion that the two full DN maps agree.

## Example references

[[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map|Positive scalar conductivity convention]]

[[thm-ip-boundary-determination-of-scalar-conductivity|Boundary jets are determined by full DN data]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the unit ball and the explicit function $\psi$ in the statement.

[F1] [[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: an admissible scalar conductivity is smooth and strictly positive on the closure of the domain.

[F2] [[thm-ip-boundary-determination-of-scalar-conductivity]]: equality of full conductivity DN maps implies equality of all boundary-normal jets; the example tests only whether equality of those jets by itself forces interior equality.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 For every integer $m\geq0$, differentiation gives $\frac{d^m}{dt^m}e^{-1/t}=P_m(1/t)e^{-1/t}$ on $t>0$ for a polynomial $P_m$, by induction on $m$. For every polynomial $P$, $P(s)e^{-s}\to0$ as $s\to\infty$; for each power $s^N$, this follows from $e^s\geq s^{N+1}/(N+1)!$. Thus every right derivative tends to zero at $t=0$, so extension by zero to $t\leq0$ is smooth and flat there. Composition with $t=1-4|x|^2$ proves $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))$, with compact support in $\overline{B(0,1/2)}$. It is nonzero at $x=0$, and $\|\psi\|_\infty<\infty$. [given, induction, construct, algebra]

1.2 The bound $|\epsilon|\|\psi\|_\infty<1$ gives $\gamma_2(x)\geq1-|\epsilon|\|\psi\|_\infty>0$, so [F1] applies. Since $\psi$ vanishes on a neighborhood of $\partial\Omega$, $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ agree on that neighborhood and all their boundary derivatives agree. At the origin, $\gamma_2(0)-\gamma_1(0)=\epsilon e^{-1}\ne0$. Thus identical boundary jets do not force interior equality. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk with boundary K, let q be a prime power, and let $W_{D,q}$ be its branched cover. Put
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr).$$
If $\chi:H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D);\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ has prime-power order, then $\chi$ vanishes on $P_D$ if and only if it extends to a character of prime-power order on $H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)$.

## Statement references

[[def-finite-order-character-of-a-branched-cover|Finite-order characters and vanishing]]

[[lem-slice-disk-induces-branched-cover-metabolizer|The disk-induced metabolizer]]

[Charles Livingston and Swatee Naik, *Introduction to Knot Concordance*, §8.2, pp. 167–168](https://chuck-livingston.github.io/math/Concordance_Book.pdf)

[[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the disk $D$, the prime-power cover $W_{D,q}$, the inclusion $i:H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)$, its kernel $P_D$, and a prime-power-order character $\chi$.

[A1] Full AC is assumed wherever the cover and orientation conventions use the choice axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] $P_D=\ker i$, and $H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)$ is finite because $W_{D,q}$ is a rational homology ball with finite CW type. [[lem-slice-disk-induces-branched-cover-metabolizer]] [[lem-prime-power-branched-cover-of-slice-disk-is-rational-homology-ball]]

[F2] A finite-order character is a homomorphism to $\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ whose element in the character group has finite order; vanishing on $P_D$ means its restriction to $P_D$ is zero. [[def-finite-order-character-of-a-branched-cover]]

## Proof



1.1 If $\chi$ extends to $\widetilde\chi:H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, then for every $x\in P_D$ one has $i(x)=0$, so $\chi(x)=\widetilde\chi(i(x))=0$. The extension has finite image because its domain is finite. [F1, F2, given, algebra, A1]

1.2 Conversely, suppose $\chi(P_D)=0$. Then $\chi$ factors uniquely through the subgroup $I=i(H_1(\Sigma_q(\partial D)))$ of the finite group $B=H_1(W_{D,q})$. Let $p$ be the prime underlying the order of $\chi$ as in [F2]. Every element of order coprime to $p$ maps to zero, since its image is killed both by a power of $p$ and by an integer coprime to $p$. Thus the factored map restricts to the $p$-primary subgroup $I_p\le B_p$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 A homomorphism from a subgroup $J$ of a finite abelian $p$-group $B_p$ into $\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z[p^\infty]$ extends when one adjoins one element $b\in B_p$: if $p^k$ is the order of $b+J$, choose $c\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z[p^\infty]$ with $p^kc=f(p^kb)$, which exists because multiplication by $p^k$ is surjective on this Prüfer group. Set $f'(j+rb)=f(j)+rc$. If $j+rb=j'+r'b$, then $(r-r')b\in J$, so $r-r'$ is divisible by $p^k$; the chosen equation makes the two values equal. The extension is therefore well-defined. Repeating this finite step extends the character from $I_p$ to $B_p$. [given, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Set the extension to zero on the complementary primary summand of $B$ and combine it with the extension on $B_p$. The resulting character on $B$ extends $\chi$ and has finite $p$-power image because $B$ is finite and the values are $p$-primary. This proves the reverse implication. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
