## Example

Consider the identity pattern I given by the core of the solid torus, the (p,1)-cable pattern for a positive integer p, and the local-knot pattern P_J obtained by tying a fixed knot J into a small arc of the core. Their winding numbers are respectively 1, p and 1. The identity pattern fixes every knot. The closure of the (p,1)-cable pattern is the unknot, so it satisfies the closure sliceness hypothesis for the localized weak-injectivity corollary. The local-knot pattern has closure J, which may be nontrivial, yet its solid-torus meridian normally generates the closure-knot group.

## Example references

[[def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-winding-number|Cable patterns and winding]]

[CDR, §§1–2 and Proposition 2.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.5058v3)

[Ray, §5](https://numdam.org/item/10.5802/wbln.39.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The identity, (p,1)-cable and local-knot patterns with the stated orientations.

[F1] Winding number is algebraic intersection with a meridional disk ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

[F2] Strong winding is normal generation by the solid-torus meridian in the closure complement ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The identity core meets a meridional disk once positively. A (p,1)-cable represents p times the core class, and the local knot changes the core by a knot tied into a ball, not its homology class. Thus the listed winding numbers are 1,p,1. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 The (p,1) torus knot is the unknot, so its closure bounds the standard disk in B⁴ and is Z[1/|p|]-slice. The identity map is K↦K. [given, algebra]

2.1 For the local-knot pattern the closure complement is the exterior of J with the axis meridian identifying to a meridian of J. Meridional Dehn filling gives S³; van Kampen therefore says the normal closure of this meridian is the whole knot group. J can be nontrivial, so knotted closure does not preclude strong winding. [F2, given, algebra] ∎

      url: https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/donaldson.pdf

---

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be an $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. Complete the connections in $H^3$ and the gauge transformations in $H^4$, and use the unbased irreducible configuration quotient. The curvature section $\Phi([A])=F_A^-$ takes values in its $H^2$ equation bundle. Choose an open subset $U$ covered by finitely many bounded Coulomb slice balls centered at smooth irreducible connections, and an open $V$ whose closure is contained in the union of strictly smaller closed balls in these charts, their images lying in $U$.

Allow smooth gauge-equivariant perturbation sections supported in $U$, whose slice representatives are smooth $H^3$-valued maps with finite uniform $H^3$ norm on the specified chart balls. Interpret them in the $H^2$ equation bundle by inclusion. Give this class the topology of the uniform $H^3$ section norm on those finitely many balls together with convergence of the section and its slice derivative $H^3\to H^2$ uniformly on compact subsets. The perturbations for which $\Phi+\sigma$ is transverse to zero at every zero in $\overline V$ form an open dense subset. Their zero sets in $V$ are smooth orientable five-manifolds, and the real determinant line of the gauge-fixed deformation family is orientable on the irreducible quotient. The based quotient may be used to pull back this orientation; it carries an additional $SO(3)$ framing fiber and is not the unbased five-dimensional moduli space.

## Statement references

[Donaldson, *An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds*, §§II.1–II.4](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/donaldson.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The sign-fixed equation is $F_A^-=0$, with unbased real operator $d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$ and charge $c_2=-1$. [[def-asd-moduli-fredholm-index-and-lattice-setup]]

[F2] Its real index is $8k-3(1-b_1+b_-)$, with full AC. Here $k=1$ and $b_1=b_-=0$, so the index is five. [[thm-asd-deformation-complex-index-formula]]

[F3] The actual high-Sobolev slice construction gives a smooth unbased quotient and equation bundle; the based quotient is a principal $SO(3)$ framing bundle. [[lem-high-sobolev-coulomb-slices-for-irreducible-su-two-connections]]

[F4] On the stated finite slice collars, bounded smoothing perturbations give an open dense transverse class in exactly the specified topology, and their regular zero sets have dimension equal to the unbased index. [[lem-bounded-smoothing-perturbations-give-open-dense-asd-transversality]]

[F5] The real $SU(2)$ determinant family is gauge-equivariantly orientable on a closed simply connected oriented four-manifold, and this persists under compact perturbations and induces the orientation of a regular zero set. [[lem-su-two-asd-determinant-lines-are-gauge-equivariantly-orientable]]

[A1] Full AC is used through the analytic, finite-model, Bott and obstruction suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** Full AC, the manifold and bundle, and the actual Sobolev, slice-collar and perturbation conditions of the Statement.

1.1 By [F3], the quotient and equation bundle are smooth in the stated $H^3/H^4$ spaces. In a slice centered at $A$ the equation is $F_A^-+d_A^-a+(a\wedge a)^-$. The derivative of each allowed perturbation factors through the compact inclusion $H^3\hookrightarrow H^2$, and [F4] proves Fredholmness of the slice derivative with the same index as [F1]. Formula [F2] gives that index as five. [F1, F2, F3, F4, A1, given, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F4] with the exact finite larger and smaller slice balls in the Statement. It proves openness from a compact set containing every zero of all uniformly nearby perturbations, using the uniform $H^4$ bound; density is the finite cokernel-complement perturbation and finite-dimensional Sard argument. Thus the claimed set is open dense, and its zero set in $V$ is a smooth five-manifold by step 1.1. [F4, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F5], the unperturbed real determinant line is orientable with every gauge transformation preserving the orientation. Scaling the compact perturbation derivative from zero to its actual value preserves this property. At a transverse zero the kernel of the slice derivative is the moduli tangent space and its cokernel is zero, so the determinant orientation gives a tangent orientation. The extra scalar gauge block is invertible and has its fixed orientation. Therefore the actual unbased moduli manifold is orientable. The based quotient only pulls this construction back and adds the three framing directions described in [F3]; it is not used to change the index in step 1.1. This proves all conclusions. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, A1, algebra] ∎

## Source notes

The complete source proof on Donaldson's printed pp.288–295 was read, including the $H^3/H^4$ exponents, the perturbations valued in $H^3$ with equation target $H^2$, Lemma 9 and Lemma 10. This replaces a defective previous formalization, not the mathematical theorem by an easier special case. A nonempty open subset of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold cannot have compact closure: in a contained coordinate ball, an orthonormal sequence at a fixed small radius has no convergent subsequence. Thus the previous phrase “relatively compact open set” did not express the finite bounded slice collars used in the source. Uniform control of the smoothing section value is the compactness mechanism for openness; arbitrary compact derivatives with only compact-open control do not supply that mechanism. The previous based-quotient wording also omitted its three framing directions. The three actual suppliers prove the corrected analytic operation and the original orientability conclusion, with full AC stated explicitly.

## Statement

Let B be a smooth 4-ball embedded in the standard smooth 4-sphere S⁴. The closure of S⁴\B is diffeomorphic to the standard 4-ball. This is the special smooth Schoenflies complement assertion used after a capped contractible 4-manifold has been identified with standard S⁴; it does not assert the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.

## Statement references

[CDR, proof of Proposition 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.5058v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A smooth embedded standard four-ball $B$ in the standard smooth sphere $S^4$.

[F1] The complement of a smoothly embedded standard four-ball in the standard smooth four-sphere is standard, by shrinking the whole parametrized ball and extending its isotopy. [[thm-smooth-4-ball-embedded-in-s4-has-standard-complement]]

## Proof

1.1 Choose a diffeomorphism $b:B^4\to B$, where the existence of this parametrization is part of saying that $B$ is a smooth four-ball. Compose it with the given embedding into $S^4$ to obtain a smooth embedding $f:B^4\hookrightarrow S^4$. This supplies an embedded standard side, rather than merely a boundary three-sphere or a contractible complementary manifold. [given, construct]

2.1 Apply [F1] to $f$. It gives a diffeomorphism from $\overline{S^4\setminus f(B^4)}=\overline{S^4\setminus B}$ to the standard $B^4$, as claimed. No smooth Poincaré assertion is needed for this complement step; any earlier identification of a capped ambient manifold with standard $S^4$ is a separate hypothesis of the application. [F1, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact irreducible piecewise linear $3$-manifold with a finite compatible triangulation. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible piecewise linear tori that are subcomplexes of that triangulation. Every component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is irreducible.

## Statement references

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, §1.2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

[Ryan Budney, *JSJ-decompositions of knot and link complements in the 3-sphere*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0506523)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the compact irreducible finite PL manifold, disjoint two-sided incompressible PL torus family and cut component of the Statement.

[A1] The original full AC assumption is [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. No essential use of it occurs in the finite argument below.

[F1] Here irreducibility and incompressibility are in the PL category specified in the Statement: an interior PL sphere bounds a PL ball, and a PL compressing disk has essential boundary on its surface and otherwise misses it. These are the geometric conventions of [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]], interpreted in that explicit category.

[F2] A two-sided PL torus in a parametrized finite PL ball has a PL compression contained in the ball's interior; its local PL flatness and compatible bicollar are supplied by the full link-disk and cut-collar proof. [[lem-two-sided-pl-tori-in-a-parametrized-pl-ball-have-pl-compressions]]

[F3] A compact PL ball and the finite PL torus polyhedra inside it have common compatible finite subcomplex subdivisions. [[lem-pl-embedded-polyhedron-admits-compatible-subcomplex-triangulation]]

## Proof

1.1 Let $S$ be a PL sphere in the interior of the selected cut component. Its image in $M$ is a PL sphere missing every cutting torus, so bounds a parametrized PL ball $B$ by [F1]. Each connected cutting torus lies wholly inside or wholly outside that sphere. If a torus lies inside $B$, its existing two-sided neighborhood can be shrunk into $\operatorname{Int}B$, by compactness and a common smaller product width. It remains a PL embedded torus there. [F3] supplies the compatible finite subdivisions needed for [F2], even if the original triangulation of $B$ was different from the one containing the torus. [F1, F3, given, construct]

2.1 Such an inside torus would have the PL compressing disk of [F2] entirely in $B\subset M$, contradicting its original incompressibility. Thus $B$ misses every cutting torus. The connected ball interior lies in the same complement component as its collar along $S$, so $B$ lifts to a PL ball in the specified cut component with boundary $S$. Every interior PL sphere there therefore bounds a PL ball. This is precisely PL irreducibility; no smooth-ball or arbitrary-topological-marking claim entered. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the chosen smooth knot-exterior data. Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, presented as the boundary of the square plumbing of one positive and one negative Hopf band, with one boundary component. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose positive normal push-off of its core has linking number $+1$ with the core; a negative Hopf band has linking number $-1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the annuli with the four boundary edges alternating between the annuli, then smooths corners. Let $F$ be this plumbed surface, and choose the compact exterior by deleting the interior of the binding neighborhood $N(K_8)\cong\partial F\times D^2$ supplied by the open book; on every page this neighborhood meets the page in an annular collar of $\partial F$. Let $a,b$ be the core curves, ordered so that $a$ is the positive-band core and $a\cdot_F b=+1$. The exterior $E_{K_8}$ fibers over $S^1$ with fiber $F$. With the twist convention that the positive twist $R_a$ sends $a\mapsto a$, $b\mapsto a+b$, and the negative twist $L_b$ sends $a\mapsto a+b$, $b\mapsto b$, the monodromy is $R_a\circ L_b$. After capping $\partial F$ by a disk, its action on the ordered homology basis $([a],[b])$ is represented by $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

## Statement references

[Danny Calegari, *Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds*, Chapter 5, §5.8.1, Example 5.39](https://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/books/foliations/oupbook.pdf)

[Kenneth Lee Baker, *Knots on Once-Punctured Torus Fibers*, §3.1 and Appendix B](https://www.math.miami.edu/~kenken/Baker-Diss-07-02-04.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The explicitly plumbed oriented knot $K_8$, the chosen compact exterior $E_{K_8}$, and the square-plumbing surface with ordered core curves $a,b$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the hypothesis of the smooth exterior convention [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] [[def-knot-exterior]]: the chosen exterior is $S^3$ with the interior of the supplied closed tubular neighborhood removed.

[F2] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]: a knot is a smooth oriented circle embedded in the standard oriented $S^3$, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy.

## Proof

1.1 In $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$, the standard Hopf link is $H=\{z_1z_2=0\}$. On its complement, $f(z_1,z_2)=z_1z_2/|z_1z_2|$ is a submersion to $S^1$. Writing $r=|z_1|^2$, $\theta=\arg z_1$, and $\phi=\arg z_2$, a fiber is $0<r<1$, $\phi=-\theta+\text{constant}$, hence an annulus. For base angle $s\in[0,2\pi]$, transport by $\theta_s=\theta+\chi(r)s$, $\phi_s=\phi+(1-\chi(r))s$, where $\chi=1$ near $r=0$ and $\chi=0$ near $r=1$, fixes both boundary circles at $s=2\pi$ and makes one full annular twist between them. The sign is determined by the signed linking of the positive normal push-off of the core with the core: changing the handedness of the Hopf band reverses the twist. With $a\cdot_F b=+1$, the positive twist about $a$ acts by $b\mapsto a+b$, while the negative twist about $b$ acts by $a\mapsto a+b$. Hence the two band monodromies have the stated actions $R_a$ and $L_b$. [given, A1, F2, construct]

2.1 Cutting a fibered exterior open along its page gives page $\times[0,1]$, with the two ends reidentified by the monodromy. In the square plumbing, the two annulus pages meet in the plumbing square $D$ and their product collars meet in $D\times[0,1]$. The interval coordinates agree on this product, so gluing the cut-open product pieces gives $(A\mathbin{\natural_D}B)\times[0,1]=F\times[0,1]$, where $A\mathbin{\natural_D}B$ denotes the surface obtained by gluing the two annuli along $D$. Reidentifying the interval ends extends each band map by the identity outside its annulus. The first return map is the composition in the stipulated plumbing order; choosing the positive band first gives $R_a\circ L_b$. The boundary knot is the standard figure-eight isotopy class by the specified plumbing presentation and [F2], and the chosen exterior is formed by deleting the binding neighborhood as in [F1]. Thus the exterior is the mapping torus of $F$ with that monodromy. [F1, F2, given, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Each annulus has Euler characteristic $0$, and the plumbing square has Euler characteristic $1$, so $\chi(F)=0+0-1=-1$. The plumbing is connected, oriented, and has one boundary component by the stated gluing; hence $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$ gives $g(F)=1$. Thus $F$ is a once-punctured torus. [given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 In the ordered basis $([a],[b])$, the columns of $R_a$ are $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$, while the columns of $L_b$ are $(1,1)$ and $(0,1)$. Their product is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$. Inclusion of the once-punctured torus into the torus obtained by capping its sole boundary induces an isomorphism on $H_1$, since attaching a disk along the boundary adds no 1-cycle or 2-cycle relation in degree one. Extending the boundary-fixing monodromy by the identity on that disk therefore has the same displayed action. [given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Diagram

The horizontal and vertical bands are plumbed along the shaded square $D$. The oriented core arcs cross once in $D$, with the indicated order giving $a\cdot_F b=+1$; their closures in the annuli are omitted from this schematic. The “positive” and “negative” labels record the Hopf-band handedness, equivalently the signs of their core push-off linking numbers. This is not a planar projection of the knot. The proof uses the explicit open-book map and product gluing, not the drawing.

## Statement

Use the Ozsvath–Szabo orientation convention $L(p,1)$ given by positive $p$-surgery on the unknot and label its Spin$^c$ structures by $i\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, represented by $0\le i<p$. For every integer $p\ge1$,
$$d(L(p,1),i)=\frac{(2i-p)^2-p}{4p}.$$
For the opposite orientation the correction terms are negated, with the conjugate Spin$^c$ label understood.

## Statement references

[[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention|The lens-space surgery orientation]]

[[def-heegaard-floer-correction-term|The correction-term convention]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Absolutely Graded Floer Homologies and Intersection Forms for Four-Manifolds with Boundary*, Propositions 4.2 and 4.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0110170v1)

[Aceto and Golla, *Dehn Surgeries and Rational Homology Balls*, Proposition 3.5 and Remark 3.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.07559v2)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[lem-lens-space-q-one-triangles-and-cyclic-handle-maps]] supplies the explicit individual index-zero, basepoint-zero count-one triangles, their cyclic maps and Chern evaluation $k=2i-p$ on a generator of square $-p$.

[F2] [[lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps]] constructs the absolute grading, with the sphere generator at degree zero, and proves the degree formula for these actual fixed-Spin$^c$ handle maps.

[F3] [[lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance]] identifies the correction term as the bottom degree of the infinity image. The convention in the statement is [[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]].

## Proof

**Given:** $p\ge1$ and a label $0\le i<p$, with the torus diagrams and fixed triangle structures of [F1].

1.1 The alpha-gamma diagram, and the diagram with those two attaching curves reversed, each have one intersection in each Spin$^c$ structure. Their infinity differentials are zero: the Maslov index of a self-disk in a torsion Spin$^c$ structure is $2n_z$, so cannot be one. The minus lattice in each summand is therefore exactly $U\mathbb F_2[U][x_i,0]$, and its plus image has bottom $[x_i,0]$. Its correction term is the absolute grading of that generator, with no unknown exponent shift. [F1, F3]

1.2 For the negative-trace map from $S^3$ to $-L(p,1)$, the fixed triangle has index and basepoint multiplicity zero and count one. It sends the sphere generator at exponent zero to $[x_i,0]$. The four-dimensional data are $c_1^2=-k^2/p$, $\chi=1$ and $\sigma=-1$. Hence its degree is $D_i=(1-k^2/p)/4$, and $d(-L(p,1),i)=D_i$. This computes the negative orientation directly. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

1.3 The cyclically reordered triangle gives the actual fixed-structure map from $L(p,1)$ to $S^3$ and sends $[x_i,0]$ to the sphere generator at exponent zero. It is the same oriented triple four-manifold with the other sphere input filled, so it has the same degree $D_i$. Consequently $0=\operatorname{gr}[x_i,0]+D_i$, and $d(L(p,1),i)=-D_i=((2i-p)^2-p)/(4p)$. This argument uses an actual turned-around triangle map rather than a general grading-duality assertion. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

1.4 The characteristic labels under orientation reversal or conjugation are paired by $k\mapsto-k$, equivalently $i\mapsto p-i$ modulo $p$. Their squares agree, so the two computations give exactly the asserted negation for the opposite orientation with the conjugate label. For $p=1$ the same computation has $k=-1$ and both correction terms zero. [F1, step 1.2, step 1.3] ∎

kind: lemma
title: The q=2 ellipsoid extremal profile minimizes the fourth-power objective

      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1853

## Statement

Assume the minimax detection-risk definition, $q=2$, and positive nondecreasing sequences $a_j$ and $\sigma_j$ with $a_j\to\infty$. Let $A,z_0>0$ and suppose $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$ is finite and nonempty. Define $\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ and assume
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2,\qquad \sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1.$$
Then $\widetilde\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$ and minimizes $\sum_{j\ge1}\eta_j^4$ over $\Theta_2(r)$; the nonnegative minimizer is unique.

## Statement references

[Ingster, Sapatinas and Suslina, *Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems*, §4.1, equations (4.4)–(4.8)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1853)

[Marteau and Sapatinas, *A unified treatment for non-asymptotic and asymptotic approaches to minimax signal detection*, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.5387)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The $q=2$ class $\Theta_2(r)$, positive nondecreasing $a_j,\sigma_j$ with $a_j\to\infty$, a finite nonempty active set $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$, positive $A,z_0$, and the profile $\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ satisfying the two displayed constraints.

[F1] [[def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separation]]: $\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$ means $\sum_j a_j^2\sigma_j^2\eta_j^2\le1$ and $\sum_j\sigma_j^2\eta_j^2\ge r^2$, with $(\sigma_j\eta_j)\in\ell^2$.

## Proof

1.1 Since $S$ is finite, $\widetilde\eta$ has finite support. The second constraint in the Given states $\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1$, and the first states $\sum_j\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2$. Thus [F1] gives $\widetilde\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$. [given, F1]

1.2 Fix any $\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$ and put $x_j=\eta_j^2$ and $\widetilde x_j=\widetilde\eta_j^2$. Both series $\sum_j\sigma_j^2x_j$ and $\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^2x_j$ are finite by [F1], so their displayed difference is absolutely convergent. For $j\notin S$, $1-Aa_j^2\le0$; since $x_j\ge0$, $$\sum_{j\in S}\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)x_j=\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)x_j-\sum_{j\notin S}\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)x_j\ge r^2-A,$$ where the first sum is at least $r^2-A$ by [F1]. For the candidate, the same quantity equals $\sum_{j\in S}\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)\widetilde x_j=r^2-A$ by its two active constraints. Multiplying the inequality by $z_0^2$ therefore gives $\sum_j\widetilde x_jx_j\ge\sum_j\widetilde x_j^2$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Expanding the difference of squared $\ell^2$ norms of the nonnegative sequences $x$ and $\widetilde x$ gives $$\sum_j\eta_j^4-\sum_j\widetilde\eta_j^4=\sum_j(x_j-\widetilde x_j)^2+2\sum_j\widetilde x_j(x_j-\widetilde x_j)\ge0$$ by step 1.2. The sums are well-defined: $\sum_jx_j^2\le(\sum_jx_j)^2$ and $\sum_jx_j=\sum_j\eta_j^2<\infty$ by [F1]. This proves minimality. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 If equality holds in the objective, step 2.1 forces $\sum_j(x_j-\widetilde x_j)^2=0$, hence $x_j=\widetilde x_j$ for every $j$. Thus the nonnegative minimizer is unique. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and suppose a product tubular embedding $\Phi:S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\to S^3$ is supplied, where $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:|z|\le r\}$. Define $N=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$, $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N$, $T=\partial E$, and let $i:T\hookrightarrow E$ be inclusion. Fix $s_0\in S^1$ and $z_0\in\partial D^2_\epsilon$. Let $\mu=\Phi(\{s_0\}\times\partial D^2_\epsilon)$ be the fibre meridian and let $\sigma:S^1\to T$ be the product section $s\mapsto\Phi(s,z_0)$. Then $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)$ is infinite cyclic generated by $i_*[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(E;\mathbb Z)$ has a unique generator $[\lambda]$ whose image under the product projection $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$ is $1$, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. The proof uses no choice axiom beyond the supplied tube.

## Statement references

[[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]] — exact sequence for the open cover used below.

[[cor-homology-of-spheres]] — $H_1(S^3;\mathbb Z)=H_2(S^3;\mathbb Z)=0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $K$, the supplied product tube $\Phi$, and the sets and curves in the statement.

[F1] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]: $K$ is a smooth embedding of the oriented circle in the fixed oriented $3$-sphere.

[F2] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]: for an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence $H_1(U\cap V;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(U;\mathbb Z)\oplus H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ is exact.

[F7] [[thm-short-exact-two-open-singular-chain-mayer-vietoris-sequence]]: the chain map from the intersection sends $c$ to $(i_U(c),-i_V(c))$, so the homology map has the same opposite-sign convention.

[F3] [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]: $H_1(S^3;\mathbb Z)=H_2(S^3;\mathbb Z)=0$.

[F4] [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]: the finite product CW structures on $S^1$, $T=S^1\times S^1$, and $S^1\times D^2$ compute their singular homology.

[F5] [[def-cellular-homology]] and [[thm-cellular-boundary-is-the-incidence-degree-matrix]]: cellular groups are free on cells and their differentials are the signed incidence maps.

[F6] [[thm-homotopy-equivalences-induce-isomorphisms-on-singular-homology]]: a deformation retraction induces an isomorphism on singular homology.

## Proof

1.1 Give $S^1$ its one-vertex, one-edge CW structure. By the oriented-knot convention [F1], the core circle has the specified positive orientation used for the section generator. The solid tube $S^1\times D^2$ retracts radially to the core circle, whose cellular boundary is zero, so $H_1(S^1\times D^2;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. The product torus $T=S^1\times S^1$ has one $0$-cell, two $1$-cells and one $2$-cell; the two endpoint incidences cancel in degree $1$, and the attaching commutator of the $2$-cell has total signed incidence zero on each $1$-cell. Thus $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^2$, with basis the fibre class $[\mu]$ and section class $[\sigma]$. The projection to the first $S^1$ sends $[\mu]$ to $0$ and $[\sigma]$ to $1$. [given, F1, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

1.2 Set $U=\Phi(S^1\times\{|z|<3\epsilon/2\})$ and $V=S^3\setminus\Phi(S^1\times D^2_{\epsilon/2})$. They are open and cover $S^3$. Radial contraction in the disk coordinate retracts $U$ to the core circle and $U\cap V$ to $T$. The homotopy $r_t(r)=(1-t)r+t\epsilon$ for $\epsilon/2<r<\epsilon$, fixed for $r\ge\epsilon$, retracts $V$ onto $E$. The intersection map in the Mayer–Vietoris sequence is therefore the map $H_1(T)\to H_1(S^1)\oplus H_1(E)$ given by $x\mapsto(p_*x,-i_*x)$, where $p$ is product projection. [given, F2, F6, F7, construct]

2.1 By exactness and [F3], this intersection map is an isomorphism. Its restriction to $\ker p_*=\mathbb Z[\mu]$ is an isomorphism onto $0\oplus H_1(E)$: injectivity follows from the isomorphism, and any $(0,y)$ has a preimage $x$ with $p_*x=0$. Hence $H_1(E)\cong\mathbb Z$, generated up to sign by $i_*[\mu]$. [F2, F3, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Write $i_*[\sigma]=c\,i_*[\mu]$ for the unique integer $c$, and define $[\lambda]=[\sigma]-c[\mu]$. Then $i_*[\lambda]=0$ and its product projection is $1$. Every class in $\ker i_*$ has the form $a[\mu]+b[\sigma]$ and satisfies $a+bc=0$, so it is exactly $b[\lambda]$; the projection condition forces $b=1$. The change-of-basis matrix from $([\mu],[\sigma])$ to $([\mu],[\lambda])$ has determinant $1$, so the latter pair is a basis. All choices were the supplied finite product data and integer operations; no choice axiom was used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

This calculation is deliberately local to a supplied product tube. It does not use the separate batch-57 theorem whose proof assumes full AC.

## Statement

Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ be a nonempty labeled oriented link in $S^3$,
let $G=\pi_1(E_L)$, and choose one based positive meridian $m_i\in G$ for each
component. For every integer $q\geq1$, the homomorphism from the free group
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ defined by $x_i\mapsto m_i$ induces a
surjection
$$F_r\longrightarrow G/\Gamma_qG.$$

## Statement references

[Milnor, *Link Groups*, §§1–3](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/milnorlink.pdf)

[Stees, §2.5](https://scholarworks.iu.edu/iuswrrest/api/core/bitstreams/54c7d68f-d982-4e1f-9550-e54140ada5ea/content)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The link, its chosen product tubes, and based component meridians.

[F1] The positive component meridians form a basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$. [[lem-string-link-exterior-homology-and-meridian-maps]]

[F2] The degree-one Hurewicz map identifies $G/\Gamma_2G$ with $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F3] The lower-central series is $\Gamma_1G=G$ and $\Gamma_{k+1}G=[G,\Gamma_kG]$. [[def-lower-central-series-and-magnus-expansion-for-links]]

[F4] Commutators add lower-central weights, and their induced pairings on graded quotients are biadditive. [[lem-hall-malcev-lower-central-commutators-add-weights]]

## Proof

**Given:** $G$ and its selected meridians $m_1,\ldots,m_r$.

1.1 Let $H=\langle m_1,\ldots,m_r\rangle$. By [F1] and [F2], the images of these meridians generate $G/\Gamma_2G$, so $G=H\Gamma_2G$. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 For every $k\geq2$, the quotient $\Gamma_kG/\Gamma_{k+1}G$ is generated by iterated commutators of weight $k$ in the selected meridians. For $k=2$, [F4] makes the pairing $G/\Gamma_2\times G/\Gamma_2\to\Gamma_2/\Gamma_3$ biadditive, so [F1] implies this layer is generated by brackets of the $m_i$. If the claim holds at weight $k$, then [F3] writes the next layer as generated by brackets of a degree-one class with a weight-$k$ class; [F4] makes that pairing biadditive, so [F1] again reduces the degree-one entries to the $m_i$, and the induction hypothesis reduces the other entries to brackets of those meridians. Each such iterated commutator is a word in $H$ lying in $\Gamma_{k+1}G$, so its class is in the image of $H\cap\Gamma_{k+1}G$ in the graded layer. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, induction]

2.1 The conclusion of step 1.2 implies $\Gamma_kG\subseteq H\Gamma_{k+1}G$ for every $k\geq2$, because each generator of the graded layer is represented by a word in the $m_i$ that lies in $H$. Starting from $G=H\Gamma_2G$ in step 1.1 and applying these inclusions successively gives $G=H\Gamma_qG$ for every finite $q$. Therefore the image of $H$, and hence of the free group map in the statement, is all of $G/\Gamma_qG$. For $q=1$ the quotient is trivial. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra, induction] ∎

## Statement

Assume the countable-choice Heegaard Floer analytic package. Let $Y$ be any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold and let $\mathbb L$ be an ordered framed $n$-component link in $Y$. On its $i$th exterior boundary torus let $\mu_i$ be the meridian and $\lambda_i$ the chosen framing longitude. Use the three filling slopes $\lambda_i$, $\mu_i+\lambda_i$ and $\mu_i$, labelled $0,1,\infty$, respectively; $\infty$ restores the original unfilled component. For $I\in\{0,1,\infty\}^n$ let $Y(I)$ be the simultaneous filling specified by $I$. Fix an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to these surgeries and the compatible perturbation and top-generator choices used by the polygon construction. The mod-two polygon maps on
$$C(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{I\in\{0,1\}^n}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2)$$
form a differential with components only from $I$ to $J\ge I$ coordinatewise. It preserves the increasing filtration
$$F_pC(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{|I|\ge n-p}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2),$$
extended by zero below zero and by the whole module at and above $n$. Its total homology is isomorphic to $\widehat{HF}(Y(\infty,\ldots,\infty);\mathbb F_2)=\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. For $n=1$, the total complex is the mapping cone of the $0$-to-$1$ surgery map and is quasi-isomorphic to the hat complex of the third, $\infty$ filling; this yields the long exact surgery sequence for every surgery triad, with its cyclic ordering. For $n=0$ the cube is the single hat complex of $Y$. No filtered quasi-isomorphism between distinct surgery presentations is included.

## Statement references

[[def-link-surgery-filtered-complex-for-double-branched-cover|Resolution-cube filtered module]]

[[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations|Disk and polygon regularity, compactness, and gluing obligation]]

[[thm-hat-heegaard-floer-is-a-closed-three-manifold-invariant|Closed-manifold Floer invariance obligation]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, §§2 and 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0309170v1)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §5](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, the ordered framed link, the $0,1,\infty$ filling data $Y(I)$, and the compatible admissible multi-diagram and top-generator choices in the Statement.

[F1] The general $Y$ vertex modules and increasing filtration are the ones explicitly specified in the Statement. The branched-cover module is their later special application, rather than a premise restricting this general surgery statement to $S^3$.

[F2] The actual analytic foundations [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]] supply finite zero-basepoint disk and polygon counts, compact one-dimensional boundaries, exhaustive gluing and the resulting identities on the stated operation-specific admissible data: global weak data for all-sector sums, or the prescribed ordinary weak or strict specified-Spin-c families. Positive-rank triples use explicit small triple-free representatives with transported labels; rank zero uses the point model. This supplies neither a subordinate surgery multidiagram nor a calculation that its distinguished top inputs are cycles or satisfy the required higher sums. It does not identify surgery total homology with a filling.

[F3] The total homology is interpreted as an invariant of the filled manifold only after closed-manifold Heegaard Floer invariance ([[thm-hat-heegaard-floer-is-a-closed-three-manifold-invariant]]).

[F4] **External input — actual surgery data and top sums.** Ozsváth–Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, arXiv:math/0309170v1, §4.2, pp.21–23, equation(10) and Lemma4.5: for an ordered framed link in an arbitrary closed oriented three-manifold, the bouquet-subordinate attaching systems use meridians $\beta_i$, framing curves $\gamma_i$, and meridian-added curves $\delta_i$, with separately labelled Hamiltonian copies for unchanged systems. On the compatible admissible surgery data the distinguished top inputs are cycles and all monotone top-input sums $M_{AB}$ below vanish. This is the imported operation-specific construction/calculation, not a consequence newly deduced from [F2]. Only its mod-two version is used.

[F5] **External input — actual single-coordinate surgery cone.** The same source, Theorem4.7 and its proof, pp.24–27, equation(12), supplies a quasi-isomorphism between the cone of the $0\to1$ two-handle triangle map and the third, meridian filling. Its quadrilateral/top-generator calculation and the cyclic Hamiltonian-copy construction are included in this import; no merely formal null-composition is substituted for that calculation. Its hypotheses are the surgery triad with the subordinate admissible choices above, not an arbitrary pair of chain maps.

[F6] **External input — total-cube filling comparison.** The proof of Theorem4.1, p.27, supplies acyclicity of the enlarged three-valued coordinate complex with its ACTUAL higher polygon entries. It yields the homology comparison with one coordinate filled by $\infty$, and induction gives the all-$\infty$ filling. Theorem4.1 and Remark4.2, p.17, identify the first differential as the sum of immediate two-handle maps and allow flattening by $|I|$. This imports the actual total construction; it does not assert guessed canonical coherent comparison maps between arbitrary presentations.

## Proof

1.1 The cube module and its increasing filtration are fixed by [F1]. The candidate total differential sums over ordered immediate-successor paths and their polygon-count maps, with diagonal disk differential. Each component from $I$ to $J\ge I$ lowers $n-|I|$ to $n-|J|$, so it preserves every increasing filtration subspace whenever the count is defined. Square-zero, count finiteness and identification of total homology still require proof. No filtered comparison between different presentations is a premise of this fixed-data assertion. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 The square-zero substitution has a precise additional finite hypothesis. Denote polygon operations by $\mu_k$ and the chosen immediate top inputs by $\theta_{IJ}$. For $A<B$, form the finite top-input sum
$$M_{AB}=\sum_{A=I_0<\cdots<I_r=B}\mu_r(\theta_{I_0I_1},\ldots,\theta_{I_{r-1}I_r}),$$
where every step changes one coordinate; $\mu_1$ is the differential on a single top input. Suppose the actual surgery data satisfy $M_{AB}=0$ for every such interval, in their actual auxiliary complexes and compatible labels. Expand the component $(D^2)_{IJ}$ as the sum over two consecutive input-containing polygon operations. The boundary identity of [F2], summed over all paths from $I$ to $J$, pairs these with exactly the terms obtained by inserting one $M_{AB}$ among the top inputs of an input-containing polygon. Every consecutive subpath is counted once in this insertion sum, including length-one differential terms. Thus $M_{AB}=0$ implies $D^2=0$. For $I=J$ this is the vertex differential identity. This is a finite substitution in the actual polygon identities; it does not calculate the top-input sums. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 There are only finitely many vertex generators, coordinate paths and required arities. Once the actual admissible subordinate data and top inputs are supplied, [F2] gives finite counts for each term and hence for every differential coefficient. The filtration calculation in step 1.1 then applies literally. In the $n=1$ case, the matrix has diagonal vertex differentials and sole off-diagonal triangle map $f_{01}$; the resulting two-summand complex is its mapping cone with the usual homological shift. This is an actual algebraic identification whenever those data exist, not yet a comparison with the third filling. For $n=0$ it is exactly the given hat complex of $Y$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F4] to the actual surgery data: its top cycles and vanishing $M_{AB}$ supply exactly the extra hypothesis of step1.2. Together with the retained local count identities [F2], steps 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 give an actual finite differential preserving the stated filtration. In particular the branched-cover definition later uses a genuine complex, not just a candidate module. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3]

2.2 For one coordinate, [F5] supplies the actual comparison of this cone with the third filling, so the cone's short exact sequence gives the surgery long exact sequence. The cyclic triad ordering is the one with slope labels $\lambda,\mu+\lambda,\mu$, as fixed in the Statement; the source's Section2, p.6, describes its cyclic symmetry. For zero coordinates the identity complex gives the asserted result. [F5, step 1.3]

2.3 For several coordinates use [F6], rather than composing unspecified vertexwise comparison maps. Filter the enlarged $\{0,1\}^{n-1}\times\{0,1,\infty\}$ complex by the first $n-1$ coordinates. Its successive quotients are the acyclic single-coordinate three-term complexes from [F5], including the quadrilateral entry. A finite filtered complex with acyclic successive quotients is acyclic, by induction through the short exact sequences of filtration pieces. The subcomplex with last coordinate $\infty$ and the quotient with last coordinate $0$ or $1$ therefore have isomorphic homology via the connecting map, with the usual cone shift. Induction identifies the latter cube's total homology with the all-$\infty$ hat homology. The source provides the higher entries of this enlarged complex and their square-zero in [F4], [F5], [F6]; no new canonical comparison map is claimed. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 Closed-manifold invariance [F3] identifies this final group with $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. The construction and every count used here are the imported compatible surgery construction, combined with the retained AComega analytic package. Its geometric data and arities for the fixed link are finite; the cyclic Hamiltonian-copy sequence used in the single-coordinate argument is countable, so the existing countable-choice branch suffices. The source itself does not formulate a choice hierarchy; this accounting uses the retained analytic CC interface and the finite/countable auxiliary selections just specified. No full-AC classification, presentation-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism, or restriction to $S^3$ is introduced. [F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $B$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$. Then the oriented tangent frame bundle of $B$ admits a Spin$^c$ lift.

## Statement references

[[def-given-spin-and-spinc-structures-and-associated-spinor-bundles|Spin-c structures as lifts of the oriented frame bundle]]

[Calegari, *Notes on 4-Manifolds*, §3.2.1, Lemma 3.2](https://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/courses/4manifolds_2018/4_manifolds_notes.pdf)

[Teichner and Vogt, *All 4-Manifolds Have Spin-c Structures*](https://math.berkeley.edu/~teichner/Papers/spin.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC and the compact connected oriented smooth rational homology four-ball $B$ in the statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is the original hypothesis. It covers the finite good-cover and integral cohomology suppliers; no weaker analytic branch is substituted for this topological one.

[F1] [[lem-finite-good-covers-of-compact-smooth-boundary-manifolds-compute-integral-cohomology]] gives a finite nerve homotopy equivalent to $B$ and coefficient-compatible cohomology comparisons, including boundary points.

[F2] [[lem-integral-two-classes-in-four-manifolds-have-surface-representatives-and-characteristic-parity]] proves that every integral degree-two class has a closed oriented embedded surface representative in the interior, and that $w_2(TB)$ evaluates to its normal Euler number modulo two. For a torsion class this integer is zero, by its actual normal Thom class calculation.

[F3] [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]] gives the coefficient-natural exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(B;\mathbb Z),G)\to H^2(B;G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(B;\mathbb Z),G)\to0$. Its last map is evaluation on integral cycles.

[F4] [[lem-spin-c-lifts-exist-iff-w2-has-an-integral-lift]] proves, by actual Spin transition functions and finite-partition cocycles, that an integral lift of $w_2(TB)$ gives a Spin$^c$ lift of the tangent frame bundle. It asserts existence, not an injective classification by determinant classes.

## Proof

1.1 By [F1], $B$ has the homotopy type of a finite simplicial complex. Its integral chain groups are finite free abelian groups. Finite integer row and column operations, using the Euclidean algorithm, give Smith forms for their boundary maps, so each integral homology group is finitely generated. Tensoring these finite matrices with $\mathbb Q$ kills exactly their finite cyclic factors and preserves their free ranks. The assumed vanishing of positive rational homology therefore makes both $H_1(B;\mathbb Z)$ and $H_2(B;\mathbb Z)$ finite torsion groups. No assertion about a choice of infinitely many generators is needed. [A1, F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Every $x\in H_2(B;\mathbb Z)$ is torsion by step 1.1. Apply [F2]: its embedded oriented surface has integer normal Euler number zero. Hence $\langle w_2(TB),\rho_2x\rangle=0$. Thus the evaluation homomorphism of [F3] with $G=\mathbb F_2$ sends $w_2(TB)$ to zero on the entire integral group $H_2(B;\mathbb Z)$. By exactness, $w_2(TB)$ is the image of a class $v\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(B;\mathbb Z),\mathbb F_2)$. This also covers zero $H_2$, without requiring mod-two $H_2$ to vanish. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 **The coefficient lift is onto, including two-torsion.** Write the finite group $H_1(B;\mathbb Z)$ as a finite direct sum of cyclic groups $\mathbb Z/n$. From the free resolution $0\to\mathbb Z\xrightarrow{n}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/n\to0$, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,G)$ gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/n,G)=G/nG$. The coefficient reduction therefore induces the explicit map $\mathbb Z/n\to\mathbb F_2/n\mathbb F_2$. If $n$ is odd its target is zero; if $n$ is even its target is $\mathbb F_2$ and the reduction is onto. Finite direct sums give a surjection $\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(B),\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(B),\mathbb F_2)$. When $H_1=0$, both groups are zero and the same conclusion holds. Choose a preimage $\widetilde v$ of the one class $v$ in step 2.1. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Let $c\in H^2(B;\mathbb Z)$ be the image of $\widetilde v$ under the integral UCT injection. Naturality of [F3] under $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb F_2$ identifies its reduction with the mod-two UCT image of $v$, which is exactly $w_2(TB)$ by step 2.1. Thus $c$ is an actual integral lift. In fact it lies in the finite Ext subgroup; no assertion that distinct such lifts label distinct Spin$^c$ structures is made. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Choose a smooth Riemannian metric by a finite trivializing atlas and a smooth partition, as in the construction of [F1]. Apply [F4] to $B$ with this metric and the integral lift $c$. Its transition-cocycle construction produces the required Spin$^c(4)$ principal bundle and its equivariant map to the oriented tangent frame bundle. This proves the original existence claim. All possible finite cyclic two-primary factors were retained in step 3.1; neither a vanishing mod-two homology assumption nor a determinant-class bijection was used. [A1, F1, F4, step 4.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk and let $X_D$ be its compact exterior. Then $X_D$ is connected, $H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, and $H_i(X_D;\mathbb Z)=0$ for every $i\ge2$.

## Statement references

[[def-smooth-slice-disk-exterior|The disk exterior and positive meridian]]

[Charles Livingston and Swatee Naik, *Introduction to Knot Concordance*, §3.2, pp. 52–55](https://chuck-livingston.github.io/math/Concordance_Book.pdf)

[[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$, its chosen tubular neighborhood $N(D)$, and its exterior $X_D$.

[A1] Full AC is assumed wherever the cover and orientation conventions use the choice axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The tubular neighborhood is $N(D)\cong D^2\times D^2$ and $N(D)\cap X_D\simeq D^2\times S^1\simeq S^1$, whose generator is the positive meridian. [[def-smooth-slice-disk-exterior]]

[F2] Mayer–Vietoris is exact for the collar-thickened decomposition $B^4=N(D)\cup X_D$. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

## Proof

1.1 Both $B^4$ and $N(D)$ are contractible, and $N(D)\cap X_D$ is connected and homotopy equivalent to $S^1$ by [F1]. The reduced degree-zero part of Mayer–Vietoris [F2] therefore gives $\widetilde H_0(X_D;\mathbb Z)=0$, so $X_D$ is connected. [F1, F2, given, A1]

2.1 In degree one, the sequence has $H_2(B^4)=0$, then $H_1(N(D)\cap X_D)\cong\mathbb Z$, then $H_1(N(D))\oplus H_1(X_D)$, then $H_1(B^4)=0$. Since $H_1(N(D))=0$, the inclusion of the overlap induces an isomorphism $H_1(N(D)\cap X_D)\to H_1(X_D)$. Its generator is the positive meridian by [F1]. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For every $i\ge2$, the adjacent groups $H_i(N(D)\cap X_D)$, $H_i(N(D))$, and $H_i(B^4)$ vanish. Exactness of [F2] then forces $H_i(X_D)=0$. This proves the asserted homology in all degrees. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented smooth four-manifold with a Riemannian metric whose intersection form is positive definite, and let $P\to X$ be a principal $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. For the equation $F_A^-=0$ in the stated orientation convention, the moduli space contains an irreducible smooth connection. The conclusion is existence for the given metric and bundle; it does not assert that every connection is irreducible or that the unperturbed moduli space is regular.

## Statement references

[Donaldson, *An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds*, §I.5, citing Taubes Theorem 1.1](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/donaldson.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The given closed-manifold setup fixes $F_A^-=0$ and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. [[def-asd-moduli-fredholm-index-and-lattice-setup]]

[F2] If $P_A=d_A^-(d_A^-)^*$ has a fixed positive spectral gap, $\|F_A\|_2$ is bounded and $\|F_A^-\|_B$ is small, there is an actual smooth self-dual correction $A+a$ on the same bundle, with $\|a\|_4\le C\|F_A^-\|_B$. The scalar kernel is $G\le C(1+d^{-2})$, and the full proof gives $2P_A=\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+s/3-2W^-+\mathcal T(F_A^-)$ and Kato's inequality. [[lem-green-weighted-asd-correction-from-a-uniform-spectral-gap]]

[F3] Hodge identifies ordinary harmonic two-forms with cohomology. Here positive definiteness excludes a nonzero anti-self-dual harmonic form, since its square integral would be negative. Compact Sobolev/Rellich and higher embeddings are available. [[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]] [[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]] [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]

[F4] Chern–Weil represents the integral second Chern class with the stated sign. The top Chern class of a complex bundle is the Euler class of its underlying complex-oriented real bundle; its local zero indices are the relative Thom values. [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]] [[thm-top-chern-class-equals-euler-class-of-the-underlying-real-bundle]] [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]]

[F5] The actual finite smooth triangulation supplies a four-dimensional CW decomposition of $X$. Relative cell obstructions have their cellular coboundary change rule; sphere degree classifies maps $S^3\to S^3$. Cellular approximation gives $\pi_1(S^3)=\pi_2(S^3)=0$. [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]] [[thm-obstruction-theory-for-lifting-through-a-fibration]] [[thm-based-sphere-maps-are-classified-by-geometric-degree]] [[thm-cellular-approximation-for-maps-of-cw-pairs]]

[F6] $H^4(X;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$, evaluated on the orientation class, by closed oriented Poincaré duality. Full AC is used through [F2]–[F6]. [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** Full AC and the metric, bundle and charge of the original sign-fixed closed-manifold problem [F1]. No regularity or orientation theorem is assumed.

1.1 **The actual BPST bundle and almost solution.** Fix $p\in X$ and oriented normal coordinates, with $g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+O(r^2)$. In quaternionic coordinates the regular BPST potential is $I_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(q\,d\bar q)/(\lambda^2+|q|^2)$. Write $q=rv$, $|v|=1$, and $\theta=v\,d\bar v$, so $d\theta=-\theta\wedge\theta$. Differentiation gives $F_{I_\lambda}=\lambda^2(\lambda^2+r^2)^{-2}\operatorname{Im}(dq\wedge d\bar q)$, which is self-dual in the oriented Euclidean metric. Its Euclidean norm square is $48\lambda^4/(\lambda^2+r^2)^4$, with integral $8\pi^2$, and its three curvature components at zero span $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Gauge transformation by $v$ gives the singular potential $\lambda^2(\lambda^2+r^2)^{-1}\bar v\,dv$, bounded by $C\lambda^2/r^3$ when $r\ge\lambda$. Fix a small coordinate radius $\rho$, independent of $\lambda$, cut off this singular potential on $\rho<r<2\rho$ to zero, and use the regular frame inside. The fixed transition $v$ on their overlap constructs one smooth bundle $P'$ independent of $\lambda$ and smooth connections $A_\lambda$ which equal the product connection outside the chart. It is this singular potential that is cut off; a cutoff of a regular potential is not assumed to commute with a gauge transformation. [F1, F2, F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Small error for the given curved metric.** The Hodge projection differs from its Euclidean value by $O(r^2)$ in the inner ball. Thus $E_\lambda=F_{A_\lambda}^-$ satisfies $|E_\lambda|\le C\lambda^2r^2/(\lambda^2+r^2)^2\le C\lambda^2/(\lambda^2+r^2)$ there, and $|E_\lambda|\le C_\rho\lambda^2$ on the fixed cutoff annulus. Direct radial integration gives $\|E_\lambda\|_2\le C\lambda^2\sqrt{1+|\log\lambda|}$ and $\|F_{A_\lambda}\|_2\le\Lambda$ uniformly. For the Green norm use [F2]'s kernel bound. If the pole has $|x|\le2\lambda$, split at radius $4\lambda$; the inner contribution is $O(\lambda^2)$ and the outer shells contribute $C\lambda^2\int_\lambda^{2\rho}dr/r$. If $s=|x|>2\lambda$, split into $|x-y|<s/2$, $|y|<2s$ outside that set, and $|y|\ge2s$. The first integral is at most $C(\lambda^2/s^2)s^2=C\lambda^2$, the second at most $Cs^{-2}\lambda^2\int_0^{2s}r^3/(\lambda^2+r^2)dr\le C\lambda^2$, and the third is bounded by the same logarithmic shell integral. A pole outside the coordinate region only improves the bound, and the fixed annulus contributes $O(\lambda^2)$. The non-singular kernel term is smaller; metric volumes are uniformly comparable. Consequently $\|E_\lambda\|_\sharp\le C\lambda^2(1+|\log\lambda|)$ and $\|E_\lambda\|_B\to0$ in the actual fixed metric. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.2 **The charge of the constructed bundle.** The bundle $P'$ and its transition map in step 1.1 are fixed as $\lambda$ varies. Its Chern–Weil integral is consequently an integer independent of $\lambda$. On the fixed inner ball, the explicit Euclidean self-dual BPST integral tends to $-1$ in the convention $c_2=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$. On the cutoff annulus its curvature is $O_\rho(\lambda^2)$, so its Chern integral tends to zero. The integral is metric independent. Hence $c_2(P')[X]=-1$ exactly. This computes the charge of the actual fixed bundle used by the contraction, not merely that of an abstract model. [F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Uniform spectral gap with no hidden inverse assumption.** From [F2]'s Weitzenböck formula, scalar Sobolev applied to $|\xi|$ using Kato, and $\|E_\lambda\|_2\to0$, absorb $C\|E_\lambda\|_2\|\xi\|_4^2$ to get $\|\nabla_{A_\lambda}\xi\|_2^2\le C(\langle P_{A_\lambda}\xi,\xi\rangle+\|\xi\|_2^2)$. If no uniform positive gap existed as $\lambda\downarrow0$, take $\|\xi_n\|_2=1$ and $\|(d_{A_{\lambda_n}}^-)^*\xi_n\|_2\to0$. The displayed estimate and Kato give a uniform $L^4$ bound, so the $L^2$ mass in every radius-$r$ ball is at most $Cr^2$. In the global singular/product frame away from $p$, $A_{\lambda_n}\to0$ smoothly by step 1.1. Local $H^1$ bounds and Rellich therefore give a strongly locally $L^2$ convergent subsequence to an ordinary adjoint-valued anti-self-dual two-form $\xi$ with $d^*\xi=0$. The small-ball bound shows $\|\xi\|_2=1$, with no lost mass. Lower semicontinuity on each punctured compact set gives a finite ordinary $H^1$ norm off $p$, uniformly as the deleted radius tends to zero. Multiply by cutoffs vanishing near $p$: their error is bounded in $L^2$ by the $L^4$ norm of $\xi$ on a shrinking annulus times the bounded $L^4$ norm of the cutoff gradient, and tends to zero by absolute continuity. Thus $\xi$ extends in $H^1$ with $d^*\xi=0$ globally. Anti-self-duality then gives $d\xi=0$, so [F3] makes it harmonic, contrary to $b_-=0$ and $\|\xi\|_2=1$. Hence a fixed gap $c>0$ exists for all sufficiently small $\lambda$. This was proved before choosing the correction threshold depending on $c$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 **Smooth solutions and actual irreducibility.** Steps 2.1–3.1 satisfy every hypothesis of [F2] for small $\lambda$. It produces smooth self-dual $A_\lambda+a_\lambda$ on the same $P'$, with $\|a_\lambda\|_4\to0$. If arbitrarily small members were reducible, choose unit parallel adjoint sections $u_\lambda$. Pull them back to the scale-$\lambda$ unit ball in the regular frame, where $A_\lambda$ is exactly $I_1$; four-dimensional $L^4$ norms of one-forms are invariant under this scaling and the fixed metric is uniformly comparable. Thus $\|\nabla_{I_1}u_\lambda\|_4\le C\|a_\lambda\|_4\to0$. Since $|u_\lambda|=1$, their ordinary $W^{1,4}$ norms are bounded in that fixed smooth frame. Rellich in $H^1\to L^2$, followed by $\|u_i-u_j\|_4^4\le C\|u_i-u_j\|_2^2$, gives a strongly $L^4$ convergent subsequence. Its limit is an $I_1$-parallel unit section; the first-order equation with smooth coefficients bootstraps it to a smooth section. Commuting derivatives at zero makes its value commute with all three curvature values of $I_1$. Those span $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, whose common centralizer in its Lie algebra is zero, a contradiction. Therefore sufficiently small corrected members are irreducible. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Comparison with the specified bundle.** Use [F5]'s finite smooth triangulation of $X$. An $SU(2)$ bundle is the unit sphere bundle of its defining quaternionic line, since $SU(2)$ acts freely and transitively on its unit vectors. It is trivial on the three-skeleton: the obstruction groups $\pi_0,\pi_1,\pi_2$ of $SU(2)=S^3$ vanish. On each oriented four-cell a three-skeleton trivialization has a boundary unit-vector map $S^3\to S^3$, with integer degree. These degrees form its four-cochain obstruction; changing a three-cell trivialization changes it by that cellular coboundary, by [F5]. Here is the general Chern identification: in the pulled-back trivial bundle over one characteristic four-disk, extend the boundary unit section as a vector-valued map and make it transverse to zero in the interior, retaining its boundary homotopy class. The boundary degree is the sum of its local zero degrees, by excising disjoint small zero-balls and the boundary homology relation. Those local degrees are precisely the relative pullback of the oriented Thom class. Thus this cellular cocycle represents the Euler class of the underlying complex-oriented real four-plane bundle, and equals $c_2$ by [F4]. This is a general relative-cell computation, not an inference from the BPST calibration. For two bundles, the obstruction to extending a three-skeleton isomorphism over a four-cell is the difference of these two degrees; pointwise multiplication of the two boundary $S^3$ maps adds their degrees, by [F5]. By [F6] and step 2.2, $P$ and $P'$ have the same degree-four class. Adjusting the isomorphism on the three-cells kills the difference cochain by its coboundary, and degree classification then extends it over every four-cell. Smooth it as an everywhere nonzero section of the quaternionic homomorphism bundle, using finite smooth charts and a partition of unity, and normalize its quaternionic norm. Uniform approximation preserves nonvanishing; unit quaternionic maps are determinant-one unitary isomorphisms. Transfer the smooth irreducible self-dual connection of step 4.1 through this actual smooth bundle isomorphism to $P$. This proves the full given-metric, given-bundle conclusion. [F1, F4, F5, F6, step 4.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra] ∎

## Source notes

This is the full original existence construction, not a citation of Taubes. Its mathematical working form was independently reviewed in the two-cycle receipt `research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-independent-original-taubes-review-final.json`; the general Euler/cell comparison is included explicitly. The preceding substantial supplier contains the completed Green-weight inverse, fixed point and same-bundle bootstrap. This proof does not consume generic moduli regularity, orientability, a classification of all charge-one spherical instantons, or an inverse small-instanton end theorem. In particular the unused former regularity and index dependencies have been removed.

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold, let $b_1(X)=\dim H^1(X;\mathbb R)$, let $b_-(X)$ be the dimension of the negative subspace of its real intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle. Put $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. For the real Fredholm operator $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$ from first Sobolev one-forms with values in $\operatorname{ad}P$ to zeroth Sobolev zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms, its Fredholm index is $8k-3(1-b_1(X)+b_-(X))$. In particular, if $\pi_1(X)=0$, the intersection form is positive definite, and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$, then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(D_A)=5$.

## Statement references

[Donaldson, *An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds*, §§I.2, II.1](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/donaldson.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the closed connected oriented Riemannian four-manifold and smooth $SU(2)$ bundle. The connection $A$ is smooth. No self-duality of $A$ or Spin structure on $X$ is required for the index calculation.

[A1] Full AC is used through the existing analytic index, Hodge and Chern–Weil theorems, not through a new choice of spin structure. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[F1] A graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection has a chiral Fredholm operator on the exact $H^1\to L^2$ domain, with complex index $\int_X[\widehat A(TX)\operatorname{ch}(V/S)]_4$. Its local multiplicity space has dimension equal to the module rank divided by four in dimension four. The reference chirality is $i^2c(e^1)c(e^2)c(e^3)c(e^4)$. Local multiplicity curvatures and their characters patch even without a global Spin lift. ([[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]], [[def-even-dimensional-spinor-bundle-chirality-and-spin-connection]], [[lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundles-are-well-defined]], [[thm-geometric-clifford-module-dirac-index-formula]])

[F2] On a compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold, every real de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative. De Rham integration identifies wedge products with singular cup products and their oriented evaluation. Thus the real intersection form is represented on harmonic two-forms by $\int_X\alpha\wedge\beta$. ([[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]], [[thm-de-rham-theorem]])

[F3] With the library's connection convention, $c(\nabla)=\det(I-F/(2\pi i))$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\nabla)=\operatorname{tr}\exp(-F/(2\pi i))$. The second Chern form represents the topological second Chern class over the reals. Integration of an exact form on closed $X$ is zero. ([[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]])

## Proof

**Given:** Full AC and the bundle, connection and orientation data in the Statement.

1.1 Construct the required Clifford module explicitly. Put $V_0^+=\Lambda^1T^*X\otimes\mathbb C$ and $V_0^-=(\Lambda^0\oplus\Lambda^-)T^*X\otimes\mathbb C$, with their metric Hermitian forms. For a real covector $\xi$ define $B_\xi a=(-\iota_{\xi^\sharp}a,\sqrt2\,\pi_-(\xi\wedge a))$ and $c(\xi)(a,b)=(-B_\xi^*b,B_\xi a)$ on $V_0^+\oplus V_0^-$. In an oriented orthonormal frame with $\xi=te^1$, the scalar part of $B_\xi a$ has squared norm $t^2|a_1|^2$, while the three forms $\sqrt2\pi_-(e^1\wedge e^j)$, $j=2,3,4$, are orthonormal. Hence $B_\xi^*B_\xi=|\xi|^2I$. Both spaces have dimension four, so for $\xi\ne0$ also $B_\xi B_\xi^*=|\xi|^2I$; the zero case is immediate. Polarization gives the Clifford relation $c(\xi)c(\eta)+c(\eta)c(\xi)=-2\langle\xi,\eta\rangle I$, and the displayed block matrix is skew-Hermitian and odd. Wedge, contraction and $\pi_-$ are parallel for the Levi–Civita connection, so the induced connection is Clifford-compatible. Its chiral Dirac operator is exactly $\widetilde D_0=d^*\oplus\sqrt2d^-$. This is an actual geometric Clifford module, not a postulated Spin factorization. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ and $G=\operatorname{ad}P\otimes\mathbb C$, with their induced unitary connections. The bundle $G$ is the trace-zero endomorphism bundle of $E$. Set $Z=-F_E/(2\pi i)$, a traceless two-by-two matrix of commuting two-forms. The determinant convention gives $c_2(E)=-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(Z^2)$ as a form. For a traceless diagonal matrix with entries $u,-u$, its commutator action on trace-zero endomorphisms has eigenvalues $0,2u,-2u$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}Z)=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{ad}Z)^2)=4\operatorname{tr}(Z^2)$. These are polynomial identities for all traceless complex matrices: matrices with distinct eigenvalues are dense, and continuity gives the rest. Polarizing the degree-two identity gives the same identity for matrices of two-forms. It follows, through degree four, that $\operatorname{ch}(G)=3-4c_2(E)$, with no degree-two term. This fixes the factor and sign directly from the stated Chern normalization. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Fix its chirality sign and multiplicity. Write $c_j=c(e^j)$. Applying $c_4c_3c_2c_1$ to $e^1\in V_0^+$ gives successively $(-1,0)$, $-e^2$, $(0,(e^{23}-e^{14})/\sqrt2)$, and $-e^1$. Reversal of four distinct generators has positive sign, so $c_1c_2c_3c_4e^1=-e^1$. The construction is $SO(4)$-equivariant, and oriented rotations carry $e^1$ to every unit one-form; therefore $-c_1c_2c_3c_4=I$ on $V_0^+$. This volume operator anticommutes with every $c_j$; since $c_1$ identifies the two summands, it is $-I$ on $V_0^-$. Thus the given grading IS the reference chirality $i^2c_1c_2c_3c_4$. In the local factorization in [F1], $\Gamma_{V_0}=\Gamma_S\otimes\Gamma_W$ consequently forces $\Gamma_W=I$. The local multiplicity has rank $8/4=2$ and is entirely even. If $\Theta=\operatorname{ch}(V_0/S)$, then $\Theta_0=2$. This conclusion patches without choosing a global spinor bundle. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.2 Calibrate the untwisted index by harmonic forms, rather than import an Euler/signature index formula. On a closed manifold, $\int_Xda\wedge da=\int_Xd(a\wedge da)=0$. Since $\alpha\wedge\alpha=(|\alpha^+|^2-|\alpha^-|^2)d\mathrm{vol}$ for real two-forms, polarization and complexification give $2\|d^-a\|_2^2=\|da\|_2^2$. Hence the smooth kernel of $\widetilde D_0$ is exactly the harmonic one-forms. Its formal adjoint is $(f,\omega)\mapsto df+\sqrt2d^*\omega$, with $\omega$ anti-self-dual. Pairing this equation with $df$ gives $\|df\|_2^2=0$, because $\langle d^*\omega,df\rangle=\langle\omega,d(df)\rangle=0$. Thus $f$ is constant and $d^*\omega=0$. For an anti-self-dual two-form the latter is equivalent to $d\omega=0$, so $\omega$ is harmonic. The Dirac regularity in [F1] identifies the Hilbert kernel and cokernel with these smooth spaces. On harmonic two-forms the Hodge star preserves the space and splits the intersection form into positive and negative definite summands: its value on $\omega^++\omega^-$ is $\|\omega^+\|_2^2-\|\omega^-\|_2^2$. By [F2] their negative dimension is precisely $b_-(X)$. Consequently $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_0=b_1(X)-1-b_-(X)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Twist the actual module of step1.1 by $G$, with the product connection. On its local multiplicity factor the curvature is $F^{V_0/S}\otimes I+I\otimes F_G$, and the two factors commute. The finite exponential and tensor-trace identities therefore give $\operatorname{ch}((V_0\otimes G)/S)=\Theta\operatorname{ch}(G)$. The identities are invariant under the local multiplicity transitions in [F1], so they are global form identities, requiring no Spin structure. Applying the actual analytic index theorem to the twisted and untwisted modules yields $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_A=3\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_0-4\int_X\widehat A_0\Theta_0c_2(E)$. Here $\widetilde D_A=d_A^*\oplus\sqrt2d_A^-$, $\widehat A_0=1$, and $\Theta_0=2$ by step2.1. Using [F3] to evaluate the Chern form gives $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_A=3(b_1-1-b_-)-8\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. No assertion that $d_A^2=0$ was used: the Clifford operator and its index calculation apply to every smooth connection. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Multiplication of the target summand $\Lambda^-\otimes\operatorname{ad}P$ by $\sqrt2$ is a bounded invertible map on $L^2$, so $\widetilde D_A$ and $D_A$ have the same kernel and isomorphic cokernels on their exact first-Sobolev domains. The complex operator just computed is the complexification of the real one. If a complexified equation holds, its real and imaginary parts satisfy the real equation; hence its kernel is the complexification of the real kernel, and the same holds for the orthogonal cokernel using the adjoint. Finite complex dimensions of these spaces equal the corresponding real dimensions. Closed range transfers to the real operator by restricting the complex estimate, or by taking real parts of convergent-image preimages in the kernel complement. Thus $D_A:H^1\to L^2$ is real Fredholm and has index $8k-3(1-b_1+b_-)$, with $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. This is not a claim about a KO-index theorem. [F1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 If $\pi_1(X)=0$, every closed real one-form is exact: define a primitive by path integration from a basepoint; nullhomotopy and local primitives make the integral independent of path. Thus $b_1=0$ by [F2]. Positive definiteness gives $b_-=0$, and the prescribed charge is $k=1$. The proved formula gives $8-3=5$. Full AC has entered exactly through [F1]–[F3]'s analytic index, harmonic representatives and characteristic-class comparison; the finite symbol, chirality, trace and sign calculations add no choice. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. For every closed oriented 3-manifold M there exists a finite constant C_M such that for every discrete group Γ and every homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→Γ for which the rho invariant is defined, |ρ(M,φ)|≤C_M. The constant may depend on M but not on Γ or φ.

## Statement references

[Cheeger–Gromov, §4](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/cheegergr.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC as in the coefficient Definition and a fixed closed oriented three-manifold $M$. First give $M$ a specified smooth structure and interpret rho by its independent smooth bounding defect.

[A1] Full AC is the standing coefficient convention. [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A rho invariant is called such only after bounding-defect independence is proved. [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

[F2] The smooth group-signature theorem constructs one fixed smooth bound $W_M$ over an acyclic envelope of $\pi_1M$ and proves smooth defect independence for all representations and injective target enlargements. It also constructs a fixed finite-projective chain model and an idempotent presentation $E_2=eR^N$ for that bound. [[thm-smooth-group-signature-defects-are-independent-and-uniformly-bounded]]

[F3] **External TOP input under CLAUDE.md §12:** every closed oriented TOP three-manifold admits a compatible smooth structure, and comparison of its collared TOP bounds with smooth bounds uses the closed TOP signature equality. The first input is [Freedman–Quinn, *Topology of4-Manifolds*,8.3A–B, printed118–119](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400861064), used only for the three-dimensional boundary; the second is [Lück–Schick, Theorem0.2 and §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209161v3). The supplied-data defect comparison is proved in [[lem-l2-rho-invariant-bordism-independence]]. These external inputs are not described as locally reconstructed smoothing or index proofs.

## Proof

1.1 For smooth $M$, choose the one $W_M$ and degree-two presentation in [F2] before choosing a target or representation. For each $\phi:\pi_1M\to\Gamma$, functoriality of the acyclic envelope extends the representation over this same bound after the injective enlargement $\Gamma\hookrightarrow A(\Gamma)$. The actual coefficient chain-homotopy identities extend under the resulting ring homomorphism, so they still model its singular complex; no flatness of that homomorphism is needed. The extended degree-two term is the range of the same size-$N$ idempotent, of von Neumann dimension at most $N$. Its reduced homology and the positive and negative spectral subspaces have dimension at most $N$, hence $|\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_{A(\Gamma)}W_M|\le N$. Ordinary augmentation gives $|\operatorname{sign}W_M|\le N$ too. Independence in [F2] therefore yields $|\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)|\le2N$, uniformly over every target cardinality and every homomorphism, including nononto maps. For finitely many components sum these constants; the empty manifold has constant zero. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 For the literal TOP reading choose one compatible smooth structure on $M$ by [F3], once before choosing $\Gamma$ or $\phi$. Step1.1 supplies its finite constant $2N$. Any rho defined by a collared TOP bound agrees with the smooth bounding-defect value by [F3] and the bordism-independence lemma; thus the same constant bounds it. Finitely many connected components use the sum of their constants. This proves the full stated signature-defect convention with an explicitly external TOP comparison. It does not claim a new analytic eta-to-defect theorem for an unrelated definition of rho. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra] ∎
