## Statement

Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding n. If P(U) is smoothly slice in an R_n-homology 4-ball, then P is weakly injective on C^{1/n}, meaning P(K)=P(U) implies K=U in that category. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then P is weakly injective on C_ex (respectively C_top). In ordinary smooth concordance, if P(U) is smoothly slice in standard B⁴ and P has strong winding number ±1, then P is weakly injective on C_sm provided the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture holds.

For any pattern P and knots K,J with P(K)=P(J) in one of these concordance groups, the connected-sum reduction constructs a pattern R for which R(−K#J) is concordant to U, whose closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K) is ribbon, and whose winding w(R)=w(P). If P is strong winding ±1, then R is strong winding ±1. This reduction turns injectivity of P into weak injectivity of R; it does not assert that P itself is weakly injective without the closure hypotheses above.

## Statement references

[[lem-satellite-operator-preserves-concordance|Concordance preservation for the satellite function]]

[[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus|Smooth and locally flat topological slice disks]]

[CDR, Proposition 3.2 and Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.5058v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A pattern P, knots K,J, and the exact category and closure-slice hypotheses stated above.

[F1] The solid-torus meridian is strong winding when it normally generates the closure-complement group ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

[F2] The zero-surgery comparison has a smooth R_n branch and category-specific exotic/topological branches with their closure hypotheses ([[lem-cdr-zero-surgery-pattern-homology-cobordism]]).

[F3] The definitions of C_ex, C_top and C^{1/n} specify the ambient 4-manifold and coefficient conditions ([[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]).

[F4] Only finite connected-sum, inverse and compatibility instances for the actual supplied knots and concordances are used here. Their choice-free compact-input specialization is established in step0.1. The general AC_omega group theorem records the same operations ([[thm-cdr-concordance-categories-form-abelian-groups]]); its stronger choice premise is not invoked in $V$ for this unqualified Statement.

[F5] The ordinary smooth branch uses the special smooth S⁴-complement assertion ([[lem-cdr-smooth-s4-complement-is-standard-ball]]).

[F6] Satellite insertion rewrites P(K#J) as P_K(J) for the simultaneous companion-insertion pattern P_K ([[lem-satellite-connected-sum-substitution]]).

[F7] The satellite rule descends to the specified concordance classes only after concordance preservation ([[lem-satellite-operator-preserves-concordance]]).

[F8] A concordance annulus with a compatible zero-framed normal neighborhood gives a zero-surgery cobordism ([[lem-concordance-annulus-induces-zero-surgery-cobordism]]).

[F9] Strong winding survives companion insertion and local connected sum ([[lem-strong-winding-stable-under-companion-insertion]]).

[F10] The reverse-mirror connected sum −J#J bounds a ribbon disk ([[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]]).

[F11] **External TOP input.** A compact contractible topological four-manifold with boundary homeomorphic to the standard $S^3$ is homeomorphic to $B^4$. This is the Freedman consequence invoked explicitly in Cochran–Davis–Ray, Proposition3.2 and its proof, printed7–8; it is imported, not locally reconstructed. A supplied boundary marking is respected: if $h:B\to B^4$ is any such homeomorphism and $k:\partial B\to S^3$ is the required marking, extend $k\circ(h|_{\partial B})^{-1}$ radially over $B^4$ by the Alexander extension and postcompose $h$. Thus the co-core boundary knot retains its actual endpoint marking. This fact applies to the underlying TOP manifold of a smooth contractible $B$ as well; it asserts no smooth standardness. The cited application in CDR printed7–8 was read directly; the original Freedman paper is cited as its authoritative source, not claimed read in full here.

[F12] **External remaining concordance input.** Zero-framed surgery on a concordance annulus descends to a homology cobordism of the zero-surgery manifolds in the same category; the coefficient ring is $R_n$ for localized concordance, and in the TOP/exotic categories the fundamental group is normally generated by either boundary knot-group image. The meridians are the normal-circle factors along the framed annulus and are identified by its product coordinate. This is the zero-surgery descent in CDR Section3, printed7, paragraph preceding Definition3.1 and diagram3.1, read directly. The local normal-GIVEN construction [F8] is retained; this explicit external input supplies its needed conclusion where an unresolved general annulus-neighborhood/descent interface would otherwise be required. No local reconstruction of that missing interface is asserted.

[F13] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. This uses the peer-checked compact annulus coding pattern of the standard connected-sum compatibility supplier only at its geometric scope; it does not assert that arbitrary homology or fundamental-group hypotheses are absolute.

## Proof

0.1 Apply [F13] to the finite compact input for the branch at hand. For TOP the ambient product or ball is already standard; for the exotic branch its actual marked product/ball homeomorphism is given and is encoded in both directions. Use two coding passes. First encode only this finite compact geometry by a real $r_0$. In $L[r_0]$, before imposing any localized homology or strong-winding condition, use the ordinary finite smooth Morse construction to obtain finite handle/CW presentations of the supplied smooth ambient manifolds and finite presentations of the relevant knot exteriors, with their comparison maps, homotopies and peripheral markings. Export these purely geometric presentations and compact comparison certificates by [F13]. No choice-free generic-Morse theorem in $V$ is being assumed. Now work in $V$: its given localized homology hypothesis applies to these actual exported presentations. Over the PID $R_n$, the augmented finite free chain complex for an $R_n$-acyclic ball, or the mapping cone for either boundary inclusion, has a finite matrix contracting homotopy; finite row/column reduction supplies it. Likewise, the given strong-winding condition supplies, for each generator in the finite closure-knot presentation, an actual finite word expressing it as a product of conjugates of the designated axis meridian. There are only finitely many such generators and certificates, so choosing this list needs only finite choice. Enlarge $r_0$ to one real $r$ containing the presentations, their actual comparison certificates, these input group words and the finite contraction matrices. Their displayed equations $dh+hd=1$ and word identities are arithmetic, and establish the exact input homology and strong-winding hypotheses inside $L[r]$. No raw homology or fundamental-group absoluteness is asserted. In that model apply the unconditional CDR weak geometry, including [F11], [F12] and the finite connected-sum identities needed in [F4]. Export the resulting compact manifolds, disks, homeomorphisms and finite homology certificates using [F13]. Both stages carry finite normal-generation certificates: the input axis words just described accompany the final CDR call, and the output cobordisms are exported with explicit words expressing each generator in their finite presentations as a product of conjugates of the designated boundary generators. These are actual finite witnesses in $V$. The only ambient hypotheses in these applications are the actual coded ones, and no family of annuli or arbitrary points is selected. In the ordinary smooth branch export only the unconditionally constructed contractible smooth $B$ and its marked co-core; do not assume the ambient smooth Poincare hypothesis in $L[r]$. After decoding in $V$, cap the actual $B$ there, and only then use the supplied smooth Poincare hypothesis in step2.3. [F2, F3, F4, F11, F12, F13, given, construct, algebra]


1.1 Suppose P(K)=P(U), with the stated closure-slice hypothesis. By [F7] this equality is witnessed by a concordance annulus; the zero-surgery descent [F12], with the retained normal-GIVEN construction [F8], gives a meridian-preserving homology cobordism from M(P(K)) to M(P(U)). Applying [F2] to K and U gives cobordisms from M(P(K)) to M(K) and from M(P(U)) to M(U). On each pattern cobordism its marked first-homology relation is [mu_companion]=n[mu_satellite], where n is a unit in R_n; the concordance cobordism from [F8] identifies the two satellite meridian classes exactly. No equality of the pattern and companion preferred meridians is assumed. [F2, F7, F8, F12, step 0.1, given]

1.2 Glue the cobordisms along the identified surgery manifolds. Mayer–Vietoris shows that the resulting boundary inclusions retain the required homology isomorphisms. In the exotic/topological branches, van Kampen shows the boundary normal-generation condition is preserved under this gluing. Hence M(K) and M(U) satisfy the corresponding surgery-cobordism relation. In the localized branch each endpoint meridian maps to a unit multiple of the same H_1 generator: compose the two winding-unit relations and the intervening exact concordance relation. In particular each endpoint meridian, including that of K, remains an R_n-module generator. In the strong-winding branches n=+1 or -1, so these multipliers are already integral units. [F2, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 In the localized category, cap the M(U)=S¹×S² end with S¹×B³. Mayer–Vietoris gives an R_n-homology circle X with boundary M(K), and its meridian class is an R_n-module generator by step1.2. Attach a smooth 2-handle along that meridian with the surgery-dual zero framing. The relative pair (B,X) has only H_2(B,X;R_n)=R_n, generated by its core; its boundary map to H_1(X;R_n)=R_n is the meridian class, hence multiplication by a unit and an isomorphism. The pair sequence gives H_i(B;R_n)=0 for all i>0 and H_0(B;R_n)=R_n. The boundary handle description is the zero-surgery presentation for K together with its zero-framed meridian; this dual meridian surgery restores S³, and the 2-handle co-core has boundary K under that identification. Thus the resulting B is an R_n-homology ball containing the required smooth proper disk, proving K=U in C^{1/n}. Only a unit meridian multiplier was used, so the corrected [F2] supplies exactly the needed premise. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 In the exotic and topological categories, the normal-generation condition makes the capped manifold after the meridian 2-handle contractible with boundary S³. The external input [F11] identifies this manifold with the boundary-marked topological $B^4$. Its co-core is smooth in the exotic branch and locally flat in the TOP branch, and its boundary is the original marked $K$. It therefore gives a pseudo-slice disk or a TOP slice disk respectively, proving $K=U$ in the required category. [F3, F11, step 0.1, step 1.2, construct]

2.3 In the ordinary smooth branch, work now in the ambient universe $V$: if P(U) is smoothly slice and P has strong winding ±1, the same cap and handle construction gives a contractible smooth 4-manifold B with boundary S³. Capping B with standard B⁴ gives a smooth homotopy S⁴; under the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture and [F5], B is diffeomorphic to B⁴. [F1, F5, step 0.1, step 1.2, step 2.2]

3.1 Now suppose P(K)=P(J). By [F6], the connected-sum identity and the ribbon inverse give $P(J)=P_K(-K\#J)$ as concordance classes. Define R as the local connected sum of −P(K) with P_K. Then R(−K#J) is concordant to U because K#(−K#J) is concordant to J and satellites preserve concordance; moreover R(U)=−P(K)#P(K). By [F10], this closure is ribbon; [F6] gives w(R)=w(P). [F4, F6, F7, F10, given, algebra]

3.2 If P has strong winding ±1, [F9] implies R also has strong winding ±1. The closure R(U) supplies the localized slice, pseudo-slice, topological-slice, and standard smooth-slice hypotheses in their respective branches. Apply the applicable earlier weak-injectivity branch to R to obtain $-K\#J=U$ and hence $K=J$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F9, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, and let $q\ge2$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module with the positive-meridian deck action $t$. Then, as abelian groups,
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong A_K/(t^q-1)A_K.
$$

## Statement references

[[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot|The meridian-mod-$q$ exterior cover and filling that define $\Sigma_q(K)$]]

[[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link|The infinite cyclic cover and positive-meridian deck action]]

[[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary|The compact exterior is a deformation retract of the open complement]]

[[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization|First homology is the fundamental group abelianization]]

[[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology|Homology exactness for the filling]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a smooth oriented knot $K$, its chosen exterior $E_K$, positive meridian $\mu$, and an integer $q\ge2$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The connected cover $E_q\to E_K$ is classified by the positive-meridian homomorphism modulo $q$; its filling kills the closed lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F2] The inclusion $E_K\hookrightarrow X_K$ is a strong deformation retraction equivalence and carries the positive meridian to the positive meridian. [[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary]]

[F3] The module $A_K$ is $H_1$ of the connected infinite cyclic cover of $X_K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F4] For a path-connected space, the first Hurewicz map identifies $H_1$ with the abelianization of its fundamental group. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F5] Connected covers of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base are classified by subgroups of its fundamental group. [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]

[F6] Mayer–Vietoris is exact for an open cover, and a deformation retraction induces an isomorphism on singular homology. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]], [[prop-singular-homology-is-invariant-under-deformation-retracts]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the Statement and Facts & Assumptions. Choose a basepoint on $T_K$ and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$, with $s\in G$ the based positive meridian loop. Write $\phi:G\to\mathbb Z$ for the homomorphism with $\phi(s)=1$, and put $N=\ker\phi$.

1.1 By [F2], inclusion of the compact exterior into the open complement induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups and identifies the positive meridian classes. The total-linking homomorphism in [F3] therefore corresponds to $\phi$; by [F4], $A_K$ is isomorphic to $N^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with the action induced by conjugation by a positive meridian, up to replacing that action by its inverse according to the left-versus-right lift convention. [A1, F2, F3, F4, given]

2.1 Put $G_q=\ker(\phi\bmod q)$. For $g\in G_q$, write $\phi(g)=qk$ and set $n=g s^{-qk}\in N$. Then $g=n s^{qk}$, and the expression is unique because $\phi(s^{qk})=qk$. Thus $G_q$ is the split extension of $N$ by the infinite cyclic group generated by $s^q$, acting on $N$ by conjugation. By [F5] and [F1], $G_q$ is the fundamental group of $E_q$. [F1, F5, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Abelianizing this split extension kills the commutators in $N$ and the relations $s^qns^{-q}=n$ for $n\in N$. By [F3], those relations impose $(t^q-1)A_K=0$ on $N^{\mathrm{ab}}$; if the inverse deck convention is used, $t^{-q}-1=-t^{-q}(t^q-1)$ generates the same submodule. The homomorphism $G_q\to\mathbb Z$, $g\mapsto\phi(g)/q$, splits by $1\mapsto s^q$, so $H_1(E_q;\mathbb Z)\cong A_K/(t^q-1)A_K\oplus\mathbb Z[s^q]$. [F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The boundary of $E_q$ is a torus cover with basis the lift $\widetilde\mu$ of $\mu^q$ and a lifted longitude. Thicken $E_q$ and the filling solid torus by collars to form an open cover. By [F6], its Mayer–Vietoris map presents $H_1(\Sigma_q(K))$ as $H_1(E_q)$ modulo $[\widetilde\mu]$: the longitude lift maps to the core generator of the attached solid torus and eliminates that generator, while the filling meridian maps to zero there. The class $[\widetilde\mu]$ is $[s^q]$, the generator of the displayed free summand in step 3.1. Quotienting by it gives the stated isomorphism. [F1, F6, step 3.1, construct] ∎

## Remarks

The quotient by $t^q-1$ is unchanged if the positive deck action is represented by its inverse, since $t^{-q}-1$ differs from $t^q-1$ by the unit $-t^{-q}$.

The group extension and filling relation are shown below. The proof uses the element calculation in steps 2.1–4.1, not the diagram.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}
1 \arrow[r] & N \arrow[r,hook] \arrow[d,equal] & G_q \arrow[r,"\phi/q"] \arrow[d,hook] & \mathbb Z \arrow[r] \arrow[d,"k\mapsto qk"] & 1 \\
1 \arrow[r] & N \arrow[r,hook] & G \arrow[r,"\phi"] & \mathbb Z \arrow[r] & 1
\end{tikzcd}
```

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

All positive $z$ multiplicities are included. ([[thm-balanced-knot-data-admit-full-marked-square-zero-holomorphic-counts]])

[F2] For THE path constructed in [F1], the full-marked compactification theorem gives an actual compact one-manifold for each pair of generators and pair of nonnegative marked vectors. Its finite boundary consists EXACTLY of broken rigid pairs and the unit boundary disks attached to a constant generator. All have actual exhaustive one-sided gluing collars. Its proof first uses actual bounded-energy bubble extraction and index additivity and then the nonpositive-index exclusion to check limiting-strip regularity; it excludes the singly pointed sphere alternative by the actual sphere avoidance. **Given:** Countable Choice and the admissible balanced pointed $S^3$ knot diagram in the Statement.

Each index-one solution is nonconstant, since a constant transverse generator has index zero. Its actual linearization is onto by [F1]. The globally finite list of actual rigid orbits in [F1] in particular makes every specified class's translation quotient finite, including the empty quotient. This uses the full-marked construction, not the zero-$z$ associated-graded branch. Every actual index-two strip is regular as well, so its translation quotient has the indicated one-dimensional interval charts. [F1, A1, given, construct]

2.1 Verify the original PER-WHITNEY-CLASS compactification. Fix an index-two class $\phi$ and its endpoints. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be one of the full-space, Dirichlet, or Neumann TV functionals. Assume that $R$ is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively one-homogeneous, and that $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-$R$ exact solution of $Au=f$ with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Define $K:=\{p\in Y:A^*p\in\partial R(0)\}$ and $D_{\alpha,w}(p):=\langle f+w,p\rangle_Y-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p\|_Y^2$ for $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$.

For each $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$, $D_{\alpha,w}$ has a unique maximizer $p_{\alpha,w}=\operatorname{Proj}_K((f+w)/\alpha)$. If $u_{\alpha,w}$ is any supplied global minimizer of $u\mapsto\frac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)$, then $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(u_{\alpha,w})$, and $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(0)$. For every such supplied minimizer, the correctly normalized primal-dual value identity is

$$\min_u\{\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)\}=\alpha D_{\alpha,w}(p_{\alpha,w}).$$

Let $P_0:=\{p\in K:\langle f,p\rangle_Y=R(u^\dagger)\}$ and let $p_0$ be its unique minimum-norm element. For every sequence $\alpha_n>0$ with $\alpha_n\to0$, $p_{\alpha_n,0}\to p_0$ strongly in $Y$ and $A^*p_{\alpha_n,0}\to A^*p_0$ strongly in $X$. For every $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$,

$$\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\frac{\|w\|_Y}{\alpha},\qquad \|A^*p_{\alpha,w}-A^*p_{\alpha,0}\|_X\le\frac{\|A^*\|\,\|w\|_Y}{\alpha}.$$

Moreover, for any $R_0>R(u^\dagger)$ the certificate yields a variational source condition on $\{u:R(u)\le R_0\}$ with exponent $2$, coefficient $\beta=0$, and index function $\psi(s)=(1+\|p^\dagger\|_Y)\sqrt{s}$. Consequently, if $\delta_n\downarrow0$, $\|w_n\|_Y\le\delta_n$, $\alpha_n\asymp\delta_n$, and exact global minimizers $u_n$ are supplied, then the variational-source rate theorem gives

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u_n,u^\dagger)=O(\delta_n),\qquad \|Au_n-(f+w_n)\|_Y=O(\delta_n).$$

## Statement references

[[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate|The classical TV source condition and certificate.]]

[[def-ip-variational-source-condition|The general variational source inequality.]]

[[thm-ip-vsc-nonlinear-regularization-rate|The Bregman and residual rates under parameter coupling.]]

[Iglesias, Mercier, and Scherzer, *A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems*, Theorem 1 and Proposition 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.06495)

[Inspected historical citation: Borwein and Vanderwerff, *Convex Functions: Constructions, Characterizations and Counterexamples*, Exercise 4.4.1; it concerns convex-conjugate examples and is not used in this proof.](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/CUP/cup-final.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the real Hilbert spaces and map in the Statement, a minimum-TV exact solution, a dual source certificate, and (where specified) supplied global minimizers.

[A1] Countable Choice supplies the nearest-point minimizing sequences and weakly convergent subsequences used below. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: $u^\dagger$ is an exact minimum-TV solution and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$; the Hilbert adjoint satisfies $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$.

[F2] [[def-ip-banach-convex-subgradient-and-dual-pairing]]: $\xi\in\partial R(u)$ exactly when $R(z)\ge R(u)+\langle\xi,z-u\rangle$ for every $z\in X$.

[F3] [[def-ip-bregman-distance]]: $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger)=R(u)-R(u^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X$.

[F4] [[lem-ip-banach-fenchel-duality-for-regularization]]: $R(u)+R^*(\xi)=\langle\xi,u\rangle$ if and only if $\xi\in\partial R(u)$.

[F5] [[def-ip-variational-source-condition]]: on a named sublevel, $-\langle\xi^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger)+\psi(\|Au-Au^\dagger\|_Y^2)$.

[F6] [[thm-ip-vsc-nonlinear-regularization-rate]]: when the exact global minimizer, noise bound, sublevel VSC, and conjugate parameter coupling hold, the Bregman distance and noisy residual have the displayed rates.

[F7] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$ in a real Hilbert space.

[F8] [[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]: every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence.

[F9] [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]: every bounded linear functional on a real Hilbert space is inner product with a vector in that space.

[F10] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: the real Hilbert norm satisfies $\|y\|_Y^2=\langle y,y\rangle_Y$.

## Proof

1.1 Put $q^\dagger=A^*p^\dagger$. Applying [F2] at $u^\dagger$ with $z=0$ and $z=2u^\dagger$, and using $R(0)=0$ and $R(2u^\dagger)=2R(u^\dagger)$, gives $\langle q^\dagger,u^\dagger\rangle_X=R(u^\dagger)$. For arbitrary $z\in X$, [F2] then yields $R(z)\ge\langle q^\dagger,z\rangle_X$, so $q^\dagger\in\partial R(0)$ and $p^\dagger\in K$. Every $p\in K$ satisfies $\langle f,p\rangle_Y=\langle u^\dagger,A^*p\rangle_X\le R(u^\dagger)$; equality holds for $p^\dagger$. Thus $P_0$ is nonempty, closed, and convex. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 The set $K$ is nonempty because $0\in\partial R(0)$, convex by the subgradient inequality, and closed because $\partial R(0)=\{q:R(z)\ge\langle q,z\rangle_X\text{ for all }z\}$ is an intersection of closed half-spaces and $A^*$ is continuous. For any nonempty closed convex subset $C$ of a Hilbert space, let $d=\inf_{c\in C}\|x-c\|$ and use Countable Choice to select $c_n\in C$ with $\|x-c_n\|^2\le d^2+1/n$. The midpoint belongs to $C$, so the parallelogram identity gives $\|c_n-c_m\|^2\le2/n+2/m$; thus $(c_n)$ is Cauchy. Completeness and closedness yield a nearest point, and strict convexity of squared norm makes it unique. Applying this to $K$ and $P_0$ defines their projections. [A1, F2, given, construct]

2.1 Completing the square gives $D_{\alpha,w}(p)=\frac{\|f+w\|_Y^2}{2\alpha}-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p-(f+w)/\alpha\|_Y^2$. Hence its unique maximizer on $K$ is $p_{\alpha,w}=\operatorname{Proj}_K((f+w)/\alpha)$. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 Let $u_{\alpha,w}$ be a supplied global minimizer and put $p=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$. For any $h\in X$ and $t>0$, objective minimality and expansion of the square give $[R(u_{\alpha,w}+th)-R(u_{\alpha,w})]/t\ge\langle A^*p,h\rangle_X-t\|Ah\|_Y^2/(2\alpha)$. As $t\downarrow0$, the lower limit of these secants is at least $\langle A^*p,h\rangle_X$; convexity makes the unit secant at least every smaller positive secant, so $R(u_{\alpha,w}+h)-R(u_{\alpha,w})\ge\langle A^*p,h\rangle_X$. This for every $h$ proves $A^*p\in\partial R(u_{\alpha,w})$. Applying [F2] with $z=0$ and $z=2u_{\alpha,w}$ gives $\langle A^*p,u_{\alpha,w}\rangle_X=R(u_{\alpha,w})$, and then [F2] for arbitrary $z$ gives $A^*p\in\partial R(0)$, so $p\in K$. By [F4] at $0$, $R^*(A^*q)=0$ for every $q\in K$; Fenchel–Young in [F4] therefore gives $\langle A^*q,u_{\alpha,w}\rangle_X\le R(u_{\alpha,w})$. Thus $D_{\alpha,w}(q)\le R(u_{\alpha,w})+\alpha\langle p,q\rangle_Y-\alpha\|q\|_Y^2/2=D_{\alpha,w}(p)-\alpha\|q-p\|_Y^2/2$. Hence $p=p_{\alpha,w}$. Finally $Au_{\alpha,w}=f+w-\alpha p$, so $\frac12\|Au_{\alpha,w}-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u_{\alpha,w})=\alpha D_{\alpha,w}(p)$, establishing the normalized value identity in the Statement. [F2, F4, step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 If $P_Kx=p$ and $P_Ky=q$, minimizing squared distance along the segment from $p$ to any $z\in K$ gives $\langle x-p,z-p\rangle\le0$. Apply this with $z=q$, and the corresponding inequality for $P_Ky$ with $z=p$. Adding yields $\|p-q\|_Y^2\le\langle x-y,p-q\rangle_Y\le\|x-y\|_Y\|p-q\|_Y$ by [F7], so $\|p-q\|_Y\le\|x-y\|_Y$. Taking $x=(f+w)/\alpha$ and $y=f/\alpha$ proves the first noise-stability bound; applying $A^*$ proves the second. [F7, step 2.1, given, algebra]

5.1 Write $p_n=p_{\alpha_n,0}$. Maximality against $p_0\in P_0$ and the support bound $\langle f,p_n\rangle_Y\le R(u^\dagger)$ give $\|p_n\|_Y\le\|p_0\|_Y$ and $\langle f,p_n\rangle_Y\to R(u^\dagger)$. The closed span of any subsequence is separable; Gram–Schmidt on rational finite linear combinations of its terms gives a finite or countable orthonormal family with dense span. Repeated use of [F8] and [A1] selects a further subsequence whose coordinates all converge. For each finite initial segment, expanding the nonnegative squared norm after orthogonal projection shows that the sum of squared limiting coordinates is at most $\|p_0\|_Y^2$; hence the coordinates define a vector $p$ in that closed span. Approximation by finite linear combinations proves weak convergence there, and [F9] represents each functional $x\mapsto\langle x,y\rangle_Y$ restricted to the span, so convergence is weak in $Y$. The limit lies in $K$: by [F2], $K=\bigcap_{z\in X}\{q:\langle q,Az\rangle_Y\le R(z)\}$, an intersection of weakly closed half-spaces. It also attains $\langle f,p\rangle_Y=R(u^\dagger)$, so $p\in P_0$. Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm and the bound force $\|p\|_Y=\|p_0\|_Y$, hence uniqueness gives $p=p_0$. Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence weakly converging to $p_0$; testing against any fixed $y\in Y$ shows that every scalar subsequence has a further subsequence converging to $\langle p_0,y\rangle_Y$, so $\langle p_n,y\rangle_Y\to\langle p_0,y\rangle_Y$. Thus $p_n\rightharpoonup p_0$. Weak lower semicontinuity and the uniform upper bound then give $\|p_n\|_Y\to\|p_0\|_Y$. The norm identity [F10] yields strong convergence, and boundedness of $A^*$ yields strong convergence of $A^*p_n$. [A1, F1, F2, F8, F9, F10, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 For $u\in\operatorname{dom}R$, [F1] and [F7] give $-\langle A^*p^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X=\langle p^\dagger,f-Au\rangle_Y\le\|p^\dagger\|_Y\|Au-f\|_Y$. Therefore the VSC [F5] holds with $\beta=0$, $p=2$, and $\psi(s)=C\sqrt{s}$, $C=1+\|p^\dagger\|_Y$, on every regularizer sublevel; [F3] identifies its Bregman term with the distance in the Statement. Its conjugate is $H(q)=C^2/(4q)$ for $q>0$. For an exact minimizer with $\|w\|_Y\le\delta$, comparison to $u^\dagger$ gives $R(u_{\alpha,w})\le R(u^\dagger)+\delta^2/(2\alpha)$; if $\alpha\asymp\delta$, this is below any fixed $R_0>R(u^\dagger)$ for small $\delta$. With $c_p=1/4$, $\rho_\delta=H(c_p/\alpha)=C^2\alpha\asymp\delta$ and $H(c_p/(2\alpha))=2\rho_\delta$, so all parameter-coupling hypotheses in [F6] hold and the stated rates follow. [F1, F3, F5, F6, F7, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)$, and set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T_K=\partial E_K$. If $K$ is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot, then every smoothly embedded $2$-sphere in $\operatorname{int}E_K$ bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $E_K$, and there is no smoothly embedded disk $D\subset E_K$ whose interior misses $T_K$ and whose boundary is an essential simple closed curve in $T_K$.

## Statement references

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, Theorem 1.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

[Stefan Friedl, *Introduction to Knots and Links*, Proposition 11.7](https://friedl.app.uni-regensburg.de/papers/2024_knot-theory-final.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the smooth oriented knot, its chosen product tube and the non-unknot hypothesis in the original Statement.

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice: restrict a choice function to the given countable family. [[def-axiom-of-choice]] [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] For a chosen smooth knot exterior under countable choice, every interior smooth sphere bounds an actual smooth standard ball contained in that exterior. [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]]

[F2] Under full AC, a nontrivial smooth knot exterior has no smooth boundary-preimage disk with essential boundary on its peripheral torus. Its proof includes boundary-fixed neatification before the disk-to-core annulus seam is rounded, so no unstated transverse-boundary assumption is needed. [[lem-nontrivial-knot-exterior-boundary-incompressible]]

## Proof

1.1 By [A1], the countable-choice hypothesis of [F1] holds. Its chosen tube and exterior are precisely those in the Statement. Apply [F1] to each specified interior sphere to obtain a smooth embedded ball in $E_K$ with that boundary, proving the first conclusion. [A1, F1, given, construct]

2.1 The full-AC and nontrivial-knot hypotheses of [F2] are exactly supplied. A disk of the kind excluded in the Statement has its interior in the exterior interior and its boundary on $T_K$, so it is one of the boundary-preimage smooth disks excluded by [F2]. Apply that result to prove the second conclusion. Neither argument uses atoroidality, a hyperbolic metric or an extra torus-classification premise. [F2, given, step 1.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

For a fixed finite regular diagram $D$ of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, with $n$ crossings and a basepoint $p\in D$ away from the crossings, choose an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to the branched-cover surgeries and the compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles of the link-surgery construction. Its first page and first differential are isomorphic as a cochain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ to the reduced Khovanov cochain complex of the mirror diagram $\overline D$, based at the corresponding point, in the specified normalized grading shifts. The resulting second page is therefore the based reduced Khovanov cohomology of $\overline D$. The isomorphism is for this fixed diagram and makes no claim about filtered chain complexes for different diagrams.

## Statement references

[[lem-os-first-differential-is-reduced-khovanov|Local first differential identification]]

[[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-based-link-over-f2|Reduced Khovanov cochain complex]]

[[lem-reduced-khovanov-over-f2-basepoint-independence|Basepoint-component independence over F2]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, Theorem 6.3 and proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0309170v1)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §5.3](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed finite regular diagram $D$ of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, its filtered surgery complex, and a marked point $p\in D$ away from the crossings.

[F1] The filtration's first differential is the sum of the cube-edge maps ([[lem-os-first-differential-is-reduced-khovanov]]).

[F2] The exact local identification, including one common vertex basis for all incident edges, the marked quotient tables and normalized mirror shifts, is the Statement of [[lem-os-first-differential-is-reduced-khovanov]]. The reduced target complex is defined in [[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-based-link-over-f2]].

[F3] Over $\mathbb F_2$, the isomorphism class of the reduced cohomology does not depend on the marked component, for a fixed diagram ([[lem-reduced-khovanov-over-f2-basepoint-independence]]).

## Proof

1.1 The filtration quotient at each cube vertex is its resolution Floer group, and the differential on the first page is the sum of components changing one crossing. [F1, given]

1.2 Applying the asserted edge identifications [F2] to each of the finitely many edges identifies this first-page differential with the reduced Khovanov cube differential; the finite direct sum of the vertex isomorphisms is an isomorphism of cochain complexes. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

2.1 Taking cohomology of the identified first-page complexes gives the based reduced Khovanov cohomology on the second page. By [F3] its graded isomorphism class is independent of the chosen link component for this fixed diagram. The local supplier [F2] includes its explicitly external actual Floer/mirror inputs and the local quotient/grading calculations, so this finite assembly proves the displayed first- and second-page identification. It asserts no map between distinct diagram presentations. [F2, F3, step 1.2] ∎

## Statement

For every integer $k\ge1$, let $U_k\subset S^3$ be a $k$-component planar unlink with an arbitrary orientation on each component, and choose a basepoint $p$ on any one component. Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

## Statement references

[[lem-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link-well-defined|Double-cover existence and local branch convention]]

[[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold|Hat Floer definition]]

[[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations|Analytic map-count obligations]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, Propositions 6.1 and 6.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0309170v1)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §5](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A planar unlink $U_k\subset S^3$ with $k\ge1$, arbitrary component orientations, a basepoint on one component, and the saddle cobordisms between its neighboring resolutions with the basepoint carried outside each saddle disk.

[F1] The double branched cover and its orientation are defined and well-defined up to oriented diffeomorphism ([[lem-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link-well-defined]]).

[F2] The group is defined by the closed-manifold disk-count complex ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]]).

[F3] The actual analytic foundations [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]] provide finite zero-basepoint disk and polygon counts, compactified boundaries, exhaustive gluing and the resulting identities under their actual operation-specific global weak, ordinary specified-sector weak or strict admissibility hypotheses. They include positive-rank pointed triple-free representatives and the rank-zero point target. These local identities do not compute the exterior-algebra basis or its $H_1$ action, prove a named top input is a cycle, or identify an unlink saddle map with a prescribed Frobenius map.

[F4] **External input — actual unlink Floer module and handle maps.** Ozsváth–Szabó, arXiv:math/0309170v1, Proposition6.1 and proof, pp.32–33: over $\mathbb F_2$, $\widehat{HF}(\#^r(S^2\times S^1))$ is a free rank-one module over $\Lambda^*H_1$, generated by a class $\Theta$. A zero-framed two-handle killing a summand generator induces the exterior quotient, and its dual split operation induces wedge with the new kernel generator. The statement includes the actual triangle-map/$H_1$-action computation, not merely the dimension of the group.

[F5] **External input — simultaneously compatible state bases.** The same source, Proposition6.2, pp.33–34, including all four cases and Figure11, identifies a based unlink state with this module using lifts $\gamma_i$ of arcs from the marked circle $S_0$ to each other circle $S_i$, with $[\gamma_0]=0$. Its commutative square(13) identifies EVERY immediate surgery edge in the same state bases. Unmarked merge identifies $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$; unmarked split has new kernel $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$; setting $\gamma_0=0$ gives both marked cases. This is an external input at the chosen finite diagram, not arbitrary unlink naturality or a new locally proved count.

## Proof

1.1 The topology assertion has a direct finite construction. Put the planar $k$-component unlink, $k\ge1$, in its standard $k$-bridge position: the upper and lower balls each contain $k$ boundary-parallel arcs with the same noncrossing matching of their $2k$ endpoints. Choose their disjoint bridge disks. Cutting either ball along those disks trivializes the branch construction. Its double cover is two balls joined by $k$ one-handles; the first joins the two zero-handles, and each remaining handle adds one genus. Thus it is a genus-$k-1$ handlebody. The two bridge matchings and disk systems agree in the projection sphere, so the cover of the unlink is the double of this handlebody with matching meridian disks. Doubling each of its $k-1$ co-core disks gives disjoint nonseparating two-spheres. Cutting them removes those one-handles and leaves a sphere with paired ball holes; regluing the pairs gives $\#^{k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$. For $k=1$ it is the double of a ball, hence $S^3$. This finite cut-and-glue construction uses the actual local branched-cover convention of [F1], and no Floer map. [F1, given, construct, construct]

1.2 Here is the complete finite algebra to which the external Floer map computation in step2.1 is applied. Order the unmarked circles of a based $k$-circle state, and assign to them generators $x_c$. The reduced state space is $\Lambda_{\mathbb F_2}\langle x_c\rangle$: the basis monomial on a subset labels those circles by $X$, the others by $1$, and the marked circle by the quotient label $1$. Exterior multiplication is commutative over $\mathbb F_2$ and each $x_c^2=0$. Thus this state space has dimension $2^{k-1}$, once an actual Floer vertex identification with it is supplied. This is a computation of the required state algebra, not yet of $\widehat{HF}$. [given, algebra]

1.3 Write $A=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$. For an unmarked merge the required map is $m(1,1)=1$, $m(1,X)=m(X,1)=X$, $m(X,X)=0$. For an unmarked split it is $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. If a marked circle merges with an unmarked one, reducing the output kills $X$ on the marked factor, so $1\otimes1\mapsto1$ and $1\otimes X\mapsto0$. If a marked circle splits, reduce the child containing the original point: $\Delta(1)$ then becomes $1_{\rm marked}\otimes X_{\rm new}$ (with factors exchanged when necessary). Hence marked split creates the unmarked label $X$, not $1$. All untouched factors are carried identically. These are literal quotient calculations and include both marked cases. [step 1.2, algebra]

1.4 Equivalently, unmarked merge is the exterior-algebra quotient identifying $x_c,x_d$ with $x_e$. Unmarked split is $(x_d+x_e)\wedge\Lambda\jmath$, where $\jmath(x_c)=x_d$ and other generators are unchanged; choosing $x_e$ instead gives the same map, since $(x_d+x_e)^2=0$. Marked merge is quotient by the disappearing $x_c$, and marked split is wedge with the newly created $x_e$. Thus these four precise quotient/wedge operations, in a common state basis, are the finite map targets for the analytic surgery-edge calculation. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F4] to the actual cover constructed in step1.1. Its rank-one exterior module gives the rank $2^{k-1}$, with generators represented by the arc lifts specified in [F5]. That same input supplies the actual Floer triangle maps and their common state bases. Under these bases the quotient/wedge operations of [F4], [F5] are precisely the four finite reduced tables proved in steps 1.2, 1.3, 1.4. In particular $[\gamma_0]=0$ kills the unwanted marked-circle factor and forces marked split to create the new $X$ label. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4]

2.2 The vertex and map computations in the preceding step are externally imported, not inferred from analytic regularity [F3] or from a chosen common-top transfer. The topology and quotient algebra remain the local finite arguments above. All coefficients are $\mathbb F_2$, so no integral sign or instanton-saddle formula is used. The actual finite diagram has finitely many states and edges, with the analytic data in the stated AComega branch. This proves the full fixed-resolution Floer TQFT assertion with its compatible marked bases. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a
nonempty labeled smooth link $L\subset\mathbb R^3$, and assume every component
has at least one underpassing point. Then $L$ is ambient isotopic through links
with the same projection and crossing data to a smooth height realization
$$\widehat L=\{(\gamma_i(s),\widehat\eta_i(s)):s\in S^1,\ 1\le i\le r\} \subset\mathbb R^2\times[-1,0]$$
such that $\widehat\eta_i(s)=-1$ exactly at the underpassing parameters on
component $i$ and $\widehat\eta_i(s)>-1$ at every other parameter.

## Statement references

[[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram|Regular oriented link diagrams and crossing data]]

[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy|Ambient isotopy extension for compact embedded submanifolds]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, a finite regular oriented diagram, its smooth embedded realization, and at least one underpassing parameter on each component.

[A1] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] A regular oriented diagram has a fixed planar projection which is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points and records which branch is over at each point. [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

[F2] A smooth isotopy of a compact embedded link in a boundaryless smooth $3$-manifold extends to an ambient isotopy under countable choice. [[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-countable-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** The diagram, its initial height functions, and [A1].

1.1 Parameterize component $i$ by $S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_i=\{u_{i,1},\ldots,u_{i,m_i}\}$ be its nonempty finite set of underpassing
parameters. Define
$$p_i(s)=\prod_{a=1}^{m_i}\bigl(1-\cos(2\pi(s-u_{i,a}))\bigr).$$
Every factor is smooth and nonnegative, and it vanishes exactly when
$s=u_{i,a}$ in $S^1$. Thus $p_i$ is smooth, vanishes exactly on $U_i$, and is
positive somewhere because a finite subset does not exhaust $S^1$. Its maximum
$P_i$ is positive by compactness. Set
$\widehat\eta_i(s)=-1+p_i(s)/P_i$. Then $-1\le\widehat\eta_i\le0$,
equality at $-1$ holds exactly on $U_i$, and all other heights are greater than
$-1$. [A1, F1, given, construct, construct]

1.2 At every projected double point, the overpassing parameter is not an
underpassing parameter: regularity excludes triple points, so the two source
parameters at that double point have distinct over/under roles. Hence the new
height difference between the over and under branches is strictly positive.
Let $\eta_i$ be the original height function and choose a smooth
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. The family
$$F_t(i,s)=\bigl(\gamma_i(s),(1-\varphi(t))\eta_i(s)+\varphi(t)\widehat\eta_i(s)\bigr)$$
is smooth and stationary near both endpoints. At each crossing its over-minus-
under height is a convex combination of two positive numbers, so it remains
positive. Since [F1] lists all projected multiple points, each $F_t$ is
injective; its projection remains an immersion, so each compact-source map is
a smooth embedding. [A1, F1, given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 The track of the isotopy in step 1.2 is compact, so choose an open ball
containing it and apply [F2] with that ball as the support neighborhood. The
resulting ambient isotopy of $\mathbb R^3$ has compact support and therefore
extends by the identity at $\infty$ to an ambient isotopy of $S^3$. It carries
the original link to $\widehat L$ and fixes the planar projection and
over/under data throughout, because every slice of $F$ has those same data.
This proves the stated normalized realization. [A1, F2, step 1.2, choose, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$
is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\Sigma_q(K)$.

## Statement references

[[def-q-fold-branched-cover-of-a-slice-disk|The branched cover of a slice disk]]

[[lem-prime-power-branched-cover-of-slice-disk-is-rational-homology-ball|The branched cover is a rational homology ball]]

[[lem-rational-homology-ball-boundary-kernel-is-linking-metabolizer|The boundary-kernel metabolizer lemma]]

[[def-finite-linking-form-and-metabolizer|The metabolizer convention]]

[[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus|The smooth slice-disk convention]]

[Charles Livingston and Swatee Naik, *Introduction to Knot Concordance*, §8.2, pp. 167–168](https://chuck-livingston.github.io/math/Concordance_Book.pdf)

[[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a smooth proper slice disk $D$ for $K$, and a prime-power cover degree $q=p^k$.

[A1] Full AC is assumed wherever the cover and orientation conventions use the choice axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The branched cover $W_{D,q}$ has boundary $\Sigma_q(K)$ by the disk-cover convention, and it is a compact connected rational homology ball for prime-power $q$. [[def-q-fold-branched-cover-of-a-slice-disk]] [[lem-prime-power-branched-cover-of-slice-disk-is-rational-homology-ball]]

[F2] For any compact connected oriented rational homology ball with connected boundary, the kernel of boundary inclusion on $H_1$ is a metabolizer for the boundary linking form. [[lem-rational-homology-ball-boundary-kernel-is-linking-metabolizer]]

[F3] The linking form on the finite first homology of a rational homology sphere is symmetric and nonsingular. [[lem-linking-pairing-on-rational-homology-sphere-is-nonsingular]]

[F4] A smooth knot is smoothly slice when it bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$. [[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus]]

[F5] A metabolizer is a subgroup equal to its orthogonal complement for the finite nonsingular linking form. [[def-finite-linking-form-and-metabolizer]]

## Proof

1.1 By [F1], the boundary of $W_{D,q}$ is the rational homology sphere $\Sigma_q(K)$, and both are compact connected oriented manifolds with the required boundary identification. The kernel of its boundary inclusion is exactly the subgroup $P_D$ displayed in the statement. [F1, F4, given, A1]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $W_{D,q}$ and its boundary. The kernel identified in step 1.1 is self-annihilating for the boundary linking form; [F3] supplies nonsingularity and [F5] the metabolizer convention. Therefore $P_D$ is a metabolizer. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $T$ be a torus. Every essential smoothly embedded simple closed curve $c\subset T$ represents a primitive element of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. If $c,d\subset T$ are essential smoothly embedded simple closed curves with $[c]=\pm[d]$, then they are ambient isotopic in $T$. If they are also disjoint and distinct, they cobound an embedded annulus in $T$.

## Statement references

[Allen Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §2.2, Example 2.36](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch2.pdf)

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth torus $T$ and the essential smooth embedded circles of the Statement.

[F1] In the standard torus, every essential smooth circle has primitive nonzero integral class; equal primitive unoriented classes are carried to one another by a jointly smooth ambient isotopy. Disjoint essential circles have smooth complementary annulus parameters. The complete finite construction assumes no choice principle. [[lem-choice-free-smooth-torus-curves-and-annulus-strips]]

## Proof

1.1 Choose a smooth parametrization $h:T\to\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$, as supplied by saying that $T$ is a smooth torus. It preserves essentiality, and its induced integral homology isomorphism preserves primitivity and equality up to sign. Apply [F1] to $h(c)$ to obtain primitivity of $[c]$. This is one supplied finite-dimensional parametrization, not a set-indexed choice. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 If $[c]=\pm[d]$, apply [F1] to their images and conjugate its ambient isotopy by $h$. This gives the required ambient isotopy in $T$. If the original curves are disjoint and distinct, the two complementary annulus parameters in [F1] pull back by $h$; either supplies an embedded annulus with exactly those original curves as boundary. No annulus is inferred for intersecting original curves, and no choice axiom is introduced. [F1, step 1.1, construct] ∎

## Sources

[Allen Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §2.2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch2.pdf)

## Statement

[[def-coprime-torus-knot|Coprime torus-knot convention, including the unknot]]

[Sivek and Zentner, §§1 and 10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1710.01957v2)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The signed torus group has central $h=x^a=y^b$ and preferred longitude $\lambda=h\mu^{-ab}$. A knot meridian normally generates its group. Exterior homology is generated by that meridian, with preferred longitude zero. [[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]] [[lem-satellite-peripheral-representations-transfer-thinness]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F2] Filling kills precisely the primitive peripheral word. An abelian satellite filling transfers to the same pattern-closure slope and, for signed $w\ne0$, to the companion slope divided by $w^2$, through the actual diagonal, Jordan and central-character-twist constructions. [[def-sl-two-abelian-surgery]] [[lem-satellite-sl2-abelian-fillings-transfer-to-pattern-and-companion]]

[F3] A supplied complete finite-volume hyperbolic knot metric has complete closed smooth hyperbolic fillings at all but finitely many primitive slopes. The complete metric has a universal $\mathbb H^3$ cover and faithful projective holonomy. For a CLOSED oriented smooth such manifold the actual complete-Heegaard Spin frame cover supplies a faithful SL2 lift. Finite-sheet covers of compact spaces are compact. [[thm-thurston-hyperbolic-dehn-filling]] [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]] [[lem-closed-oriented-hyperbolic-holonomy-has-a-faithful-sl2-lift]] [[thm-compactness-is-invariant-under-finite-sheeted-coverings]]

Signed torus polynomials have the explicit symmetric absolute-parameter formula. [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]] [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]] [[thm-torus-knot-alexander-and-genus-formulas]]

They are not consequences asserted from the local ASD foundations alone.

[L2] The retained minimal-genus derivation uses the actual knot-exterior trichotomy, with the residual metric step described in [[thm-thurston-hyperbolization-for-atoroidal-knot-exteriors]]. Its local proof is not certified here. The full original classification is instead supplied directly by [F6], retaining all actual signed filling and satellite operations already proved locally.

[F6] **External input:** Baldwin–Sivek, arXiv:2405.19197v2, Theorem 1.1 (p.1), with Theorem 5.1 and its proof in §5, asserts for ANY knot in $S^3$ that infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgeries occur if and only if it is a torus knot. Here “abelian” means EVERY homomorphism has abelian image, not only every irreducible homomorphism; this is their opening definition. Their §2 includes the unknot among torus knots. The actual statement, definitions and §5 theorem/transfer interfaces were consulted directly; the remaining published classification proof is imported, not locally reconstructed.

## Proof

1.1 **The full torus direction by its actual group.** Let $K=T(a,b)$ with signed coprime nonzero parameters. For every positive integer $n$, the rational slope $(abn+1)/n$ is primitive since $\gcd(abn+1,n)=1$. Its filling relation is $\mu^{abn+1}\lambda^n=\mu h^n=1$ by [F1]. Since $h$ is central, the meridian becomes central. It normally generates, so the entire quotient group is cyclic and EVERY representation has abelian image. The slopes $ab+1/n$ are distinct. This proves the direction for all signed torus knots, including the unit-parameter unknot, without an unproved lens-surgery classification or a restriction to irreducible representations. [F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 **Actual closed lifts exclude the supplied hyperbolic case.** For a primitive rational slope $p/q$ with $p\ne0$, filling abelianization is $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$: quotient the meridian-generated exterior abelianization by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]=p[\mu]$. At each all-but-finitely-many hyperbolic filling in [F3], its closed metric has a faithful SL2 lift. An abelian image would make the whole group abelian and hence that finite cyclic group. Its universal cover $\mathbb H^3$ would then be a finite-sheet cover of a closed compact space and so compact, a contradiction. Thus every such nonzero hyperbolic filling has a nonabelian representation. Discarding the single zero slope is harmless. This proves that a supplied finite-volume hyperbolic knot has only finitely many SL2-abelian rational fillings; the closed Spin lift, not the exterior's second cohomology, is essential. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]

1.3 **Filling transfer and the exact conditional limit argument.** Every SL2-abelian filling is SU2-abelian since $SU(2)\subset SL_2(\mathbb C)$. For a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian essential satellite WITH the actual fibered and adjacent-top properties, apply [F4], giving $w\ne0$ and nontrivial pattern closure. In the final reduction these properties are supplied by choosing the actual knot or mirror furnished by [L1] before this row is invoked. Fact [F2] supplies infinitely many actual SL2-abelian slopes for $P(U)$ and $C$, namely $r_i$ and $r_i/w^2$ from distinct satellite slopes $r_i$. Under [L1], the original SU2-abelian slope set is bounded; every infinite subset therefore has a convergent subsequence, and uniqueness of its accumulation point makes its limit $r(K)$. Indeed infinitely many distinct points outside any fixed neighborhood of that point would have a second accumulation point by compactness of a bounded closed interval. Thus the transferred subsets have limits $r(K)$ and $r(K)/w^2$. Applying [L1] to the nontrivial components identifies $r(P(U))=r(K)=w^2r(C)$. No assertion that a mere infinite subset shares a finite accumulation point without boundedness has been used. [F2, F4, L1, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Conditional minimal-genus reduction.** By [L2] and step1.2, a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian nontorus knot would be an essential satellite. Choose such a satellite of least genus. By [L1], one of this knot and its mirror has the actual fibered and specified Alexander properties. Reflection reverses the positive meridian and preserves the degree-one zero-homology longitude by [F1]; the resulting exterior group isomorphism therefore identifies its filling groups with those at negated slopes. It also carries spanning surfaces in both directions, preserving minimal genus, and sends torus knots to torus knots. Replace the least-genus counterexample by that chosen mirror if needed, and choose its essential satellite decomposition by [L2] and step1.2. We now use its ACTUAL supplied fiber and Alexander properties, without an extra assumption on mirror invariance of those coefficients. Thus [F4] and step1.3 give nontrivial $P(U),C$, nonzero $w$, and $g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C)$. Both positive genera are strictly smaller, even for $|w|=1$. Each component has infinitely many SL2-abelian slopes by [F2], so minimality and [L2], with step1.2, make both torus knots. For a signed torus knot the cyclic filling family in step1.1 accumulates at the parameter product; the uniqueness in [L1] identifies its limit slope with that product. Their signed parameter products have the same nonzero sign by step1.3. Let $a>b\ge2$ and $c>d\ge2$ be their respective ABSOLUTE parameter pairs, interchanging parameters when needed. Taking absolute values of that slope relation gives $ab=cdw^2$. The symmetric torus polynomial in [F5] depends only on these absolute parameters, so no further mirroring of the actual satellite and no extra instanton property for either component is needed. [F1, F2, F4, L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, construct, algebra]

3.1 We supply the classical satellite Alexander formula used in [L2], instead of assuming it from a satellite Definition. Write $X=V\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu P$ for the pattern exterior and $E_K=X\cup_T E_C$ for the satellite exterior, with outer meridian $\mu_V$ identified with $\mu_C$ and preferred outer longitude with $\lambda_C$. Let $w\ne0$ be the winding number, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ act on covers by the satellite's positive-meridian deck transformation. Total linking restricts to $w$ times companion linking on $E_C$, to $w$ on $\mu_V$ and zero on the outer longitude. The pulled-back cover of $T$ has $|w|$ cylinder components, so $H_1(\widetilde T)=\Lambda/(t^w-1)$ generated by a lift of $\lambda_C$; its $H_0$ is the same module. The cover of $E_C$ has $|w|$ components, with module $H_1=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C$, where $s$ acts by $t^w$. Its $H_0$ map from $T$ is an isomorphism, because the two linking images are the same subgroup $w\mathbb Z$. Its longitude class is zero in $H_1$: a Seifert surface for $C$ lifts, since linking vanishes on all its loops by normal push-off, and its boundary is that lifted longitude. Replace $C$ by the unknot to obtain the pattern closure $P(U)$. Its companion-side cover has $|w|$ contractible components, the same $H_0$ and zero $H_1$. In both lifted Mayer–Vietoris sequences the $H_0$ map is injective, since its companion-side coordinate is an isomorphism. The only $H_1(\widetilde T)$ image is consequently in the SAME pattern-side module. Quotienting that image yields, respectively, $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}\oplus\bigl(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C\bigr)$. All gluings and the chosen longitude bounds are in the actual peripheral marking; no companion character transfer is used in this module calculation. [F1, F5, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 For $w\ne0$, $\Lambda$ is free of rank $|w|$ over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$ via $s=t^w$, with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{|w|-1}$ after reversing the exponent convention if $w<0$. Extension of scalars is therefore exact, and [F5] supplies a square presentation of its companion summand by the companion Seifert matrix with $s$ replaced by $t^w$. The direct sum in step 3.1 has a block-diagonal square presentation. Taking its determinant gives $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\Delta_{P(U)}(t)\Delta_C(t^w)$. With symmetric normalization and value one at $t=1$, the Laurent unit ambiguity disappears. The winding-zero case gives the same polynomial identity with $\Delta_C(1)=1$: its companion-side cover is now a disjoint union of copies of $E_C$, with $H_1=\Lambda[\mu_C]$ and $H_0=\Lambda$. The torus-side groups are $H_1=\Lambda^2$, $H_0=\Lambda$, and the meridian map onto the companion $H_1$ is an isomorphism while the longitude maps to zero. The same maps hold for an unknot companion. Eliminate the companion meridian generator in both sequences; their identical remaining pattern quotient is $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}$. This proves the Alexander satellite formula also for $w=0$, without claiming that such a pattern can be an instanton L-space satellite. [F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Put $v=|w|$; the symmetric companion polynomial satisfies $\Delta_C(t^w)=\Delta_C(t^v)$. The finite torus-pattern obstruction is also elementary once the stated coefficient restrictions in [L1] have been supplied. Write $a>b\ge2$ coprime and $g=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. The formula in [F5], expanded at infinity, is $\Delta_{T_{a,b}}(t)=t^g(1-t^{-ab})(1-t^{-1})/((1-t^{-a})(1-t^{-b}))$. Modulo terms of degree at most $g-a$, its expansion is $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor a/b\rfloor}(t^{g-ib}-t^{g-ib-1})$. Thus, for $0\le v<a$, its coefficient $c_{g-v}$ is $1$ if $v=0\pmod b$, $-1$ if $v=1\pmod b$, and zero otherwise. Suppose the companion's normalized polynomial has leading terms $t^h-t^{h-1}+O(t^{h-2})$ and the satellite's nonzero coefficients alternate with absolute value one, exactly the two externally supplied instanton conclusions in [L1]. By step 4.1 its coefficient in degree $g+hv-v$ is $c_{g-v}-1$. If $v=1\pmod b$ this is $-2$, impossible. If $v=qb+r$ with $2\le r<b$, it is $-1$, while the preceding nonzero coefficient is the $-1$ in degree $g+hv-qb-1$: all intervening torus coefficients vanish and no lower companion term reaches those degrees. These consecutive negative coefficients contradict alternation. Consequently $b$ divides $v$ whenever $0<v<a$. This argument is a proved finite polynomial implication and uses the externally supplied instanton properties, without proving their gauge-theoretic foundations. [F5, L1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 In particular the torus-pattern configuration required by the minimal-satellite argument is incompatible with those coefficient restrictions. If $ab=k v^2$ for an integer $k\ge1$, then $v<a$, since otherwise $ab\ge a^2>ab$. Step 5.1 makes $b\mid v$, whence $a=k b(v/b)^2$ contradicts $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $b\ge2$. Mirroring a torus pattern does not change its symmetric Alexander polynomial, so the same contradiction applies after the prescribed mirror reduction. Also $v=1$ is already excluded as soon as both nontrivial pattern and companion have leading terms $t^g-t^{g-1}$ and $t^h-t^{h-1}$: their product has second leading coefficient $-2$. This is the finite polynomial contradiction needed for the conditional configuration in step2.1; it does not supply the externally supplied instanton conclusions. [L1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 The companion torus in step2.1 has the adjacent leading terms required in step5.1 by its explicit torus formula [F5], without another instanton hypothesis on that companion. With $v=|w|$, the configuration of step2.1 satisfies $ab=cdv^2$; applying step6.1 to this positive $v$ gives a contradiction. Steps1.1–1.2 unconditionally prove the full signed-torus direction and the supplied-metric hyperbolic exclusion; [F2] proves all actual pattern/companion filling cases. Steps1.3–6.1 supply the remaining converse assembly with the exact externally supplied or explicitly conditional premises [L1, L2]. The exact full iff is now supplied independently by [F6], rather than claimed as a newly local gauge or hyperbolization proof. The original full Statement and representation scope remain unchanged. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 5.1, step 6.1]

8.1 Apply [F6] to the given smooth knot. Its rational filling and all-representations abelian conventions coincide with the Statement, and its torus convention includes the unknot. It gives the converse to the locally proved signed-torus direction and hence the full original equivalence. [F6, given, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $X$ be a compact oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary. A **kinky handle** is a standard $2$-handle whose core disk has finitely many transverse self-plumbings; a **framed Casson-handle tower** is a nested sequence of such stages in which each self-plumbing point of one stage is replaced by a framed kinky handle at the next stage, with the attaching regions matching the preceding stage. Suppose a finite family of these tower $4$-neighborhoods is embedded pairwise disjointly in $X$, with attaching circles in $\partial X$, and carries the algebraic dual data of a disk-embedding datum. If each embedded tower has a homeomorphism of pairs to the standard open $2$-handle $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$ that takes its specified framed attaching region, including its core circle and normal-framing class, to the standard attaching region $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with its standard framing, then the inverse images of the cores $D^2\times\{0\}$ form a pairwise disjoint family of locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$, with the prescribed framed boundary circles.

## Statement references

[[def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embedding-data|The relative disk and dual-sphere interface]]

Stefan Behrens et al., *The Disc Embedding Theorem*, Chapters 17–18 and 24–28, https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198841319.001.0001

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The stated family of towers and their relative standardization homeomorphisms.

[F1] [[def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embedding-data]]: A disk-embedding datum specifies proper disk boundary circles and their boundary normal-framing classes.

## Proof

1.1 A standard open $2$-handle is $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$, and its core $D^2\times\{0\}$ is a locally flat properly embedded disk whose boundary is the core attaching circle with the standard normal-framing class. [given, construct]

1.2 Pull back each core by the corresponding framing-preserving homeomorphism of pairs. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $L$, the bigraded integral groups $Kh^{i,j}(L):=H^i(C^{*,j}(D))$, where $D$ is any finite regular oriented diagram of $L$ and $C(D)$ is the normalized Khovanov cochain complex, are independent of the choice of $D$ up to bigraded isomorphism.

## Statement references

[[def-countable-choice|Countable choice axiom]]

[[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem|Oriented Reidemeister equivalence]]

[[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties|Finite cochain-complex output]]

[[lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopies|Local chain homotopy equivalences]]

[[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence|Chain homotopy equivalence convention]]

[Khovanov, *A categorification of the Jones polynomial* (1999), §§5.1–5.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9908171v2)

[Bar-Natan, *On Khovanov's categorification of the Jones polynomial* (2002), §§3.5.1–3.5.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0201043)

[Kauffman, *An Introduction to Khovanov Homology* (2022), §§4–5](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/kaufmann.pdf)

[Zhang, *Notes on Khovanov homology* (2025), §§3.6–3.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03115v1)

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, two finite regular diagrams of the same oriented link, and their normalized cochain complexes.

[F1] AC$_\omega$ is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under AC$_\omega$, diagrams of the same oriented link are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] Every planar isotopy and oriented Reidemeister I, II or III move induces a bigraded chain homotopy equivalence of the normalized complexes ([[lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopies]]).

[F4] A bounded cochain complex has defined cohomology in each bidegree, and chain homotopy equivalent complexes induce isomorphic cohomology ([[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]], [[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]]).

## Proof

1.1 By [F1] and [F2], choose a finite sequence $D=D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_r=D'$ whose successive diagrams differ by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. By [F3], each pair has a bigraded chain homotopy equivalence, with chain maps in both directions and homotopies from their composites to the respective identities. The normalization in that supplier cancels the raw shifts, so these maps have bidegree $(0,0)$. [F1, F2, F3, given, choose]

2.1 A chain map takes cocycles to cocycles and coboundaries to coboundaries. If two chain maps differ by $dh+hd$, their values on a cocycle differ by a coboundary, so they induce the same cohomology map. Thus each equivalence in step 1.1 gives mutually inverse maps in every bidegree. Composing the finitely many induced isomorphisms identifies the cohomology of $C(D)$ and $C(D')$. It follows that the groups $Kh^{i,j}(L)$ are independent of the chosen diagram up to bigraded isomorphism. The empty sequence gives the identity, and no assertion of a canonical isomorphism for all move sequences is needed. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
