## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m,n,B\ge1$, let $\eta$ be a reference probability on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $\pi$ be the proper joint law of an unknown $X_1\in\mathbb R^d$ and data $Y\in\mathbb R^m$ in a specified Bayesian inverse model. Write $\pi_Y$ for the data marginal and $\pi_y$ for a posterior-kernel version of the conditional law of $X_1$ given $Y=y$. Assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m}|x_1|^2\,\pi(dx_1,dy)+\int_{\mathbb R^d}|x_0|^2\,\eta(dx_0)<\infty.$$
Choose a jointly measurable parameterized vector-field family $v_\theta:[0,1]\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d$, with parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ for some $p\ge1$, whose candidates have finite population squared loss under the training law below.

**Declared inputs.** Supply independent sampling routines for $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, $\eta$, and $\pi$; here $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ is Lebesgue probability on the unit interval. Supply an initialiser $\mathrm{Init}$ returning a parameter in $\Theta$ or failure; an optimizer update callable $\mathrm{Update}(k,\theta,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$ returning a parameter in $\Theta$ or failure, with each call counting as one optimizer step; a named statistic callable $S(k,\theta,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$ returning a finite real value when evaluation succeeds; a finite step budget $M\ge1$ and tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm opt}>0$; a flow-check callable; and a numerical ODE solver with a declared finite step or tolerance budget $h$. Every callable must return its specified value or a failure status in finite time. Any randomization used by these callables is part of the declared input.

**Training and optimizer instructions.** Draw $n$ independent triples
$$(t_i,X_{0i},(X_{1i},Y_i))\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi,$$
and form $X_{t_i}=(1-t_i)X_{0i}+t_iX_{1i}$ and $V_i=X_{1i}-X_{0i}$. Let $\mathcal D_n=((t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i,V_i))_{i=1}^n$ and evaluate the empirical squared loss
$$\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl|v_\theta(t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i)-V_i\bigr|^2.$$
If sampling fails, return **sampling-failed**. Otherwise call $\mathrm{Init}$; if it fails or returns a parameter outside $\Theta$, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field. Set $k=0$ and repeat the following steps in order: evaluate $\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta_k)$ and $S(k,\theta_k,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$; if either evaluation fails or either value is nonfinite, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field; if $S\le\varepsilon_{\rm opt}$, stop with status **converged**; if $k=M$, stop with status **budget-exhausted**; otherwise call $\mathrm{Update}(k,\theta_k,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$, returning **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field if the call fails, returns a parameter outside $\Theta$, or yields a nonfinite value, and then set $\theta_{k+1}$ to its output and increase $k$ by one. For either successful stopping status, return $\widehat v=v_{\theta_k}$, its achieved training loss, the last value of $S$, $k$, $M$, $\varepsilon_{\rm opt}$ and the optimizer status. A finite-data stopping status does not certify $\widehat v=v^*$.

The population least-squares target is the conditional-expectation class
$$v^*(t,x,y)=\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$$
coordinatewise, evaluated at $(t,x,y)$ through a chosen measurable representative. A conditional expectation is only an almost-sure equivalence class, so this formula does not specify an off-support pointwise extension.

**Flow and sampling instructions.** For a query datum $y$, call the flow checker on $\widehat v$ and the data-parameter domain containing $y$. It returns **pass** only when it certifies all hypotheses of the ODE flow lemma, including joint continuity and the integrable global spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth bounds on compact data-parameter sets containing $y$. If it does not return pass, return **field-regularity-failed** with the optimizer record and no terminal samples. Otherwise, for $j=1,\ldots,B$, draw independent $Z_0^j\sim\eta$ and call the declared solver to integrate on $0\le t\le1$
$$\dot Z_t^j=\widehat v(t,Z_t^j,y),\qquad Z_0^j,$$
with budget $h$. Record the returned finite endpoint as the terminal approximation $\widehat Z_1^j$ only when the solver reports success; treat a success response with a nonfinite endpoint as a failed integration. Also record each status and any certified solver error estimate, marking an unavailable estimate unquantified. Continue through all $B$ calls after a solver failure. Return the successful terminal approximations and all per-call records, together with the field and optimizer records; the overall status is **completed** if every integration succeeds and **solver-failed** otherwise. A sampling-call failure returns **sampling-failed** and the records collected so far.

If the exact triangular flow of $\widehat v$ were known to satisfy $T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi$, the exact transport theorem would imply $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every $y$. Finite regression loss, optimizer termination, and solver success alone do not establish this joint pushforward identity or exact posterior sampling. Record posterior model, discretization, kernel, burn-in, Monte Carlo and solver components under the declared posterior-computation error budget when applicable. The budget does not supply a learned-flow regression or optimizer-error estimate; report those separately as measured or certified quantities, and mark unavailable quantities unquantified rather than zero.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; proper joint posterior law $\pi$ on finite-dimensional unknown/data spaces; independent reference law $\eta$; finite second moments; a chosen measurable vector-field family with finite squared population loss; finite optimizer and ODE budgets; and a numerical solver that returns either an endpoint or an explicit status.

[A1] AC is assumed for the conditional-expectation projection and standard-Borel posterior-kernel interfaces. Its implications include Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for the flow lemma. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

[F1] In a proper Bayesian model, $\pi$ is the joint unknown/data law and $\pi_y$ is a version of the posterior conditional law; values on a $\pi_Y$-null set are not fixed by the conditional identity. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]], [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]

[F2] For a square-integrable target, the conditional expectation given $\sigma(t,X_t,Y)$ is the unique $L^2$ minimizer of the population squared prediction loss, coordinatewise. [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]]

[F3] Under AC, a conditional expectation given a random element in a standard Borel space has a measurable representative as a function of that conditioning element; the identity with the conditional expectation holds almost surely. [[cor-conditional-expectation-as-a-measurable-function-of-the-conditioning-variable]], [[lem-finite-euclidean-space-is-standard-borel]]

[F4] Independent sampling from $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, $\eta$, and $\pi$ gives the stated product training law; product probabilities have the rectangle formula, and the expectation of a finite sum of integrable losses is the sum of their expectations. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]

[F5] A fitted field satisfying the integrable spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth assumptions has a unique global flow and a continuous terminal map; these facts do not certify that its output law is the target. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

[F6] If the exact triangular terminal map has joint pushforward $\pi$, its exact conditional fibers push $\eta$ to $\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every datum; this needs the joint identity as a separate hypothesis. [[thm-ip-exact-triangular-transport-disintegrates-to-posterior]]

[F7] The six-term posterior-computation budget is a telescoping ledger and supplies no learned-flow regression or optimizer bound. [[def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budget]]

## Verification

**Given:** The hypotheses and procedure in the Definition.

1.1 The sampled variables have joint law $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi$ by the algorithm's independent-draw specification and [F4]. Since $\pi$ is the proper Bayesian prior-predictive joint law, [F1] identifies its selected conditional kernel as a posterior version. The moment assumption makes $V=X_1-X_0$ square-integrable, so [F2] identifies its unique population squared-loss regression class and [F3] represents that class measurably in the coordinates $(t,X_t,Y)$. Each empirical loss is a finite sum of finite residuals; for an integrable candidate loss, [F4] gives $\mathbb E[\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta)]=\mathcal L(\theta)$. This establishes the regression target and population meaning of the empirical objective without claiming the finite optimizer attains the population minimum or that the stopping statistic bounds population error. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 If the fitted field passes the stated regularity check, [F5] supplies the exact mathematical ODE flow and terminal map. If that exact map also satisfies the distinct joint pushforward hypothesis in [F6], the exact transport theorem gives the posterior fiber law. The algorithm instead returns numerical endpoints only when the solver reports success, so its actual finite-budget output remains an approximation unless an error certificate establishes otherwise. By [F7], a missing training or optimizer term in the posterior ledger remains separately reported rather than inferred as zero. [F5, F6, F7, given] ∎

      url: "https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/living.pdf"

    - title: "Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram Signature: A Survey"
      url: "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.04477"
      locator: "§2.1 and Remark 2.10, printed pp. 3–5: the Hermitian signature and metabolic vanishing."

## Statement refuted

Assume full AC, and let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil whose positive-push Seifert matrix in the ordered Hopf-core basis is $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. The claim refuted is that $T$ bounds a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$.

## Statement references

[[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix|The trefoil matrix and its positive-push convention]]

[[thm-locally-flat-slice-implies-fox-milnor-factorization|The necessary Fox–Milnor norm condition]]

[[cor-nonfactorization-obstructs-sliceness|The necessary sliceness obstruction]]

[[thm-metabolizer-implies-levine-tristram-signature-vanishing|The metabolic signature obstruction]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the positive-push trefoil matrix $V$, and the claim that the trefoil is locally flat slice to be refuted.

[A1] Full AC is the choice axiom assumed by the Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The positive Hopf-plumbed right-handed trefoil has $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ in the stated basis. [[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix]]

[F2] The determinant $\det(V-tV^T)$ generates the Alexander polynomial up to a Laurent unit. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F3] At a nonroot $\omega\ne1$, the Levine–Tristram signature is the signature of $H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F4] If this Seifert form is metabolic and $\Delta_T(\omega)\ne0$, then $\sigma_\omega(T)=0$. [[thm-metabolizer-implies-levine-tristram-signature-vanishing]]

[F5] A locally flat slice disk gives a primitive Seifert metabolizer and hence the Fox–Milnor reciprocal norm, with the full-AC geometric and algebraic inputs explicitly stated in those suppliers. [[thm-locally-flat-slice-implies-fox-milnor-factorization]], [[lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer]]

[F6] Failure of this reciprocal-norm condition obstructs a locally flat slice disk, by the contrapositive corollary. [[cor-nonfactorization-obstructs-sliceness]]

## Counterexample

1.1 By [F1] and [F2], $\Delta_T(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)=(1-t)^2+t=t^2-t+1$. Thus $|\Delta_T(-1)|=3$, since every Laurent unit $\pm t^k$ evaluates to $\pm1$ at $-1$. [A1, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 If $\Delta_T(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$ for some $f\in\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, then evaluating at $t=-1$ gives $3=f(-1)^2$ or $-3=f(-1)^2$. Neither is possible because an integer square is nonnegative and $3$ is not an integer square. Hence the trefoil polynomial is not an integral reciprocal norm. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 At $\omega=-1$, one has $H_{-1}(V)=2(V+V^T)=\begin{pmatrix}-4&-2\\-2&-4\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues are $-2$ and $-6$. Since $\Delta_T(-1)\ne0$, its Levine–Tristram signature is $-2$. By [F4], a metabolic Seifert form would have signature $0$ there, so the trefoil Seifert form is not metabolic. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F6] and step2.1, the trefoil does not bound a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball. Independently, if such a disk existed then [F5] would give a metabolic Seifert form, contradicting the signature calculation in step2.2 and [F4]. Thus the original locally flat sliceness claim is refuted by both necessary tests, with their TOP geometric inputs supplied rather than inferred from the numbers alone. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

      locator: "Printed pp.5–7; the sutured Floer invariant associated to a sutured manifold and its diagram-independence construction"

## Definition

For a balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$, a **balanced sutured Heegaard diagram** is a tuple $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta)$ where $\Sigma$ is a compact oriented surface with boundary and each of $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$ is a finite family of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves in $\operatorname{int}\Sigma$. It defines $M$ by attaching $3$-dimensional $2$-handles to $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ along $\boldsymbol\alpha\times\{0\}$ and $\boldsymbol\beta\times\{1\}$, with sutures $\partial\Sigma\times\{1/2\}$ on $\gamma=\partial\Sigma\times[0,1]$. The diagram is balanced when the two families have equal cardinality $d$ and the natural maps from components of $\partial\Sigma$ to components of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup\boldsymbol\beta$ are both surjective. A **domain** is an integral two-chain generated by the closures of regions of $\Sigma\setminus(\bigcup\boldsymbol\alpha\cup\bigcup\boldsymbol\beta)$ disjoint from $\partial\Sigma$. A **periodic domain** is a domain whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves. The diagram is **admissible** when each nonzero periodic domain has at least one positive and one negative region coefficient.

The symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)=\Sigma^d/S_d$ is the space of unordered $d$-tuples of points. The product tori $\mathbb T_\alpha,\mathbb T_\beta$ are the images of the products of the $d$ attaching curves in this symmetric product. A **generator** is a point of $\mathbb T_\alpha\cap\mathbb T_\beta$, equivalently a collection of $d$ transverse intersection points, one on each attaching curve in each family. A **Whitney disk class** from generator $\mathbf{x}$ to generator $\mathbf{y}$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a disk into $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on the product tori and whose endpoints are $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}$; $\pi_2(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ denotes the set of these classes. Fix a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures on $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$, where an almost complex structure is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J$ with $J^2=-\operatorname{id}$. A representative of a Whitney disk class is a smooth strip $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_su+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(s,0)\in\mathbb T_\alpha$, $u(s,1)\in\mathbb T_\beta$, and limits $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}$ as $s\to-\infty,+\infty$. Its Maslov index is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy--Riemann operator at a representative, and $\mathcal M_J(\phi)$ denotes the space of representatives of class $\phi$. Translation of the real coordinate gives the $\mathbb R$ action on this moduli space.

When $d=0$, $\operatorname{Sym}^0(\Sigma)$ is a point, both product tori are that point, and the unique generator is the empty collection.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain of regions of $\Sigma$ whose boundary is an integral sum of attaching curves and whose boundary coefficient on $\partial\Sigma$ is zero. Its coefficients are its multiplicities on the regions. The diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain has at least one positive and one negative region coefficient. A Whitney disk from generator $\mathbf x$ to generator $\mathbf y$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a disk into $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on the product tori and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its Maslov index is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy--Riemann operator at a representative. A coherent orientation system assigns orientations to these operators' determinant lines compatibly with gluing.

For a fixed admissible diagram, the **sutured Floer disk-count module** $SFC(\mathcal H;R)$ is the free $R$-module on its generators, where $R=\mathbb F_2$ or $\mathbb Z$. For $R=\mathbb F_2$, its formal differential counts translation classes modulo two:
$$\partial\mathbf{x}=\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\\\mu(\phi)=1}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_J(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,\mathbf{y}.$$
For $R=\mathbb Z$, use a coherent orientation system, which assigns orientations to determinant lines of the linearized disk operators compatibly with gluing, and replace $\#_2$ by the signed count $\#_{\mathfrak o}$. The homology of this diagram-level differential is denoted $H_*(SFC(\mathcal H;R))$ once the moduli counts are finite and the differential squares to zero. When $d=0$ the unique empty generator has zero differential. Once admissible diagram-change maps are proved to be chain homotopy equivalences, their common homology is denoted $SFH(M,\gamma;R)$. This definition fixes the chain-level and coefficient conventions; it does not assert analytic compactness, gluing, invariance, or surface-decomposition results.

## Definition references

[[def-balanced-taut-sutured-manifold-and-product-region|Balanced and taut sutured manifolds, product regions, and horizontal surfaces]]

[[def-admissible-pointed-heegaard-floer-data|Whitney disks, product tori, Maslov index, and holomorphic disk counts]]

[Juhasz, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, §§2–3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609779v3)

[Ni, *Knot Floer homology detects fibred knots*, §2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0607156v4)

## Example

Assume full AC. The disk Seifert surface of the oriented unknot has the rank-zero Seifert lattice and is metabolic. In the positive-push convention, the standard positive Hopf-band plumbing for the right-handed trefoil has matrix $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Since $V$ is invertible, its rational isometric structure has symmetric form $B=V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$, which is negative definite; the integral Seifert lattice is not metabolic.

## Example references

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert matrix convention]]

[[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance|The definition of a metabolic Seifert lattice]]

[[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix|The positive Hopf-plumbing matrix calculation]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the disk Seifert surface of the oriented unknot, and the standard positive Hopf-plumbing Seifert surface of the right-handed trefoil.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the knot Seifert-pairing interface. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The rank-zero lattice is allowed; its zero subgroup is a primitive rank-zero metabolizer. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

[F2] The positive Hopf-plumbing basis has matrix $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. [[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix]]

[F3] Since $V$ is invertible, $(V+V^T,V^{-1}V^T)$ satisfies the rational isometric-structure definition. [[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures]], [[lem-invertible-seifert-matrix-gives-rational-isometric-structure]]

[F4] A metabolic lattice must have a rank-half direct summand on which the Seifert pairing vanishes. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

## Proof

1.1 The disk has $H_1=0$, so its Seifert matrix is the empty matrix. The subgroup $M=0$ has rank zero, is a direct summand, and the pairing vanishes on it. By [F1], this is metabolic and represents the identity class. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F2] and [F3], the trefoil's rational structure has symmetric form $B=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$. For a vector $(m,n)\in\mathbb Q^2$, $B((m,n),(m,n))= -2(m^2+mn+n^2)=-2(m+n/2)^2-3n^2/2$, which is negative whenever $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$. Thus the rational structure has no nonzero isotropic line. For an integral vector the Seifert self-pairing is $-(m^2+mn+n^2)<0$, so no rank-one subgroup has identically zero Seifert pairing, and [F4] rules out an integral metabolizer. [F2, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

id: lem-ip-weighted-coefficient-spaces-are-hilbert
kind: lemma
title: Weighted coefficient spaces form a Hilbert scale
status: draft

pipeline_run: inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19

axiom_use: "Countable choice is assumed only through the published square-summable orthogonal-series and Parseval results used to identify coefficient norms and reconstruct vectors from their coordinates."
provenance:

  proof: ai-altered
sources:
  references:
    - title: "E. Giné and R. Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models (Cambridge University Press, 2016)"
      url: "https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~nickl/Site/__files/FULLPDF.pdf"
      locator: "§4.2, orthonormal wavelet bases; §§4.3.4–4.3.5, coefficient norms for Besov spaces."
    - title: "M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (arXiv:1302.6989)"
      url: "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.6989"
      locator: "§2.3, coefficient summability in Besov-prior regularity."
---

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $H_0$ be a separable real Hilbert space with a complete orthonormal basis indexed by the disjoint union of a finite set $I_*$ and the level indices $(\ell,k)$ with $\ell\ge0$ and $0\le k<2^\ell$. Write the basis vectors as $(e_i)_{i\in I_*}$ and $(e_{\ell k})$. For $r\ge0$, define
$$H_r:=\left\{x\in H_0:\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle x,e_i\rangle_{H_0}|^2+\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{2r\ell}\sum_{k<2^\ell}|\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle_{H_0}|^2<\infty\right\},$$
with inner product given by the corresponding weighted coefficient sum and norm squared
$$\|x\|_{H_r}^2:=\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle x,e_i\rangle_{H_0}|^2+\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{2r\ell}\sum_{k<2^\ell}|\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle_{H_0}|^2.$$
Then $H_r$ is a separable real Hilbert space. Its displayed basis is complete and orthogonal in $H_r$, with squared basis norms $1$ on the finite family and $2^{2r\ell}$ on level $\ell$, and the inclusion $H_r\hookrightarrow H_0$ is continuous with operator norm at most $1$.

## Statement references

[[def-countable-choice|countable choice, used by the cited countable-basis expansion results]]

[[def-hilbert-space|a Hilbert space is complete for its induced norm]]

[[def-separable-space|separability means an at most countable dense subset]]

[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis|an orthonormal basis has dense linear span and its coefficients determine vectors]]

[[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set|the square-summable coefficient norm]]

[[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space|real square-summable sequences form a Hilbert space]]

[[lem-square-summable-orthogonal-families-have-norm-convergent-finite-sums|square-summable coefficients reconstruct a vector from an orthonormal family]]

[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family|Parseval's identity under countable choice]]

[Giné and Nickl, §§4.2–4.3.5, full book](https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~nickl/Site/__files/FULLPDF.pdf)

[Dashti and Stuart, §2.3, full text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.6989)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, $H_0$, its finite orthonormal family and level-indexed orthonormal families, and $r\ge0$.

[A1] Countable choice is the principle that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] Under countable choice, a complete orthonormal family satisfies Parseval's identity: the sum of squared coefficients of each vector equals its squared norm. [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]

[F2] Real square-summable sequences with their canonical inner product are complete and hence Hilbert. [[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space]]

[F3] Under countable choice, square-summable coefficients on an orthonormal family give a norm-convergent sum whose limit has those coefficients and the corresponding squared norm. [[lem-square-summable-orthogonal-families-have-norm-convergent-finite-sums]]

[F4] A topological space is separable when it has an at most countable dense subset. [[def-separable-space]]

## Proof

**Given:** Countable choice, $H_0$, $(e_{\ell k})$, and $r\ge0$ as in the Statement.

1.1 Write $m=|I_*|$ and enumerate the basis by placing the finite family first, followed by $(\ell,k)$ at index $m+2^\ell+k$. For $x\in H_r$, define $T_rx$ by $(T_rx)_t=\langle x,e_{i_t}\rangle_{H_0}$ for the finite coordinates and $(T_rx)_{m+2^\ell+k}=2^{r\ell}\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle_{H_0}$. Parseval [F1] gives $\|T_rx\|_{\ell^2}^2=\|x\|_{H_r}^2$, so $T_r$ is an isometry into real $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$. [A1, F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Given $b\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, set the finite-family coefficients equal to its first $m$ coordinates and put $a_{\ell k}=2^{-r\ell}b_{m+2^\ell+k}$. Since $r\ge0$, the sum of squares of all these coefficients is at most $\sum_n|b_n|^2<\infty$. By [F3], their orthonormal expansion converges in $H_0$ to a vector $x$ with those coefficients. Thus $x\in H_r$ and $T_rx=b$, so $T_r$ is onto. By [F2], the isometric pullback of the real $\ell^2$ inner product makes $H_r$ complete, and hence a real Hilbert space. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

3.1 The finite-support rational sequences form a countable subset of real $\ell^2$: each is encoded by a finite list of coordinate indices, integer numerators, and positive denominators, and such finite integer lists have an explicit natural-number encoding. Given $b\in\ell^2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, choose $N\ge1$ so that the norm of its tail after $N$ is below $\varepsilon/2$, then choose rationals $q_1,\dots,q_N$ with $|b_n-q_n|<\varepsilon/(2\sqrt N)$ for each $n\le N$. The finite-support rational sequence $q$ then satisfies $\|b-q\|_2<\varepsilon$, so these sequences are dense. Because $T_r$ is an isometric bijection by steps 1.1 and 2.1, their inverse images are a countable dense subset of $H_r$. Hence $H_r$ is separable by [F4]. [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Each basis vector has a single nonzero coefficient, so its squared $H_r$ norm is $1$ on $I_*$ and $2^{2r\ell}$ on level $\ell$; distinct basis vectors are orthogonal under the weighted inner product. The finite-support coefficient vectors are dense by step 3.1, so the orthogonal family is complete in $H_r$. Finally Parseval [F1] gives $\|x\|_{H_0}^2=\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2+\sum_{\ell,k}|\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle|^2\le\|x\|_{H_r}^2$ for $x\in H_r$, because $2^{2r\ell}\ge1$. Thus the inclusion has operator norm at most $1$. [A1, F1, step 3.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the following are equivalent: $K$ bounds a ribbon immersion of a disk in $S^3$; and $K$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball for which squared radial distance is Morse in the interior with only critical points of indices zero and one. In the second presentation the disk has product collars at its boundary.

## Statement references

[[def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot|Ribbon immersions, bands, and movies without maxima]]

[[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars|Proper surfaces and boundary collars]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** ACω, a smooth oriented knot $K$, and one of the two presentations in the Statement.

[A1] ACω is the assumption used by smooth isotopy extension, parametric transversality, and the Morse-handle suppliers. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] A ribbon immersion has finitely many double arcs with disjoint proper and interior preimage arcs and no other multiple points. A band move is prescribed by a framed embedded rectangle meeting the boundary link only along its two attaching edges. [[def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot]]

[F2] A compact collared Morse surface has a finite handle presentation; minima add disks and index-one points add rectangles along opposite edges. At regular intervals, normalized gradient flow identifies the boundary circles. Conversely the standard disk and rectangle handle models have one minimum or one saddle, respectively, and glue along regular collars. [[thm-morse-functions-and-handle-decompositions-correspond]], [[cor-a-morse-function-on-a-compact-manifold-has-finitely-many-critical-points]]

[F3] A smooth isotopy of a compact boundary link extends ambiently in $S^3$. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

[F4] A smooth arc may be perturbed relative to its endpoint collars to be transverse to finitely many immersed surface sheets and disjoint from finitely many immersed arcs in a three-manifold. The first condition has zero-dimensional inverse image and the second has empty inverse image; finite-dimensional bump families and parametric transversality give both simultaneously. [[thm-parametric-transversality]]

## Proof

**Given:** $K$ and the indicated presentation.

1.1 First start with a disk movie without maxima. Its neat boundary collar gives a neighborhood with no radial critical points. The critical set is therefore a compact discrete subset of the disk interior, hence finite by [F2]. On each regular radial interval, radial projection to the unit three-sphere gives an isotopy of the level link, extended by [F3]. A local minimum has the usual disk model and creates a split round unknot in a small ball; a local saddle has the rectangle model and changes the link by its framed band move. These assertions follow in coordinates from the Morse equations $x^2+y^2$ and $x^2-y^2$: the first level is a small circle born in a ball, and in the second the two attaching sides of the rectangle are replaced by the other two sides. Critical points sharing a value have disjoint small ambient neighborhoods, so the corresponding local events may be processed successively. Thus there is a finite sequence of births, band attachments, and boundary-link isotopies, whose abstract disk and band handles give exactly the original disk. We will realize this same sequence by immersed surfaces in $S^3$. [A1, F2, F3, given, construct]

1.2 For the reverse implication, start with a ribbon immersion $f:D^2\to S^3$. Remove narrow disjoint strip neighborhoods of all its proper preimage arcs. Choose them disjoint from every interior preimage arc; this is possible because all preimage arcs are disjoint compact sets. Cutting along a proper arc of a disk separates it into two disks, so cutting along all these strips leaves finitely many disk components. Their images are embedded and pairwise disjoint, since every original multiple point had one preimage in a removed strip. The removed strips themselves are embedded bands with pairwise disjoint images, and are disjoint from the disk boundaries except along their attaching edges: their remaining intersections with the disk components are exactly the original ribbon arcs, away from these boundaries. Rounding the cut corners gives a finite presentation by disjoint embedded disks and disjoint embedded bands. The boundaries of the disks form an unlink. Indeed each disk has a disjoint small product neighborhood, and shrinking concentric circles in its disk coordinates gives an isotopy to a small round unknot in that neighborhood; [F3] extends these disjoint isotopies. The band surgeries on this unlink recover the original boundary $K$. [F1, F3, construct]

2.1 The inductive invariant is a compact oriented ribbon-immersed surface with the current oriented level link as embedded boundary. Begin with the empty surface. An isotopy event acts on the whole immersion by [F3]. For a birth, its ball is disjoint from the old boundary link. The old immersed surface has empty interior in $S^3$: in each immersion chart its image is a smooth two-dimensional sheet, and finitely many such charts cover its compact domain. Its image is also closed. Hence there is a small ball inside the birth ball disjoint from the entire old image. Add an embedded disk there. Its boundary is a split unknot isotopic within the birth ball to the required newborn component, and apply [F3] to match the new boundary link. This introduces no multiple point. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 For a band event, first shrink its attaching intervals in their boundary collars and slide them along the boundary, if needed, to avoid the finitely many endpoints of old ribbon arcs. This changes the banded boundary by an isotopy supported in its attaching collars. The immersion is embedded on these collars. Keep the prescribed normal framing of the band core. Perturb the core relative to these collars, as in [F4], to avoid the old double arcs and meet each regular old sheet transversely. Away from its endpoints it is compact and disjoint from the old boundary, so all resulting intersections with the old surface lie in its regular interior sheets; transversality makes their inverse image a finite discrete set. The perturbation can be arbitrarily small, so the core remains embedded, the band framing persists, and the boundary band move is unchanged up to isotopy. Shrink the framed band about that core, including its attaching intervals. This shrinking is an isotopy of the banded boundary: in the rectangle coordinates contract the width, extend the same contraction along the two attaching link intervals, and round corners in their disjoint collars. At an intersection with an old sheet the transverse core parameter is a local defining coordinate for that sheet, so the implicit function theorem expresses its intersection with a sufficiently narrow band as a single arc running across the full band width. Compactness away from these finitely many intersections allows one width small enough to exclude every other intersection. Each new double arc consequently has one proper preimage in the new band and one interior preimage in the old surface. The new band is embedded, it avoids all old double arcs, and the neighborhoods of its new intersections are disjoint, so no triple point is introduced. Glue and smooth the band at its attaching collars. The old proper preimage arcs remain proper because those collars avoided all their endpoints. The new proper arcs have endpoints on the two free band sides, hence on the new surface boundary. This proves the invariant at the saddle. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct, choose]

4.1 Finite induction over the movie now gives a ribbon-immersed oriented surface with boundary $K$. It is the original abstract surface: births added its zero-handles, saddles added its one-handles in the same order and with the same oriented attaching data, and boundary isotopies changed neither handle topology nor orientation. Thus its domain is a disk, not merely a surface of Euler characteristic one. Step 3.1 also shows that its only multiple points are finitely many disjoint transverse ribbon double arcs and its boundary is embedded. This proves the implication from the disk movie to a ribbon immersion. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 Realize that presentation in a radial shell $S^3\times[a,1]\subset B^4$, $a>0$. At early distinct radii create a minimum disk for each unlink component, using its embedded disk to give the trace down to its cap. Between these caps and the bands keep product annuli on the unlink. At later radii attach the disjoint bands by the standard saddle traces of [F2]. Each saddle trace meets the existing surface only at its attaching collars: below that radius the surface contains only the product boundary annuli at those levels, and the band interior is disjoint from the current boundary link. The interiors of the zero-handle disks lie at earlier radii, so band intersections with their projections in $S^3$ cause no intersection in the four-ball. Distinct bands have disjoint images and disjoint attaching intervals, so they can also be placed at successive radii. Finish with a product collar up to radius one. Smooth the finitely many seams in their product charts. This is a smooth embedded disk because its abstract disks and bands reconstruct the original domain disk of step 1.2. Its radius has exactly the chosen minimum and saddle models; squared radius is their composition with an increasing smooth function having positive derivative on $[a,1]$, so it has the same nondegenerate critical points and indices. Its boundary is $K$, and the final product collar makes it proper and neat. This proves the converse and the equivalence. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $X_0$ take values $-1$ and $1$ with equal probability, let $X_\sigma=X_0+\sigma Z$ with $\sigma>0$ and standard Gaussian noise independent of $X_0$, and let $Y\mid X_0=u$ have density $\varphi_\tau(y-u)$ for $\tau>0$. At the observation $y=0$, the exact measurement density $r_\sigma(0\mid x)=\mathbb E[\varphi_\tau(-X_0)\mid X_\sigma=x]$ is constant in $x$, so its score is zero. The exact posterior mean is $m_\sigma(x)=\mathbb E[X_0\mid X_\sigma=x]=\tanh(x/\sigma^2)$, where $\tanh(t)=(e^{2t}-1)/(e^{2t}+1)$. The plug-in density $\varphi_\tau(-m_\sigma(x))$ has score $-m_\sigma(x)m_\sigma'(x)/\tau^2$, which is nonzero for $x\ne0$. Thus evaluating the measurement likelihood at the exact posterior mean does not in general recover the exact measurement score; this example does not rule out equality in special models.

## Statement references

[[lem-ip-conditional-score-and-tweedie-identities]]

[[def-ip-diffusion-prior-score-and-measurement-score]]

[Daras et al., §2.4.4, Eq. 2.20, and §3.1.4, Eq. 3.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.00083)

[Chung et al., §3.1, Eqs. 7–15 and Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.14687)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two-point prior, the independent Gaussian noising and observation noises, and $\sigma,\tau>0$.

[A1] $P(X_0=1)=P(X_0=-1)=1/2$ and $X_\sigma=X_0+\sigma Z$ with $Z$ standard Gaussian independent of $X_0$.

[A2] Conditional on $X_0=u$, the observation has Gaussian density $\varphi_\tau(y-u)$, with independent noise and $\tau>0$.

[A3] The Gaussian density is $\varphi_\tau(v)=(\sqrt{2\pi}\tau)^{-1}\exp(-v^2/(2\tau^2))$.

[F1] Under additive Gaussian noising, the posterior mean is $m_\sigma(x)=x+\sigma^2\nabla\log p_\sigma(x)$. [[lem-ip-conditional-score-and-tweedie-identities]]

[F2] The exact measurement score is $g_\sigma(x,y)=\partial_x\log r_\sigma(y\mid x)$, where $r_\sigma(y\mid x)$ averages the clean-state likelihood over the conditional law of $X_0$ given $X_\sigma=x$. [[def-ip-diffusion-prior-score-and-measurement-score]]

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 For $x\in\mathbb R$, Bayes' formula gives $\displaystyle\frac{P(X_0=1\mid X_\sigma=x)}{P(X_0=-1\mid X_\sigma=x)}=\frac{\varphi_\sigma(x-1)}{\varphi_\sigma(x+1)}=\exp(2x/\sigma^2)$. Therefore the posterior mean is $(e^{2x/\sigma^2}-1)/(e^{2x/\sigma^2}+1)=\tanh(x/\sigma^2)$, agreeing with the conditional-mean version in [F1]. [A1, F1, algebra]

1.2 At $y=0$, both possible clean states have the same likelihood density: $\varphi_\tau(0-1)=\varphi_\tau(0+1)=\varphi_\tau(1)$. Averaging these equal values over the conditional law from [F2] gives $r_\sigma(0\mid x)=\varphi_\tau(1)$ for every $x$, so its logarithmic derivative and the exact measurement score are zero. [A1, A2, A3, F2, algebra]

2.1 The plug-in log density is $\log\varphi_\tau(-m_\sigma(x))=-\log(\sqrt{2\pi}\tau)-m_\sigma(x)^2/(2\tau^2)$. Differentiating the quotient expression in step 1.1 gives $m_\sigma'(x)=4e^{2x/\sigma^2}/(\sigma^2(e^{2x/\sigma^2}+1)^2)>0$. Hence the plug-in score is $-m_\sigma(x)m_\sigma'(x)/\tau^2$, which is nonzero whenever $x\ne0$. [A3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The exact score in step 1.2 and the plug-in score in step 2.1 disagree for every nonzero $x$. Thus the exact posterior mean does not, in general, make likelihood-at-the-mean guidance equal to the exact measurement score. The calculation permits special cases of equality but refutes a general identity. [step 1.2, step 2.1, given] ∎

## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice for knot Seifert pairings. Let $G_{\mathbb Q}$ be the rational Witt group of finite-dimensional even-dimensional nonsingular symmetric rational forms equipped with an invertible isometry $T$ for which $I-T$ is invertible, modulo metabolic $T$-invariant subspaces, and let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group of Seifert lattices. The rational algebraic concordance classification due to Levine and the integral classification completed by Stoltzfus identify each of these abelian groups, as an abstract group, with
$$
\mathbb Z^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}.
$$
Here $A^{(\mathbb N)}$ denotes the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of the abelian group $A$; the statement does not identify Levine's rational classification with the distinct integral group or claim that their defining objects are the same.

## Statement references

[[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures|The definitions of the integral and rational Witt groups]]

[[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance|The integral metabolic relation]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and the two groups in the Statement, with their original defining objects and metabolic relations.

[A1] Full AC is assumed as stated. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The integral group uses finite integral Seifert lattices with unimodular skew part, and the rational group uses the even-dimensional rational isometric structures in the Statement. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]], [[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures]]

[F2] Integral Seifert classes admit invertible representatives, and the associated rational structure defines an injective homomorphism $\iota:G_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}$. This includes singular-matrix reduction and saturation of rational metabolizers. [[thm-integral-seifert-witt-group-injects-into-rational-isometric-group]]

[F3] Rational isometric classes split as the direct sum of their self-reciprocal primary groups. For each irreducible $p\ne t+1$ the primary group is the hermitian Witt group of the number field $E=\mathbb Q[t]/(p)$ with involution $t\mapsto t^{-1}$, and the $t+1$ group is the even-dimensional symmetric Witt group over $\mathbb Q$. [[thm-rational-isometric-witt-group-has-reciprocal-primary-decomposition]], [[thm-rational-primary-isometric-classes-are-hermitian-witt-classes]]

[F4] The kernel of all hermitian signatures over each quadratic number-field extension is killed by four. The rational symmetric signature kernel is also killed by four, including on its even-dimensional subgroup. [[thm-hermitian-number-field-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]], [[thm-rational-symmetric-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]]

[F5] The explicit integral matrices $F_b=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&b\end{pmatrix}$, $P_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-n^2\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-(3q-1)/4\end{pmatrix}$, for $b,n\ge1$ and primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $q\ne3$, lie in distinct quadratic primary components. The first family is independent of infinite order, the second has exact order two, and the third exact order four. The $P_n$ have independent images in $G_{\mathbb Z}/2G_{\mathbb Z}$. [[lem-integral-algebraic-concordance-has-independent-free-two-and-four-torsion-families]]

[F6] A countable abelian group mapping to a countable direct sum of copies of $\mathbb Z$ with exponent-four kernel splits into countably many free, order-two, and order-four summands. The three multiplicities are infinite under the precise independent-family tests in that lemma. [[lem-countable-signature-groups-with-exponent-four-kernel-split]]

## Proof

1.1 Both groups in [F1] are countable. A rational structure is specified, after one finite basis choice, by its dimension and two finite rational matrices; the isometry and nonsingularity conditions select a subset of this countable set. An integral Seifert lattice is likewise specified by a finite integer matrix. The corresponding presented groups are quotients of the countable sets of finite signed lists of these matrices: finite lists of rationals or integers have explicit natural-number codes, so a countable union over their lengths is countable. Quotients are countable by the surjection from these codes. This argument does not identify the two types of object. Use the injection [F2] to regard $G_{\mathbb Z}$ as a subgroup of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ for the rest of the proof. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 For each primary group of [F3] other than $t+1$, the involution on $E$ is nontrivial. Indeed if its distinguished generator equalled its inverse, its irreducible polynomial would divide $t^2-1$; $t-1$ is excluded by invertibility of $I-T$ and $t+1$ was separated. If $F=E^{\sigma}$, choose $0\ne\delta$ with $\sigma\delta=-\delta$. Every $z\in E$ has the unique decomposition $(z+\sigma z)/2+\delta(z-\sigma z)/(2\delta)$ with coefficients in $F$, so $E/F$ is quadratic. Take all hermitian signatures at real places of $F$ where $E$ becomes complex, and take the ordinary rational signature on the $t+1$ component. These form a homomorphism $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathbb Z$. The index set $J$ is at most countable: there are countably many rational irreducible polynomials and finitely many real places for each number field. Each individual class has only finitely many primary components, so its total signature has finite support. With [A1] fix an enumeration of this index set, adding zero coordinates if needed, to put the target inside $\bigoplus_{n\ge1}\mathbb Z$. [A1, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 If $s(x)=0$, each of the finitely many nonzero primary components of $x$ has all its signatures zero. By [F4] four times each such component is zero; the primary direct-sum isomorphism [F3] gives $4x=0$. Thus $4\ker s=0$. The same holds for the kernel of $s\iota$ on $G_{\mathbb Z}$, since $\iota$ is injective. Applying [F6] separately to these two countable groups gives decompositions of each with at most countable free, order-two and order-four multiplicities. In particular every torsion class has order dividing four; the proof has used signatures to identify all torsion, rather than merely exhibiting some finite-order classes. [F2, F3, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 In either group, the elements $F_b,P_n,Q_q$ of [F5] meet the three infinitude tests of [F6]. A finite nonzero integer combination of the $F_b$ cannot be torsion: if some nonzero multiple vanished, projection to each distinct primary factor would contradict the infinite order of its $F_b$. The $2Q_q$ are independent order-two elements, by distinct primary factors and exact order four. For the rational quotient by doubles, project to the quadratic primary factor of $P_n$, identified with a hermitian Witt group by [F3], and then take hermitian rank modulo two. This is a homomorphism because metabolic hermitian forms have even rank. The two-dimensional rational structure of $P_n$ has rank one over its quadratic field, so the homomorphism takes value one there; it vanishes on the other $P_m$ by their distinct primary factors, and on every double by its target $\mathbb Z/2$. Hence the $P_n$ are independent modulo doubles in $G_{\mathbb Q}$ as well as in $G_{\mathbb Z}$, the latter also following directly from [F5]. Thus the $P_n$ are independent in the quotient by doubles in each group. This last condition forces independent order-two summands after splitting; independent order-two elements alone would not suffice, since doubles of order-four elements also have order two. There are infinitely many indicated primes $q$ by the finite Euclidean argument in [F5]. [F2, F3, F5, F6, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By [F6] and step 4.1, all three multiplicities in both decompositions from step 3.1 are infinite, and their countable upper bounds make them precisely $\aleph_0$. This is the displayed abstract group isomorphism for each of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ and $G_{\mathbb Z}$. The integral result here follows from its proved injection, the shared exponent bound, the splitting argument and the actual integral families. No assertion that primary summands split integrally, no identification of the rational group with its integral subgroup, and no unspecified integral localization or coupling theorem is needed for this abstract isomorphism. In particular the allowed $t+1$ component of the original rational Definition has been retained throughout. [F1, F2, F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement refuted

Assume the Axiom of Choice. The counterexample uses the following category: objects are finite-dimensional rational vector spaces $U$ with a linear involution $S_U:U\to U$ satisfying $S_U^2=1_U$; morphisms $f:U\to W$ are rational-linear maps satisfying $fS_U=S_Wf$, with ordinary addition and scalar multiplication on each morphism space; tensor product has involution $S_U\otimes S_W$, the unit is $\mathbb Q$ with identity involution, and associators and unitors are the usual vector-space maps. The braiding is the ordinary flip $u\otimes w\mapsto w\otimes u$. The chosen left dual of $U$ is $U^*$ with involution $S_{U^*}=(S_U^{-1})^*$, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_U(f\otimes u)=f(u)$, and coevaluation $\operatorname{coev}_U(1)=\sum_i e_i\otimes e^i$ for any basis $(e_i)$ and its dual basis $(e^i)$. The twist is $\theta_U=S_U$. This is a $\mathbb Q$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$. For $X=\mathbb Qe_+\oplus\mathbb Qe_-$ with $S_X=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, the twist is invertible and nonscalar, its one-strand identity ribbon trace is $0$, and its positive two-strand stabilization ribbon trace is $2$. Therefore no nonzero scalar writhe correction works.

## Statement references

[[thm-twist-correction-removes-framing|The scalar-twist theorem and its absolute-simplicity hypothesis]]

[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid|Ribbon trace on a closed braid]]

[[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object|Standard vector-space duality]]

[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism|Drinfeld morphism formula]]

[Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, §§8.9–8.10](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/egnobookfinal.pdf)

[Turaev, *Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds*, Chapter I, §1.5](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/turaev5.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The false claim in the preceding section, the braid trace convention, and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] The ribbon evaluation of an $X$-colored closed braid is $t_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\rho_n(\beta))$ with $j=u\theta$ ([[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]).

[F2] The scalar writhe-correction theorem assumes an absolutely simple color whose twist is the scalar $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\ne0$ ([[thm-twist-correction-removes-framing]]).

[F3] Under the Axiom of Choice, two braids have equivalent oriented closures exactly when related by conjugations, stabilizations, and destabilizations ([[thm-markovs-closed-braid-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F4] A braiding is a natural isomorphism satisfying the two hexagon identities ([[def-braiding]]).

[F5] A ribbon twist is natural, obeys the balancing identity, and is compatible with duality ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]).

[F6] Left-dual evaluation and coevaluation satisfy the two snake identities ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]).

[F7] The Drinfeld morphism is defined by composing coevaluation, the braiding, and evaluation ([[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]).

[F8] The ribbon-induced pivotal comparison $j=u\theta$ is monoidal, with $j_{U\otimes W}=d_{U,W}(j_U\otimes j_W)$ ([[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Counterexample

1.1 Let $\mathcal C$ have objects finite-dimensional rational vector spaces $U$ equipped with a linear involution $S_U$ ($S_U^2=1$), and morphisms commuting with the involutions. Use $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$, the ordinary flip braiding, standard vector-space duality, and define $\theta_U=S_U$. This is a ribbon category: the twist is natural because every morphism commutes with $S$; its tensor rule is $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$ and the double flip is the identity; and on the dual, $S_{U^*}=(S_U^{-1})^T=S_U^T=(\theta_U)^*$, giving ribbon dual compatibility. The unit is $\mathbb Q$ with trivial involution, so $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=\mathbb Q$. By [F7], the Drinfeld morphism in this symmetric vector-space category is the canonical double-dual identification: on $v\in U$ and $f\in U^*$ its evaluation is $u_U(v)(f)=f(v)$. Thus the ribbon-induced pivotal map $j_U=u_U\theta_U$ is the canonical double-dual identification composed with $S_U$. [F1, F4, F5, F6, F7, given, construct]

2.1 Take $X=\mathbb Q e_+\oplus\mathbb Q e_-$ with $S_X=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. It is decomposable and its twist is invertible but nonscalar. For the identity $e\in B_1$, [F1] gives $t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}(S_X)=1+(-1)=0$. For $\sigma_1\in B_2$, the braid action is the flip $P$. By [F8], under the canonical vector-space double-dual comparison, $j_{X\otimes X}$ has matrix $S_X\otimes S_X$, so the trace of $(S_X\otimes S_X)P$ is $2$: the basis tensors $e_+\otimes e_+$ and $e_-\otimes e_-$ contribute diagonal entries $1$, while the two mixed basis tensors are exchanged and contribute no diagonal entries. [F1, F2, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The braid $\sigma_1$ is the positive Markov stabilization of the identity braid in $B_1$, so [F3] says their oriented unframed closures are equivalent. Their exponent sums are $w(e)=0$ and $w(\sigma_1)=1$. For any proposed $\lambda\in\mathbb Q^\times$, the corrected values are $0$ and $2\lambda^{-1}$, which are unequal because $2\ne0$ and $\lambda$ is invertible. This contradicts the false claim. The counterexample has precisely the missing hypothesis identified by [F2]: its invertible twist is not scalar on the decomposable color. [F2, F3, step 2.1, A1, algebra] ∎

        3-Manifolds
      url: https://scholarworks.iu.edu/iuswrrest/api/core/bitstreams/54c7d68f-d982-4e1f-9550-e54140ada5ea/content
      locator: §2.5, printed pp. 16–18 (PDF pp. 24–26)
verification:

## Definition

Let $D^2$ be the oriented closed disk and give $C=D^2\times[0,1]$ the product orientation. An $r$-component string link is an ordered family of pairwise disjoint smooth proper embeddings $\tau_i:[0,1]\to C$, for $1\le i\le r$, with fixed distinct endpoints $\tau_i(0)=(p_i,0)$ and $\tau_i(1)=(p_i,1)$ and fixed product collars at the endpoints. Orient each interval from bottom to top. The exterior $X_\tau$ is obtained by removing the relative interiors of chosen pairwise disjoint product tubes around the intervals. The bottom and top punctured disks $P_-$ and $P_+$ are the copies of $D^2$ with the interiors of the endpoint tube disks removed.

Choose a basepoint on the outer boundary of $P_-$, a path in the side boundary of $C$ to the corresponding top basepoint, and basing paths from these points to the component meridians. Each end inclusion, with the chosen connecting path for the top end, induces a based homomorphism $\iota_\pm:\pi_1(P_\pm)\to\pi_1(X_\tau)$. For each string component choose a parallel path on its tube boundary from the bottom endpoint to the top endpoint, and choose access paths that close it to a based loop using the fixed side connector. The resulting element of $\pi_1(X_\tau)$ is its based string-link longitude; the parallel and access paths are part of the peripheral datum. The positively oriented boundaries of the endpoint tube disks are the designated meridian loops. Stacking two string links means rescaling them into the lower and upper halves of $C$ and identifying their matching endpoint collars; closure joins each top endpoint to the matching bottom endpoint outside $C$ and retains the component labels.

For a nonempty labeled oriented link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ in the oriented three-sphere, choose pairwise disjoint closed product tubes $N(K_i)$, put $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}\bigl(\bigcup_iN(K_i)\bigr)$, and write $T_i=\partial N(K_i)$. A positive meridian $\mu_i$ is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, with the disk orientation fixed by the rule that the oriented tangent of $K_i$ followed by the disk orientation gives the ambient orientation. A degree-one parallel is a simple closed curve on $T_i$ whose projection to $K_i$ has degree $+1$. A based longitude is the class of such a parallel transported to the common basepoint by a specified path. When the positive meridians form a basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$, the self-meridian coordinate of a longitude is its coefficient on $[\mu_i]$. A preferred zero-self-meridian longitude is a chosen degree-one parallel whose self-meridian coordinate is zero. The choice, when it exists, is part of the peripheral datum; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Changing a common basing path conjugates the peripheral group elements simultaneously.

## Definition references

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy|Smooth oriented links in the standard oriented three-sphere]]

[[def-knot-exterior|Chosen tubular exterior and boundary orientation]]

[[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude|Positive meridian and degree-one peripheral curve]]

[[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing|Oriented crossing and framing conventions]]

## Remarks

The product-tube choices, endpoint collars, basepoints, connecting path, labels, and longitude basings are part of the input. The term preferred zero-self-linking longitude names a condition on the peripheral data, not an existence theorem.

## Definition

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. The **enhanced A-polynomial** $\widetilde A_K(M,L)$ is the primitive square-free Laurent polynomial defining the union of one-dimensional peripheral-eigenvalue image components arising from irreducible characters of $\pi_1(E_K)$. It is defined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$. The ordinary A-polynomial is the least common multiple $A_K=\operatorname{lcm}(\widetilde A_K,L-1)$, up to a Laurent unit, where the least common multiple uses each distinct irreducible Laurent factor only once; the factor $L-1$ is the contribution of the abelian character component, and an irreducible component may also contribute that same factor.

## Definition

Use the upper half-space model
$$\mathbb H^3=\{(x+iy,t):x,y\in\mathbb R,\ t>0\},\qquad ds^2=t^{-2}(dx^2+dy^2+dt^2),$$
whose ideal boundary is $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$. An oriented ideal tetrahedron in normalized position has ideal vertices $0,1,\infty,z$, where $\operatorname{Im}z>0$. Its three edge-shape parameters are
$$z,\qquad z'=\frac1{1-z},\qquad z''=\frac{z-1}{z},$$
each assigned to one pair of opposite edges; the parameter at a corner of a truncated ideal vertex triangle is the parameter of the incident edge. For an oriented path $\gamma$ in a triangulated torus link of ideal vertices, its cusp multiplier $H(\gamma)$ is the product of the corner parameters encountered along $\gamma$, using the parameter when the path cuts off that corner on its left and its reciprocal when it cuts off the corner on its right.

## Definition

Use the standard PL three-sphere given by the boundary of a fixed PL four-simplex and the product PL structure on $S^3\times I$. A PL map is a map that is affine on every simplex after finite subdivisions of triangulated domain and target. An oriented PL knot is the image of a PL embedding of an oriented triangulated circle into this PL three-sphere. Two such knots are PL concordant when a PL embedding of a triangulated annulus into $S^3\times I$ has them as its lower and upper boundary circles with boundary orientation $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$, and the embedding is proper, locally flat in the PL category, and has PL product collars at the two boundary circles. PL local-flatness means that each interior pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$ and each boundary pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$. Annuli with cone singularities or other non-locally-flat points are excluded. This definition makes no assertion identifying PL concordance with smooth or locally flat topological concordance.

## Example

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $U$ be the standard unknot, let $T_{2,3}$ be the closure of the positive two-strand braid with three crossings, and let $T_{2,3}^{\dagger}$ be its reverse mirror. In the normalized right-trefoil staircase over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$, generators $a,b,c$ have Maslov gradings $0,-1,-2$, Alexander levels $1,0,-1$, and differential $\partial b=Ua+c$, $\partial a=\partial c=0$; multiplication by $U$ lowers both filtrations by one. Choose the polynomial minus lattice $C^-=\mathbb F_2[U]\langle a,b,c\rangle$ inside this Laurent complex, with each displayed generator at first filtration coordinate zero. Its hat complex is the quotient $C^-/UC^-$; setting $U=0$ refers to this lattice quotient, not to the Laurent complex in which $U$ is invertible. The full reverse-mirror Laurent staircase is the filtered dual, with generators $a^\vee,b^\vee,c^\vee$ at Alexander levels $-1,0,1$ and differential $\partial a^\vee=Ub^\vee$, $\partial c^\vee=b^\vee$, $\partial b^\vee=0$. Its chosen polynomial dual lattice has hat quotient with $\partial c^\vee=b^\vee$ and $\partial a^\vee=\partial b^\vee=0$. The normalized unknot complex has one generator at level zero and zero differential. These models give
$$\tau(U)=0,\qquad \tau(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \tau(T_{2,3}^{\dagger})=-1.$$
Both trefoils have smooth four-ball genus one.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The standard unknot, the positive right-handed trefoil, its reverse mirror, and Countable Choice. The displayed staircases are conclusions to be identified, not additional geometric hypotheses.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] defines the normalized threshold by the first nonzero filtered inclusion into total hat homology.

[F2] [[lem-tau-of-the-unknot-is-zero]] supplies the normalized one-generator unknot complex.

[F3] [[lem-diagonal-five-grid-filtered-staircase-reduction]] supplies the complete finite calculation for the grid $O_r=(r+1/2,r+1/2)$, $X_r=((r+2)\bmod5+1/2,r+1/2)$: its all-variable-zero filtered complex is $S_-\otimes V^{\otimes4}$, where $S_-$ has $(M,A)=(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and only $\partial c=b$. This accepted finite calculation is reused without replaying its matrices.

[F4] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] supplies the normalized full grid comparison, including the ordinary-collapse $V$ factors and associated-graded identification. Its retained closure is used directly, not the historical hold formerly recorded here.

[F5] [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] supplies actual normalized Laurent duality for the reverse mirror and conjugation exchanging the two filtrations. In particular each coordinate hat specialization has total homology $\mathbb F_2$ in normalized degree zero. [[lem-knot-floer-mirror-complex-duality]] supplies the finite hat-dual threshold identity.

[F6] [[thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and-genus]] gives genus $(1-s+c)/2$ for the connected one-boundary-component disk-and-band surface. [[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus]] defines its smooth four-ball minimum.

[F7] [[lem-knot-floer-large-surgery-and-filtered-cobordism-input]] supplies the genus inequality using Hom’s direct $\mathbb F_2$ four-ball genus theorem and a local cut-arc reduction. Apply it to an actual spanning surface punctured near one interior point to obtain $|\tau(K)|\le g$ for that surface. This does not rely on the formerly held movie construction or on an integral-to-mod-two surgery-map inference.

## Proof

1.1 The finite grid in [F3] is an actual negative trefoil diagram. Subtract $1/2$ from the marking coordinates for this projection description. Its row segments are $[0,2]$ in row $0$, $[1,3]$ in row $1$, $[2,4]$ in row $2$, $[0,3]$ in row $3$, and $[1,4]$ in row $4$, with the orientations $O\to X$. Vertical segments run $X\to O$ and pass over. The only interior crossings are $(2,1),(3,2),(1,3)$. Following the single component $O_0\to O_2\to O_4\to O_1\to O_3\to O_0$ encounters them as $A_{\rm over},B_{\rm under},C_{\rm over},A_{\rm under},B_{\rm over},C_{\rm under}$. The first two crossings have upward over-strand and rightward under-strand; the third has downward over-strand and leftward under-strand. Thus all have the same negative sign. Smoothing the degree-two grid corners gives the standard alternating three-crossing negative trefoil projection: each successive over-under pair forms one of the three braid crossings, and its two exterior connecting arcs give the closure. This is the closure of $\sigma_1^{-3}$, with the displayed cyclic traversal fixing its orientation. Reflection gives the positive trefoil convention of the Example. This finite knot admission uses the actual segments, not a deduction of knot type from a Floer polynomial. [F3, given, construct]

1.2 By [F3, F4], the normalized all-variable-zero complex of this negative trefoil is filtered equivalent to both $S_-\otimes V^{\otimes4}$ and $\widehat{CFK}(T^\dagger)\otimes V^{\otimes4}$. Total homology in Maslov degree zero is one-dimensional in both tensor products: every non-top $V$ factor lowers Maslov degree, whereas $H(\widehat{CFK})$ is supported in degree zero. Its first filtered appearance in the first product is $-1$. In the second product its threshold is the threshold in $\widehat{CFK}$: inclusion into the top $V$ summand and projection onto that summand are filtered maps, with composition identity. Hence $\tau(T^\dagger)=-1$. Duality [F5] gives $\tau(T)=1$, independently of the genus inequality. The unknot value is [F2]. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 The same finite calculation also identifies the associated-graded generator ranks needed for the full Laurent staircase. Record bigraded ranks by Laurent polynomials in $m,a$. The associated graded of $S_-$ has one generator in each bidegree $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and zero differential. Thus the accepted associated-graded comparison gives
$$P_{\widehat{HFK}(T^\dagger)}(m,a)(1+m^{-1}a^{-1})^4=(a^{-1}+m+m^2a)(1+m^{-1}a^{-1})^4.$$
Cancel the nonzero factor in the integral Laurent polynomial domain. Duality gives for the positive trefoil exactly one group in each bidegree $(0,1),(-1,0),(-2,-1)$, and no others, over $\mathbb F_2$. This is a mod-two conclusion; no integral rank formula is inferred. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Reduce the actual finite free Laurent complex at its differential terms preserving both coordinates. Normalize each finite basis vector to first coordinate zero. Such a term has coefficient $1$, preserves Alexander grading, and lowers Maslov grading by one. Elementary cancellation of this unit term is bifiltered: the coefficient and its inverse have zero filtration shift, and the usual finite formulas $d'=d-dh d$, $i'=i-hd i$, $p'=p-pd h$ stay in both filtrations. Maslov homogeneity prevents a second, different $U$ power in the same matrix entry. Consequently no power-series inverse is needed. Each cancellation removes two generators, and finite linear changes within a fixed bidegree and these cancellations leave precisely the three generators represented by the associated-graded homology from step 2.1. This gives an actual bifiltered Laurent equivalent complex with generators $a,b,c$ of the Example, rather than promoting a rank polynomial alone to a filtered equivalence. [F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 The only possible differential entries in that reduced positive-trefoil complex, by Maslov degree and the two filtration inequalities, are
$$\partial a=\alpha b,\quad\partial b=\beta Ua+\gamma c,\quad\partial c=\delta Ub,\qquad \alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in\mathbb F_2.$$
In its first-coordinate hat specialization the total homology is one-dimensional. If $\alpha=1$, its surviving class would be $c$ at level $-1$, contrary to step 1.2; if $\alpha=\gamma=0$, the hat homology would have rank three. Hence $\alpha=0$, $\gamma=1$. Squaring the differential gives $\delta=0$. In the other coordinate hat specialization the only possible remaining differential is $b\mapsto\beta Ua$; if $\beta=0$, it would have rank-three homology, contrary to conjugation [F5]. Thus $\beta=1$. This proves the displayed full Laurent staircase. Its dual has $\partial a^\vee=Ub^\vee$, $\partial c^\vee=b^\vee$; after $U=0$ its hat differential is exactly the displayed reverse-mirror differential. [F1, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.1 The oriented smoothing of the positive two-strand three-crossing braid has two circles and three bands. Its surface has genus $(1-2+3)/2=1$. Reflection gives the same for its reverse mirror, and an inward push gives smooth spanning surfaces in the four-ball. Therefore both smooth four-ball genera are at most one. By [F7] every smooth spanning surface has genus at least the absolute value of the independently computed tau invariant, which is one. Thus both genera equal one. [F6, F7, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 This proves all original Example clauses: the actual admitted finite grid and retained comparison/duality supply the invariant-level thresholds and both normalized filtered models, while Hom’s direct $\mathbb F_2$ genus input supplies the matching smooth lower bound. No integral Floer ranks or merely topological genus conclusion has been substituted. [F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.3, step 3.1] ∎
