## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $X$ be a one-dimensional irreducible component of its $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety whose peripheral image is a curve in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$. With Bénard–Florens–Rodau's variable order $A_K(L,M)$ and their slope convention, on the admissible smooth locus where the displayed derivatives are nonzero,
$$s_K(\rho)=-\frac{M}{L}\frac{\partial_M A_K}{\partial_L A_K}.$$
At an ideal point of the curve, if the associated Culler-Shalen surface has boundary slope $r$ measured by $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ with $r=b/a$, the limiting Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is $-r$.

## Statement references

[Bénard, Florens, and Rodau, Theorems 1.3, 1.5, 4.1 and 5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.14151)

[Hatcher, *Boundary Slopes of Incompressible Surfaces*](https://www.math.unl.edu/~mbrittenham2/classwk/990s08/public/hatcher.bdyslopes.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and the ENTIRE original locus in the Statement. The rational extension and the actual specialized homology slope are distinguished; no smaller locus is silently substituted into that Statement.

[F1] The accepted local theorem proves the rational projective logarithmic Gauss identity, its finite affine values, and the conditional peripheral ideal-point limit for the actual stipulated Culler–Shalen construction. Its proof explicitly does not identify every exceptional specialized homology kernel with the rational extension. [[thm-adjoint-logarithmic-gauss-slope-and-ideal-point]]

[F2] The ordered boundary basis is $(v_\rho\otimes\lambda,v_\rho\otimes\mu)$, and a kernel generator $(a,b)$ has slope $-b/a$. Admissibility means the given basis exists and the inclusion kernel is a line; it does not impose dimension one on the exterior cohomology or reducedness of a relator scheme. The rational extension is projective-valued and is not defined to replace every actual admissible homology value. [[def-character-variety-logarithmic-slope-invariant]]

[F3] The actual generic adjoint calculation supplies a generic matrix representation, the rank-one boundary inclusion, all word-cocycle evaluations and common-eigenbasis correction, and specialization compatibility on a nonempty dense rank-chart open. Its field-linear rank and derivation operations are reproduced over the needed finitely generated field in step1.1 rather than assuming a tangent-space identification. [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]]

[F4] Actual representation and common-eigenline incidence varieties are finite type and have finitely many components; affine-domain dimension is function-field transcendence degree. [[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]] [[lem-classical-affine-algebraic-set-finite-irreducible-components]] [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]]

[F5] The ordinary A-polynomial is the square-free Laurent equation for the union of one-dimensional eigenvalue-image components, and is defined up to a Laurent unit. Boundary class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has unoriented slope $b/a$, with $a=0$ interpreted projectively. [[def-knot-a-polynomial]] [[def-boundary-slope-of-an-incompressible-surface]]

[L1] **External input for the exceptional actual-point clause:** Bénard–Florens–Rodau, *A slope invariant and the A-polynomial of knots*, arXiv:2103.14151, Theorem 4.1 (p.15), states the displayed identity for ALL characters on an irreducible component with one-dimensional peripheral image; Remark 4.2 explicitly includes characters not scheme-reduced. Definitions 3.1–3.2 use exactly the actual homology inclusion kernel and slope $-b/a$. This theorem is imported at the admissible locus of the Statement, rather than inferred from generic rational equality. Theorem 5.2 (pp.16–17; introduction Theorem 1.5) supplies the ideal-point interpretation. These statements, definitions, Remark 3.7, Proposition 3.8 and the complete displayed §4–§5 arguments were consulted; their exceptional specialization assertion is used externally and is not represented as a new local proof.

## Proof

1.1 **The image curve is an actual A-component.** This instantiation requires excluding a larger peripheral image component. Take the actual generic matrices on an irreducible common-eigenline incidence chart of [F4], over its finitely generated function field $F$. A two-dimensional image would make $M,L$ algebraically independent and the meridian matrix nonparabolic. Over this field the trace form, cap boundary identity and pair exact sequence in [F3] give boundary dimension two and $2=\dim\ker i_*+\operatorname{rank}i_*=2\operatorname{rank}i_*$; hence its kernel is a line. Every $\mathbb C$-derivation $D$ of $F$ differentiates the actual relators to a cocycle. The explicit word/eigenbasis calculation in [F3] makes $(DL/L,DM/M)$ annihilate that SAME line. Extend $M,L$ to a finite transcendence basis and take its two coordinate derivations. Each extends through the finite algebraic extension to $F$ by $D\alpha=-(Dp)(\alpha)/p'(\alpha)$ at a minimal polynomial $p$; characteristic zero makes the denominator nonzero. Their two logarithmic pairs are independent, a contradiction. Generically reducible representations instead have $L=1$ by knot abelianization and cannot supply a two-dimensional image. Thus every peripheral-image component has dimension at most one. The closed irreducible nonconstant image curve $Y$ in the Statement is contained in their finite union, so it equals one of the one-dimensional components: a proper closed subset of an irreducible affine curve has dimension zero. Consequently [F5] supplies its defining Laurent factor $P$ in the full ordinary polynomial. No omitted two-dimensional component is presumed absent merely from the A-polynomial Definition. [F3, F4, F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 **Variable order and sign.** Keep $M$ the meridian eigenvalue and $L$ the longitude eigenvalue. Writing $A_{\mathrm{BFR}}(L,M)=A_{\mathrm{library}}(M,L)$ only changes the order in which the arguments are displayed. Differentiation with respect to the NAMED variables therefore gives the same meridian derivative and the same longitude derivative, not their reciprocal. In the basis [F2], the generic kernel of $(a,b)\mapsto a\,dL/L+b\,dM/M$ has generator $(-dM/M,dL/L)$, so its slope is $(dL/L)/(dM/M)$. This fixes both the sign and the order of the quotient. A common invariant-vector rescaling changes neither coordinate ratio. Swapping the common eigenline inverts $M,L$ and changes both logarithmic differentials by minus one, preserving the projective ratio; [F3] already proves model/conjugation independence. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 **Full-polynomial versus component derivatives.** Write $A=uPB$, where $u$ is a Laurent unit and $B$ is the product of the other distinct factors. At a point of $Y$ with both full derivatives nonzero, $B$ cannot vanish: if another factor vanished, every term of either product derivative would contain a vanishing factor, giving zero. On $P=0$ one has $A_M=uB P_M$ and $A_L=uB P_L$. Thus the two component derivatives are nonzero there and the common nonzero factor $uB$ cancels from their quotient. Multiplication of the whole representative by any further Laurent unit has the same effect, since its differentiated unit term is multiplied by $A=0$. This also proves that the stated derivative locus is intrinsic and avoids intersections of distinct peripheral factors. It does not exclude an extra character component with CONSTANT peripheral image at the same point. [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The complete rational instantiation.** The component formula in [F1] is $s^{\mathrm{rat}}=[-MP_M:LP_L]$. Combining steps1.2 and2.1 gives exactly $s^{\mathrm{rat}}=-M A_M/(L A_L)$ in the native BFR variable order wherever the displayed derivatives are nonzero. In particular it is finite there, and the projective extension still retains zero/infinity away from that affine locus. This instantiates the proved component theorem with the FULL square-free ordinary polynomial without changing either convention. It is so far an identity of the rational extension, not a proof about all exceptional actual kernels. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Actual homology on the proved dense open.** Intersect the nonempty rank-chart open supplied by [F3] with the original smooth/derivative locus, whenever that latter locus is nonempty. The component is irreducible, so this intersection is dense and nonempty. At every point there, the finite homology specialization in [F3] identifies the rational line with the actual ordered peripheral inclusion kernel. Thus step3.1 proves the ACTUAL displayed formula on this open. This uses the direct generic/rank-chart construction, not an unverified extension of the separate rationality lemma beyond its stated dense scheme-smooth hypothesis. It does not assert that every smooth admissible point belongs to the chosen rank chart. [F2, F3, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

4.2 **The full stipulated ideal-point clause.** The curve in the preceding clause is the peripheral eigenvalue curve $Y$. Use its normalized smooth completion, exactly as in [F1], rather than replacing it by an arbitrary character ideal point with affine peripheral image. At its stipulated ideal point the actual local DVR has nonzero valuation pair $(v(L),v(M))$, and the finite representation-field valuation extends with one positive ramification factor. For a boundary circle $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ of the actual associated Culler–Shalen construction, [F1]'s inverse-image midpoint and boundary-preserving compression argument gives $a v(L)+b v(M)=0$. The logarithmic projective limit in [F1] is $[v(L):v(M)]=[-b:a]$. By [F2] this is $-b/a=-r$, including zero and infinity in the projective convention. This proves the ENTIRE conditional ideal-point clause: the construction/surface is stipulated by the original conditional, and no existence theorem for an arbitrary unrelated surface is imported or required. [F1, F2, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **The actual exceptional-point clause uses the external theorem.** A reducible representation has longitude eigenvalue $L=1$ because its diagonal characters factor through the knot abelianization. Since $A=(L-1)Q$, its meridian derivative is $A_M=(L-1)Q_M$ and vanishes at every such peripheral point. The stipulated nonzero-derivative locus therefore contains only irreducible characters. At every actual admissible smooth point of that locus, including points outside the local rank chart, apply the ALL-character formula of the external Theorem 4.1 in [L1], in the actual homology convention of its Definitions 3.1–3.2. Steps1.2 and2.1 identify the named variables, signs and full square-free representative. This proves the first clause at its entire original locus; the exceptional specialization is supplied externally, not by a density argument. [F2, F5, L1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

6.1 Step4.2 already proves the full conditional ideal-point assertion with the stipulated associated surface; [L1]'s Theorem 5.2 independently gives the same valuation and sign convention. Together with step5.1 this establishes both original clauses without narrowing the admissible smooth locus or adding scheme-smoothness. [F1, L1, step 4.2, step 5.1] ∎

## Statement

For the rank-eight lattice $L_{E_8}$ with Gram matrix $C$ specified in its definition, the form is positive definite, has determinant $1$, and takes even values on every vector. It has no vector of squared norm $1$, so it is not isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ and admits no isometric full-rank embedding into that lattice.

## Statement references

[[def-e8-root-lattice|The E8 Gram matrix and node-edge convention]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Gram matrix $C$ with diagonal entries $2$ and off-diagonal entries $-1$ on the seven stated edges.

[F1] The ordered basis and full list of E8 edges determine the Gram matrix $C$. [[def-e8-root-lattice]]

[F2] A full-rank unimodular sublattice of the standard dot-product lattice of the same rank has index one. [[lem-full-rank-unimodular-sublattice-has-index-one]]

## Proof

**Given:** The matrix and lattice convention in [F1].

1.1 Let $A_7$ be the $7\times7$ leading principal block on vertices $1,\ldots,7$. Its leading principal determinants $d_k$ satisfy $d_0=1$, $d_1=2$, and $d_k=2d_{k-1}-d_{k-2}$ for $2\le k\le7$, by expansion along the last row of the tridiagonal chain matrix. Induction gives $d_k=k+1$, so these seven determinants are positive. [F1, algebra, induction]

1.2 The vector $x=A_7^{-1}e_3$ has coordinates $x_i=\min(i,3)(8-\max(i,3))/8$ for $1\le i\le7$: substitution into $2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}=\delta_{i3}$ with $x_0=x_8=0$ verifies $A_7x=e_3$. Hence $e_3^{\mathsf T}A_7^{-1}e_3=15/8$. The Schur-complement determinant of $C=\begin{pmatrix}A_7&-e_3\\-e_3^{\mathsf T}&2\end{pmatrix}$ is $\det(A_7)(2-15/8)=8/8=1$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 By Sylvester's criterion, the positive leading principal determinants $d_1,\ldots,d_7$ from step 1.1 and $\det C=1$ from step 1.2 make $C$ positive definite. For any $z\in\mathbb Z^8$, $z^{\mathsf T}Cz=2\sum_i z_i^2-2\sum_{\{i,j\}\text{ an edge}}z_i z_j$ is even. Every nonzero vector therefore has positive even integral norm, hence norm at least $2$; in particular there is no norm-one vector. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 The standard lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ contains norm-one basis vectors, so no isometry from $L_{E_8}$ onto $\mathbb Z^8$ exists by step 2.1. If there were an isometric full-rank embedding, its Gram determinant would be $1$ by step 1.2, and [F2] would force its image to be all of $\mathbb Z^8$, which would be an isometry, again contradicting step 2.1. [F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

([[thm-balanced-knot-full-minus-auxiliary-continuations-are-filtered-equivalences]], [[thm-pointed-heegaard-floer-invariance-under-moves-and-stabilization]], [[lem-pointed-basepoint-cone-and-variable-collapse]])

[F4] The normalized doubly pointed total zero-w hat homology is one-dimensional in Maslov degree zero. Analytic conjugation identifies its Alexander-associated-graded homology in degrees (m,a) and (m-2a,-a), independently of any grid comparison. Its Alexander origin is the negative modified-Morse field with zero-relative-Euler Seifert cap, hence the stated half-Chern pairing. ([[lem-relative-s-three-maslov-gradings-have-a-unique-hat-homology-normalization]], [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]], [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]])

[F5] The grid is admissible. The grid algorithm's full and associated-graded rectangle matrices square to zero and have the stated variable actions. ([[lem-grid-diagram-is-admissible]], [[lem-grid-rectangle-differential-squares-to-zero]], [[alg-grid-knot-floer-complex]])

## Proof

1.1 Use the standard genus-one splitting of the oriented three-sphere: the horizontal circles bound parallel meridian disks in one solid torus, and the vertical circles bound parallel meridian disks in the other; their primitive meridians meet once. Taking all n parallel disks cuts each side into n balls. The row and column marking condition puts one O and one X in every corresponding cut ball. Push the horizontal O-to-X segments into the lower side and the vertical X-to-O segments into the upper side, using their evident rectangular bridge disks. These simultaneous arcs give exactly the oriented knot of the grid, since every vertical segment passes over every horizontal segment. Thus this is an actual balanced 2n-pointed diagram of K, not only an abstract torus count. Its analytic symmetric rank is $1+n-1=n$, and w=O,z=X. Give it the actual flat integrable data of [F1]. The identity on states identifies its full polynomial count matrix with the algorithmic one. [F1, F5, given, construct]

2.1 Check the remaining good-endpoint condition before applying [F3]. Positivity gives a nonnegative domain D for every actual integrable strip. Its index $n_x(D)+n_y(D)$ is nonnegative. If it is zero, every cell touching either state has coefficient zero. The local equation $\Delta D=1_x-1_y$ then forces x=y, since at any changed vertex the four coefficients would have nonzero alternating sum. Consequently $\Delta D=0$, and telescoping its row and column differences gives $D_{ij}=a_i+b_j$. Because x is one point in every row and column, the n cells immediately northeast of its state points have total coefficient $\sum_i a_i+\sum_j b_j=0$. The sum of ALL cell coefficients is n times that sum, hence zero. Nonnegativity gives D=0. The actual ordered-root energy bound is then zero, so the strip is constant. Therefore no nonconstant index-at-most-zero strip exists. Finiteness, index-one regularity and square zero were already supplied by [F1,F5]; no index-two regularity of this special integrable path is assumed. The precise endpoint hypotheses of [F3] hold. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Apply the actual full-minus auxiliary and diagram equivalences of [F3] to this endpoint. They identify its chosen-action restriction with a doubly pointed full complex, and identify its ordinary collapse with that complex tensor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$. They also give the quotient-by-all-variables and associated-graded identities by specializing the actual finite maps and homotopies. At this stage use ONLY the relative formulas of [F1]: on the connected state set, its numerical J-gradings differ from the transported normalized analytic origins by one integer Maslov constant b and one integer Alexander constant c. In particular, if H denotes normalized doubly pointed associated-graded zero-U homology, the grid tilde homology has the relative identification $H\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ with common shifts (b,c). This constructs the comparison before determining either shift; no assertion of the theorem under proof is a premise. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix b without using Alexander centering. List the O markings in order of increasing row, with distinct column indices $o_0,\ldots,o_{n-1}$. Replace X by $X^*$ having in row i the column $o_{i+1}$, with cyclic indices. This is disjoint from O and is a one-component grid: its marking permutation sends row i to row i+1. Its vertical segments join successive row heights, except for the one segment from the last row to the first. The short vertical segments meet no other horizontal height, so every crossing lies on that sole long vertical segment, which passes OVER the complementary embedded planar arc. This is an unknot: raise the long segment into an upper ball and lower the complementary planar arc into a lower ball; both are boundary-parallel arcs, with the rectangular upper bridge disk and the planar lower bridge disk. Match their boundary chords on the separating plane and join the two disks along that chord to obtain an embedded spanning disk, rounding its finite corners. The FULL unfiltered rectangle matrix and M_O do not depend on X, so replacing X by $X^*$ changes neither this matrix nor its Maslov grading. By the purely combinatorial graded chosen-action equivalences and move generation in [F2], this same unfiltered complex is graded equivalent to a size-two unknot grid. In that grid the two states have M_O=0,-1; direct rectangle enumeration gives the cone $\mathbb F_2[U_1,U_2]\xrightarrow{U_1+U_2}\mathbb F_2[U_1,U_2]$ with source degree -1 and target degree zero. The monic polynomial retraction in [F3] evaluates the other variable at the chosen one, so after quotienting that chosen U its total homology is one-dimensional in M_O degree zero. The combinatorial inverse homotopies specialize too, so this is true for the original grid's chosen-action total zero-U complex. Step 3.1 compares it to the analytic total hat homology, whose normalized degree is zero by [F4]. Its common Maslov shift is therefore b=0. This also proves nontriviality without treating the Alexander-associated-graded complex as total hat homology. [F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Fix c by a finite reciprocal symmetry. Define the finite Laurent polynomial $P_G(t)=\sum_x(-1)^{M_O(x)}t^{A_G(x)}$ and put $D_n(t)=(1-t^{-1})^{n-1}$. The Euler characteristic of a finite bigraded complex equals that of its homology degree by degree: split each finite degree into boundaries, a homology complement and a complement mapped isomorphically to boundaries; the latter pairs cancel with opposite Maslov signs. Thus [F2] implies that $Q_G=P_G/D_n$ is unchanged by every grid move, as a rational function: commutation preserves P and stabilization multiplies P by $1-t^{-1}$, precisely the Euler polynomial of V. Construct $G^T$ by transposing the square and INTERCHANGING O and X. The ambient rotation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(y,x,-z)$ has determinant plus one and changes old vertical overpasses to new horizontal underpasses. An old horizontal O-to-X arc becomes a new vertical X-to-O arc; an old vertical X-to-O arc becomes a new horizontal O-to-X arc. Hence it carries the SAME oriented knot to $G^T$, rather than a mirror or assumed orientation reversal. Both grids have size n, so [F2] gives $P_{G^T}=P_G$. Transposition preserves the strict pair relation defining J, while mark exchange swaps M_O and M_X. The literal formulas are therefore $A_{G^T}(x^T)=-A_G(x)-(n-1)$ and $M_{O^T}(x^T)=M_O(x)-2A_G(x)-(n-1)$. Since A_G is integral, their signs give $P_G(t)=(-1)^{n-1}t^{-(n-1)}P_G(t^{-1})$. Using $D_n(t^{-1})=(-1)^{n-1}t^{n-1}D_n(t)$ yields $Q_G(t)=Q_G(t^{-1})$. This derives reciprocity from actual J formulas and purely combinatorial moves; no analytic grading identification or unproved Alexander determinant formula has been used. [F1, F2, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Write $Q_H(t)=\sum_{m,a}(-1)^m\dim H_{m,a}\,t^a$. This is a finite Laurent polynomial. By [F4]'s ACTUAL conjugation, $H_{m,a}$ is isomorphic to $H_{m-2a,-a}$. The degree difference is even, hence $Q_H(t)=Q_H(t^{-1})$. For clarity, this symmetry is supplied by the normalized analytic coordinate-swap map: on the vertical corner $(i,j)=(0,a)$ it lands on the horizontal corner $(a,0)$, and multiplying by $U^a$ identifies that corner with $(0,-a)$ and lowers Maslov degree by 2a. It is a map of the corner subquotients, not a declaration that the full positive-z hat differential preserves A. Moreover $Q_H(1)=1$. Indeed the associated graded and total zero-U doubly pointed complexes have the same finite chain groups with their Maslov degrees, so their ordinary Euler characteristics coincide; the latter has exactly one homology class of normalized degree zero. Therefore Q_H is NONZERO. The relative comparison in step 3.1 and b=0 now give $P_G=t^c D_n Q_H$, or $Q_G=t^c Q_H$. Substituting the two reciprocal identities yields $(t^c-t^{-c})Q_H=0$ in the Laurent polynomial domain $\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$. Since Q_H is nonzero, c=0. This is precisely the missing absolute combinatorial Alexander anchor, with no appeal to grid equality to establish its own shift. [F3, F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 The identity in step 1.1 and the actual analytic equivalences in step 3.1 consequently preserve both normalized origins, by steps 4.1 and 5.1. Compose with [F3]'s normalized comparison to the diagram H in the Statement; its inverse and inverse homotopies remain finite and filtered. Taking the Alexander associated graded of these identities gives the claimed associated-graded minus equivalences. Each term retains every individual O weight until the explicitly stated restriction or quotient. The ordinary collapse and all-variable-zero associated-graded specialization are exactly the two actual constructions of [F3], yielding respectively $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ and $\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$, with the displayed bidegrees now absolutely centered. The chosen-action restriction yields $CFK^-(K)$ instead. Composing the comparisons for two grids gives their normalized filtered equivalence and inverse homotopies. Finally [F4] identifies the preserved Alexander origin with the zero-framed capped-Seifert half-Chern expression of the Statement. Its cap and negative-Morse convention are inherited from that supplier, not replaced by a winding-number convention. Every original conclusion follows with all positive z terms and all stated scalar distinctions retained. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. Then $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(-1)\ne0$, and in that case
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)|=|\Delta_K(-1)|.
$$
Moreover, $\Delta_K(-1)$ is odd, so the first homology of every double branched cover is finite.

## Statement references

[[lem-double-branched-cover-homology-from-seifert-matrix|The double-cover homology presentation by $V+V^T$]]

[[lem-square-integer-cokernel-finiteness-and-order|The determinant criterion for a square integer presentation]]

[[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial|The Seifert determinant represents the Alexander polynomial]]

[[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization|The integer Laurent-polynomial normalization $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$]]

[[def-oriented-seifert-surface|The definition and genus convention for a Seifert surface]]

[Rolfsen, *Knots and Links*, Chapter 8.D](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/rolfsen.pdf)

[[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface|Existence of a connected compact oriented Seifert surface for every knot]]

[[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups|The compact surface normal form and free fundamental group]]

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert matrix convention]]

[[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization|First homology is the abelianization of the fundamental group]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and a smooth oriented knot $K$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by the cyclic branched-cover definition and Seifert determinant presentation. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For a positive-push Seifert matrix $V$, $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(V+V^T)$. [[lem-double-branched-cover-homology-from-seifert-matrix]]

[F2] The cokernel of a square integer matrix is finite exactly when its determinant is nonzero, and then its order is the absolute determinant. [[lem-square-integer-cokernel-finiteness-and-order]]

[F3] $\det(V-tV^T)$ represents $\Delta_K(t)$ up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F4] $\Delta_K(t)$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$. [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]]

[F5] Full AC supplies the countable-choice hypotheses used by the surface-existence and surface-normal-form results: apply its choice function to the range of any sequence of nonempty sets and reuse the selected element at each index. Thus the sequence assertions in [[def-countable-choice]] and [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]] hold. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F6] Every smooth oriented knot bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with its given boundary, which is a Seifert surface under [[def-oriented-seifert-surface]]. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]]

[F7] For a connected compact oriented surface with one boundary component and genus $g$, the fundamental group is free of rank $2g$. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F8] A connected smooth surface $F$ is locally path-connected, so its path components are open and it is path-connected. The first Hurewicz map identifies $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with the abelianization of $\pi_1(F)$; for the genus-$g$ surface in [F7], this gives $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2g}$ and an ordered integral basis. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the Statement and Facts & Assumptions. By [F5]--[F8], choose a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface $F$ with oriented boundary $K$ and an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix as defined in [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], and put $D(t)=\det(V-tV^T)$. [A1, F5, F6, F7, F8, given, choose]

1.1 By [F1], the double-cover homology is presented by the square integer matrix $V+V^T=V-(-1)V^T$. Its determinant is $D(-1)$. By [F2], the homology is finite exactly when $D(-1)\ne0$, and then its order is $|D(-1)|$. The hypothesis needed by [F1] is the Axiom of Choice in [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F3], $D(-1)=\pm(-1)^k\Delta_K(-1)$ for some integer $k$, so $|D(-1)|=|\Delta_K(-1)|$ and the zero tests agree. This proves the finiteness criterion and order formula. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write $\Delta_K(t)=\sum_{r=m}^n c_rt^r$ with integers $c_r$ and finitely many terms. Since $(-1)^r\equiv1\pmod2$ for every integer $r$, including negative $r$, [F4] gives $\Delta_K(-1)\equiv\sum_rc_r=\Delta_K(1)\equiv1\pmod2$. Thus $\Delta_K(-1)$ is odd and nonzero; step 1.1 then gives finiteness for every knot. [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ of an oriented link $L$ realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link: $c(D)=c(L)$.

## Statement references

[Calegari, *Introduction to Knot Theory*, §5.2](https://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/notes/knot_theory.pdf)

[Kauffman, *New Invariants in the Theory of Knots*, §III](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1988__163-164__137_0.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, an oriented link $L$, and a connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ representing it.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects from every countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The crossing number is the least crossing count among regular diagrams of the underlying unoriented link ([[def-crossing-number-of-link]]).

[F2] A disconnected projection represents a split link ([[lem-disconnected-link-diagram-represents-a-split-link]]).

[F3] A connected alternating diagram represents a nonsplit link ([[lem-connected-alternating-link-is-nonsplit]]).

[F4] Every connected reduced alternating diagram has bracket span $4c(D)$, and every connected diagram $E$ has bracket span at most $4c(E)$ ([[lem-connected-diagram-bracket-span-bound-and-alternating-equality]]).

[F5] The normalized bracket is an oriented link invariant under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

[F6] A reduced alternating diagram is connected and alternating by definition ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]]).

## Proof
1.1 Let $E$ be any regular diagram representing the same underlying unoriented link type as $L$. If its projection were disconnected, [F2] would make $L$ split, contradicting [F3] applied to $D$ and [F6]. Hence every competing diagram $E$ is connected. Orient each component of $E$ so an ambient isotopy to $L$ preserves its orientation. [given, F2, F3, F6, choose, contradiction]

2.1 By [F4], $\operatorname{span}_A\langle D\rangle=4c(D)$ and $\operatorname{span}_A\langle E\rangle\le4c(E)$. The normalized bracket multiplies each raw bracket by a monomial, which shifts all exponents equally and preserves span. By [A1] and [F5], the normalized bracket values for the oriented diagrams $D$ and $E$ agree. Therefore $4c(D)\le4c(E)$ and $c(D)\le c(E)$. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The diagram $D$ is one of the regular diagrams in the nonempty crossing-count set of [F1], so $c(L)\le c(D)$. Step 2.1 shows that $c(D)$ is no larger than any member of that set, and therefore $c(D)\le c(L)$. Combining the inequalities proves $c(D)=c(L)$. [F1, step 2.1, choose] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, the common normalized filtered knot Floer threshold $\tau(K)$ is independent of the admissible diagram and is invariant under smooth concordance. For all smooth oriented knots $K,J$, it satisfies
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$
If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$|\tau(K)|\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K).$$

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The normalized filtered threshold defining tau]]

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth concordance with product collars]]

[[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus|The smooth four-ball genus]]

[[lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid|The diagram and grid comparison needed for a knot invariant]]

[[lem-knot-floer-large-surgery-and-filtered-cobordism-input|The genus shift for smooth knot cobordisms]]

[[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product|The filtered tensor product for connected sums]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Knot Floer homology and the four-ball genus*, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0301149v4)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §§3.1–3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

[Ozsvath, Stipsicz, and Szabo, *Grid Homology for Knots and Links*, Chapters 6, 8, and 13](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~petero/GridHomologyBook.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, smooth oriented knots, and the standard normalized filtered knot Floer models.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] states that every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function; this is the axiom branch used by the slice-genus minimum and the finite diagram choices.

[F1] [[lem-tau-of-the-unknot-is-zero]] computes the normalized tau value of the standard unknot as zero.

[F2] [[lem-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus-minima-exist]] proves that the nonempty set of smooth slice-surface genera has a least element under its stated countable-choice branch.

[F3] [[lem-puncturing-smooth-four-ball-surfaces-gives-genus-preserving-knot-cobordisms]] moves an interior point of a smooth properly embedded genus-$g$ four-ball surface to zero, flattens it near zero by supported ambient isotopies, and removes a sufficiently small actual round ball. The explicitly concentric shell is $S^3\times[0,1]$ and the residual surface is a connected genus-$g$ smooth cobordism with product collars between its boundary knot and a standard unknot. It fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar, not an arbitrary entire collar.

[F4] The normalized knot/grid and analytic comparisons supply diagram independence, the actual hat threshold, and common absolute Alexander normalization. [[lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid]]

[F6] The genus-$g$ inequality $|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g$ is supplied for the actual smooth oriented knot cobordism with its product collars. Its proof cuts the cobordism along an arc to obtain a genus-$g$ spanning surface for $K_1\#(-K_0)$, then applies Hom’s direct $\mathbb F_2$ four-ball genus theorem and the local connected-sum/mirror identities. It does not infer mod-two nonvanishing from an integral surgery map. [[lem-knot-floer-large-surgery-and-filtered-cobordism-input]]

[F5] The full supplied filtered connected-sum tensor comparison gives tau additivity in the same normalization. [[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product]]

## Proof

1.1 By [F4] the diagramwise threshold defines a single invariant $\tau(K)$, and [F5] proves $\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J)$. Apply [F6] to a smooth genus-zero concordance to obtain $|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le0$, hence equality. These give diagram independence, concordance invariance and connected-sum additivity in the original normalization. The geometric input is the explicitly imported $\mathbb F_2$ genus theorem together with the local cut-arc construction in [F6], not a conclusion inferred solely from absolute grading. [F4, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 Let $g=g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ and choose a smooth genus-$g$ surface realizing the minimum by [F2]. Apply [F3] to this actual embedded surface. Its supported ambient diffeomorphism fixes the boundary knot, flattens the surface near the center, and permits removal of a sufficiently small concentric round ball. The explicit round shell contains the residual connected genus-$g$ cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot $U$, with the required product collars. No complement of an arbitrary embedded chart ball is identified with a standard shell. The supplied inequality [F6] gives $|\tau(K)-\tau(U)|\le g$; by [F1], $\tau(U)=0$, yielding the desired bound. This proves the genus bound for the chosen minimizing surface and therefore for the minimum genus. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F6, given, construct, algebra] ∎

## External-input boundary

The original Statement follows from the displayed local deductions and the accepted model/tensor interfaces. Its geometric genus inequality uses Hom’s explicitly coefficient-qualified $\mathbb F_2$ genus theorem and the local cut-arc reduction recorded in [F6]. No full-AC hypothesis or general movie theorem is substituted. The puncturing argument retains the actual concentric-shell and smaller-collar conventions.

## Statement refuted

Every abstract oriented cobordism between two oriented knot circles in the standard three-sphere can be realized by a smoothly embedded concordance annulus in $S^3\times[0,1]$.

## Statement references

[[def-abstract-oriented-knot-cobordism|Abstract oriented cobordisms of knot circles]]

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth embedded annulus concordance]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The standard unknot $U$, the standard right-handed trefoil $T$, and the claim in the Statement refuted.

[F1] An abstract oriented cobordism is a compact oriented surface with boundary $-C_0\sqcup C_1$ and contains no ambient embedding data. ([[def-abstract-oriented-knot-cobordism]])

[F2] The Seifert matrix convention in the library is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ for a chosen oriented surface and basis; the surface and basis are part of the data until invariance is proved. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F3] A trefoil Seifert surface admits a rank-two Seifert matrix whose symmetric sum is $\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}$; if the cited convention uses the transpose matrix, the symmetric sum is unchanged. For a real symmetric matrix, its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues. (Collins, Theorem 2.2.9 and Example 2.2.13, https://era.ed.ac.uk/bitstream/handle/1842/5034/Collins2011.pdf?sequence=4)

[F4] The standard unknot bounds a disk in $S^3$; the disk is contractible, so its first homology is zero and its symmetrized Seifert form has signature $0$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F5] A metabolizer for a rank-two integral Seifert form is a rank-one direct summand $L$ with $V(x,y)=0$ for $x,y\in L$. Thus every nonzero $x\in L$ satisfies $x^T(V+V^T)x=2V(x,x)=0$. This is immediate from the defining bilinear relation, with no signature-invariance or general signature-vanishing theorem. ([[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]])

[F6] Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, a knot is smoothly slice if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. ([[lem-smooth-slice-iff-concordant-to-unknot]])

[A1] Full Axiom of Choice is assumed by the supplied Seifert-pairing definition. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Full Axiom of Choice implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by [F6]. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

[F7] For a smooth slice disk, the actual smooth branch of [[lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer]] constructs a metabolizer for every specified smooth Seifert surface: its Proof1.1–2.2 uses the actual smooth hypersurface and positive product constructed in Proof1.1–7.1 of [[lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-seifert-hypersurface]]. The separate unresolved TOP branches are not used here. This direct finite-form obstruction needs neither surface-choice invariance nor a general signature-vanishing theorem.

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct finite-form obstruction using the proved smooth slice-to-metabolizer branch.

1.1 Let $C_0$ be the oriented circle underlying $U$ and $C_1$ the oriented circle underlying $T$. Take the abstract annulus $S^1\times[0,1]$ and identify its lower and upper boundary circles orientation-preservingly with $C_0$ and $C_1$, orienting the annulus so its boundary is $-C_0\sqcup C_1$. By [F1] this is an abstract oriented cobordism from $U$ to $T$. [F1, given, construct]

2.1 For the fixed trefoil matrix in [F3], $$V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}.$$ Its characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2+4\lambda+3=(\lambda+1)(\lambda+3)$, so its eigenvalues are $-1,-3$ and its signature is $-2$. More directly, for $x=(a,b)\ne0$ over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$,
$$x^T(V+V^T)x=-2(a^2-ab+b^2)=-(a-b)^2-a^2-b^2<0.$$
Consequently $V$ cannot have a rank-one metabolizer: a nonzero vector in one would have zero value by [F5]. This is a calculation for the displayed Seifert surface and basis; no knot-level signature invariance is being inferred. The unknot's rank-zero form in [F4] still has signature zero. [F2, F3, F4, F5, A1, algebra]

3.1 If $U$ were smoothly concordant to $T$, reverse the interval coordinate to obtain smooth concordance of $T$ to the unknot. By [F6] and [A2], $T$ would bound a smooth proper disk. Apply the proved smooth branch [F7] to the particular trefoil Seifert surface in [F3]. It gives a rank-one metabolizer for $V$, contradicting the strict negative-definiteness calculation and [F5] in step 2.1. Thus the displayed abstract oriented annulus has no realization as a smooth concordance between its specified endpoint knots, refuting the claimed universal realization. No locally flat TOP slice-to-metabolizer assertion is used. [A2, F3, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$. The parameter and Cartan-generator conversion from Korinman's convention is $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$; the root generators $E,F$ correspond unchanged. The vector basis order remains $(v_+,v_-)$. Korinman displays $\rho(E)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\rho(F)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$; converting those displayed action matrices to the column-action convention used here transposes them. Thus the module matrices are
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. The parameters $q_K$ and $q_L$ are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Korinman's §2.2 matrix
$$C_K=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix}$$
is an equivariant map $V^*\to V$ in its indicated dual and vector bases. It is a duality isomorphism, not an endomorphism of $V$, so it is not the matrix of $\Omega^{-1}$.

To specify the half-ribbon action, use the Snyder–Tingley convention $q_{\mathrm{ST}}=q_K$, $K_{\mathrm{ST}}=K_K=K_L^{-1}$, $E_{\mathrm{ST}}=E$, and $F_{\mathrm{ST}}=F$ in the same ordered basis. Since $q_K=\omega^{-4}$, choose $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$. Let $X=JT_{w_0}$ be their half-ribbon element and let $\Omega$ be its operator on $V$. On the fundamental highest- and lowest-weight vectors, their formula gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. The half-ribbon action therefore gives the actual inverse matrix and its square:
$$\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Omega^2=-\omega^{-6}\operatorname{id}_V=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V.$$
Snyder–Tingley’s associated Hopf-algebra ribbon element is $X^{-2}$; the positive categorical twist in this Kauffman-bracket convention is its inverse $X^2=\Omega^2$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.

## Definition references

[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra|Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra presentation]]

[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra|Library coproduct convention]]

[[def-absolutely-simple-object|Absolute simplicity]]

[[def-braiding|Braiding definition]]

[[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure|Ribbon twist definition]]

[[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object|Left-dual maps and snake identities]]

[Korinman, *Finite presentations for stated skein algebras and lattice gauge field theory*, §2.2](https://msp.org/agt/2023/23-3/agt-v23-n3-p05-p.pdf)

[Snyder and Tingley, *The half-twist for $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ representations*, §§3–5](https://msp.org/ant/2009/3-7/ant-v3-n7-p04-p.pdf)

[Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, §§8.3, 8.9–8.10](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/egnobookfinal.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The generic parameter $A$, the basis $(v_+,v_-)$, and the two explicitly distinguished parameters $q_K=A^2$ and $q_L=A^{-2}$.

[F1] The Drinfeld–Jimbo presentation has $K E K^{-1}=q^2E$, $K F K^{-1}=q^{-2}F$, and $EF-FE=(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ case ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F2] In the library convention, $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K\otimes F$, and the antipode is $S(E)=-EK$, $S(F)=-K^{-1}F$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

[F3] A braiding is a natural isomorphism $c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\to Y\otimes X$ satisfying the two hexagon identities ([[def-braiding]]).

[F4] A ribbon twist is a natural automorphism satisfying $\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and compatible with duality ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]).

[F5] Korinman's full-text §2.2 gives the generic two-dimensional module, its duality isomorphism $C_K:V^*\to V$, the positive braiding matrix, and the Kauffman-bracket quantum dimension $-q_K-q_K^{-1}$; the parameter, Cartan-generator, and column-action conversions used here are stated in the Definition ([Korinman, §2.2](https://msp.org/agt/2023/23-3/agt-v23-n3-p05-p.pdf)).

[F6] Snyder–Tingley Lemma 3.10 computes the action of $X=JT_{w_0}$ on highest- and lowest-weight vectors; Theorems 3.11 and 5.2 establish its standard braiding and half-ribbon structure, with associated Hopf-algebra ribbon element $v=X^{-2}$ satisfying $\Delta(v)=(v\otimes v)(R_{21}R)^{-1}$ ([Snyder–Tingley, §§3, 5](https://msp.org/ant/2009/3-7/ant-v3-n7-p04-p.pdf)).

[F7] Absolute simplicity means $\operatorname{End}(V)=k'\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]).

[F8] A left dual has evaluation $V^\vee\otimes V\to\mathbf1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf1\to V\otimes V^\vee$ satisfying both snake identities ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data in the Definition.

1.1 The displayed $E,F,K_K$ satisfy the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations: conjugating $E$ by $K_K$ multiplies its only nonzero entry by $q_K^2$, conjugating $F$ multiplies its only nonzero entry by $q_K^{-2}$, and $EF-FE=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)=(K_K-K_K^{-1})/(q_K-q_K^{-1})$, with nonzero denominator since $q_K-q_K^{-1}=\omega^{-4}-\omega^4\ne0$ in $k'$. Replacing $(q_K,K_K)$ by $(q_L,K_L)=(q_K^{-1},K_K^{-1})$ leaves the commutator quotient unchanged and gives the stated library toral relations. The coproduct conversion in the Definition is exactly [F2] after this substitution. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 Any $U_{q_K}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-endomorphism of $V$ commutes with $K_K$, whose distinct eigenvalues force it to be diagonal in $(v_+,v_-)$. Commuting with $E(v_-)=v_+$ forces the two diagonal entries to agree. Thus $\operatorname{End}(V)=k'\operatorname{id}_V$, which is [F7]'s absolute-simplicity condition. [F7, given, algebra]

1.3 In Korinman's convention the positive braiding is $P D(1+(q_K-q_K^{-1})E\otimes F)$, where $P$ is the flip and $D=\operatorname{diag}(A,A^{-1},A^{-1},A)$ in the displayed tensor basis. Since $E^2=F^2=0$, $(E\otimes F)^2=0$ and the source $q$-exponential truncates after its linear term. Applying this operator to the four basis vectors gives, in order, $A v_+\otimes v_+$, $A^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+$, $A^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-+(A-A^{-3})v_-\otimes v_+$, and $A v_-\otimes v_-$. These are exactly the columns of the displayed matrix; [F6] supplies the half-ribbon completion in which this finite action is a braiding. [F3, F5, F6, given, algebra]

1.4 The bilinear map $B$ and vector $U(1)$ are $U_{q_K}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ intertwiners. The $K_K$-weights in each nonzero pairing and coevaluation term multiply to $1$. For the only nonzero $E$-pairing, $\Delta(E)(v_-\otimes v_-)=q_K^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+$, whose $B$-value is $q_K^{-1}-q_K^{-1}=0$; the other basis inputs give zero or a multiple of $v_+\otimes v_+$, also killed by $B$. For $F$, the only nonzero check is $\Delta(F)(v_+\otimes v_+)=v_-\otimes v_++q_K^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-$, whose $B$-value is $-q_K^{-1}+q_K^{-1}=0$. On coevaluation, $\Delta(E)$ sends $-q_Kv_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+$ to $-q_Kv_+\otimes v_++q_Kv_+\otimes v_+=0$, and $\Delta(F)$ sends it to $-q_Kv_-\otimes v_-+q_Kv_-\otimes v_-=0$; the $K_K$-weight is zero. Since these checks hold on the generators and $\Delta,\varepsilon$ are algebra maps, they establish invariance of $B$ and $U$ for every algebra element. The Hopf identity $\sum x_{(1)}\otimes x_{(2)}S(x_{(3)})=x\otimes1$ then gives $B(xv,w)=\sum B(x_{(1)}v,x_{(2)}S(x_{(3)})w)=\sum\varepsilon(x_{(1)})B(v,S(x_{(2)})w)=B(v,S(x)w)$. Thus $\phi(v)=B(v,-)$ intertwines the stated contragredient action. Its matrix from $V$ to $V^*$ has nonzero determinant $A^{-2}$, so it is an isomorphism. Transporting the standard coevaluation $1\mapsto v_+\otimes v_+^*+v_-\otimes v_-^*$ by $\phi^{-1}$ gives exactly the displayed $U$. The snake composites are identities: $(B\otimes1)(1\otimes U)$ returns $v_+$ and $v_-$ with coefficients $B(v_+,v_-)=1$ and $(-A^2)B(v_-,v_+)=1$, respectively, while $(1\otimes B)(U\otimes1)$ returns them with coefficients $(-A^2)B(v_-,v_+)=1$ and $B(v_+,v_-)=1$. By [F8], these are the defining left-dual identities. The closed loop is $B(U(1))=-A^2-A^{-2}=\delta$. Thus these maps give the stated self-duality and quantum dimension. [F2, F5, F8, given, algebra]

2.1 For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, the fundamental highest weight $\lambda$ satisfies $(\lambda,\lambda)=1/2$, $(\lambda,\rho)=1/2$, and $\langle2\lambda,\rho^\vee\rangle=1$. Snyder–Tingley’s formula [F6] therefore gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. With $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$, this yields $\operatorname{Mat}(\Omega)=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega^{-3}\\-\omega^{-3}&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\operatorname{Mat}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose square is $\Omega^2=-A^3I$. The Hopf ribbon identity in [F6] gives $\Delta(v^{-1})=(v^{-1}\otimes v^{-1})R_{21}R$; since the monodromy $R_{21}R$ is $c_{Y,X}c_{X,Y}$, this inverse acts as the categorical twist for the balancing convention in [F4]. Thus the positive categorical twist is $v^{-1}=X^2=\Omega^2$. [F4, F6, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

## Example

Fix an FWI velocity-model solver $\mathcal S$ with a declared finite admissibility predicate $\operatorname{adm}_{\mathcal S}(v)$ that checks that solver's coefficient, boundary, mesh, and time-step conditions, including its solver-specific Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) condition. If an optimization method proposes a candidate velocity map $\widetilde v$ with $\operatorname{adm}_{\mathcal S}(\widetilde v)=\mathrm{false}$, the benchmark records the call as a solver/admissibility failure and does not assign a data-fit or reconstruction score to that iterate. In its FWI DAPS experiment, InverseBench reports that a smaller learning rate gave numerically stable but data-ineffective outputs, while a slightly larger learning rate produced a noisy velocity map that violated the PDE solver's CFL condition and failed. The paper gives no exact violating iterate or universal CFL threshold; this example claims neither.

## Example references

[[def-ip-benchmark-risk-and-compute-budget|Failed solver calls remain visible in benchmark results]]

[[def-ip-pde-solver-admissibility-contract|An admissibility predicate and CFL condition are solver-specific]]

[[rem-ip-inversebench-scoped-findings|The step-size/CFL observation is empirical and task-scoped]]

[Zheng et al., *InverseBench*, §4.3 and Figure 3](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/e297068f5ec7f483a017948715b591fb-Paper-Conference.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

      url: "https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/rolfsen.pdf"
      locator: "Chapter 8.D, printed pp. 212–214; double-cover matrix and general cyclic-cover presentation"
    - title: "Jozef H. Przytycki and Akira Yasuhara, Linking Numbers in Rational Homology 3-Spheres, Cyclic Branched Covers and Infinite Cyclic Covers"
      url: "https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0111203v1"
      locator: "Section 3, printed pp. 12–14; block matrix M_{q,V}, whose surgery presentation is attributed to Akbulut–Kirby"
---

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and choose any ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $M_q(V)$ be the symmetric block matrix of size $2g(q-1)$ whose $2g\times2g$ block in position $(k,\ell)$, for $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$, is $V+V^T$ if $k=\ell$, $-V^T$ if $\ell=k+1$, $-V$ if $k=\ell+1$, and $0$ if $|k-\ell|\ge2$. Then
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(M_q(V)).
$$
For $q=2$ this presentation matrix is $V+V^T$; when $g=0$ the empty matrix has trivial cokernel.

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-seifert-surface|Connected compact oriented spanning surfaces and their genus]]

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert matrix convention]]

[[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined|Bilinearity and basis-change behavior of the Seifert pairing]]

[[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface|The framed-link matrix of the branched 4-manifold]]

[[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot|The exterior cover and filling that define $\Sigma_q(K)$]]

[[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality|Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for the handlebody pair]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$, an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, its positive-push matrix $V$, and $q\ge2$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the cyclic-cover and duality suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The cover $\Sigma_q(K)$ is the boundary of the $q$-fold branched cover of $B^4$ along a push-in of $F$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]], [[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface]]

[F2] For the disk-band basis, that 4-manifold has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, with intersection matrix $M_q(V)$. [[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface]]

[F3] Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)$ by capping with the relative fundamental class. [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]

[F4] The homology long exact sequence of the pair $(W,\partial W)$ is exact. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]]

[F5] The Seifert pairing is bilinear on homology classes; changing an integral basis by $P\in\operatorname{GL}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$ changes its matrix to $P^TVP$. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the Statement and Facts & Assumptions. First use the disk-band basis from the surgery construction, and write $Y=\partial W=\Sigma_q(K)$ and $m=2g(q-1)$.

1.1 The handle decomposition in [F2] has cellular chain groups $C_2(W;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^m$, $C_1(W;\mathbb Z)=0$, and $C_0(W;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$. Hence $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^m$, $H_1(W;\mathbb Z)=0$, and $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^m$. By [F3], $H_2(W,Y;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^m$ as well. [A1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 In the handle bases, the map $j:H_2(W;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(W,Y;\mathbb Z)$ sends each absolute handle class to its intersection coordinates with the relative dual handle classes. A diagonal coordinate is the handle framing, and an off-diagonal coordinate is the linking of the corresponding attaching circles; by [F2] this matrix is $M_q(V)$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given, construct]

3.1 The pair sequence [F4] contains $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{j}H_2(W,Y;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_1(W;\mathbb Z)=0$. By [F1], $Y=\partial W=\Sigma_q(K)$. Exactness and step 2.1 therefore give $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(M_q(V))$ in the disk-band basis. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For any other ordered integral basis, [F5] gives $V'=P^TVP$ with $P$ unimodular. Let $P_q=\operatorname{diag}(P,\ldots,P)$ with $q-1$ diagonal blocks. Blockwise substitution in the definition shows $M_q(V')=P_q^TM_q(V)P_q$. Left and right multiplication by unimodular integer matrices preserve the isomorphism class of the cokernel, so the presentation holds in the stated basis. For $q=2$ the block matrix has the single block $V+V^T$, and for $g=0$ it is empty. [F5, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1853
    - title: "Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §6.2.3"
      url: https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~rn289/Site/__files/FULLPDF.pdf

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For each $n$, let $G_{n,1},\ldots,G_{n,m_n}$ be independent standard normal random variables, and let $w_{n,j}\ge0$ satisfy $2\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}^2=1$. If $\max_{1\le j\le m_n}w_{n,j}\to0$, then
$$T_n=\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}(G_{n,j}^2-1)$$
has mean zero and variance one for every $n$ and converges in distribution to $N(0,1)$.

## Statement references

[Ingster, Sapatinas and Suslina, *Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems*, §4.1, equations (4.2)–(4.3)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1853)

[Giné and Nickl, *Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models*, §6.2.3, Gaussian white-noise signal detection](https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~rn289/Site/__files/FULLPDF.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; for each $n$, independent standard normal coordinates $G_{n,j}$; nonnegative weights with $2\sum_jw_{n,j}^2=1$ and $\max_jw_{n,j}\to0$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is the hypothesis of the Lindeberg–Feller supplier.

[F1] [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: for $G\sim N(0,1)$, $\mathbb E G^2=1$ and $\mathbb E G^4=3$; hence $V=G^2-1$ has mean $0$, variance $2$, and finite second moment.

[F2] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: an independent centered triangular array with positive row standard deviations and the Lindeberg condition has its normalized row sums converging in distribution to $N(0,1)$.

[F3] [[thm-dominated-convergence]]: an integrable dominating function allows limits to pass through the expectation.

## Proof

1.1 By [F1], each $V_{n,j}=G_{n,j}^2-1$ is centered with variance $2$. Independence within each row gives $\mathbb E T_n=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}(T_n)=2\sum_jw_{n,j}^2=1$. Thus the row standard deviation is $s_n=1>0$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Fix $\delta>0$ and put $w_n^* =\max_jw_{n,j}$. If $w_{n,j}=0$, its Lindeberg summand is zero. Otherwise $w_{n,j}|V_{n,j}|>\delta$ implies $|V_{n,j}|>\delta/w_n^*$. Therefore $$\sum_j\mathbb E\!\left[w_{n,j}^2V_{n,j}^2\mathbf1_{\{w_{n,j}|V_{n,j}|>\delta\}}\right]\le \frac12\mathbb E\!\left[V^2\mathbf1_{\{|V|>\delta/w_n^*\}}\right].$$ Because $w_n^*\to0$ and $V^2$ is integrable by [F1], the right side tends to zero by [F3]. This is the Lindeberg condition for the array $w_{n,j}V_{n,j}$. [given, F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The array in step 2.1 is centered and independent within rows, has finite second moments, and has row standard deviation $1$. By [F2] and the Lindeberg condition just proved, $T_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

    - title: Ryan Stees, Milnor’s Invariants for Knots and Links in Closed Orientable
        3-Manifolds
      url: https://scholarworks.iu.edu/iuswrrest/api/core/bitstreams/54c7d68f-d982-4e1f-9550-e54140ada5ea/content

## Statement

Use integral homology. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ be a nonempty labeled oriented smooth link in $S^3$ with chosen pairwise disjoint product tubes and exterior $E_L$. Then $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, with the positive meridians as its ordered basis. Each boundary torus $T_i$ has a product basis consisting of its positive meridian and a degree-one section. There is a unique degree-one class on $T_i$ whose image has zero $i$th meridian coordinate; this class is primitive and has a simple closed representative.

Let $\tau$ be an $r$-component string link with chosen disjoint product tubes in $D^2\times[0,1]$, exterior $X_\tau$, and bottom and top punctured disks $P_-$ and $P_+$. Then each $\pi_1(P_\pm)$ is free of rank $r$. Positive endpoint meridians with the compatible accesses transported from a point-punctured-disk spine form an ordered free basis. For arbitrary independently chosen access paths, the corresponding meridian is $c_i m_i c_i^{-1}$, where $m_i$ is the compatible-stem meridian and $c_i$ is the recorded access-path difference; these conjugates need not be a free basis. In particular $H_1(P_\pm;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, and $H_2(P_\pm;\mathbb Z)=0$. The exterior satisfies $H_1(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$ and $H_2(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)=0$. Each end inclusion sends its ordered positive meridian basis to the ordered positive meridian basis of $H_1(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)$. Consequently both induced homomorphisms on $H_1$ are isomorphisms and both induced homomorphisms on $H_2$ are surjective.

## Statement references

[[def-based-string-link-and-labeled-link-peripheral-system|Chosen string-link tubes, ends, and meridian orientations]]

[[thm-excision-for-singular-homology|Relative homology excision]]

[[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology|Long exact sequence of a pair]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The link and string-link tube data specified in the statement.

[F1] Excision identifies relative homology after removing a subset whose closure lies in the interior of the subspace. [[thm-excision-for-singular-homology]]

[F2] Each pair of spaces has its long exact singular-homology sequence, natural for maps of pairs. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]]

[F3] A circle has $H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$; $S^3$ has $H_1(S^3;\mathbb Z)=H_2(S^3;\mathbb Z)=0$. [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]

[F4] The tube and positive-meridian orientations are those in the based peripheral definition. [[def-based-string-link-and-labeled-link-peripheral-system]], [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]

[F5] The fundamental group of a wedge of $r$ circles is free on the $r$ once-around loops. [[thm-fundamental-group-of-finite-wedge-of-circles]]

[F6] Homotopic maps induce the same singular-homology map, and a point has homology $\mathbb Z$ in degree zero and zero in higher degrees. [[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]], [[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]]

[F7] The cellular chain complex computes singular homology for CW complexes and cellular maps. [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]

[F8] A disk with finitely many point punctures has the homotopy type of a wedge of circles, with a compatible positive meridian free basis, by the explicit rotation, shear, radial and vertical retractions. No choice axiom is assumed. [[lem-a-finitely-punctured-disk-retracts-to-a-wedge-of-circles]]

[F9] The degree-one Hurewicz map is the abelianization map; in particular loop concatenation adds homology classes and conjugation leaves them unchanged, without any choice axiom. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

## Proof

**Given:** The chosen tubes and oriented meridian conventions.

1.1 Let $P=D^2\setminus\bigcup_i\operatorname{int}D_i$ be either endpoint surface. The supplied product tubes parametrize the pairwise disjoint endpoint disks by $\phi_i:D^2\to D_i$, with $\phi_i(0)=p_i$. Put $Q=D^2\setminus\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$. On $D_i\setminus\{p_i\}$ write a point as $\phi_i(ru)$ with $0<r\le1$, $|u|=1$, and set $$R_t(\phi_i(ru))=\phi_i(((1-t)r+t)u).$$ Put $R_t=\mathrm{id}$ outside the interiors of these disks. At $r=1$ the formulas agree, so finite pasting gives a deformation retraction $Q\to P$. This uses the supplied disk coordinates, not a triangulation of an arbitrary smooth planar region. A collar of the outer unit circle misses all $p_i$. In its radial coordinate a continuous inward push, equal to the identity off that collar, gives a homotopy inverse to $\operatorname{int}D^2\setminus\{p_i\}\hookrightarrow Q$; throughout the homotopy no puncture is crossed. By [F8] the open punctured disk has a finite circle-wedge model and a positive meridian free basis. Transfer it across these displayed equivalences, changing basepoint along the recorded collar path when needed. Small loops about $p_i$ become the positive endpoint meridians: the annulus $\phi_i(ru)$ carries their orientation to the tube boundary. The accesses are the jointly transported stem paths of that finite spine; their images need not be arbitrary preselected accesses. If $a_i$ and $a_i'$ are compatible and arbitrary accesses to the same meridian circle, then $c_i=a_i'a_i^{-1}$ is a based loop and $a_i'\mu_i(a_i')^{-1}=c_i(a_i\mu_i a_i^{-1})c_i^{-1}$. Thus independent basings conjugate generators, without asserting they remain a free basis. Conjugation leaves their homology classes unchanged by [F9]. The homotopy type and abstract free rank are unchanged. [F4, F5, F8, F9, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 For a closed link, enlarge each solid torus tube by a small radial collar and apply [F1] to the pair $(S^3,E_L)$; the collar deformation retracts the enlarged-tube pair to $(S^1\times D^2,S^1\times S^1)$. The product torus has a CW structure with one vertex, two edges, and one face attached by a commutator, so [F7] gives $H_1(S^1\times S^1)\cong\mathbb Z^2$ with meridian and section basis. The solid torus retracts to its core circle, so [F3, F6] give $H_2(S^1\times D^2)=0$ and $H_1(S^1\times D^2)\cong\mathbb Z$, with the meridian mapping to zero and the section to a generator. The pair sequence [F2] therefore identifies $H_2(S^1\times D^2,S^1\times S^1)$ with the kernel generated by the meridian. Excision gives $H_2(S^3,E_L)\cong\mathbb Z^r$. By [F2] and [F3], the boundary homomorphism $H_2(S^3,E_L)\to H_1(E_L)$ is an isomorphism. Each relative generator is a normal disk and its boundary is the positive meridian by [F4]. Hence the positive meridians form the ordered basis of $H_1(E_L)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F7, construct]

2.1 Let $D_i^+$ be disjoint disks slightly larger than the removed endpoint tube disks. The closed complement of their interiors lies in the interior of $P$ relative to $D^2$. By [F1], $H_*(D^2,P)$ is the direct sum of the relative groups of the $r$ disk pairs $(D_i^+,D_i^+\setminus\operatorname{int}D_i)$. Radial collars identify each pair with $(D^2,S^1)$. By [F2], [F3], and [F6], the relative group of this disk pair is $\mathbb Z$ in degree $2$ and zero in every other degree. Its boundary map sends the relative disk to the positive endpoint meridian. Applying [F2] to $(D^2,P)$, with $D^2$ contractible by radial contraction, therefore gives $H_1(P)\cong\mathbb Z^r$ with that basis and $H_2(P)=0$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 For each string component, enlarge its chosen product tube by a small radial collar. The complement of these enlarged tubes has closure in the interior of $X_\tau$; excising it by [F1] reduces $(D^2\times[0,1],X_\tau)$ to the disjoint union of tube pairs. In each pair, the radial collar deformation retracts the pair to $([0,1]\times D^2,[0,1]\times S^1)$: the endpoint cap annuli retract to their boundary circles and the lateral shell retracts to the original tube boundary. Contracting the interval factor identifies this pair with $(D^2,S^1)$. By [F2], [F3], and [F6], each pair has relative homology $\mathbb Z$ in degree $2$ and zero in every other degree. Therefore $H_2(D^2\times[0,1],X_\tau)\cong\mathbb Z^r$ and its relative homology vanishes in degrees $1$ and $3$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, given, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 The ambient cylinder is contractible, so its positive-degree homology vanishes by [F6]. Its pair long exact sequence from [F2], together with step 3.1, gives $H_2(X_\tau)=0$ from the segment $H_3(B,X_\tau)\to H_2(X_\tau)\to H_2(B)$, and gives an isomorphism $\partial:H_2(B,X_\tau)\to H_1(X_\tau)$ from the segment $H_2(B)\to H_2(B,X_\tau)\xrightarrow{\partial}H_1(X_\tau)\to H_1(B)$. Thus $H_1(X_\tau)\cong\mathbb Z^r$. [F2, F6, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For each endpoint, map the pair $(D^2,P)$ into $(B,X_\tau)$ using the endpoint disk and its product tube. Naturality of the connecting map in [F2] sends the relative class of the $i$th endpoint disk to the relative cross-sectional disk class of the $i$th tube. By step 4.1 those classes map to the ordered basis of $H_1(X_\tau)$. By step 2.1 their boundaries are the positive meridian basis of $H_1(P_\pm)$. Each end inclusion therefore induces the asserted $H_1$ isomorphism. Since $H_2(P_\pm)=H_2(X_\tau)=0$, it also induces the asserted $H_2$ epimorphism. [F2, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 The product torus $T_i$ has $H_1(T_i)\cong\mathbb Z^2$ with basis the positive meridian and the chosen degree-one section. Write the image of the section in the basis from step 1.2 and let $k_i$ be its $i$th coordinate. Subtracting $k_i$ times the meridian gives the unique degree-one class with zero $i$th coordinate. Its coordinates in the product basis are $(-k_i,1)$, so it is primitive; the curve $t\mapsto(e^{2\pi it},e^{-2\pi i k_i t})$ in product coordinates is an embedded representative. [F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra, construct] ∎

## Remarks

The diagram illustrates compatible access paths for $r=3$. Step 1.1 uses the supplied disk-coordinate retraction and the explicit finite punctured-disk spine, not this drawing or an unproved smooth triangulation.

## Statement refuted

Assume full AC. Let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil and let $S=T\#T^\dagger$ be the square knot in the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. The universal converse assertion “if a knot has nonunit Alexander polynomial, then it is not topologically slice” is false: $S$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard unit four-ball $B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ whose squared radial function has only index-$0$ and index-$1$ interior critical points, while $\Delta_S(t)\doteq(t^2-t+1)^2$. Here $\doteq$ means equality up to a unit of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$; those units are exactly $\pm t^k$, and the displayed polynomial has nonzero terms in degrees $0$ through $4$, so it is not a unit. A knot is topologically slice when it bounds a locally flat disk in $B^4$, and every smooth proper disk is locally flat. The trefoil itself also has nonunit Alexander polynomial, but this fact alone only places it outside the hypothesis of the Alexander-one sufficient theorem and proves no nonsliceness claim about the trefoil.

## Statement references

[[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars|Smooth proper disks are locally flat topological disks]]

[[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix|The right-handed trefoil's positive-push Seifert matrix]]
