## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a path-connected CW complex and let $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$.
For any based classifying map $c:X\to BG$ inducing the identity on fundamental
groups, the induced homomorphism
$$c_*:H_2(X;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_2(BG;\mathbb Z)=H_2(G;\mathbb Z)$$
is surjective.

## Statement references

[McCleary, §8bis.2](https://pages.vassar.edu/mccleary/files/2011/04/MC08bis.fin_.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a path-connected CW complex $X$, a basepoint $x_0$, and
$G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$.

[A1] Full AC, written AC, is [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[L1] Full AC implies DC: apply AC to the family of nonempty successor sets of a serial relation, choose an initial element, and iterate the resulting choice function. [[def-dependent-choice]]

[F1] Under AC, $BG$ is a connected CW model with $\pi_1(BG)\cong G$ and
$\pi_k(BG)=0$ for $k>1$. [[cor-classifying-space-of-a-discrete-group-is-a-k-g-one]]

[F2] The long exact sequence of a Serre fibration computes the homotopy groups
of its fiber. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-homotopy-groups-of-a-fibration]]

[F3] The homological Serre spectral sequence gives the exact five-term sequence
for the homology of a fibration. [[thm-homological-serre-spectral-sequence]],
[[thm-five-term-exact-sequence-of-a-first-quadrant-homological-spectral-sequence]]

[F4] A simply connected path-connected space has zero first homology by the
degree-one Hurewicz theorem. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F5] Under AC there is a connected CW model $K(G,1)$, and under DC its homology with trivial coefficients is the bar-model group homology. [[thm-existence-and-homotopy-uniqueness-of-eilenberg-maclane-spaces]], [[lem-diagonal-bar-coinvariants-compute-group-homology]], [[def-dependent-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data above and [A1].

1.1 By [F1, F5], choose a connected CW classifying-space model $BG$. Define a based map on the one-skeleton of $X$ sending its loops to
loops in $BG$ that represent the same elements of $G$. Each two-cell attaching
loop then maps to the identity in $\pi_1(BG)$, so its map extends over the disk.
For every cell of dimension at least three, its attaching sphere extends
because the corresponding higher homotopy group of $BG$ vanishes. AC supplies
the simultaneous cellwise extensions. The resulting based map $c:X\to BG$
induces the identity on $\pi_1$. [A1, F1, given, construct]

1.2 Replace $c$ by its mapping-path Serre fibration $p:E\to BG$. The total
space $E$ is homotopy equivalent to $X$. The homotopy long exact sequence [F2]
shows that the fiber $F$ is path-connected and has
$\pi_1(F)=\ker(\pi_1(c))=1$. Hence $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)=0$ by [F4]. [F1, F2,
step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 By [A1] and [L1], the DC hypothesis in [F5] holds, so $H_2(BG;\mathbb Z)=H_2(G;\mathbb Z)$. Apply [F3] to $F\to E\to BG$. Its five-term sequence has consecutive
terms
$$H_2(E;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_2(BG;\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow H_0(BG;H_1(F;\mathbb Z)).$$
The last group is zero by step 1.2. Exactness therefore makes the first map
surjective. Under the homotopy equivalence $E\simeq X$, this first map is
$c_*$, proving the assertion. [A1, L1, F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $\pi_1(X)=0$. Its integral intersection lattice on $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ is a finite-rank free abelian group and its intersection pairing is unimodular.

## Statement references

[[def-integral-intersection-lattice-of-a-simply-connected-four-manifold|The integral intersection lattice and its pairing convention]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold $X$ with trivial fundamental group.

[F1] The first Hurewicz map identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the abelianization of $\pi_1(X)$; in particular it is zero here. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F2] Poincaré duality for a closed oriented four-manifold gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{PD}:H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$, whose inverse sends a homology class to its cohomological dual. [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]]

[F3] The universal-coefficient exact sequence for cohomology is $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(X;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)\to H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(X;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)\to0$. [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]

[F4] A closed smooth manifold has finite CW homotopy type under full AC, so its integral homology groups are finitely generated. [[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]

[F5] The definition of the integral intersection pairing is the Poincaré-duality cup-product pairing on $H_2$ modulo torsion. [[def-integral-intersection-lattice-of-a-simply-connected-four-manifold]]

[A1] Full AC is assumed; it supplies the CW homotopy-type result [F4] and the stated cohomological duality/UCT branch.

## Proof

**Given:** The data and suppliers [F1]–[F5].

1.1 By [F1] and [A1], $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)=0$, so the Ext term in [F3] is zero and evaluation identifies $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(X;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$. [given, F1, F3, A1, algebra]

1.2 By [F4] and [A1], $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated. Its quotient $L=H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ is therefore free of finite rank, and every homomorphism from $H_2$ to $\mathbb Z$ factors uniquely through $L$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(H_2,\mathbb Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb Z)$. [F4, A1, algebra]

2.1 Under the isomorphism [F2], the map $L\to\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb Z)$ sending $\bar x$ to $(\bar y\mapsto Q_X(\bar x,\bar y))$ is the composite of the inverse Poincaré-duality map $H_2\to H^2$ with the evaluation map of [F3]; [F5] identifies that composite with the intersection pairing. Both component maps are isomorphisms by steps 1.1–1.2 and [F2]. Hence the pairing map is an isomorphism. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $K_0$ and $K_1$ are concordant in the smooth category and $J_0$ and $J_1$ are concordant in the same category, then $K_0\#J_0$ and $K_1\#J_1$ are smoothly concordant. The same implication holds when both given concordances and the resulting concordance are required to be locally flat and topological.

## Statement references

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth concordance annuli]]

[[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance|Locally flat topological concordance annuli]]

[[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot|The oriented connected sum]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, concordance annuli $A$ from $K_0$ to $K_1$ and $B$ from $J_0$ to $J_1$ in one of the two categories.

[F1] Each annulus is proper, has product collars at its endpoint knots, and has boundary orientation $-K_0\sqcup K_1$ or $-J_0\sqcup J_1$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]], [[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance]])

[F2] The oriented connected sum is obtained by deleting short trivial arcs and gluing with the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map; its class is independent of the local choices under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $S^3$ is simply connected, continuous homotopies into a smooth manifold can be smoothly approximated relative to a closed region where they are already smooth, finite-dimensional smooth perturbations can be chosen transverse, and isotopies of compact smooth sources extend ambiently in a boundaryless target with support in any prescribed neighborhood of their tracks. In the isotopy-extension construction, the velocity extension may be prescribed to be zero on a closed subtrack where the input isotopy is stationary, so that subtrack is fixed pointwise. Smooth submanifolds have tubular neighborhoods. ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F4] Ambient-isotopic oriented knot representatives may be changed by smooth families of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$. A chosen point on a knot can be moved to any prescribed point by an isotopy of embeddings of that point, which extends ambiently under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F5] Bare locally flat proper arcs with specified product end collars can be straightened by [[thm-locally-flat-codimension-three-arc-unknotting]]. This retained local result is not being strengthened into a relative transverse pair-tube or complement theorem.

[F6] **External TOP input, initially in ordinary ZFC:** connected sum descends to locally flat topological concordance classes of smooth oriented knots represented by proper annuli in $S^3\times I$. Donald and Owens, §2, Lemma 2.3 and proof, establish well-definedness by taking connected sum along the concordance annulus; §4, Theorem 4.1 and proof, state the locally flat TOP version and identify the topological knot concordance group as a direct summand. The paper gives the annulus construction as a proof sketch, not a detailed pair-tube proof. Ray, §3, Definition 3.5 and discussion through Proposition 3.6, also states the TOP concordance group, while explicitly saying the group claim is asserted but not proved there. We use the well-defined TOP operation as an external input, not as a locally reconstructed annulus-adapted tube/complement argument. For the collared annuli of [F1], it implies that the two given concordances yield an oriented locally flat annulus between the endpoint connected sums. The compact real-code/$L[r]$ specialization below addresses the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis; it does not enlarge the external input's geometric scope.

[F7] **External set-theoretic input:** for a real $r\subseteq\omega$, the relativized constructible class $L[r]$ is a transitive inner model of ZFC containing $r$ and all natural numbers. Karagila, §8.3, closing remarks, printed p.42, gives the $L[A]$ construction and its inner-ZFC conclusion; for a real parameter, $r\subseteq\omega\subseteq L[r]$, so the parameter belongs to that model. No ambient full AC is assumed by this input. The compact coding argument below, rather than an implication from ambient full AC, supplies the Countable Choice specialization of [F6].

## Proof

**Given:** The two annuli $A,B$ and the fixed connected-sum convention.

1.1 First consider smooth concordances. Pick one point on each endpoint knot. By [F4], apply separate endpoint ambient isotopies carrying both marked points to a common point $p\in S^3$; extend them over disjoint product collars of the concordance and interpolate by the identity between the collars. This changes the representatives only within their ambient-isotopy classes. Choose a smooth spanning arc in each annulus joining the marked points and fixed in product collars. For one annulus, write this arc as $\alpha$ and the standard product arc as $\beta(s)=(p,s)$. Since $S^3\times(0,1)$ is simply connected by [F3], the middle portions of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are homotopic rel endpoints after their common endpoint collars are deleted. Relative smooth approximation in [F3] gives a smooth homotopy $H(s,t)$ fixed on those collars. We now perturb this homotopy through a finite-dimensional family. First, local coordinate bumps whose $s$-derivatives span the four target coordinates at each zero of $\partial_sH$ make the total derivative family transverse to the zero section of the rank-four tangent bundle; its source has dimension two, so a generic parameter has $\partial_sH\ne0$ everywhere. Compactness then supplies a uniform $\delta>0$ for local injectivity of every slice when $|s-s'|<\delta$. On the compact configuration set $|s-s'|\ge\delta$, use two disjoint source-supported coordinate bumps near each pair to vary $H(s,t)$ and $H(s',t)$ independently. A finite cover of the possible diagonal preimage makes the total pair map transverse to the diagonal in $(S^3\times I)^2$. Its source-pair-time dimension is three and the diagonal has codimension four, so the generic slice has no double points. Both perturbations are supported away from the endpoint collars and can be chosen small enough to preserve immersion and local injectivity. Thus every time-slice is a smooth embedding, giving an isotopy of proper arcs rel collars. The isotopy is stationary on common source end collars, so restrict to the compact middle arcs containing its moving part; these lie in $S^3\times(0,1)$, a boundaryless smooth manifold. Apply [F3] there with support in the interior, choosing the extension to fix the adjacent stationary arc collars, and extend it by the identity across the fixed end collars. This gives an ambient isotopy of $S^3\times I$ fixed near both end levels and carrying the whole spanning arc to the vertical product arc without changing the concordance or its oriented endpoint knot types. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, construct, choose]

2.1 For each vertical arc, double the ambient product across its two boundary levels by gluing to a second copy of $S^3\times I$, and glue a second copy of the concordance annulus using its product collars. The doubled ambient manifold is $S^3\times S^1$ and the doubled annulus is a smooth embedded torus. Doubling the spanning arc across its endpoints gives a smooth embedded circle $C$ in that torus. Apply the tubular-neighborhood theorem to the closed torus in $S^3\times S^1$ and to $C$ inside the torus. Over $C$, the normal line of $C$ in the torus and the rank-two normal bundle of the torus in the ambient manifold are trivial, so their product gives a neighborhood $D^1\times D^2\times S^1$ of $C$ whose intersection with the torus is exactly $D^1\times S^1$. Restrict to the half corresponding to the original arc; this gives the required product neighborhood $D^3\times I$ meeting the original annulus exactly in $D^1\times I$, with product end faces from the collars. Removing the interior of this strip from each annulus leaves a rectangle. Remove the two product neighborhoods from two copies of $S^3\times I$ and glue their boundary cylinders $S^2\times I$ by the fixed product identification. At each level this glues two three-balls along their boundary spheres, giving $S^3\#S^3\cong S^3$; since the gluing is independent of the interval parameter, the resulting ambient cobordism is $S^3\times I$. Glue the two surface rectangles across the two side intervals in the connecting cylinder, choosing the side identifications to extend the orientations on the cut annuli. At the lower end the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map joins the incoming arcs with boundary orientation $-(K_0\#J_0)$; at the upper end the same product convention gives $K_1\#J_1$. The result is connected, orientable, has two boundary circles, and has Euler characteristic $0$ (two rectangles, each of Euler characteristic $1$, glued along two intervals); hence it is an annulus. The product collars give the required smooth concordance. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 The preceding construction proves the smooth implication. [step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 For the TOP implication, first code the actual input as compact metric data. Parametrize the two annuli by the standard compact annulus, and choose finitely many local pair charts covering each, together with their inverses and the given end-collar maps. Such a finite selection is possible by compactness and finite choice; using countably many relatively compact chart restrictions instead would require only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Include the endpoint knots and the chosen connected-sum representatives from [F2]. For these smooth knots and the finite smooth coordinate maps used in their sums, also code the derivatives of every finite order, their continuity moduli and rational difference-quotient remainder bounds; thus the inner model sees smooth knots, not merely continuous embeddings. Continuous maps on these standard metric domains are coded by their values on fixed countable rational dense sets and uniform continuity moduli on compact exhaustions; include inverse moduli for embeddings and chart inverses. All this countable numerical data is one real $r$. [F1, F2, F6, F7, given, construct, choose]

4.2 We use certificates, not an unqualified assertion that homeomorphism existence is absolute. For every open chart domain record its rational-ball code (relative rational half-balls at a boundary chart), compact exhaustion, and positive-distance margins putting the images of exhaustion pieces in the corresponding open image. Record both map/inverse identities on dense sets. For the pair condition record the parametrization of the linear plane section and its identities with the annulus parametrization; on smaller charts also record positive separation from the compact remainder of the annulus outside that patch. A finite parameter-patch cover and a Lebesgue-number certificate cover the entire annulus. Properness is certified on the compact subannuli $S^1\times[1/j,1-1/j]$ by positive separation from the ambient end levels. Equalities with the oriented endpoint parametrizations and the product collars are dense-set equalities with their continuity moduli. The smooth derivative identities are certified by rational difference quotients and their coded remainder bounds at each finite order. These certificates express input validity using only rational inequalities, integer indices and quantification over natural numbers. They therefore have the same truth in $L[r]$ and in the ambient universe; in particular the coded input is valid in $L[r]$. [F1, F2, F7, step 4.1, construct]

4.3 Apply [F6] inside $L[r]$, which satisfies full Choice by [F7]. It gives a locally flat annulus for the two connected sums. In that model choose its finite pair-chart cover, inverse maps, compact-exhaustion moduli, open-image margins and end-collar certificates of the same form as in step 4.2; collect them into a real $s\in L[r]$. Decode $s$ in the ambient universe by completion from the rational dense domains. The coded forward and inverse moduli give continuous inverse maps on their coded domains; the dense-set identities extend to all points, and the open-image and separation certificates make these actual local pair charts with no additional surface branch. The finite cover certificate, properness margins, and endpoint/collar identities likewise persist. Thus the decoded object is an actual oriented proper locally flat annulus in the ambient $S^3\times I$, with the required endpoint connected sums and product collars. This transfer uses arithmetic certificates for the particular compact objects, not preservation of arbitrary sets or homeomorphisms between inner models. [F1, F2, F6, F7, step 4.1, step 4.2, construct]

4.4 Steps 4.1–4.3 earn the required compact specialization of the external TOP input under the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, without assuming ambient full AC. Together with the retained smooth construction in steps 1.1–3.1, this proves both implications in the unchanged Statement. No annulus-adapted transverse tube or ambient complement is inferred from the bare-arc theorem [F5]; that former local proof gap is bypassed by the explicitly external input [F6]. [F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, step 3.1, step 4.3]

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with two full twists in the clasp, using the twist convention of Hedden and Ording. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The normalized tau threshold]]

[[def-rasmussen-s-invariant|Rasmussen's s invariant and filtration convention]]

[Hedden and Ording, *The Ozsvath-Szabo and Rasmussen concordance invariants are not equal*, Theorem 1.1 and §§2.1–2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0512348v1)

[Rasmussen, *Khovanov homology and the slice genus*, §§3–4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0402131v1)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §§3.1 and 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, the specified positive-clasped two-twisted Whitehead double, and the source's twist convention.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is the axiom branch used by the knot invariant, the finite diagrams, and the smooth four-ball genus.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] defines tau by the first Alexander filtration level mapping nontrivially to total hat homology.

[F2] [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]] defines $s$ from the filtration levels of the two Lee homology generators.

[L1] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] identifies the actual full grid rectangle complex with the analytic knot Floer complex, preserving the normalized Seifert Alexander and Maslov gradings and all positive marked degrees. Its all-variable-zero specialization is the full hat complex tensored with the stated bigraded basepoint factors.

[L2] [[thm-rasmussen-s-bounds-smooth-four-ball-genus]] states the smooth genus bound used in the source to choose the value $s=2$ from the Khovanov calculation's alternatives, for actual embedded smooth surfaces; the bound alone does not compute the finite Khovanov groups, whose calculation is now supplied by [F3].

[L3] [[lem-lee-cobordism-filtration-genus-bound]] is the exact Lee-cobordism input required by [L2]; its smooth surface is required to be properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$ with product collars.

[F3] [[lem-two-twisted-positive-whitehead-trefoil-double-has-s-two]] proves $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$ from the admitted code, its exact finite Khovanov matrices, the Lee spectral sequence and the actual embedded genus-one bound.

[F4] [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] supplies the normalized Maslov-zero same-oriented-knot conjugation with both filtrations exchanged, its inverse and homotopies, and the normalized full reverse-mirror duality. Its finite hat dual has filtration given by the annihilator of the complementary filtration; the total three-sphere hat class has Maslov degree zero.

## Proof

**Given:** Countable Choice and the positive-clasped double with the two-full-twist convention in the Statement. All grid differentials below retain positive $X$ multiplicity.

1.1 Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. These conditions verify the individual isotopies and the displayed endpoint. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and two-full-twist framing retained. The complete integer arrows and finite move list are recorded with the computation data below; neither a knot-table name nor a Floer rank identifies this knot. [given, construct, algebra]

1.2 The orientation junction preserves the normalized filtered invariant without an ambient invertibility assumption. For a doubly-pointed diagram of an oriented knot $J$, swapping only $w,z$ presents $J^r$. The actual disks are unchanged and their two marked degrees exchange, so $I:[x,i,j]\mapsto[x,j,i]$ is a Laurent-linear swap-filtered chain isomorphism to that diagram. The carried zero-Seifert cap gives $A'(x)=-A(x)$. The relative disk index then gives $M'(x)=M(x)-2A(x)+c$ for one integer $c$, so $I$ has constant full Maslov degree $c$. Compose it with the normalized same-oriented-knot conjugation of [F4], whose Maslov degree is zero and which swaps the two filtrations, including its inverse and homotopies. The composite is an ordinary bifiltered equivalence to $J^r$ of degree $c$. Its vertical hat quotient is an isomorphism between the two total three-sphere hat groups, each concentrated in normalized Maslov degree zero; hence $c=0$. This proves equality of the normalized inclusion thresholds for $J,J^r$. It also identifies their normalized bigraded knot Floer homologies. Apply this to the grid in step 1.1. Reflecting its columns, $O_r\mapsto11-O_r$ and $X_r\mapsto11-X_r$, gives a grid for its mirror: $(x,y,h)\mapsto(-x,y,h)$ reverses ambient orientation and keeps vertical strands over horizontal strands. No further knot-recognition premise is needed for this second grid. [F1, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Compute the full tilde differential of each of these two explicit grids. For a permutation state $p$, use $M_O(p)=I(p,p)-I(p,O)-I(O,p)+I(O,O)+1$ and $2A(p)=M_O(p)-M_X(p)-11$, with marks at half-integer cell centers and $I$ counting pairs strictly increasing in both coordinates. In the quotient $Q=C/F_0C$ retain exactly the states with $A>0$. Only Maslov degrees $-1,0,1$ enter $H_0(Q)$; discarding the outgoing differential from degree $-1$ does not change that group. The inventory is exhaustive by the following finite assignment recurrence. For used columns $S$ in the first $r=|S|$ rows, choosing $c\notin S$ increments the state-state term by $|\{b\in S:b<c\}|$. Add $-\#\{k\ge r:O_k\ge c\}-\#\{k<r:O_k<c\}$ to obtain the Maslov increment; the Alexander increment is the corresponding $X$ expression minus its $O$ expression. Accumulating the resulting two-variable polynomial over the $4096$ column subsets counts every permutation exactly once. For every retained state and ordered pair of distinct rows, take its southwest/northeast rectangle, reject a rectangle containing an interior state point or $O$, and retain every other rectangle, including those containing $X$. Its output transposes the two chosen columns; discard that output only when its Alexander value is at most zero. Summing modulo two gives the actual quotient matrix. The first grid has $45\,824$ retained states, $159\,685$ rectangle orbits, including $24\,181$ with positive $X$ multiplicity, and $158\,523$ nonzero matrix entries. The reflected grid has $6080$ retained states and $11\,474$ rectangle orbits and nonzero entries. Every term has Maslov drop one and Alexander drop exactly its $X$ multiplicity; actual matrix multiplication gives $d^2=0$ in both quotients. These are the literal rectangle counts of [L1], rather than a formal-domain enumeration. [L1, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.2 Exact column elimination over $\mathbb F_2$ gives $$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}&\dim Q_1&\dim Q_0&\dim Q_{-1}&\operatorname{rank}d_1&\operatorname{rank}d_0\\\hline G&12347&17919&15558&8384&9535\\G^{\mathrm{mirror}}&4385&1463&232&1243&220.\end{array}$$ To specify the finite rank operation, encode a column by its row bits; repeatedly cancel its highest nonzero row with the previously retained pivot column at that row, or retain it as a new pivot if no such column exists. The counts of retained pivots are the displayed ranks. The saved complete columns and pivot-reduction traces give these computations directly. A separate exact verification used the complete joint assignment polynomial, checked every state and both normalized grid gradings, reconstructed every retained rectangle, checked $d^2$, and recomputed both ranks. Thus $$\dim H_0(Q_G)=17919-8384-9535=0,\qquad\dim H_0(Q_{G^{\mathrm{mirror}}})=1463-1243-220=0.$$ This uses the full filtered quotients, including the positive-$X$ terms in the first matrix. [L1, step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 Apply [L1]'s absolutely normalized filtered comparison and specialize all marking variables to zero. The full tilde complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the doubly-pointed full hat complex tensored with $V^{\otimes11}$, where the two degrees of $V$ are $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$. Its total Maslov-zero homology is consequently one-dimensional, represented by the normalized three-sphere generator tensored with the sole degree-zero vector of $V^{\otimes11}$. Its filtration threshold is exactly $\tau(J)$: inclusion into that tensor factor and projection onto it are filtered degree-zero chain maps, so they give both threshold inequalities. The exact sequence $0\to F_0C\to C\to Q\to0$ and step 2.2 show that this total Maslov-zero class comes from $H_0(F_0C)$ for each grid. Hence $\tau(J)\le0$ and $\tau(mJ)\le0$, for the actual knot $J$ of step 1.1 and its mirror. [F1, L1, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

3.1 For completeness derive the required threshold sign from [F4]'s normalized reverse-mirror duality. Let $D$ be the finite normalized doubly-pointed full hat complex and write $t$ for its inclusion threshold. Its dual filtration is $F_sD^\vee=\{\lambda:\lambda(F_{-s-1}D)=0\}$. Choose a total generator cycle $z\in F_tD_0$. Then $z\notin\operatorname{im}(d:D_1\to D_0)+F_{t-1}D_0$: any such expression would give a homologous cycle at level $t-1$. Finite-dimensional linear algebra therefore gives a functional $\lambda$ vanishing on that sum and taking value one on $z$. It is a nonzero dual homology class at filtration $-t$. Conversely every functional at level $s<-t$ vanishes on $F_tD$, hence on $z$, and cannot represent the nonzero dual class. Thus the dual threshold is exactly $-t$. The absolute normalization and full duality in [F4], together with the orientation junction of step 1.2, give $\tau(mJ)=-\tau(J)$. Combining the two actual quotient inequalities of step 2.3 forces $\tau(J)=0$. By step 1.2 this is the normalized tau value of the actual two-twisted positive Whitehead trefoil in the Statement. [F1, F4, step 1.2, step 2.3, construct, algebra]

3.2 The admitted diagram and framing in step 1.1 are also those of [F3]. That accepted finite Lee computation gives $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$. Together with the independently established normalized value in step 3.1 this proves both numerical assertions of the Statement. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Computation data

The complete new geometric certificate is [the sixteen-crossing-to-twelve-grid admission](../research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-supervision-20261020/floer-weighted/d2-grid/admission-proof.md), with the integer arrows and all $986$ moves in that directory. The exact quotient inputs, state inventories, full positive-$X$ matrix columns and pivot traces are in [the direct D2 computation](../research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-supervision-20261020/floer-whitehead/d2-grid-count/). The count is implemented by `count-high-quotient.cpp`; the separate complete verification is `verify-quotients.py`, with its successful output in `quotient-verification.json`. The formulas, finite enumeration and linear-algebra operations are specified in the proof; these files retain their full finite execution data.

## Statement

No closed nonorientable piecewise-linear surface embeds in the standard oriented piecewise-linear three-sphere $S^3$.

## Statement references

[[cor-homology-of-spheres]] — $H_2(S^3;\mathbb F_2)=0$.

[[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] — finite simplicial and singular homology agree.

[[def-r-orientation-of-a-topological-manifold]] — orientation is a continuous generating section of the local integral homology system.

[[def-pl-embedding-and-subpolyhedron]] — the PL embedding and subpolyhedron convention.

[[lem-pl-embedded-polyhedron-admits-compatible-subcomplex-triangulation]] — a subdivision of a fixed triangulation makes the embedded surface a subcomplex.

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] — the standard orientation of $S^3$.

[[def-oriented-cellular-chain-group]] — oriented cellular generators and induced face signs.

[[def-induced-boundary-orientation]] — oriented cellular generators and induced face signs.

[[lem-the-cellular-boundary-squares-to-zero]] — the cellular boundary of a cellular boundary is zero.

[Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger, Corollary 5.5](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hass/Research/Papers/Complexity/hlp.pdf) — a knot exterior has no embedded projective plane because it embeds in $S^3$.

[Rourke–Sanderson, §§1.7 and 2.12](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/rsplx.pdf) — the subpolyhedron convention and compatible finite subdivisions used below.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A closed PL surface $F$ embedded in the standard oriented PL $3$-sphere.

[F1] [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]: $H_2(S^3;\mathbb F_2)=0$.

[F2] [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]: the finite triangulation used below computes singular homology with coefficients in $\mathbb F_2$.

[F3] [[def-cellular-homology]] and [[thm-cellular-boundary-is-the-incidence-degree-matrix]]: the cellular chain groups are generated by oriented cells, and each boundary coefficient is the signed sum of incident-cell coefficients.

[F4] [[def-r-orientation-of-a-topological-manifold]]: an orientation of an $n$-manifold is a continuous section choosing a generator of each local integral homology group $H_n(M,M\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)$; this is the definition used for both the ambient sphere and the surface $F$.

[F5] [[def-oriented-cellular-chain-group]]: an orientation of a tetrahedral cell selects its integral cellular generator.

[F6] [[lem-pl-embedded-polyhedron-admits-compatible-subcomplex-triangulation]]: a finite subdivision of the ambient triangulation contains $F$ as a subcomplex.

[F7] [[def-induced-boundary-orientation]]: the orientation induced on a face is determined by the outward-normal-first convention.

[F8] [[lem-the-cellular-boundary-squares-to-zero]]: the cellular boundary operator satisfies $\partial^2=0$.

[F9] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] and [[def-pl-embedding-and-subpolyhedron]]: the ambient is the standard oriented PL $3$-sphere. The finite triangulation in [F6] is a subdivision of its standard combinatorial triangulation, so every triangular face has link $S^0$ and exactly two tetrahedral cofaces.

## Proof

1.1 By [F6], take a finite subdivision of the standard triangulation in which $F$ is a subcomplex. Sum its triangular faces with coefficient $1$ in cellular $2$-chains over $\mathbb F_2$. Each edge of the closed surface is incident to exactly two of these triangles, so the sum $z$ has zero boundary. [given, F3, F6, construct]

2.1 By [F1] and [F2], $[z]=0$ in $H_2(S^3;\mathbb F_2)$, so $z=\partial c$ for a finite cellular $3$-chain $c$. Give each tetrahedron its coefficient $0$ or $1$ in $c$. [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 Orient each tetrahedron by the local orientation of $S^3$ in [F4] and take the integral cellular chain $C$ with the same coefficients $0$ or $1$ as $c$; [F5] identifies these oriented cells with the integral chain generators. For any triangular face outside $F$, its coefficient in $\partial c$ is zero modulo $2$, so its two incident tetrahedra have equal coefficients. Their induced face orientations are opposite: in an oriented PL coordinate ball at an interior point of that face, the tetrahedra occupy opposite half-balls, and the outward-normal-first rule [F7] reverses the face sign. Their contributions to $\partial C$ therefore cancel. For a face in $F$, the coefficient of $\partial c$ is one modulo $2$, so exactly one incident tetrahedron has coefficient one; its contribution to $\partial C$ is $+1$ or $-1$. Thus $w=\partial C$ is supported on $F$ with coefficient $+1$ or $-1$ on each triangle. [given, F3, F4, F5, F7, F9, step 2.1]

4.1 By [F8], $\partial w=\partial^2C=0$. Hence along each edge of $F$ the two incident oriented triangles induce opposite edge orientations. The triangles around any vertex form a cycle because $F$ is a triangulated surface; these compatible edge orientations therefore give one local orientation on its star. Interior points of triangles, edges and vertex stars cover $F$, and the local generators agree on their overlaps. They define the continuous orientation section of [F4], contradicting nonorientability. [F4, F8, step 3.1, construct, contradiction] ∎

## Statement

Let $T$ be an oriented torus and let $([\mu],[\lambda])$ be an ordered basis of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. An unoriented essential simple closed curve on $T$ has homology class $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ for a unique pair $(p,q)$ up to simultaneous sign, and that pair is primitive: $\gcd(p,q)=1$. Conversely, every primitive pair $(p,q)$ determines an essential simple closed curve, unique up to isotopy and simultaneous reversal of orientation.

## Statement references

[William P. Thurston, *The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds*, Chapter 4, §4.5](https://library.slmath.org/nonmsri/gt3m/PDF/4.pdf)

[Danny Calegari, *Kleinian Groups*, §2.3.2](https://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/courses/kleinian_groups_2015/kleinian_groups.pdf)

[Benson Farb and Dan Margalit, *A Primer on Mapping Class Groups*, Chapter 1, Proposition 1.10](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/~a019210/Farb%20Magalit_Primer%20on%20Teichmuller%20theory.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An oriented torus $T$ and an ordered integral basis $([\mu],[\lambda])$ of its first homology.

[A1] Identify $T$ with $\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ so the coordinate loops represent $[\mu]$ and $[\lambda]$; the chosen basis fixes this coordinate convention.

## Proof

1.1 Let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $\gcd(p,q)=1$. Bézout's identity gives $r,s\in\mathbb Z$ with $ps-qr=1$. The matrix with columns $(p,q)$ and $(r,s)$ lies in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$, so it induces a homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$. The image of the first coordinate circle is embedded, essential, and represents $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. Reversing its parameter negates both coefficients, so the unoriented curve is unchanged. [given, A1, construct, algebra]

1.2 If $\gamma$ is an essential simple closed curve on $T$, it is nonseparating; cutting along it gives an annulus. An arc joining the two annulus boundary circles closes to a simple curve $\delta$ meeting $\gamma$ once, so the algebraic intersection is $[\gamma]\cdot[\delta]=\pm1$. Writing $[\gamma]=p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ and $[\delta]=a[\mu]+b[\lambda]$ gives $pb-qa=\pm1$ because the ordered basis has intersection form $\pm1$. Any common divisor of $p,q$ would divide $pb-qa$, so $\gcd(p,q)=1$. [given, A1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Suppose $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are essential simple closed curves whose primitive classes agree up to sign. Reverse one orientation if necessary so their classes agree, and isotope them to be transverse. Let $v$ be their common primitive class and let $A=\mathbb R^2/\langle T_v\rangle$ be the cyclic cover of $T$ corresponding to the subgroup generated by $v$. A lift of each curve to $A$ is an embedded essential circle representing the generator of $H_1(A;\mathbb Z)$. Their algebraic intersection in the annulus $A$ is zero, so if they meet the signed crossing count in a fundamental period has both signs. Lift these circles to the universal cover $\mathbb R^2$ of $A$. Their chosen lifts are proper lines invariant under the same translation $T_v$; they have the same two ends at infinity. Opposite-sign crossings on this pair of lines have a bounded complementary disk between subarcs, by the Jordan curve theorem. Among all such disks choose one with the fewest interior intersections with lifted curves, and among ties one of least transverse width modulo the deck translations. Any lifted arc entering its interior cuts off a disk with fewer interior intersections; any nontrivial translate meeting it yields a disk of smaller transverse width. Thus its interior misses every lift and translate, so it projects injectively to an embedded bigon in $T$. Isotoping one curve across this bigon removes exactly two intersections and creates none. Since the original intersection set is finite, repetition terminates and makes the curves disjoint. Cutting $T$ along $\gamma_0$ gives an annulus, and the disjoint essential curve $\gamma_1$ is parallel to its core, so the two curves cobound a subannulus. Isotopy across that annulus carries $\gamma_0$ to $\gamma_1$. Thus the primitive class modulo simultaneous sign determines exactly one unoriented isotopy class. [given, A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct] ∎

## Diagram

Each unit grid square is a fundamental domain for $\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$; the bold $2$-by-$1$ rectangle is a display window containing two such squares. The red segment joins $(0,0)$ to its exact lattice translate $(2,1)$, so its lattice translates project to one simple closed curve because $\gcd(2,1)=1$. The blue arrows mark the $\mu$ and $\lambda$ lattice directions. This picture illustrates one primitive pair; the proof establishes the claim for every pair.

```tikz
  \draw[thick] (0,0) rectangle (2,1);
  \draw[->,blue,thick] (0.12,0.06) -- (0.92,0.06) node[midway,below] {$\mu$};
  \draw[->,blue,thick] (0.08,0.10) -- (0.08,0.88) node[midway,left] {$\lambda$};
  \draw[->,red,very thick] (0,0) -- (2,1);
  \node[red,above] at (1.15,0.65) {$2\mu+\lambda$};
  \node at (1,-0.32) {display window};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Statement

Let $M$ be a connected smooth $3$-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$
be a nonempty closed connected smooth embedded surface with
$\pi_1(S)=1$. Suppose there is an open neighborhood $N$ of $S$ such that
$N$ is path-connected and simply connected, and $N\setminus S$ has exactly two
path-connected simply connected components $N_-$ and $N_+$. Suppose also that
$M\setminus S$ is path-connected and contains an embedded compact arc
$\nu$ joining $N_-$ to $N_+$, with an open tubular neighborhood $T$ such that
$T\cap N$ consists of exactly two disjoint open $3$-balls, one in each side
component. Then
$$
\pi_1(M)\cong \pi_1(M\setminus S)*\mathbb Z.
$$
The cyclic factor is represented by a loop that joins the two sides of $N$ and
returns between them through $M\setminus S$.

## Statement references

[Friedl, Theorem 5.1](https://friedl.app.uni-regensburg.de/papers/2024_knot-theory-final.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The manifold, embedded surface, neighborhood, and path-connectivity and simple-connectivity hypotheses in the statement.

[F1] For an open cover by two path-connected sets with path-connected intersection, the fundamental group of the union is the pushout of the two inclusion homomorphisms. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data above.

1.1 Put $U=M\setminus S$ and $V=N\cup T$. These are path-connected open sets covering $M$. Their intersection consists of $N_-$, $N_+$, and the tube joining their end balls. Cover the intersection by the two side components with the respective half of the tube. Each set is path-connected and simply connected, and their overlap is a contractible middle tube. Hence [F1] gives $\pi_1(U\cap V)=1$. [given, F1, construct]

1.2 Join the centers of the two end balls by an embedded arc $\alpha$ in the connected smooth $3$-manifold $N$, and let $Q$ be a thin open tubular neighborhood of $\alpha$ in $N$, enlarged at its ends to meet those balls. The open sets $N$ and $W=T\cup Q$ cover $V$. The set $W$ is a thickened loop formed by the two tubes $T$ and $Q$, so $\pi_1(W)\cong\mathbb Z$; $N\cap W$ is $Q$ together with the two end balls and is contractible. Since $N$ is simply connected, [F1] gives $\pi_1(V)\cong\mathbb Z$. [given, F1, step 1.1, construct]

2.1 Apply [F1] to the open cover $M=U\cup V$. Step 1.1 gives $\pi_1(U\cap V)=1$, while $\pi_1(U)=\pi_1(M\setminus S)$ and step 1.2 gives $\pi_1(V)=\mathbb Z$. The pushout is therefore the free product $\pi_1(M\setminus S)*\mathbb Z$. A generator of the second factor is represented by $\alpha$ followed by $\nu^{-1}$, proving the stated description. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The normalized finite filtered complex and tau threshold]]

[[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot|The fixed oriented connected-sum gluing convention]]

[[lem-tau-additive-for-filtered-tensor-products|Additivity of the threshold under a filtered tensor product]]

[[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined|Independence of local connected-sum choices]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Knot Floer homology and the four-ball genus*, Proposition 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0301149v4)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

[Ozsvath, Stipsicz, and Szabo, *Grid Homology for Knots and Links*, Chapters 5, 6, and 13](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~petero/GridHomologyBook.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, the knots and oriented Seifert surfaces, and the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. We work first over $R=\mathbb F_2[U]$ with the full disk differential, retaining every positive $z$ multiplicity; localization will give the infinity complex. An ordinary doubly pointed model has one $w$ and one $z$, with generators placed at $(i,j)=(0,A_F(x))$.

[F1] Actual full-marked disk counts, finite polynomial differentials, connected-generator relative indices and relative Alexander gradings are established. Good end paths exclude nonconstant strips of nonpositive index. [[thm-balanced-knot-data-admit-full-marked-square-zero-holomorphic-counts]] [[thm-balanced-s-three-knot-generators-admit-consistent-relative-gradings]]

[F2] Actual strictly admissible polygon counts apply also to intermediate three-manifolds other than $S^3$. They retain all nonnegative marked degrees, and give finite triangle maps, their chain-map equations, coherent perturbations and the required parameter homotopies. These statements do not themselves give a top cycle or the multiplication equivalence constructed below. [[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]] [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]]

[F3] The actual constant-root inverse, torus mean inverse and supported dipole responses, and the exhaustive torus-target plumbing calculation are available. We use the displayed responses of ordinary stabilization, not its conclusion for a cancelling $S^3$ handle, and check below the changed two-crossing torus and marked-point transfer. [[lem-transverse-linear-strip-cauchy-riemann-isomorphism]] [[lem-real-boundary-strip-cauchy-riemann-inverse-with-free-end-constants]] [[lem-flat-complex-torus-cauchy-riemann-mean-inverse-and-normalized-dipoles]] [[thm-balanced-knot-ordinary-stabilization-has-full-minus-inverse-maps]]

[F4] Same-handlebody top generators are actual cycles; their top products have count one and no positive marked terms. Full-minus auxiliary and attaching-move maps have finite polynomial filtered inverses and inverse homotopies. [[lem-same-handlebody-model-top-counts-have-no-positive-marked-terms]] [[thm-balanced-knot-full-minus-auxiliary-continuations-are-filtered-equivalences]] [[thm-balanced-knot-attaching-moves-have-full-minus-inverse-maps]] Its actual small-copy operation retains one positive core in each old region, balances exact-copy lunes, and proves the unique nearest thin triangle by a bounded scalar inverse. [[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]], Proof3.1–6.1.

[F5] The polygon relative index identifies actual Spin-c differences, rather than formal domains only. The negative modified Morse field on the knot exterior has the explicit zero-relative-Euler zero-surgery cap. Its normalized Alexander value is half the relative Euler number of its perpendicular plane on the exterior Seifert surface, with boundary section $\partial_\lambda=-\partial_\theta$; the cap contributes zero. The local tube model is $f=\sin t(1-r^2/2)$, its selected generator trajectory modifications are outside that tube, and its value is preserved by followed mark-free attaching isotopies. The normalized full-minus comparisons preserve this absolute origin and the degree-zero total-hat Maslov origin. [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]] [[thm-doubly-pointed-s-three-moves-preserve-the-seifert-normalized-filtration]] [[thm-handle-cancellation]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-spin-c-difference-is-the-capped-periodic-domain]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-relative-maslov-variation-is-chern-plus-marks]]

[[lem-tau-additive-for-filtered-tensor-products]] [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]] [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

## Proof

1.1 Choose finite doubly pointed good diagrams $(\Sigma_1,\alpha,\beta,w_1,z_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,\xi,\eta,w_2,z_2)$ and their actual full count data from [F1]. Remove disks at $z_1,w_2$ and join their oriented boundaries; retain $w_1,z_2$. The two knot arcs ending at the removed points concatenate across that cylinder. Their other ends, and the boundary-parallel arc witnesses in both handlebodies, are unchanged. This is the oriented connected-sum neck. For the multiplication triple use the three systems $A=\alpha\cup\xi'$, $B=\beta\cup\xi$, $C=\beta'\cup\eta$, where primes are separately labeled sufficiently small exact Hamiltonian copies. Give each copied circle a Morse function with one maximum and one minimum, chosen away from its finitely many old intersection points. The maximum crossings specify $\Theta_\beta,\Theta_\xi$. In a cut handlebody, carry its complete disk system to meridians of the standard boundary-connected sum of solid tori; this gives an actual split product-circle model for these copied systems. These are diffeomorphisms of the diagram and its arc witnesses, not extra analytic identifications. [F1, F4, F6, given, construct]

1.2 We first establish the required split one-handle inclusion, including a mark moved across its neck. Let $E$ be a flat torus with a circle and a small exact Hamiltonian copy, having top and bottom crossings $c_+,c_-$. Put its plumbing point $a$ and its new mark $b$ off the narrow isotopy annuli and off these crossings. Let $D_1,D_2$ be its two elementary bigons. Lifting boundary paths to the plane identifies the relative class ambiguity with the kernel of $\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z^2$ sending the two circle windings to their common primitive slope; since the torus has zero second homotopy, this kernel is precisely the annular period $P=D_1-D_2$. Its area is zero by exactness and it has both signs. A self-end domain is $kP$; a forward domain is $(k+1)D_1-kD_2$, nonnegative only for $k=0,-1$; a reverse domain has coefficients $k-1,-k$, never both nonnegative. Thus a nonconstant holomorphic self-end strip would have zero area and cannot exist. From $c_+$ to $c_-$ there are exactly the two positive bigons in the isotopy annuli, each a disk with its two corners and hence a unique representative modulo translation by the disk Riemann map; reflection or the transverse strip inverse gives its regularity and count one. Both bigons miss $a,b$. A reverse-direction class has negative area, so cannot occur. The other periodic classes change neither these areas nor the mark vectors. These are the actual split $S^1\times S^2$ top data, not the once-intersecting cancelling torus. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 Plumb $E$ at a point $q$ in the region of the old mark to be transferred, and place the transferred mark at $b$. Choose $q$ a regular simple-root value for every old rigid strip, with distinct physical incidence positions; this is possible in a small disk of its old marked region because the finitely many protected holomorphic root maps have finitely many critical and discriminant values there. Moving the mark within that region changes no domain coefficient or represented pointed knot. Use a smaller disk on which the whole incidence tensor is standard. At a self-end limit the principal torus root is the constant $c_+$ by step 1.2. Every old simple incidence at $q$ then contributes one inclusion copy of $E$ with two source punctures, one at $a$ and one at $c_+$. Its local equations are exactly the constant-root equations in [F3]: for residues $\lambda_j=\epsilon L_j$ at positions $b_j$ the transverse strip response is $\sum\chi_j\lambda_j/(z-b_j)-Q_\perp D(\sum\chi_j\lambda_j/(z-b_j))$; the physical projection uses the real/real inverse, retaining its right real end constant. The torus response subtracts its mean using a supported density away from both punctures. Transfer of a positive Laurent mode multiplies it by $(\epsilon/r^2)^n$ or $(\lambda_j/r^2)^n$. The resulting trace equation has operator norm $O(|\epsilon|)$, and its divided mean equations are $A_j+L_j+O_{C^1}(|\epsilon|)=0$, where $A_j\ne0$ is the old simple-root inverse derivative. Thus they have the unique solution $b_j=w_j+O(|\epsilon|)$, $L_j=-A_j+O(|\epsilon|)$. The two transverse boundary lines near $c_+$ may have any fixed nonzero angle: their strip inverse in [F3] applies unchanged. No global straightness of the two copied circles is needed by this response. [F1, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.2 **Construct the compatible connected Morse data.** Use [F5]'s actual tube coordinates on each input, with its Seifert collar $\theta=0$ and its function $f=\sin t(1-r^2/2)$. Choose the connecting disks about $z_1,w_2$ so small that their knot-tube neighborhoods miss every selected index-one/index-two generator trajectory tube. The lower and upper pieces of the connected surface bound the boundary-connected sums of the respective handlebodies. Before cancelling their tree handles the lower half has its two old minimum balls and the joining one-handle; the upper half has its two old maximum balls and the joining two-handle. Put the joining handle cores on the concatenated lower and upper bridge arcs. This is possible in the product neighborhoods of their boundary-parallel witness disks: the joining core and the two old bridge pieces are an interval in that product, and the collars of $F_1,F_2$ extend across it as the untwisted connected-sum Seifert ribbon. The lower interval contains, in order, one old minimum, the new index-one point, and the other old minimum. Cancel the first minimum with the joining index-one point; dually cancel the second maximum with the joining index-two point in the upper interval. These are the tree-edge zero/one cancellations (and their reversed two/three versions): one joining-handle foot is on each old ball, hence the attaching zero-sphere meets the cancelled ball's belt sphere once. No old higher-index handle or selected generator trajectory is cancelled. After cancellation there is precisely one minimum and maximum and the two original higher-index systems. Thus the result is actual compatible Morse data for the connected diagram of step 1.1, with its concatenated bridge witnesses, not an arbitrarily assigned nonzero exterior field. [F1, F5, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Verify exhaustion and the index, rather than assuming a tensor differential. The root determinant transition is $-\epsilon/\xi^2$ at each target matching; its squared winding is minus four, cancelled by the four additional projection branch orders of the torus dipole. Consequently a self-end reference has the old index. Any additional same-domain ambiguity here is an exact-copy annular period with zero Chern evaluation in the torsion pair sector, so the general relative index formula [F5] gives the same index for each actual class; the comparison is not relying on the new manifold being $S^3$. The extraction in [F3] uses only fixed old-core estimates, bounded nonnegative domain coefficients, Laurent expansion on target annuli, and finite projection branching. Those arguments apply to this same plumbing before identifying its torus principal map: here step 1.2 makes it constant at its specified crossing. The additional torus annular periods have zero area, so cannot add a positive component or an unbounded domain ray. Old boundary disks and closed horizontal degrees have index at least two, exactly as in the referenced determinant calculation. At total index one a self-end limit therefore contains exactly one old rigid strip. Its simple incidences force one degree-one torus per incidence and no branching matching tree. The converse response and residue estimate $\lambda+\epsilon A+o(\max|\lambda|+|\epsilon|)=0$ force every convergent solution into step 2.1's unique response neighborhood. Its normalized kernel is zero by the same trace/mean inverse, so the actual operator is onto. A top-to-bottom limit has the single bigon of step 1.2 and old index zero; the good old path forces its old component to be constant and its incidence list empty. Its two bigons cancel with identical marked vectors. For a bottom self-end the identical constant-root argument applies; a bottom-to-top principal component has negative area by step 1.2 and is impossible. These facts for ALL the split-factor generators also exclude a nonconstant nonpositive-index end path. Finally each degree-one inclusion torus passes through $b$ once, so the NEW $b$ multiplicity equals the OLD $q$ multiplicity, including positive multiplicities. All other marks are untouched. Hence $x\mapsto x\times c_+$ is an actual full-polynomial chain inclusion preserving the transferred and retained mark degrees. This proves the operation for the supplied split factor; no assertion about arbitrary nontrivial summand-neck disk matching has been used. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Write the relevant interval as $K=\{y=z=0\}$ and its Seifert ribbon as $F=\{z=0,y\ge0\}$. ## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be an irreducible one-dimensional character component whose peripheral eigenvalue image is a curve component $A_X(M,L)=0$ of the ordinary A-polynomial. At a smooth point where $M,L\ne0$, $\partial_M A_X\ne0$, and $\partial_L A_X\ne0$, the rational adjoint-twisted slope is
$$s_K=-\frac{M}{L}\frac{\partial_M A_X}{\partial_L A_X}.$$
If $x$ is an ideal point of the smooth projective completion of this curve and the associated Culler-Shalen construction yields an essential surface of boundary slope $r$ in the fixed meridian-longitude convention, the limiting slope at $x$ is $-r$.

## Statement references

[Bénard, Florens, and Rodau, Theorems 1.3 and 1.5 and §§4–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2103.14151)

[Culler and Shalen, §3](https://marc-culler.info/static/home/papers/CharacterVarieties.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a one-dimensional character component, an admissible generic locus, its peripheral eigenvalue curve, and an ideal point with the associated surface specified in the statement.

[F1] The rationality lemma supplies this projective extension on components containing irreducible characters when its stated dense scheme-smooth, non-boundary-parabolic admissible locus is nonempty. Its hypotheses are not automatic for every component in the present Statement. The generic word-chain calculation in [F3] proves the needed rational extension on the specified curve components; its Proof8.1 handles the reducible-only component explicitly, where the peripheral curve is $L=1$ and the slope is zero. Thus the rationality lemma is used only within its stated scope, and it independently records the corresponding extension when that scope applies. [[lem-adjoint-twisted-slope-is-rational-on-a-character-component]]

[F2] The Bénard–Florens–Rodau convention orders the boundary basis as $(v\otimes\lambda,v\otimes\mu)$ and defines $s=-b/a$ for a kernel generator $a(v\otimes\lambda)+b(v\otimes\mu)$ ([[def-character-variety-logarithmic-slope-invariant]]).

[F3] [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]] gives the actual generic representation, rank-one peripheral inclusion, differentiated word-chain functional, and the projective identity $s=[-M(A_X)_M:L(A_X)_L]$. It explicitly includes infinite slopes and requires no cotangent-space identification or scheme-reducedness premise.

[F4] [[lem-logarithmic-ideal-point-limits-and-lattice-fixed-peripheral-slopes]] constructs finite-field extending valuations, proves the logarithmic projective limit at a peripheral-curve ideal point, and proves the boundary-slope equality for an actual supplied equivariant inverse-image witness. It does not supply that witness or identify a character ideal point with a peripheral ideal point.

[F5] In the associated Culler–Shalen construction stipulated by the Statement, the initial surface is the transverse inverse image of edge midpoints of the actual equivariant dual map. Interior compressions and deletion of components leave each surviving boundary circle unchanged up to boundary isotopy. This is the construction stipulated in the conditional assertion, not a surface-existence premise inferred from a citation ([[def-adjoint-twisted-homology-and-culler-shalen-data]]).

## Proof

1.1 **The rational affine identity.** By [F3], the actual generic peripheral inclusion kernel, in the ordered basis [F2], is the kernel of $(a,b)\mapsto a\,\mathrm dL/L+b\,\mathrm dM/M$. Its dimension is one, and the differential pair is nonzero. Differentiating $A_X(M,L)=0$ gives $$L(A_X)_L\,\mathrm dL/L+M(A_X)_M\,\mathrm dM/M=0.$$ Therefore [F2] and [F3] give the projective rational slope $[-M(A_X)_M:L(A_X)_L]$. Its affine ratio at the stated smooth point is $-M(A_X)_M/(L(A_X)_L)$, since the denominator there is nonzero. The rational extension is the one constructed by [F3]; where [F1]'s hypotheses hold, it agrees with the extension recorded there. This identity therefore includes its values wherever that displayed denominator is nonzero and does not rely on an unproved identification of exceptional pointwise homology kernels. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 **The peripheral ideal point and its actual valuation.** The curve whose completion occurs in the second clause is the preceding peripheral curve $A_X(M,L)=0$. Use its normalized affine open and the actual local DVR at its stipulated ideal point $x$, with valuation $v$. By [F4], $(v(L),v(M))\ne(0,0)$: if both coordinates were units, their affine coordinate ring and its integral closure would lie in the local DVR, and separatedness would put its center in that normalized affine open, contrary to idealness. The actual generic representation and common peripheral eigenline may be taken over a finite extension of this peripheral function field by [F3]: its field is finitely generated of transcendence degree one and finite over the field generated by the nonconstant coordinates $M,L$. By [F4] the valuation extends to this finite field, or to any further finite field used by the stipulated construction, with restriction $e v$ for an integer $e>0$. Thus no valuation on the representation field is merely assumed to exist. [F3, F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The boundary relation survives the stipulated construction.** Consider a surviving boundary circle of the associated essential surface, representing the primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ of its asserted boundary slope. Before the boundary-preserving compressions in [F5], that same circle is a boundary circle of the transverse inverse image of edge midpoints. A lift of the circle is connected and maps into the discrete midpoint set, so its image is one midpoint. Equivariance implies that its deck element fixes that midpoint. Access-path changes conjugate the element and the fixed point together. By [F4], its determinant-one peripheral matrix therefore has eigenvalue $L^aM^b$ of valuation zero: a fixed midpoint implies that its square fixes a lattice vertex, and the integral characteristic polynomial at that lattice excludes both positive and negative eigenvalue valuation. Consequently $$a\,v(L)+b\,v(M)=0.$$ An interior compression replaces an annular neighborhood of a circle in the interior of the surface by two disks in the interior of the exterior, and hence does not change the boundary one-manifold. Deleting a component only deletes its boundary circles. Boundary isotopy changes no homology class; orientation reversal changes both $a,b$ by a common sign. The same relation therefore holds for every boundary circle retained in the associated essential surface after these operations. This proves the boundary calculation for the actual stipulated construction; no essential-surface existence theorem or assertion about an unrelated vertex-stabilized surface is used. [F4, F5, step 1.2, given, construct, algebra]

3.1 **Evaluate the projective limit, including infinity.** By [F4], the rational logarithmic pair $[\mathrm dL/L:\mathrm dM/M]$ has value $[v(L):v(M)]$ at $x$. More explicitly, with a uniformizer $t$ and $D=\mathrm d/\mathrm dt$, writing $f=t^{v(f)}u$ gives $t Df/f=v(f)+t Du/u$, where $D$ preserves the actual local ring; the unit term vanishes on reduction. The valuation pair is nonzero by step 1.2. Its relation in step 2.1 identifies its projective line as $[-b:a]$. By step 1.1 this logarithmic pair is the rational slope, so its limiting value is $-b/a=-r$ in the fixed convention. The same homogeneous computation gives $0$ when $b=0$ and $\infty$ when $a=0$; neither case requires division by a zero valuation. All assertions of the Statement follow. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC, as in the smooth Casson–Gordon bordism convention. For every prime-power integer $d$ and $G=\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$, the oriented bordism group $\Omega_3^{SO}(K(G,1))$ is finite.

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space|The oriented bordism group of maps]]

[[lem-oriented-bordism-classes-over-a-space-form-an-abelian-group|The group structure]]

[Charles Livingston and Swatee Naik, *Introduction to Knot Concordance*, Theorem 8.4.7, pp. 170–171](https://chuck-livingston.github.io/math/Concordance_Book.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The standing AC convention of the smooth Casson–Gordon bordism construction, a prime power $d$, and $G=C_d\times\mathbb Z$.

[F1] These are geometric smooth oriented bordism groups of maps. [[def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space]], [[lem-oriented-bordism-classes-over-a-space-form-an-abelian-group]]

[F2] The complete relative-source cutting, low-dimensional coefficient fillings, skeletal exact-couple and periodic cyclic-resolution calculation gives $\Omega^{SO}_3(K(C_d\times\mathbb Z,1))=\mathbb Z/d$, for every positive integer $d$, under AC. [[lem-low-degree-geometric-bordism-over-finite-cyclic-times-circle]]

## Proof

1.1 Apply [F2] to the specified prime-power integer $d$. Its explicit cyclic resolution works for all $d$ without assuming $d$ prime, and its geometric skeletal comparison uses the same smooth bordism convention [F1]. It gives the isomorphism $\Omega^{SO}_3(K(G,1))\cong\mathbb Z/d$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The group $\mathbb Z/d$ has $d$ elements and is finite, including every exponent in a prime power. This proves the assertion under the stated AC convention, rather than inferring the prime-power calculation from its prime-order special case. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F\subset S^3$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy|The smooth oriented knot model in the standard three-sphere]]

[[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection|Existence of regular projections under countable choice]]

[[lem-seifert-bands-embedded-orientable-boundary-correct|The disk-and-band correctness lemma]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[F1] A link in the standard $S^3$ may be moved by an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy to lie in $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]])

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every oriented link contained in $\mathbb R^3$ has a dense set of regular projection directions. ([[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]])

[F3] A regular oriented diagram of one knot component has a connected compact smooth oriented embedded disk-and-band realization with that oriented boundary. ([[lem-seifert-bands-embedded-orientable-boundary-correct]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence principle stated in the item. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

1.1 By [F1], move $K$ by an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy into $\mathbb R^3$. Apply [F2] and [A1] to choose a regular projection direction. The resulting decorated projection is a finite regular oriented diagram $D$ of a single knot. [given, F1, F2, A1, choose]

2.1 Apply [F3] to $D$ to obtain a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $D$. ## Statement

Assume ACω. For every closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, the homology of the hat Heegaard Floer complex over $\mathbb F_2$ is independent, up to isomorphism, of the pointed admissible Heegaard diagram used to define it. The assertion is invariance of the group $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$; it does not assert a diagram-independent filtered chain homotopy type.

## Statement references

[[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold|Diagram-level hat Floer complex]]

[[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations|Required disk and polygon analytic foundations]]

[Ozsváth and Szabó, *Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds*, §§2–4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0101206)

[Lipshitz, *Heegaard Floer Homologies*, §§2–5](https://floer.wiki/more/courses/floer-homology/2024/lipshitz_heegaard_floer_homology.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, Y and two pointed admissible diagrams in the corrected full-module sense. No torsion or rational-homology-sphere hypothesis is imposed on Y.

[F1] Full-module admissibility tests EVERY intended Spin-c sector, even an empty-generator one. The finite Heegaard Spin construction supplies a determinant-trivial sector, so this is equivalent to the global mixed-sign condition. Every supplied complete geometric diagram has the actual finite winding preparation to a globally weak one. Actual globally weak chosen hat complexes and their square-zero finite differentials exist. ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], [[lem-complete-heegaard-data-have-a-zero-chern-spin-c-sector]], [[thm-globally-weak-closed-heegaard-data-admit-a-finite-chosen-hat-complex]], [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]])

[F2] The actual circular top cycles, top-triangle products and quadrilateral counts give handleslide chain maps with the displayed explicit inverse homotopies. Actual attaching isotopies have regular-interval transport and birth/death equivalences. Their proof supplies the uniform paired-dual winding preparation and explicit unit-pair cancellation. ([[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]], [[thm-globally-weak-hat-attaching-isotopies-have-actual-inverse-maps]])

[F3] Ordinary stabilization in a disk in the basepoint region has literal inverse chain isomorphisms $x\mapsto x\times c$ and $x\times c\mapsto x$, with zero inverse homotopies. Its separator proof is applied only in that region. ([[thm-hat-heegaard-stabilization-has-explicit-inverse-chain-maps]])

[F4] Transported diagram data identify actual counts by inverse chain isomorphisms. Actual fixed-background continuation now allows independently supplied generator jets and full boundary tensors. After that operation aligns chosen canonical data, the stated fixed-background full-boundary and changing-background theorems give actual equivalences with their common generator prescriptions. ([[lem-closed-pointed-diagram-isomorphisms-identify-hat-counts]], [[thm-fixed-symmetric-background-hat-complexes-with-different-boundary-values-are-equivalent]], [[thm-changing-complex-background-zero-marked-continuations-are-chain-equivalences]], [[thm-fixed-background-hat-continuations-allow-independent-generator-data]])

[F5] Any two supplied complete pointed splittings of this Y are joined by the actual finite general-manifold based geometric move theorem. It makes no assertion that its intermediate diagrams are admissible. ([[thm-based-heegaard-moves-generate-closed-three-manifold-diagram-equivalence]])

[F6] Broad auxiliary disks have same-boundary neat preparations and smooth standard cut balls. The finite graph model embeds an abstract handlebody in $S^3$ for this preparation. Smooth Schoenflies there supplies actual smooth balls. Marked planar cap transfers are actual disk slides, and two rooted-tree reductions of one extended ball cut are connected by actual marked slides. ([[lem-proper-compression-disks-admit-neat-witnesses-with-standard-cut-balls]], [[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], [[lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides]], [[lem-empty-cut-ball-births-erase-to-balanced-disk-slides]])

1.1 By [F1] both full-module admissible endpoints are globally weak. This implication uses the zero-Chern sector whether or not it is represented by a generator; testing existing generators alone would be insufficient. Use the actual generic hat data of [F1], retaining any independently supplied generic endpoint count choices. Generator charts are auxiliary parts of the construction, and need not have been agreed in advance. The independent-generator operation in [F4] first compares arbitrary supplied data at its OWN fixed background and area form to the canonical choices used in the finite comparisons below. Transported charts on actual diagram isomorphisms still give literal operator identifications. All subsequent comparisons are the actual operations in [F4]. Every comparison below is between actual finite count complexes. No knot-specialized result is substituted for a closed-manifold operation. [F1, F4, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 First prove the based complete-disk comparison needed on ONE handlebody. Prepare two systems as neat auxiliary witnesses and make their intersections transverse. A handlebody is irreducible using exactly [F6], without any irreducibility assumption about Y: carry its finite graph neighborhood to the standard handlebody model in $S^3$. An interior sphere bounds the two Schoenflies balls. The connected boundary of the handlebody lies on one side, so the ball on the other side misses that boundary and lies inside the handlebody, since its collar at the sphere does. Remove closed disk intersections as follows. Take a circle innermost on the first family over the entire second family. Its cap misses that second family. Replace the second disk's interior cap by a parallel of the first cap and round. Their sphere bounds the just proved interior ball. No other proper disk lies inside that ball, since its boundary is on the exterior handlebody boundary. Thus the boundary-fixed cap transfer preserves the whole second system's topological ball cuts and reduces the circle count. Only auxiliary witnesses change, with the same boundary curves. If using the topological cap transfer, the NEW smooth cut spheres have their actual smooth parametrizations from [F6]; no ambient smooth tangency change or arbitrary TOP smoothing is asserted. Iterate finitely. [F6, construct, algebra]

2.1 An outermost arc on a second-family disk now bounds a cap B missing the first family. Surgery of its first-family disk $D_i$ along B gives two disks pushed disjoint from that family. Cut the other first-family disks; the remaining manifold is a solid torus. Exactly one surgery disk is an essential meridian: their oriented relative classes add to the primitive old meridian, while an essential simple disk boundary is a primitive meridian and an inessential one bounds a ball by step 1.2. Two nonzero primitive classes could sum only to zero or twice a primitive class. Replacing $D_i$ by the essential disk $D_i'$ is therefore a complete system. In the original cut ball $D_i'$ separates the two faces of $D_i$; otherwise it would cut off a ball after regluing those faces and would be inessential. Choose its boundary cap not containing z. It contains exactly one $D_i$ face and finitely many other faces. [F6]'s planar construction slides $D_i$ across those faces until its outer rim is precisely $\partial D_i'$, followed by the empty-annulus isotopy. Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately. This is an actual based slide word, not just disk surgery or homology. The replacement uses one old subdisk and a parallel of B, so it strictly decreases the total remaining arc count. After finitely many exchanges the two families are disjoint. Their union cuts the first ball into balls: each proper disk has two rounded smooth sphere boundaries in the standard ball model, and [F6] gives both balls. Choose a tiny trivial arc near z missing this finite union, with a second endpoint w. The two original systems are two rooted-tree reductions of that common extended ball cut. 3.1 Prepare a finite same-system slide/isotopy word while its opposite system is fixed.
